jobs.title: COUNTRY DIRECTOR - PAKISTAN
jobs.description:
About : Action contre la Faim

Créée en 1979, Action contre la Faim est une organisation non gouvernementale internationale qui lutte contre la faim dans le monde. Sa charte des principes humanitaires - indépendance, neutralité, non-discrimination, accès libre et direct aux victimes, professionnalisme, transparence - fonde son identité depuis 45 ans. Sa mission est de sauver des vies en éliminant la faim par la prévention, la détection et le traitement de la sous-nutrition, en particulier pendant et après les situations d'urgence liées aux conflits et aux catastrophes naturelles. Action contre la Faim coordonne ses programmes autour de 7 domaines d'activités : Nutrition et Santé - Santé Mentale, Soutien Psychosocial - Sécurité Alimentaire et Moyens d'Existence - Eau, Assainissement et Hygiène - Plaidoyer - Climat - Recherche. En 2024, Action contre la Faim est venue en aide à plus de 26 millions de personnes dans 57 pays à travers le monde. www.actioncontrelafaim.org

Mission :

As Country Director, you will be responsible for implementing a sound and relevant delegation system, which will allow you to be accountable for all the following responsibilities
Responsible for providing the overall leadership and strategic guidance of the Country Office.
Responsible for overseeing the development, funding and implementation of the country strategy and the growth of program portfolio that effectively addresses the underlying causes and effects of malnutrition in line with ACF's values (Charter), Programming Principles, and Strategy.
Ensure that systems / procedures are in place and being properly implemented, and that they ensure the proper management, well being and safety of ACF staff, and the proper use of ACF resources.
Build on best practices previously developed on the mission
Create a shared vision among all staff and be responsible for promoting ACF Charter and ensuring an organizational culture where ACF core values are embedded, team work is encouraged and all staff feels valued.
Responsible for establishing and maintaining good working relationships with host government officials, donors and other partners.
Manage team : 8 direct reportees. The country team is composed of 43 staff.

Profile :

PROFILS
Essential:
Postgraduate (master) degree (or Bachelor degree with 8 years relevant professional experience)
At least 7 years of humanitarian and development experience and at least 4 years of senior management or leadership experience, including team leadership;
At least 2 years of previous experience as Country Director or equivalent leadership role;
Strong ability to think strategically; and out of the box;
Excellent knowledge and understanding of working in a complex, and sensitive environment;
Significant experience of managing strategic partnership;
Experience of managing security in a volatile environment;
Significant experience with external representation and promotion of programs with stakeholders and potential donors, and you are
High understanding and sensitivity to gender and inclusion ;
Excellent adaptation and culturally sensitivity skills; and knowledge and understanding of the Pakistani and South Asian context essential;
Fluent spoken and written English;
Preferred:
Urdu, Pashto or Baluch language skills;
A great sense of humour;
Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply.

EMPLOYMENT CONDITIONS
24 months fixed-term contract under Pakistani law, starting from 1st march 2027
Monthly basic salary range (based on the candidate's experience) : from 967,428 to 1,552,968 PKR
Other benefits :
Education allowance for children (maximum 4 children, under the age of 16 years) as per actual school fee invoice paid by ACF:80% of the Education Cost with a maximum of euros3,500/- per child per year will be covered; with a maximum of euros15,000/- per year / per family
Kindergarten / day care and university fee are not applicable.
Health Insurance covering whole family: self, spouse, children and parents:OPD Allowance: 130,000 PKR per Year - covering whole family: Self, spouse, children, and parents
Hospitalization Allowance: PKR 350,000 (Per Person, Per Ailment and Per Confinement). 50% enhancement in case of on-road/off-road accident in IPD Limit.Maternity Limit: Normal Delivery - 200,000 PKR, C-Section Limit - 250,000
Major Medical Care (MMC) per person, per annum - only for self, spouse & children : 500,000 PKR
Life Insurance:Death due to any cause (natural): 6 Million PKR
Accidental Death: 12 Million PKR
Communication Allowance: 2750 PKR per month
Pick & Drop - from residence to office and back
A temporary COLA might also be included

jobs.title: National Consultant – Technical Specialist on Community-Based Flood Management (CBFM) and GEDSI Implementation, Cambodia
jobs.description:
**A. About the Asian Disaster Preparedness Center**
Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization established for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes, with the vision of creating safer communities and fostering sustainable development through strengthened disaster risk reduction (DRR) and climate resilience across Asia and the Pacific. Since its establishment in 1986 as a regional technical capacity-building center, ADPC has evolved into a leading regional organization supporting countries to reduce disaster and climate risks through evidence-based, innovative, and inclusive approaches.
ADPC delivers a wide range of programs across its strategic priority areas, including:
● Risk Knowledge and Geoinformatics
● Policy and Institutional Systems
● Effective Localization for Resilience
● Climate Services
● Resilient Planning and Implementation
● Preparedness and Anticipatory Action
● Nature-based Solutions
● Financing for Resilience
● Resilient Recovery
● Food and Water Security
● Disaster Risk Finance and Insurance
● Health Risk Management
● Urban and Infrastructure Resilience
● Private Sector Engagement
● ADPC Knowledge Academy
These priority areas are reinforced by ADPC’s cross-cutting themes, which are embedded across all programs and operations:
● Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)
● Disaster and Climate Innovations
● Regional and Transboundary Cooperation
ADPC supports countries in implementing global frameworks including the Sendai Framework for Disaster Risk Reduction 2015–2030, the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), the Paris Agreement/UNFCCC, and the New Urban Agenda, while contributing to national and regional policy advancement on resilience. Through multi-sectoral partnerships, technical advisory services, capacity development, and program implementation across multiple countries, ADPC works to strengthen systems, institutions, and communities to better manage disaster and climate risks.
For additional details, please visit: http://www.adpc.net/

**B. Department Introduction**
The Preparedness and Climate Actions Department enhances the preparedness and climate action capacities of governments, NGOs, the private sector, and communities. It focuses on:

- Ensuring frameworks and implementation plans for disaster preparedness, response, and recovery are in place before disaster strikes.
- Strengthening institutional and community capacities for anticipatory action and resilient recovery.
- Promoting locally led DRR and climate resilience interventions through multi- stakeholder partnerships.

**C. Statement of Intent**
ADPC is supporting the implementation of the Climate Risk and Early Warning Systems (CREWS) 2.0 Project in Cambodia, which aims to strengthen people-centered early warning systems, preparedness, and community resilience to climate and disaster risks.

As part of the project, ADPC will support the implementation of Community-Based Flood Management (CBFM) approaches in three target communities in Cambodia, in close coordination with the National Committee for Disaster Management (NCDM), relevant subnational authorities, community representatives, and other project stakeholders.

The CBFM intervention will focus on strengthening community capacities to understand and manage flood risks; improving community-level preparedness, coordination, warning communication, and response arrangements; and promoting practical measures that can be sustained by communities and local authorities.

To strengthen national-level technical coordination and ensure the quality of CBFM and GEDSI interventions, ADPC seeks to engage a National Technical Specialist to provide technical guidance, technical review, institutional coordination, and quality assurance support throughout the implementation process.

The Consultant will serve as ADPC's designated national-level technical focal point for agreed activities, facilitating coordination with NCDM and other relevant national stakeholders and providing technical recommendations to ensure that project outputs are aligned with the agreed objectives, quality standards, and sustainability considerations.

Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI) will be integrated throughout the intervention. Attention will be given to ensuring the meaningful participation of women, persons with disabilities, older persons, and other groups that may face barriers in accessing early warning information, preparedness services, decision-making processes, and emergency support.

**D. Responsibilities and Tasks**

The purpose of this consultancy is to provide national-level technical and coordination support to ADPC for the effective implementation of CBFM and GEDSI activities under the CREWS 2.0 Project in Cambodia.

The Consultant will:

- Serve as ADPC's national-level technical focal point and support coordination of CBFM and GEDSI activities with NCDM and relevant government stakeholders.
- Provide strategic and technical guidance on the planning, implementation, and monitoring of community-based flood management activities.
- Review and provide technical recommendations on community-based awareness, training, vulnerability mapping, hazard zoning, and proposed flood risk management measures.
- Provide technical inputs and quality assurance support for the development and updating of Community Flood Management Plans (CFMPs) and CBFM manuals.
- Advise on the systematic integration of GEDSI considerations into community assessments, flood preparedness planning, early warning communication, and response arrangements.
- Support national-level consultations and technical discussions to strengthen institutional coordination, inclusive participation, and implementation quality.
- Provide technical guidance on community simulation exercises, review implementation findings, and contribute to documentation of lessons learned and good practices.

Review key project deliverables and submit concise technical advisory notes, observations, and recommendations to ADPC for strengthening implementation, sustainability, and potential scaling of CBFM approaches.

**Key Deliverables**
Under the guidance of the program manager, the consultant shall be responsible for the delivery of the following outputs:
1\. Inception Report and Implementation Work Plan

- Support national-level coordination with NCDM. Review the CBFM and GEDSI implementation work plan and provide technical recommendations. Submit a brief advisory note.

2\. Community-Based Awareness, Training and Vulnerability Mapping

- Review training approaches, vulnerability mapping, hazard zoning, and proposed flood risk management measures. Provide technical guidance and recommendations to NCDM.

3\. Community Flood Management Plans (CFMPs) and Updated CBFM Manuals

- Provide technical inputs on preparedness arrangements, early warning communication, and GEDSI integration.

4\. Implementation of Flood Risk Management Measures and Gender Mainstreaming

- Advise implementation approaches and GEDSI integration in community-level activities, including vulnerability and exposure data collection. Submit technical observations and recommendations.

5\. Community Simulation Exercises and Voices from the Field Report

- Provide technical guidance on simulation exercises. Review findings and contribute recommendations to the Voices from the Field Report.

6\. National Reflection Workshop and Final Consolidated Implementation Report

- Support national-level reflection and review consolidated implementation findings. Submit recommendations on lessons learned, sustainability, and potential scaling of CBFM approaches.

**E. Working Principles**
**Overall Supervision and Reporting:**
In performing the duties and responsibilities indicated above, the Consultant will be supervised by the Program Manager, ADPC. The Consultant will also closely work with other Unit Heads, Program Managers and Coordinators for the delivery of the project.

**Administrative Coordination and Liaison:**
The Consultant will coordinate closely with the PCA Department's administrative and support teams to ensure smooth operational functioning. This includes scheduling meetings, coordinating with internal and external stakeholders, and managing communications related to program documentation and knowledge management activities.

**General Requirements:**
The consultant must operate within all ADPC Guidelines & Procedures/ Policies and within the specific program needs

**F. Qualifications**

- An advanced university degree, preferably a Master's degree, in Disaster Risk Management, Climate Change, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Policy, Gender Studies, financing or a related discipline.
- At least 10 years of relevant professional experience in disaster risk management, climate resilience, humanitarian action, community development, or related fields.
- Demonstrated experience in community-based disaster risk management, community preparedness, flood risk management, or early warning systems.
- Demonstrated experience working directly with communities and local government authorities in Cambodia.
- Experience in integrating gender equality, disability and social inclusion considerations into disaster risk reduction, climate resilience, humanitarian, or development interventions.
- Experience in facilitating community consultations, participatory assessments, training, workshops, and community preparedness activities.
- Familiarity with Cambodia's institutional arrangements for disaster risk management and relevant national and subnational government structures.
- Experience working with government agencies, civil society organizations, international organizations, and community-based actors.
- Strong experience in technical documentation, activity reporting, and preparation of implementation reports.
- Proficiency in Khmer and working proficiency in English.

**Preferred Qualifications:**

- Self-motivated, proactive, and takes initiative.
- Demonstrated ability to plan and organize work and time independently.
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, team-oriented work style, and experience working in a multicultural environment.
- With a strong desire to learn, undertake new challenges, a willingness to work hard, and a good sense of humor, balanced with seriousness about the quality and excellence of work.

**Duty Station:** Phnom Penh, Cambodia, and field missions based on program needs

**Contract Duration:** This is an output-based consultancy from Dec 2026 – April 2027

**Itinerary:** In case of official missions outside the duty station, the Consultant will be entitled to local/international travel, daily subsistence allowance, accommodation, and other related travel costs as per ADPC travel policy. All travel must be pre-approved and undertaken only upon written request and consent by the Program Manager, ADPC.

jobs.title: MEAL Coordinator
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**Organizational Background**

The IRC’s Emergency Unit (EmU) leads the organization’s global emergency preparedness and response activities. Its mission is to meet immediate survival needs and reduce the suffering of affected populations during the acute phase of an emergency.

**Response Background**

The Ministry of Health of the Democratic Republic of the Congo officially declared the country’s 17th Ebola virus disease outbreak on 15 May 2026, after confirming cases caused by the Bundibugyo virus species (BDBV) in Ituri Province. The outbreak was initially detected in and around the Mongbwalu, Rwampara and Bunia health zones.

On 17 May 2026, the World Health Organization (WHO) assessed the outbreak as a public health emergency of international concern, owing to the risk of regional spread and the challenging operational context. The IRC is preparing its support to contain the outbreak in Ituri and North Kivu. The response rests on three complementary pillars: infection prevention and control and WASH (IPC/WASH); risk communication and community engagement (RCCE); and integrated protection, including safeguarding, PSEA, MHPSS, GBV referral mechanisms and protection risk mitigation.

**Scope of the Position**

The MEAL Coordinator leads the monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) of the IRC’s emergency response programs in the DRC. Based in Bunia, Ituri, the Coordinator travels frequently to other areas of intervention, notably Beni and Butembo in North Kivu. The position ensures that the projects of the IRC and its partners meet their MEAL commitments to clients, donors and the Ministry of Health.

The Coordinator ensures that monitoring, evaluation, accountability and data management systems are in place, adequately resourced and effectively used, from data collection through to data visualization.

The Coordinator integrates MEAL principles at every stage of the project cycle. The position provides technical assistance, capacity sharing, mentoring and training to IRC staff, partners and health zone teams, so that data, client feedback and learning inform program quality and evidence-based decisions.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Technical Oversight**

- Provide technical leadership on data systems and processes throughout the project cycle, for IRC and partner projects, from design and start-up through to close-out and capitalization.
- Develop and operationalize logical frameworks, indicator reference sheets, MEAL plans, data collection tools, coverage and beneficiary tracking tools, and data management procedures.
- Monitor the performance indicators of the emergency response’s Strategic Action Plan (SAP), notably timeliness, scale of coverage, quality and accountability to clients, and support teams in identifying and implementing corrective actions.
- Lead the design and harmonization of Ebola response tools: screening and triage reports in health facilities, screening of hospitalized patients (in-facility), IPC supply tracking, alert tracking, summaries of two-way communication, rumor and misinformation tracking, and RCCE training registers.
- Monitor quality indicators for the IPC/WASH, RCCE and Protection sectors, analyze results against targets and IRC quality standards, and promote the use of data to improve the quality of interventions.
- Clearly define reporting frequencies, deadlines and data flows from health facilities and field teams to the Bunia office and the country program, and ensure they are respected.
- Coordinate monthly monitoring and reporting of response reach (reach tracking), by program model, geographic area and implementation modality (IRC and partners), tracking unique clients reached, targets and coverage of affected populations.
- Put in place data quality assurance: routine checks, data quality audits, data verification in health facilities, removal of duplicates and consistency checks across tools.
- Strengthen partners’ MEAL capacity and ensure harmonization of indicators, data collection tools, data quality assurance processes and reporting requirements in line with IRC standards.
- Ensure that data platforms (CommCare, Kobo/ODK, Power BI extracts) are properly configured and used, and promote the use of mobile data collection and online dashboards.
- Produce high-quality data analyses, donor reports, presentations and dashboards that support learning and decision-making, and present findings at program and management meetings.
- Lead the design and conduct of evaluations, baseline studies, post-distribution monitoring and end-of-project studies, together with program coordinators, technical advisors and external partners.
- Develop the MEAL budget and MEAL staffing structure for each project,
- Use internal and external learning and evidence to inform the design of proposals and theories of change.

**Accountability to Affected Populations**

- Establish a client feedback and response mechanism in line with IRC standards, including hotlines, help desks, suggestion boxes and community meetings.
- Ensure that feedback and rumors from communities are recorded, referred, addressed and used to adapt programs, in coordination with RCCE teams.
- Ensure that accountability systems are safe and accessible to women, children, persons with disabilities and other at-risk groups, and that sensitive complaints are referred through safeguarding channels.

**Strategic Leadership**

- Lead all MEAL functions across all sectors (health, IPC, RCCE, protection and others), at all intervention sites.
- Promote a culture in which data is regularly reviewed and used for evidence-based decisions and program adaptation.
- Define MEAL approaches suited to an emergency response: rapid scale-up, broad coverage, partner implementation, insecurity and access constraints.
- Establish mutual capacity-strengthening partnerships with MEAL counterparts in partner organizations, local organizations and health authorities.
- Represent the IRC in relevant MEAL coordination mechanisms and promote the systematic use of data, client feedback and learning to guide decision-making and program adaptation.
- Integrate cross-cutting priorities into MEAL: gender, protection, safeguarding, diversity, equity and inclusion, and the “Do No Harm” principle, including the collection of sex- and age-disaggregated data.
- Contribute to regional and global MEAL learning initiatives and events.

**Staff Management and Development**

- Establish an effective MEAL team structure with a balanced workload.
- Supervise the MEAL team: set performance objectives, hold regular check-ins, manage work plans and conduct performance reviews.
- Coach, train and mentor MEAL staff, and oversee a learning and training plan based on a skills assessment.
- Train and support program staff, partner focal points, health facility staff and enumerators on tools, data quality and reporting.
- Ensure the continuity and sustainability of MEAL systems through documentation of tools and procedures, skills transfer and preparation of handovers during staff transitions and at the close of the response.
- Lead or support the recruitment and onboarding of MEAL staff, consultants and partner MEAL focal points.

**Working Relationships**

- Reports to: Emergency Programme Lead
- **Technical support:** Technical Advisor, MEAL – Emergency Unit
**Directly supervises:** MEAL Managers and Officers,
- **Other internal and/or external contacts:**
- **Internal:** IPC/Health, WASH, Protection and RCCE coordinators and managers
- **External:** partners, government authorities, clients.

**Education and Experience**

- University degree in statistics, data management, public health, epidemiology, social sciences or a related field.
- At least 5 years of experience in MEAL roles, including leading data collection and analysis for multisectoral, multi-donor humanitarian programs.
- Experience in health or outbreak response (Ebola, cholera, mpox, COVID-19 or similar) is strongly preferred, including experience with surveillance data.
- Experience in setting up or strengthening MEAL systems in emergency contexts, insecure environments, remote management or partner-implemented settings, preferably in eastern DRC or the Great Lakes region.
- International NGO experience required; experience with humanitarian coordination mechanisms (clusters, working groups) is an asset.

**Technical Skills**

- Strong command of quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis methods.
- Proven ability to design simple, user-friendly systems that turn routine and survey data into program improvements and decisions.
- Good understanding of accountability mechanisms and proven ability to set up client feedback and response systems.
- Proficiency in mobile data collection tools (CommCare, Kobo, ODK) and advanced Excel;
- Knowledge of Power BI is an asset.
- Excellent data presentation and report writing skills; ability to explain complex analyses simply to varied audiences.
- Proven ability to train, coach and mentor staff and partners.
- Strong planning and organizational skills; ability to manage multiple activities and deadlines simultaneously.

**Languages**

- Professional proficiency in **French**, written and spoken, required.
- Good working knowledge of **English** required, for reporting and technical exchanges.
- **Swahili** and/or **Lingala**: an asset; knowledge of local languages of Ituri is a plus.

**Work Environment**

- The position is based in Bunia, with frequent travel to other areas and intervention sites (Beni and Butembo).
- The context is complex and evolving, marked by the risk of Ebola transmission, insecurity, population movements, community mistrust, stigma, logistical constraints and access difficulties.
- The post holder must strictly comply with IRC safety and security protocols, travel procedures, infection prevention and control measures, safeguarding standards and public health guidance.

**French version:**

**Contexte organisationnel**

L'Unité urgence de l'IRC (Emergency Unit - EmU) dirige les activités mondiales de préparation et de réponse aux urgences de l'organisation. Sa mission est de répondre aux besoins immédiats de survie et de réduire les souffrances des populations touchées pendant la phase aiguë d'une urgence.

**Contexte de la réponse**

Le ministère de la Santé de la République démocratique du Congo a officiellement déclaré la 17e épidémie de maladie à virus Ebola du pays le 15 mai 2026, après la confirmation de cas causés par l'espèce virale Bundibugyo (BDBV) dans la province de l'Ituri. L'épidémie a été initialement détectée dans et autour des zones de santé de Mongbwalu, Rwampara et Bunia.

Le 17 mai 2026, l'Organisation mondiale de la Santé (OMS) a évalué l'épidémie comme une urgence de santé publique de portée internationale, en raison du risque de propagation régionale et du contexte opérationnel difficile. L'IRC prépare son appui à l'endiguement de l'épidémie en Ituri et au Nord-Kivu. La réponse repose sur trois piliers complémentaires : la prévention et le contrôle des infections et le WASH (IPC/WASH), la communication sur les risques et l'engagement communautaire (RCCE), ainsi que la protection intégrée, notamment la sauvegarde, la PSEA, le MHPSS, les mécanismes de référencement VBG et l'atténuation des risques de protection.

**Portée du poste**

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) MEAL dirige le suivi, l’évaluation, la redevabilité et l’apprentissage (MEAL) des programmes de réponse d’urgence de l’IRC en RDC. Basé à Bunia, en Ituri, il/elle effectue de fréquents déplacements vers les autres zones d’intervention, notamment Beni et Butembo, dans le Nord-Kivu. Le poste veille à ce que les projets de l’IRC et de ses partenaires respectent leurs engagements MEAL envers les clients, les bailleurs de fonds et le ministère de la Santé.

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) veille à ce que les systèmes de suivi, d’évaluation, de redevabilité et de gestion des données soient en place, dotés des ressources nécessaires et effectivement utilisés, de la collecte des données jusqu’à leur visualisation.

Le/la Coordinateur(trice) intègre les principes MEAL à chaque étape du cycle de projet. Le poste fournit une assistance technique, du partage de capacités, du mentorat et des formations au personnel de l’IRC, aux partenaires et aux équipes des zones de santé, afin que les données, les retours des clients et l’apprentissage orientent la qualité des programmes et les décisions fondées sur des données probantes.

**Principales responsabilités**

**Supervision technique**

- Assurer le leadership technique sur les systèmes et processus de données tout au long du cycle de projet, pour les projets de l’IRC et de ses partenaires, de la conception et du démarrage jusqu’à la clôture et la capitalisation.
- Élaborer et opérationnaliser les cadres logiques, les fiches de référence des indicateurs, les plans MEAL, les outils de collecte de données, les outils de suivi de la couverture et des bénéficiaires, ainsi que les procédures de gestion des données.
- Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de performance du Strategic Action Plan (SAP) de la réponse d’urgence, notamment la rapidité, l’échelle de couverture, la qualité et la redevabilité envers les clients, et appuyer les équipes dans l’identification et la mise en œuvre des actions correctives.
- Diriger la conception et l’harmonisation des outils de la réponse à Ebola : rapports de dépistage et de triage dans les formations sanitaires, dépistage des patients hospitalisés (intra-FOSA), suivi des intrants PCI, suivi des alertes, synthèses de la communication bidirectionnelle, suivi des rumeurs et de la désinformation, et registres des formations RCCE.
- Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de qualité des secteurs IPC/WASH, RCCE et Protection, analyser les résultats par rapport aux cibles et aux standards de qualité de l’IRC, et promouvoir l’utilisation des données pour améliorer la qualité des interventions.
- Définir clairement les fréquences de rapportage, les échéances et les flux de données depuis les formations sanitaires et les équipes de terrain vers le bureau de Bunia et le programme pays, et veiller à leur respect.
- Coordonner le suivi et le rapportage mensuel de la portée de la réponse (reach tracking), par modèle de programme, zone géographique et modalité de mise en œuvre (IRC et partenaires), en assurant le suivi des clients uniques atteintes, des cibles et de la couverture des populations affectées.
- Mettre en place l’assurance qualité des données : contrôles de routine, audits de qualité des données, vérification des données dans les formations sanitaires, suppression des doublons et contrôles de cohérence entre les outils.
- Renforcer les capacités MEAL des partenaires et veiller à l’harmonisation des indicateurs, des outils de collecte, des processus d’assurance qualité des données et des exigences de rapportage conformément aux standards de l’IRC.
- Veiller à ce que les plateformes de données (CommCare, Kobo/ODK, extractions Power BI) soient correctement paramétrées et utilisées, et promouvoir l’utilisation de la collecte mobile de données et des tableaux de bord en ligne.
- Produire des analyses de données, des rapports aux bailleurs, des présentations et des tableaux de bord de haute qualité qui soutiennent l’apprentissage et la prise de décision, et présenter les résultats lors des réunions de programme et de direction.
- Diriger la conception et la réalisation des évaluations, études de base, suivis post-distribution et des études de fin de projet, avec les coordinateurs de programme, les conseillers techniques et les partenaires externes.
- Élaborer le budget MEAL et la structure du personnel MEAL de chaque projet,
- Utiliser l’apprentissage et les données probantes internes et externes pour éclairer la conception des propositions et des théories du changement.

**Redevabilité envers les populations affectées**

- Mettre en place un mécanisme de retour d’information et de réponse aux clients conformément aux normes de l’IRC, y compris les lignes d’assistance téléphonique, les points d’accueil, les boîtes à suggestions et les réunions communautaires.
- Veiller à ce que les retours et les rumeurs provenant des communautés soient enregistrés, référés, traités et utilisés pour adapter les programmes, en coordination avec les équipes RCCE.
- Veiller à ce que les systèmes de redevabilité soient sûrs et accessibles aux femmes, aux enfants, aux personnes en situation de handicap et aux autres groupes à risque, et à ce que les plaintes sensibles soient référées via les canaux de sauvegarde.

**Leadership stratégique**

- Diriger l’ensemble des fonctions MEAL dans tous les secteurs (santé, PCI, RCCE, protection et autres), sur l’ensemble des sites d’intervention.
- Promouvoir une culture dans laquelle les données sont régulièrement examinées et utilisées pour des décisions fondées sur des données probantes et l’adaptation des programmes.
- Définir des approches MEAL adaptées à une réponse d’urgence : montée en puissance rapide, large couverture, mise en œuvre par les partenaires, insécurité et contraintes d’accès.
- Établir des partenariats de renforcement mutuel des capacités avec les homologues MEAL des organisations partenaires, des organisations locales et des autorités sanitaires.
- Représenter l’IRC dans les mécanismes de coordination MEAL pertinents et promouvoir l’utilisation systématique des données, des retours d’information des clients et des apprentissages pour orienter la prise de décision et l’adaptation des programmes.
- Intégrer les priorités transversales dans le MEAL : genre, protection, sauvegarde, diversité, équité et inclusion, et principe « Ne pas nuire », y compris la collecte de données ventilées par sexe et par âge.
- Contribuer aux initiatives et aux événements d’apprentissage MEAL régionaux et mondiaux.

**Gestion et développement du personnel**

- Mettre en place une structure d’équipe MEAL efficace avec une charge de travail équilibrée.
- Superviser l’équipe MEAL : fixer les objectifs de performance, tenir des points réguliers, gérer les plans de travail et conduire les évaluations de performance.
- Accompagner, former et encadrer le personnel MEAL, et superviser un plan d’apprentissage et de formation fondé sur l’évaluation des compétences.
- Former et appuyer le personnel des programmes, les points focaux des partenaires, le personnel des formations sanitaires et les enquêteurs sur les outils, la qualité des données et le rapportage.
- Assurer la continuité et la pérennisation des systèmes MEAL à travers la documentation des outils et procédures, le transfert des compétences et la préparation des passations lors des transitions de personnel et de la clôture de la réponse.
- Diriger ou appuyer le recrutement et l’intégration du personnel MEAL, des consultants et des points focaux MEAL des partenaires.

**Relations de travail**

- Le poste rend compte au : Emergency Programme Lead
- **Appui technique :** Conseiller(ère) technique MEAL Equipe d’Urgence
**Le poste supervise directement :** Managers et Officiers MEAL,
- **Autres contacts internes et/ou externes :**
- **Internes :** Coordinateurs et managers IPC/Health, WASH, protection, RCCE
- **Externes :** partenaires, autorités gouvernementales, clients.

**Formation et expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire en statistique, gestion des données, santé publique, épidémiologie, sciences sociales ou dans un domaine connexe.
- Au moins 5 ans d’expérience dans des fonctions MEAL, y compris la direction de la collecte et de l’analyse de données pour des programmes humanitaires multisectoriels et multi-bailleurs.
- Une expérience dans la santé ou la riposte aux épidémies (Ebola, choléra, mpox, COVID-19 ou similaire) est fortement souhaitée, y compris en matière de données de surveillance.
- Expérience dans la mise en place ou le renforcement de systèmes MEAL en contexte d’urgence, d’insécurité, de gestion à distance ou de mise en œuvre par des partenaires, de préférence dans l’est de la RDC ou dans la région des Grands Lacs.
- Expérience en ONG internationale exigée ; une expérience des mécanismes de coordination humanitaire (clusters, groupes de travail) est un atout.

**Compétences techniques**

- Solide maîtrise des méthodes de collecte et d’analyse de données quantitatives et qualitatives.
- Capacité avérée à concevoir des systèmes simples et conviviaux qui transforment les données de routine et d’enquête en améliorations des programmes et en décisions.
- Bonne compréhension des mécanismes de redevabilité et capacité avérée à mettre en place des systèmes de retour d’information et de réponse aux clients.
- Maîtrise des outils de collecte mobile de données (CommCare, Kobo, ODK) et d’Excel avancé);
- La connaissance de Power BI est un atout.
- Excellentes compétences en présentation de données et en rédaction de rapports ; capacité à expliquer simplement des analyses complexes à des publics variés.
- Capacité avérée à former, accompagner et encadrer le personnel et les partenaires.
- Solides compétences en planification et en organisation ; capacité à gérer plusieurs activités et échéances simultanément.

**Langues**

- Maîtrise professionnelle du **français** écrit et parlé exigée.
- Bonne connaissance pratique de l’**anglais** exigée, pour le rapportage et les échanges techniques.
- **Swahili** et/ou **lingala** : un atout ; la connaissance des langues locales de l’Ituri est un plus.

**Environnement de travail**

- Le poste est basé à Bunia, avec des déplacements fréquents vers les autres zones et sites d’intervention (Beni et Butembo).
- Le contexte est complexe et évolutif, marqué par les risques de transmission d'Ebola, l'insécurité, les mouvements de population, la méfiance communautaire, la stigmatisation, les contraintes logistiques et les difficultés d'accès.
- Le/la titulaire doit respecter strictement les protocoles IRC de sûreté et sécurité, les procédures de déplacement, les mesures de prévention et contrôle des infections, les normes de sauvegarde et les orientations de santé publique.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Protection Coordinator
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**CONTEXT**

Following recurrent outbreaks of Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) and the persistent humanitarian crisis affecting eastern DRC, IRC is implementing a multisectoral emergency response in Ituri and North Kivu provinces. The response integrates Health, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), WASH, Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE), and integrated Protection, including Child Protection, Gender-Based Violence (GBV) prevention and response, Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), Cash for Protection and Community-Based Protection.

The Integrated Emergency Protection Coordinator will provide strategic, technical and operational leadership for all protection interventions implemented under the emergency response, ensuring that protection risks are identified, mitigated and addressed through high-quality, safe, accountable and survivor-centered programming.

**JOB PURPOSE**

The Integrated Emergency Protection Coordinator leads the design, implementation, monitoring and quality assurance of IRC’s integrated protection response within the Ebola emergency framework in Ituri and North Kivu.

The position ensures strategic coordination across Child Protection, GBV, MHPSS, Protection Monitoring, Community-Based Protection and Protection Mainstreaming, while ensuring alignment with humanitarian principles, Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures and donor requirements.

The coordinator provides overall supervision to protection teams, contributes to emergency preparedness and response planning, oversees budgets and grants, supports resource mobilization efforts and represents IRC in relevant coordination platforms.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Strategic Leadership and Program Quality**

- Provide overall leadership for integrated protection programming.
- Ensure effective integration of GBV, Child Protection, MHPSS, Cash for Protection and Community-Based Protection interventions.
- Lead protection risk analysis and identify protection priorities in outbreak-affected communities.
- Ensure all protection activities comply with humanitarian standards, IASC guidelines and IRC technical standards.
- Ensure all interventions systematically integrate Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures.
- Lead contextual and protection trend analysis and adapt response strategies accordingly.
- Ensure protection programming remains conflict-sensitive and follows the Do No Harm principle.

**2. Program Management and Technical Oversight**

- Oversee implementation of emergency protection activities in all operational locations.
- Develop annual, quarterly and monthly work plans.
- Supervise quality implementation through regular field visits.
- Ensure case management services meet applicable global standards.
- Monitor service quality, referrals, confidentiality and safeguarding compliance.
- Ensure quality data collection and analysis for decision-making.
- Lead adaptive management processes responding to epidemiological and protection trends.

**3. Team Management and Capacity Building**

- Directly supervise Senior Protection Officers, Protection Managers and technical focal points.
- Establish performance objectives and regular supervision mechanisms.
- Conduct individual performance reviews.
- Facilitate weekly technical supervision meetings.
- Develop staff capacity-building plans.
- Promote staff wellbeing and Staff Care initiatives.
- Strengthen emergency surge team readiness and deployment capacity.

**4. Coordination and Representation**

- Represent IRC in the Protection Cluster, Child Protection Working Group, GBV Working Group, MHPSS Working Group, Ebola Response Coordination Structures, and meetings with provincial and health authorities.
- Strengthen collaboration with Health, RCCE, WASH and IPC actors.
- Support harmonization of protection approaches across response partners.
- Lead protection advocacy initiatives based on evidence and field findings.

**5. Grants, Budget Management and Reporting**

- Lead protection grants implementation and budget monitoring.
- Conduct monthly Budget versus Actual (BvA) reviews.
- Ensure expenditure rates remain aligned with implementation plans.
- Support proposal development and emergency resource mobilization initiatives.
- Contribute technical content for donor reports.
- Prepare high-quality monthly, quarterly and final reports.

**6. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL)**

- Ensure quality monitoring systems are functional.
- Track protection indicators and project targets.
- Ensure accountability mechanisms are accessible and operational.
- Promote client feedback and participation.
- Use monitoring results to improve programming quality.

**7. Safeguarding, Risk Management and Compliance**

- Ensure compliance with IRC safeguarding standards.
- Strengthen safe programming approaches.
- Ensure confidential handling of protection information.
- Monitor security, operational and programmatic risks.
- Implement mitigation plans for identified risks.
- Ensure compliance with donor and IRC requirements.

**KEY DELIVERABLES**

- Protection strategy and implementation plan.
- Monthly protection trend analyses.
- Quality assurance reports from field monitoring visits.
- Donor narrative reports.
- Budget monitoring reports.
- Capacity-building plans.
- Protection emergency preparedness plans.
- Protection advocacy briefs.
- Final project reports.

**MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

**Education**

Master’s degree in Social Sciences, Gender Studies, Human Rights, Psychology, Social Work, Public Health, International Development, Humanitarian Affairs or a related field.

**Professional Experience**

- Minimum 5 years of progressive experience in humanitarian protection programming.
- Minimum 3 years in a senior coordination or management role.
- Demonstrated experience managing GBV, Child Protection and MHPSS programs.
- Previous experience in emergency response and outbreak settings is highly desirable.
- Experience managing multi-donor grants and large teams.
- Experience working within humanitarian coordination mechanisms.

**TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES**

**Strong knowledge of**

- GBV programming.
- Child Protection programming.
- Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS).
- Case Management.
- Community-Based Protection.
- Cash for Protection.

**Strong understanding of**

- Ebola Virus Disease response.
- Infection Prevention and Control (IPC).
- Humanitarian principles.
- Sphere Standards.
- IASC Protection Policy.
- GBVIMS and CPIMS+.

**Strong skills in**

- Strategic planning.
- Team leadership.
- Budget management.
- Proposal writing.
- Coordination and representation.
- Advocacy and negotiation.

**LANGUAGES**

- French: Fluent (mandatory).
- English: Professional working proficiency (mandatory).
- Swahili: Highly desirable.

**PROPOSED SUPERVISION**

- Senior Emergency GBV Officer.
- Senior Emergency Protection Officer - Information Management.
- Integrated Protection Managers - Ituri & North Kivu.

The position will also maintain a dotted-line technical coordination relationship with the Health, RCCE, IPC and WASH emergency leads to ensure full multisectoral integration of the EVD response and smooth collaboration with Country Program counterparts.

**French Version:**

**CONTEXTE**

À la suite de la récurrence des épidémies de maladie à virus Ebola (MVE) et dans un contexte de crise humanitaire persistante dans l’est de la RDC, l’IRC met en œuvre une réponse d’urgence multisectorielle dans les provinces de l’Ituri et du Nord-Kivu. Cette réponse intègre la Santé, la Prévention et le Contrôle des Infections (PCI), l’EHA/WASH, la Communication sur les Risques et l’Engagement Communautaire (CREC/RCCE), ainsi que la Protection intégrée, notamment la Protection de l’Enfance, la prévention et la réponse aux violences basées sur le genre (VBG), la Santé Mentale et le Soutien Psychosocial (SMSPS/MHPSS), le Cash pour la Protection et la Protection à base communautaire.

Le/la Coordinateur·rice de la Protection Intégrée en Situation d’Urgence assurera le leadership stratégique, technique et opérationnel de l’ensemble des interventions de protection mises en œuvre dans le cadre de la réponse d’urgence. Il/elle veillera à ce que les risques de protection soient identifiés, atténués et pris en charge à travers des programmes de qualité, sûrs, redevables et centrés sur les survivant·e·s.

**OBJECTIF DU POSTE**

Le/la Coordinateur·rice de la Protection Intégrée en Situation d’Urgence dirige la conception, la mise en œuvre, le suivi et l’assurance qualité de la réponse intégrée de protection de l’IRC dans le cadre de la réponse d’urgence à Ebola en Ituri et au Nord-Kivu.

Le poste assure la coordination stratégique entre la Protection de l’Enfance, les VBG, la SMSPS/MHPSS, le monitoring de protection, la Protection à base communautaire et l’intégration transversale de la protection, tout en garantissant l’alignement avec les principes humanitaires, les mesures de Prévention et de Contrôle des Infections (PCI) ainsi que les exigences des bailleurs.

Le/la Coordinateur·rice assure la supervision générale des équipes de protection, contribue à la préparation et à la planification des réponses d’urgence, supervise les budgets et les subventions, soutient les efforts de mobilisation des ressources et représente l’IRC au sein des mécanismes de coordination pertinents.

**PRINCIPALES RESPONSABILITÉS**

**1. Leadership stratégique et qualité des programmes**

- Assurer le leadership global de la programmation intégrée de protection.
- Garantir une intégration efficace des interventions VBG, Protection de l’Enfance, SMSPS/MHPSS, Cash pour la Protection et Protection à base communautaire.
- Diriger l’analyse des risques de protection et identifier les priorités de protection dans les communautés touchées par l’épidémie.
- Garantir que toutes les activités de protection respectent les standards humanitaires, les directives de l’IASC et les standards techniques de l’IRC.
- Veiller à l’intégration systématique des mesures de Prévention et de Contrôle des Infections (PCI) dans toutes les interventions.
- Diriger les analyses contextuelles et des tendances de protection et adapter les stratégies d’intervention en conséquence.
- Veiller à ce que les programmes de protection restent sensibles aux conflits et respectent le principe « Ne pas nuire ».

**2. Gestion des programmes et supervision technique**

- Superviser la mise en œuvre des activités de protection d’urgence dans toutes les zones opérationnelles.
- Élaborer les plans de travail annuels, trimestriels et mensuels.
- Superviser la qualité de la mise en œuvre à travers des visites régulières sur le terrain.
- Veiller à ce que les services de gestion de cas respectent les standards internationaux applicables.
- Suivre la qualité des services, les mécanismes de référencement, la confidentialité et le respect des normes de sauvegarde.
- Garantir une collecte et une analyse de données de qualité pour soutenir la prise de décision.
- Diriger les processus de gestion adaptative permettant d’ajuster les interventions aux évolutions épidémiologiques et aux tendances de protection.

**3. Gestion des équipes et renforcement des capacités**

- Superviser directement les Senior Protection Officers, les Protection Managers ainsi que les points focaux techniques.
- Définir les objectifs de performance et mettre en place des mécanismes réguliers de supervision.
- Conduire des évaluations individuelles de performance.
- Faciliter les réunions hebdomadaires de supervision technique.
- Élaborer des plans de renforcement des capacités du personnel.
- Promouvoir le bien-être du personnel et les initiatives de soutien aux équipes (Staff Care).
- Renforcer le niveau de préparation et les capacités de déploiement des équipes d’urgence/surge.

**4. Coordination et représentation**

- Représenter l’IRC au Cluster Protection, au Groupe de travail Protection de l’Enfance, au Groupe de travail VBG, au Groupe de travail SMSPS/MHPSS, dans les structures de coordination de la réponse à Ebola et lors des réunions avec les autorités provinciales et sanitaires.
- Renforcer la collaboration avec les acteurs de la Santé, CREC/RCCE, WASH/EHA et PCI.
- Soutenir l’harmonisation des approches de protection entre les différents partenaires de la réponse.
- Diriger les initiatives de plaidoyer en matière de protection sur la base des données probantes et des constats issus du terrain.

**5. Gestion des subventions, du budget et rapportage**

- Diriger la mise en œuvre des subventions de protection et assurer le suivi budgétaire.
- Réaliser mensuellement les revues Budget versus Actual (BvA).
- Veiller à ce que le niveau des dépenses reste aligné sur les plans de mise en œuvre.
- Soutenir l’élaboration des propositions et les initiatives de mobilisation de ressources pour les réponses d’urgence.
- Contribuer à la rédaction du contenu technique des rapports destinés aux bailleurs.
- Préparer des rapports mensuels, trimestriels et finaux de haute qualité.

**6. Suivi, Évaluation, Redevabilité et Apprentissage (MEAL)**

- Veiller au bon fonctionnement de systèmes de suivi de qualité.
- Assurer le suivi des indicateurs de protection et des cibles des projets.
- Veiller à ce que les mécanismes de redevabilité soient accessibles et opérationnels.
- Promouvoir les retours d’information et la participation des clients.
- Utiliser les résultats du suivi pour améliorer la qualité des programmes.

**7. Sauvegarde, gestion des risques et conformité**

- Veiller au respect des standards de sauvegarde de l’IRC.
- Renforcer les approches de programmation sûre.
- Garantir le traitement confidentiel des informations relatives à la protection.
- Suivre les risques sécuritaires, opérationnels et programmatiques.
- Mettre en œuvre des plans d’atténuation des risques identifiés.
- Garantir la conformité aux exigences des bailleurs et de l’IRC.

**PRINCIPAUX LIVRABLES**

- Stratégie de protection et plan de mise en œuvre.
- Analyses mensuelles des tendances de protection.
- Rapports d’assurance qualité issus des visites de suivi sur le terrain.
- Rapports narratifs destinés aux bailleurs.
- Rapports de suivi budgétaire.
- Plans de renforcement des capacités.
- Plans de préparation aux urgences en matière de protection.
- Notes de plaidoyer sur les enjeux de protection.
- Rapports finaux des projets.

**QUALIFICATIONS MINIMALES**

**Formation**

Master en sciences sociales, études de genre, droits humains, psychologie, travail social, santé publique, développement international, affaires humanitaires ou dans un domaine connexe.

**Expérience professionnelle**

- Minimum de 5 années d’expérience progressive dans la programmation humanitaire de protection.
- Minimum de 3 années d’expérience dans un poste senior de coordination ou de management.
- Expérience démontrée dans la gestion de programmes VBG, Protection de l’Enfance et SMSPS/MHPSS.
- Une expérience préalable dans les réponses d’urgence et les contextes épidémiques est fortement souhaitée.
- Expérience dans la gestion de subventions financées par plusieurs bailleurs ainsi que dans la gestion d’équipes importantes.
- Expérience de travail au sein des mécanismes de coordination humanitaire.

**COMPÉTENCES TECHNIQUES**

**Solides connaissances dans les domaines suivants**

- Programmation VBG.
- Protection de l’Enfance.
- Santé Mentale et Soutien Psychosocial (SMSPS/MHPSS).
- Gestion de cas.
- Protection à base communautaire.
- Cash pour la Protection.

**Bonne maîtrise des domaines suivants**

- Réponse à la maladie à virus Ebola.
- Prévention et Contrôle des Infections (PCI).
- Principes humanitaires.
- Standards Sphère.
- Politique de protection de l’IASC.
- GBVIMS et CPIMS+.

**Solides compétences en**

- Planification stratégique.
- Leadership et gestion d’équipe.
- Gestion budgétaire.
- Rédaction de propositions de projets.
- Coordination et représentation.
- Plaidoyer et négociation.

**LANGUES**

- Français : courant, obligatoire.
- Anglais : niveau professionnel, obligatoire.
- Swahili : fortement souhaité.

**SUPERVISION PROPOSÉE**

- Senior Emergency GBV Officer.
- Senior Emergency Protection Officer - Information Management.
- Integrated Protection Managers - Ituri & Nord-Kivu.

Le poste entretient également une relation fonctionnelle de coordination technique avec les responsables d’urgence Santé, CREC/RCCE, PCI et WASH, afin de garantir une intégration multisectorielle complète de la réponse MVE et une collaboration fluide avec les homologues du Programme Pays.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Programme Assistant
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Land Resources Division (LRD)**provides effective expert scientific advice, capacity building and services on conservation, development and utilization of plant genetic resources, forest and landscape management, resilient agricultural systems, diversification of livelihood strategies and access to markets to maintain ecosystem services and improve land productivity and the food, nutrition security and resilience of Pacific communities. LRD has expertise in genetic resource conservation, resilient agriculture, biosecurity, pest and disease management, agricultural extension, plant pathology, entomology and animal health. It collaborates with governments, regional organisations, civil society and other SPC divisions to pinpoint the needs and priorities of Pacific countries and communities and provide technical expertise to address them. This mission is realized through four main thematic work areas, or pillars, and a progressively integrated approach to programming that works towards achieving SPC’s development goals.

The role – **Programme Assistant** will provide administrative, logistical, coordination and records support to the Genetic Resources Programme, including the Centre for Pacific Crops and Trees (CePaCT), to support the effective day-to-day operation of the programme.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Administrative Support**

- Manage the office front desk and support visitors, stakeholders and client enquiries for the GRP.
- Facilitate Programme meetings and hosted stakeholder engagements, including staff, partner and visitor meetings, and coordinate meeting-room arrangements and preparation of meeting minutes/records as required.
- Maintain Programme stakeholder contact and distribution lists and circulate approved communications on behalf of the Programme Leader.
- Monitor key events, staff movements and relevant calendars.

**Logistical Support**

- Support Programme procurement requirements by obtaining quotations and collating required administrative documentation, in liaison with relevant LRD Finance/Procurement staff.
- Coordinate administrative and logistical arrangements for the distribution of germplasm and/or biological samples, in consultation with the Curator or relevant technical staff and the Documentation & Database Technician as required.
- Provide administrative support to Programme procurement processes and standard contract documentation, in liaison with relevant LRD Finance/Procurement staff.
- Coordinate logistical arrangements for Programme meetings, workshops and stakeholder events, including venues, accommodation, service providers and participant arrangements, in accordance with relevant SPC procedures.

**Programme Records and Filing**

- Maintain Programme administrative records and filing in approved physical and electronic storage systems, including SharePoint and shared network drives, in alignment with LRD and GRP administrative document-management and filing structures.
- Digitise and appropriately file programme documents and records, including documents provided by the Programme leader and other Programme staff, in approved electronic storage systems.
- Collect, organize and archive supporting documentation for meetings, donor and project files, agreements, reports, consultancies, contracts, staff travel and other Programme activities.

**Other Duties**

- Provide administrative support to Programme reporting and verification processes, including collation of relevant supporting information and records.
- Assist with administrative aspects of staff onboarding and offboarding.
- Provide administrative and logistical support to other relevant LRD teams when required and agreed with the supervisor.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- Tertiary certificate or diploma in office management, administration, secretarial studies, or related discipline from a recognised institution or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 3 years of relevant experience in a similar role undertaking programme administration, coordination, logistical support and records management, including physical and electronic filing.
- Good computer skills, including experience using Microsoft Office/Microsoft 365 and electronic document and filing systems.
- Demonstrated experience coordinating medium- to large-scale meetings, workshops or stakeholder events, including participant liaison, travel and logistical arrangements.
- Good interpersonal, customer service and communication skills, with the ability to liaise effectively with internal and external stakeholders.
- Demonstrated commitment to gender equality and human rights-based approaches.
- Ability to work as part of a team and autonomously in a multi-cultural environment.
- Excellent public relations and communications skills.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **1 year** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration –** The **Programme Assistant** is a band 6 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a commencing taxable salary range of FJD 1,987-2,483 per month, plus local staff benefits. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised locally (EPAL) whose duty station is Suva –** SPC provides medical and life insurance for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Recruitment principles** –SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**.

Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s Privacy Policy.

jobs.title: Youth Services Specialist
jobs.description:
**This position is open to candidates with existing work authorization in the location where the position is advertised.**

**Job Overview:** The Youth Services Specialist supports IRC's Refugee School Impact (RSI) program, helping ORR-eligible refugee students (ages 6-18) and their parents or guardians’ access and succeed in the U.S. education system. The Specialist helps families enroll their children in school, leads student and parent orientations, provides after-school tutoring and academic support during the school year, and runs a summer academic program. The Specialist also checks in regularly with students to track academic progress and coordinates with school staff, community partners, and the Education & Youth Services Manager to keep services aligned with program goals.

**Major Responsibilities:**

Responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- Assist newly arrived ORR-eligible families with school enrollment for children ages 6–18, including interpretation support as needed.
- Provide school orientation to enrolled students and lead Extended School Orientation workshops for parents and guardians, covering topics such as school choice, transportation, attendance, and how to support their child's education.
- Coordinate with Jefferson County Public Schools (JCPS) Office of Multilingual Learners and other school staff to identify enrollment issues early and keep teachers informed of students' academic progress.
- Support families choosing private schools, homeschools, or districts outside JCPS, including newly arrived refugee families served through the Program of Initial Resettlement.
- Deliver the after-school program twice a week during the school year, providing tutoring in reading and writing and other academic support, with the help of interns or volunteers.
- Conduct regular one-on-one check-ins with students at school to track grades, homework completion, and attendance, and coordinate with teachers to address concerns early.
- Refer students and families to IRC programs or other community resources when needs arise outside of school.
- Plan and lead the summer academic program, including academic reinforcement, enrichment activities, field trips, and transportation to and from students' homes.
- Maintain accurate and timely documentation of services, referrals, and orientations in ClientTrack.
- Assist in the recruitment, training, and supervision of interns or other youth program staff.
- Attend regular meetings with the Education & Youth Services Manager to discuss programming and any concerns.
- Support case closures, transition planning, and other closeout activities as the program year winds down.
- Other duties as assigned.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in social work, education, or a related field of study preferred.

**Work Experience:**

- Experience working with refugee, immigrant, or other multicultural youth and families, preferably in a school, resettlement, or case management setting.

**Demonstrated Skills & Competencies:**

- Demonstrated success working and communicating effectively in a multicultural environment.
- Self-starter with excellent problem-solving skills combined with the proven ability to prioritize and manage time effectively.
- Attention to detail and accuracy in work product.
- Fluent in English, both spoken and written; proficiency in language(s) spoken by client group is desired.
- Proficient in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, Outlook); ability to use the internet and other digital tools for data entry, research, and problem-solving purposes.
- Familiarity with the U.S. education system, or willingness to learn local school district processes and requirements, is preferred. Experience with a client database system (such as ClientTrack) is a plus.
- Valid driver’s license and access to a personal, insured vehicle, with the ability to transport clients as needed.
- Required to drive clients for school enrollment, summer programs, and after school.
- First Aid and CPR certification preferred (or willingness to obtain before the start of the program).

**Working Environment:**

- A combination of standard office environment, remote work, and ‘field’ time within the service delivery area to perform the above-outlined responsibilities.
- Occasional domestic (non-local) travel required; up to 10%.
- May require occasional weekend and/or evening work.

***This position is expected to end on September 30, 2027.***

**Compensation:** (Pay Rate: $21-$23/hr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Associate Designer
jobs.description:
***This is a hybrid position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Nigeria, Chad, and Cameroon.***

**Présentation du poste**

Airbel est le laboratoire d'innovation de l'IRC. Nous travaillons aux côtés des personnes touchées par les conflits et les crises pour concevoir des services plus utiles, plus dignes et plus durables. Ce poste place un·e designer au cœur de ce travail en Afrique de l'Ouest et centrale, au plus près des communautés, du personnel de première ligne et des questions qui déterminent si un produit ou un service aide réellement quelqu'un.

Vous serez nos yeux et nos mains sur le terrain. Vous mènerez la recherche design, échangerez avec les clients et les prestataires, observerez ce qu'ils font et pourquoi, et transformerez vos découvertes en prototypes que vous testerez et affinerez sur le terrain. Vous travaillerez en étroite collaboration avec la Responsable du design centré sur l'humain, qui vous appuiera sur la synthèse et le développement des concepts pendant que vous façonnez votre propre travail.

**Responsabilités principales**

• Mener la recherche design sur le terrain : entretiens, observation et temps passé avec les clients et le personnel de première ligne.

• Rester au contact d'une même zone géographique ou d'un même axe de travail assez longtemps pour repérer les tendances qui n'apparaissent qu'avec le temps.

• Donner du sens à ce que vous observez sur le terrain et repérer les étincelles d'innovation déjà présentes dans les solutions et les idées des gens eux-mêmes.

• Transformer la recherche en prototypes, les tester avec de vraies personnes et itérer au fil de vos apprentissages, plutôt que de suivre un script figé.

• Restituer ce que vous apprenez sous une forme utile à l'équipe : notes claires, visuels, parcours utilisateur, tout ce qui rend une observation parlante.

• Collaborer avec les équipes programmes pays, les responsables techniques et le personnel de première ligne avec soin et respect, en gagnant l'accès dont dépend une bonne recherche.

• Intervenir en Afrique de l'Ouest et centrale francophone, et dans d'autres contextes humanitaires selon les besoins, en vous adaptant rapidement à de nouveaux contextes et à de nouvelles équipes.

**Exigences du poste**

**Expérience professionnelle**

Nous aimerions comprendre votre façon de penser et de travailler, notamment :

• Une expérience de recherche auprès des personnes, dans n'importe quel cadre : recherche design, ethnographie, recherche UX ou produit, recherche participative ou recherche-action, ou tout autre type de recherche qualitative. Ce qui compte, c'est que vous soyez allé·e au-delà d'un script pour comprendre pourquoi les gens agissent comme ils le font.

• Vous avez construit ou mis en place quelque chose (un service, un petit pilote, un outil, une application, voire une version papier sommaire d'une idée), vous l'avez testé avec les personnes concernées et vous l'avez fait évoluer en fonction de ce que vous avez appris. Nous appelons cela du « prototypage », mais vous n'avez pas besoin d'avoir employé ce mot.

• Un sens de l'observation des opportunités du quotidien : les solutions de contournement, les petits détails et ce que les gens ont déjà trouvé par eux-mêmes.

• Quelque chose qui montre votre façon de penser : un portfolio, une étude de cas, un compte rendu de recherche, des photos d'un prototype ou un projet que vous avez contribué à façonner. Ce n'est pas grave si ce n'est pas abouti, mais nous aimerions voir votre réflexion sous une forme ou une autre.

**Compétences démontrées**

• De solides compétences en recherche : vous savez concevoir et mener un travail de terrain, échanger avec tout le monde, respecter l'éthique auprès de personnes en situation de vulnérabilité, et lire une situation pour ce qu'elle révèle, avec soin dans votre manière de recueillir et de consigner ce que vous trouvez.

• De solides compétences en test de prototypes : vous construisez de façon sommaire, testez tôt et ajustez en cours de test plutôt que d'attendre une version finie.

• Une réelle curiosité pour ce qui pousse les gens à agir comme ils le font, et le discernement pour y déceler l'étincelle d'une idée.

• De l'aisance sur le terrain : vous pouvez passer deux semaines d'affilée sur un site et y faire du bon travail.

• Une capacité d'adaptation à des cultures, des langues et des plans qui changent, portée par l'humilité et le soin des personnes avec qui vous travaillez.

**Compétences linguistiques**

Un français et un anglais fonctionnels, suffisants dans les deux langues pour mener des recherches et travailler avec des équipes ailleurs sur le continent. Les propositions et présentations peuvent être rédigées dans l'une ou l'autre langue, puis traduites.

**Expérience et compétences souhaitées**

• Un œil pour rendre les enseignements lisibles à travers des visuels, des cartes et des présentations simples.

• Une expérience dans des contextes humanitaires, de santé ou communautaires.

**Autorisation de travail**

Les candidat·e·s doivent disposer du droit légal de travailler dans le pays où le poste est base.

**Environnement de travail**

Ce poste est basé dans un bureau pays de l'IRC en RDC, au Nigéria ou au Tchad, avec une installation de bureau standard. Le travail implique des déplacements fréquents, jusqu'à 40 %, vers des sites situés dans divers contextes humanitaires, dans la région et à l'international. Une mission de recherche design ou de prototypage peut représenter deux semaines d'affilée dans des lieux reculés, à faibles ressources et parfois peu sûrs, avec un hébergement sommaire, une connectivité limitée et de longues journées. Si c'est justement le fait d'être au plus près du terrain qui vous attire, ce poste est fait pour vous.

IRC et les employés de IRC doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes contenus dans le IRC WAY (normes de conduite professionnelle). Ce sont l'Intégrité, Egalite, le Service, et la Responsabilité. En conformité avec ces valeurs, IRC opère et fait respecter les politiques sur la protection des bénéficiaires contre l'exploitation et les abus, la protection de l'enfant, le harcèlement sur les lieux de travail, l'intégrité financière, et les représailles.

**Employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances** : L'IRC est un employeur garantissant l'égalité des chances. L'IRC évalue tous les candidats sur la base du mérite, sans distinction de race, de sexe, de couleur de peau, d'origine nationale, de religion, d'orientation sexuelle, d'âge, de situation matrimoniale, de statut d'ancien combattant, de handicap ou de toute autre caractéristique protégée par la législation en vigueur.

**Normes professionnelles** : Tous les collaborateurs de l’International Rescue Committee (IRC) doivent adhérer aux valeurs et principes fondamentaux énoncés dans le document « IRC Way – Normes de conduite professionnelle ». Nos normes sont l’intégrité, le service, l’égalité et la responsabilité. Conformément à ces valeurs, l’IRC met en œuvre et applique des politiques relatives à la protection des personnes, aux conflits d’intérêts, à l’intégrité financière, au signalement des irrégularités et à la protection contre les représailles. L’IRC s’engage à prendre toutes les mesures préventives nécessaires et à créer un environnement où chacun se sent en sécurité, ainsi qu’à prendre toutes les mesures nécessaires et correctives en cas de préjudice. L’IRC constitue des équipes de professionnels qui favorisent la réflexion critique, le partage des responsabilités, le débat et l’objectivité afin d’offrir les meilleurs services possibles à nos bénéficiaires.

**Job Overview**
