**Join MSF OCG as a Associate Philanthropy Advisor – Private Major Donors!**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

MSF Switzerland was created in 1981 and it is headquartered in Geneva. The Philanthropy Unit is one of the eight units at the Communications and Fundraising Department. To ensure a good geographical coverage of the Swiss fundraising market, the Unit is divided into two offices: Geneva and Zurich. The Unit’s mission is to strengthen MSF’s relationship with its private major supporters, including wealthy individuals, foundations, companies, and other philanthropic organisations. It also manages grants and donations from Swiss cantons and communes. Last but not least, it is also in charge of legacy fundraising, including management of heritages as well as contacts with potential legators and confirmed bequestors.

The Associate Philanthropy Advisor for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland is a key member of the Philanthropy Unit, ensuring an efficient and effective cultivation approach for private major donors in German speaking Switzerland and Liechtenstein. The mission is to secure and grow income for MSF from private major donors in German speaking Switzerland.

## Tasks & Responsibilities

*Strategy and action plan*

- Actively contribute to the implementation of the yearly plan

*Cultivation and stewardship*

- Manages a portfolio of Major Donors and potential Top Major Donors and, alongside the Team Coordinator, design and develop the donor journey for donors giving between CHF 10’000 and CHF 20’000 annually.
- Regularly reports to and consults with the Team Coordinator on the strategy for the pool regarding upgrading donors within this segment.
- Determine the best approach and journey for each individual donor depending on their wishes and level of engagement.
- Prepare and facilitate one-to-one meetings, calls, presentations and other meaningful interactions with major donors.
- Interact and collaborate with key spokespersons within MSF (President, General Director, Director of Operations, other management team members), as well as field staff, with the aim of bringing donors closer to the organisation to demonstrate our life-saving mission and work in the projects.
- Define, propose and organise visits to MSF offices and projects, in line with MSF criteria and guidance.
- Ensure that the nature / identity of donors is in line with MSF gifts acceptance policy.
- Ensure that the donor journey runs smoothly, and donors are thanked and stewarded promptly.
- Ensure the database is kept up-to-date.
- Draft engaging communication for the MDs about MSF projects.

*Solicitation/ask*

- In line with the yearly plan and past giving history of main donors, proactively present asks to selected donors for gifts (general and individualized asks) and consult with the Team Coordinator about the solicitation plan
- Ensure that the major donors journey strategy is followed and that major donors are solicited according to their motivations in a personalised way.

*Information and data management*

- Closely work with the System Support Team to ensure most efficient use of Customer Relationship Management Database.
- Support the Team Coordinator in income forecasting and quarterly analysis of results.

*Others*

- Participate in the Community of Practice for Individual Major Donors of MSF in particular with other German-speaking sections.
- Work proactively on projects as needed in the Unit, upon request by her/his supervisor.

## Your profile

*Education*

- University degree in Business Management, Marketing,
- Communications, Political Science, International
- Relations or other relevant areas

*Experience*

- First professional experience in the non-profit sector or in the fields of marketing/sales/communication or client relationship management

*Languages*

- German mother tongue & very good English
- French and Italian an asset.

*Skills/ Technical competencies*

- Proven excellent writing skills (drafting and editing)
- Excellent in oral public presentations
- Strong knowledge of the Windows environment (Word, Excel, Power Point) and tech-savvy
- Strong Analytical skills
- Knowledge of the humanitarian and development sector in Switzerland.

*Personal Abilities/Qualities*

- Excellent interpersonal skills
- Service oriented
- Dynamic, proactive and autonomous
- Rigorous and good organizational skills
- Empathic, enthusiastic, optimistic
- Discretion
- Team spirit.

## Terms of employment

- Full-time position 100% (40h/week)
- Open-ended contract
- Working place: Zurich, Switzerland
- Ideal start date: As soon as possible
- Gross annual salary (for 100%): from CHF 80’856.- to CHF 97’224.- (salary commensurate with equivalent experience and internal salary grid)
- Paid vacation: 25 days per year, prorate temporis, plus any Swiss public holidays falling within the contract period.
- Pension plan: pension contribution covered 3/4 by MSF, 1/4 by staff member.
- Relocation support available for eligible candidates.

jobs.title: Community Health Worker- CHW (Syria - Hama)
jobs.description:
**Job Title: Community Health Worker- CHW**

**Job location: Syria - Hama – Zayzun, Kafr Nabutha, Hawash, Joziyeh ( Jerniyeh )PHC**

**Reports to: Project Coordinator**

**Number of positions: 4**

**JOB SUMMARY**

The Community Health Worker works within the nutrition program at the assigned health facility and its catchment community. The role is responsible for distributing nutrition supplies, monitoring the stock of supplem

entary feeding products for Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) cases, dispensing Ready-to-Use Supplementary Food (RUSF) to admitted beneficiaries, and carrying out community activities, with a particular focus on tracing defaulters and following up non-responding cases to ensure continuity of treatment.

**MAIN DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES**

1\. Distribute nutrit

ion supplies and materials (supplements, micronutrients and awareness materials) to beneficiaries according to the program distribution plan and eligibility criteria.

2\. Dispense RUSF to children aged 6–59 months and pregnant and lactating women (PLW) admitted with MAM, according to the prescribed ration and visit schedule, and record each distribution in the program registers and ration cards.

3\. Monitor the stock of MAM supplements at the health facility: receive deliveries, record stock movements on stock cards, conduct regular physical counts, check expiry dates and storage conditions, and report shortages or discrepancies promptly to the supervisor.

4\. Prepare weekly and monthly stock and distribution reports, and reconcile quantities dispensed against the number of beneficiaries served.

5\. Trace defaulters (cases who missed their follow-up visits) through home visits and phone calls, identify the reasons for defaulting, and encourage caregivers to return to the program.

6\. Follow up non-responding cases through home visits to check correct use of RUSF, sharing of the ration within the household, feeding and hygiene practices, and refer them to the nutritionist or physician for medical review.

7\. Conduct community activities, including active case finding through MUAC screening and awareness sessions on Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF), malnutrition prevention and correct use of supplements.

8\. Refer identified malnutrition cases, and cases showing danger signs or medical complications, to the health facility or stabilization centers.

9\. Keep accurate records of home visits, follow-ups and community activities, and submit them to the supervisor on time.

10\. Coordinate with the nutrition team, community health workers and local community leaders to facilitate community activities and beneficiaries' access to services.

11\. Perform any other related tasks assigned by the direct supervisor.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND SKILLS**

Should have the following skills, education, and experience:

1\. Secondary school certificate as a minimum; an institute or university degree in nutrition, nursing, health sciences or a related field is an advantage.

2\. At least one year of experience in community outreach, nutrition programs or health awareness with non-governmental organizations.

3\. Knowledge of CMAM / MAM programs and basic stock management is an advantage.

4\. Good communication skills and the ability to deal respectfully with the local community.

5\. Basic computer skills (Word, Excel) and the ability to keep accurate records.

6\. Ability to work in the field, conduct home visits and work under pressure.

7\. Residence in the governorate and good knowledge of the area are preferred.

**ABOUT UITYD**

UITYD is a global humanitarian non-profit organization providing medical and health education services to people in need, including refugees and displaced persons, in disaster and underserved regions. The organization is composed of medical and public health professionals of diverse backgrounds.

**CODE OF CONDUCT**

UITYD Code of Conduct reflects the profession’s core set of beliefs and values of care, respect, trust, and integrity. These beliefs and values are fundamental to UITYD employees, volunteers, interns, consultants, and contractors to guide their practice and conduct. The Code is organized into categories, as follows:

1\. Always act with fairness, honesty, integrity, and openness; respect the opinions of others and treat all with equality and dignity without regard to gender, race, color, creed, ancestry, place of origin, political beliefs, religion, marital status, disability, age, or sexual orientation.

2\. Provide a positive and valued experience for those receiving service within and outside UITYD.

**CHILD PROTECTION POLICY**

Child abuse in all forms is unacceptable to UITYD, which recognizes its responsibility to protect children from harm in all areas of its work. UITYD is committed to ensuring a child-safe environment and is applying a zero-tolerance approach towards any kind of child abuse and exploitation.

**DISCRIMINATION, ABUSE AND HARASSMENT POLICY**

UITYD provides equal employment opportunities to all employees and applicants for employment and expressly prohibits and will not tolerate any form of discrimination, abuse, harassment (sexual or otherwise), based upon race, ethnicity, religion, religion, national origin, gender, age, marital status, citizenship status, disability, or military status. UITYD employees and related personnel must under no circumstances take part in any form of discrimination, harassment, or abuse (physical, sexual or verbal), intimidation or exploitation, or in any other way infringe the rights of others inside or outside the organization.

**Safeguarding & Code of Conduct**

All **UITYD** employees must adhere to PSEA's protection policies

Principles and rules of conduct. Strict compliance with safety and ethical standards is required.

jobs.title: Rehabilitation Specialist - Ukraine
Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator - BU Support
jobs.description:
## About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications

## About the Role

Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator plays a critical role in ensuring smooth and efficient execution of procurement projects by closely aligning with business units (BUs) needs, controlling spend, and improving procurement processes. This role involves managing the full procurement lifecycle for assigned BU procurement projects, supporting supplier and stakeholder relationships, driving process improvements, and maintaining strict contract management and compliance. The coordinator also provides performance tracking and reporting to facilitate strategic decision-making and continuous enhancement of procurement activities.

## Responsibilities

Targeted process and performance improvement

- Support cross-functional improvement initiatives by helping develop templates, SOPs, and training materials.
- Coordinate periodic reviews with assigned Business Units to clear aged Procurement Requests (PRs) and Purchase Orders (POs).
- Perform root cause analysis to identify bottlenecks and improve PR to PO turnaround time.
- Identify capability gaps and propose practical, incremental improvements to strengthen processes and team performance.
- Facilitate effective collaboration between BU and PRO teams to ensure alignment on priorities, timelines, and deliverables.
- Promote proactive communication between BU units and PRO to support timely planning, coordination, and issue resolution.

Strategic sourcing responsibilities

- Define the scope and profile of assigned procurement categories.
- Conduct comprehensive spend analysis, market analysis, and profile demand/supply markets to identify opportunities.
- Develop strategic sourcing strategies, setting clear objectives for cost savings, quality improvement, risk mitigation, and determining appropriate tactics.
- Identify, evaluate, and pre-qualify potential suppliers based on strategic needs.
- Lead RFx processes, including negotiation of pricing, Service Level Agreements (SLAs), payment terms, delivery windows, and change management processes, while integrating selected suppliers into planning systems.
- Finalize and execute contracts, ensuring all terms and conditions are clearly defined and favorable.
- Monitor supplier performance against contract terms, drive continuous improvement initiatives, and hold regular business review meetings to ensure costs are consistently driven down.

Reporting and documentation

- Prepare routine reports and dashboards on procurement project progress, highlighting status updates, risks, and key actions for timely decision-making.
- Support data collection and analysis, including responding to ad-hoc market research requests that inform sourcing decisions and category strategies.
- Capture and document supplier performance data to help drive improvements in service levels, quality, and on-time delivery.
- Analyse cost drivers by Business Unit, identifying short-, medium-, and long-term trends to support planning and spend management.
- Work with other BU coordinators to promote standardization and consolidation of requirements, helping reduce duplication and improve sourcing efficiency across BUs.
- Monitor KPI performance for assigned procurement projects and follow up on corrective actions when targets are not met.
- Maintain clear, organized, and audit-ready documentation for all procurement transactions to support compliance and transparency.
- The Tupande Procurement Senior Coordinator will also perform any other duties as assigned by the manager.

## Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- Strong communication skills.
- Analytical Skills: Ability to apply logical thinking and problem-solving techniques to break down complex issues and reach sound conclusions.
- Data Analysis Skills: Proven ability to collect, analyze, and interpret large datasets to inform decision-making. Advanced proficiency in data manipulation and visualization tools, including expertise in Excel (Pivot Tables, Lookups, and Array formulas).
- Solid stakeholder management skills
- Strong working knowledge of process improvement tools and methodologies, DMAIC, 5Whys
- Supply chain risk management skills
- Commercial contracting skills
- Strategic sourcing skills
- Supplier relationship management skills
- Commercial negotiation skills
- Minimum 3 years of work experience in a demanding professional environment.
- Bachelor's degree in procurement, project management, business strategy, or related discipline. Candidates with higher diploma and extensive relevant experience may also qualify.
- Professional qualification e.g CIPS, CILT preferred
- Familiarity with procurement models, sourcing frameworks, and PR-PO systems such as Odoo or Power BI
- Language: Fluent in English and Kiswahili preferred.

## Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

## Job Location

Kakamega, Kenya

## Benefits

Health insurance, paid time off

## Eligibility

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Kenya.

## Application Deadline

02 December 2026. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

*One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. jobs.title: Grants officer (F/M) - Afghanistan
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?

For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

## MdM in Afghanistan

Médecins du Monde re-opened its mission in Afghanistan in 2021 and currently implements programmes in primary healthcare, sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR), mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS), nutrition and harm reduction through a combination of direct implementation and partnerships with local organizations. The mission operates in a complex environment marked by restrictions imposed by de facto authorities, constraints affecting women’s participation and access to services, evolving humanitarian needs and significant challenges for the health system. Current programmes are implemented in Wardak, Farah and Nimroz provinces and place a strong emphasis on community engagement, quality of care and access to essential health services.

In 2025 and 2026, the mission significantly expanded its operations through new funding secured from ECHO, CDCS, and GFFO. The current funding strategy focuses on diversifying the donor portfolio and securing additional funding sources to further expand programmatic coverage. To support this objective, a donor mapping tool has been developed and is regularly updated by the grants officer, in coordination with the deputy general coordinator, to ensure systematic monitoring and follow-up of potential funding opportunities.

## About the role

You will be responsible for coordinating and overseeing grants management, donor compliance, resource mobilization, and partnership and donor engagement for MdM in Afghanistan. In addition, you will be responsible for the mission's communication and will promote visibility on MdM works, particularly when it comes to ensuring implementation of donors’ communication requirements.

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator, your main responsibilities are the following:

**Proposal management:**

- Lead and coordinate concept notes and proposals
- Write the non-technical sections (context, needs analysis, cross-cutting)
- Ensure coherence between narrative, logframe and budget as well as alignment with MdM strategy and donor requirements

**Reporting:**

- Track all active grants and deadlines
- Coordinate donor and internal reports (including the monthly situation report)
- Ensure quality and consistency between programmatic and financial information

**Donor engagement:**

- Maintain donor mapping and a database of calls for proposals
- Train teams on donor rules, prepare meetings and briefing materials for the general coordinator
- Support audits and evaluations

**Partnerships:**

- Support the development of MoUs and partnership agreements
- Coordinate due diligence
- Manage collaboration with partners, including in a consortium

**Communication:**

- Develop communication products (factsheets, country profiles, success stories)
- Contribute to the visibility strategy, train staff on guidelines
- Collect field content, and manage social media in line with MdM and donor guidelines

**Who you’ll work with**

You will work closely with the program officer at HQ, the Institutional Funding Unit, the technical coordinators, the support coordinators, the MEAL team, and the communication teams at HQ and in the field, among others.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Hold a Master’s degree in the following or related field: Development, International Relations, Humanitarian Management
- Have at least two years of experience in a similar role
- Have demonstrated experience in coordinating and preparing strong narrative and financial reports for a variety of donors
- Have a strong understanding of donor compliance, especially for ECHO/INTPA, FCDO, BHA, GFFO
- Have a previous experience with Médecins du Monde (MdM) (strong asset)
- Speak English fluently

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Don't have experience in multi-donors’ budgets
- Don't have the ability to work under pressure, in insecure and fast-changing contexts, with sound judgment, diplomacy and adaptability
- You are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow during the month of November.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 069 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting as soon as possible
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Kabul, Afghanistan
- Regular field visits

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility.

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Logistics & Procurement Assistant - Consultancy Contract
jobs.description:
The Logistics & Procurement Assistant is responsible for supporting the efficient implementation of logistics management (procurement, fleet, assets, stocks, facilities), and administrative functions to ensure timely and effective programme operations. The role contributes to maintaining compliance with Johanniter International Assistance (JIA) and donor regulations while supporting the Country Office and implementing partners in the planning, implementation, monitoring, and documentation of logistics and procurement activities. The Logistics & Procurement Assistant provides day-to-day technical support to implementing partners under the guidance of the JIA focal point.

Strategy and Vision

- actively supports the values of Johanniter and performs duties in accordance with these values
- supports the implementation of the country strategy within their area of responsibility

Leadership

- actively lives the Johanniter leadership principles by fostering trust, embracing diversity, communicating openly, supporting wellbeing, and taking responsibility to contribute to a positive, inclusive, and adaptable work environment
- this is reflected in the day-to-day activities in line with the Code of Conduct and related policies to achieve our goals

Logistics and Procurement Management

- supports the implementation of logistics management activities, including but not limited to, procurement, fleet management, assets management, stock management, and facilities management in accordance with Johanniter policies and procedures, and donor regulations
- ensures the accurate completion and timely submission of all reports as required
- assists in the preparation, processing, and follow-up of procurement requests, requests for quotations (RFQs), purchase orders, contracts, and supplier communications
- coordinates with suppliers to ensure timely delivery of goods and services, and resolves delivery issues when required
- verifies procurement and logistics documentation for completeness, accuracy, and compliance before filing.
- coordinates the receipt, inspection, dispatch, and transportation of programme supplies and relief items
- liaises with transport providers to ensure timely and cost-effective transportation of staff, assets, and programme supplies
- supports with customs clearance and other import/export procedures when applicable
- arranges staff travel, including flight and accommodation bookings, visa applications, and ground transportation in accordance with organizational procedure
- maintains an updated supplier database and supports market assessments and supplier performance evaluations
- assists in preparing procurement plans and monitors procurement progress against approved plans
- supports emergency procurement activities when required
- drives vehicles owned, leased or rented by the organization for reasons directly related to the responsibilities of the role

Fleet, Asset and Inventory Management

- maintains an accurate asset register and ensures all organizational assets are properly tagged, recorded, and assigned
- monitors asset allocation, transfers, maintenance, disposal, and annual physical verification
- maintains inventory records and ensures accurate stock movements through appropriate documentation
- conducts routine physical asset and stock counts and reconciles discrepancies
- ensures proper storage conditions, stock management documentation, and warehouse organization
- monitors minimum stock levels and reports replenishment needs
- coordinates preventive maintenance and servicing of vehicles and generators
- monitors vehicle usage, fuel consumption, maintenance schedules, insurance, registrations, and licensing
- ensures fleet operations comply with Johanniter safety and operational standards

Facilities and Office Support

- supports the maintenance of office facilities, equipment, utilities, and service contracts
- coordinates repairs and maintenance with external service providers
- monitors office supplies and ensures timely replenishment
- supports office setup and logistics arrangements for meetings, workshops, and training events

## **Documentation and Reporting**

- maintains accurate electronic and hard-copy filing systems for procurement, logistics, fleet, assets, inventory, and facilities
- ensures all logistics documentation is complete, properly authorized, and readily available for audits and donor verification
- prepares Logistics Monthly Closing and other reports as necessary, and ensures timely submission
- assists in preparing logistics information required for internal and donor reporting
- maintains comprehensive and well-organized records for Country Office operations and implementing partner documentation where applicable

Safeguarding

- actively upholds the organisation's safeguarding policies and Code of Conduct by fostering a safe and respectful environment, completing mandatory safeguarding training, maintaining professional boundaries, and taking responsibility to prevent harm through the timely and confidential reporting of any concerns or incidents

## **Security and Safety**

- supports the Field Coordinator in maintaining accurate and up-to-date awareness of the country context
- supports the Field Coordinator with movement planning and tracking

**Person Specification**

Professional Qualification and Experience:

Essential:

- bachelor's degree or Diploma in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration, or another relevant field
- minimum of 1 year of professional experience in logistics, procurement, supply chain, or operations within an NGO or humanitarian organization
- experience in fleet management, inventory management, and asset management

Desirable:

- familiarity with NGO logistics procedures, or willingness to learn them on the job
- experience supporting programme implementation in a fast-paced operational environment
- experience working with or supporting implementing partners is considered an asset
- valid driving license

Skills

- good knowledge of procurement and logistics procedures
- good understanding of donor compliance requirements
- strong organizational and documentation skills
- ability to prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines
- good analytical and problem-solving skills
- excellent communication and interpersonal skills
- ability to work independently and collaboratively within multicultural teams
- good report writing skills
- proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Excel, Word, Outlook)
- safe and efficient driving skills
- high level of integrity, accountability, and attention to detail

jobs.title: Head of Programme
jobs.description:
**What we are looking for**

Are you an accomplished humanitarian leader with the strategic vision, fundraising expertise, and leadership influence to shape refugee and humanitarian portfolio in Jordan?

This is not simply a programme management position. We are looking for a strategic leader who can identify opportunities, influence key stakeholders, strengthen localization, and secure the funding required to expand impact for refugees and vulnerable communities across Jordan.

You will be entrusted with shaping the future direction of NRC's programme portfolio while ensuring excellence in programmatic delivery, accountability, compliance, learning, and organisational growth.

***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***

**What you will do**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is seeking an exceptional **Head of Programme** to join its senior leadership team in Jordan. This is a pivotal Country Management Group (CMG) role, responsible for leading programme strategy, resource mobilization, grants, MEAL, partnerships, and programme quality across a complex and dynamic humanitarian environment.

As a key member of the country leadership team, you will play a central role in delivering NRC Jordan's 2026-2030 Country Strategy while driving sustainable growth through innovative programming, strategic donor engagement, and strong partnerships with national and international stakeholders.

Key responsibilities:

- Provide strategic leadership and oversight to the Programme, Grants, and MEAL functions.
- Lead the implementation of NRC Jordan's strategic objectives and ensure alignment with country priorities and annual action plans.
- Drive the development and execution of NRC Jordan's fundraising and resource mobilization strategy.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with donors, strategic partners, consortium members, government bodies, and humanitarian actors.
- Identify emerging funding opportunities and position NRC competitively for future growth.
- Lead grant portfolio management, ensuring high-quality proposal development, compliance, reporting, and donor stewardship.
- Champion programme quality, evidence-based programming, accountability, and organisational learning.
- Strengthen partnerships with local and national actors and lead NRC's transition towards more locally led programming approaches.
- Foster collaboration between technical and operational teams to ensure effective programme delivery.
- Lead, mentor, and develop a high-performing team of technical specialists and programme support functions.

**What you will bring**

- Bachelor’s degree in Development Studies, Social Sciences, International Relations, or a related field**.**
- Minimum 6 years of experience in a senior management position within a humanitarian or recovery context, with responsibility for programme and/or project management.
- Experience in NRC Core Competency programming (ICLA, Shelter, and Education) is an asset.
- A strong and demonstrated track record in fundraising and donor engagement, including securing significant institutional funding, developing donor relationships, identifying funding opportunities, and shaping winning resource mobilization strategies.
- Deep knowledge of humanitarian programming, programme quality standards, grants management, and MEAL systems. Experience in integrating evidence-based approaches and programme quality standards throughout the project cycle.
- Strong understanding of donor priorities, compliance requirements, and the evolving humanitarian and refugee landscape in Jordan and the region
- Proven experience building and managing partnerships with local and national actors.
- Experience leading multi-sector, consortium-based, and partnership-driven programmes.
- Outstanding stakeholder engagement, influencing, and representation skills with strong strategic, analytical, problem-solving, team-building, interpersonal and conflict-resolution capabilities.
- The ability to lead, inspire, and develop diverse teams in complex and rapidly changing environments.
- Fluency in English, both written and verbal and excellent writing skills.

Please download [the detailed job description](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:b:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQDLfnFLI5MKTaemBSTg1EC-Adc-h353hZJskxlm_J4cHhM?e=zKz0i0) to learn more about the position.

**What we offer**

- Duty station: Amman, Jordan
- Fixed term contract: 12 months, renewable based on funding, performance and the need for the position
- Travel: 30% to Area and Field Offices (NRC Operational Areas)
- Salary/benefits: Grade 11 on NRC's national grading structure.
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- We invite applications from qualified candidates. ***Applicants must be legally eligible to work in Jordan, We are unable to provide work permits or visa sponsorships for this position.***
- Please ensure you attach copies of your academic and professional certificates.
- To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email address or click on Opportunity Marketplace.
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted. We receive many applicants for each vacant position.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity

[Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

[Learn more about NRC Jordan](https://www.nrc.no/countries/middle-east/jordan)

jobs.description:

*Strategic Government Engagement and Partnerships*
• Build and maintain strategic relationships with key government institutions involved in recovery and ‎reconstruction of joint opportunities. ‎
• Develop and maintain a stakeholder map of government actors, recovery institutions, and public sector ‎partners relevant to the URCS recovery priorities. ‎
• Identify opportunities for URCS engagement within national, regional, and local recovery programmes and ‎initiatives. ‎
• Support URCS leadership in high-level engagement with government counterparts and recovery stakeholders.‎
• Represent URCS in recovery-related coordination platforms, consultations, and working groups. ‎
• Advise leadership on government engagement priorities, risks, and emerging opportunities.‎

*Recovery Resource Mobilization Opportunities ‎*
• Identify funding, partnership, and co-financing opportunities for URCS recovery programmes. ‎
• Develop relationships with donors, development partners, financial institutions, and private sector actors. ‎
• Support the development of funding proposals, concept notes, and partnership opportunities. ‎
• Advise teams on resource mobilization strategies and donor positioning.‎

*Alignment of URCS Programmes with National Recovery Priorities*
• Align URCS recovery programmes with national, regional, and local recovery priorities. ‎
• Identify opportunities to position URCS programmes within government-led recovery efforts. ‎
• Support programme teams to incorporate government priorities into project design and implementation. ‎
• Facilitate engagement with government stakeholders during programme development

I*nternal Coordination and Advisory Support*
• Coordinate closely with programme teams, branch development and branch networks, and relevant ‎counterparts to advance recovery opportunities. ‎
• Provide technical advice on government engagement, partnerships, and resource mobilization. ‎
• Support a coordinated organizational approach to recovery stakeholder engagement. ‎
• Strengthening institutional capacity in recovery partnership development and positioning.‎

*Policy Analysis, Intelligence, and Reporting*
• Monitor recovery policies, plans, funding opportunities, and stakeholder developments. ‎
• Analyse opportunities and risks relevant to URCS recovery objectives. ‎
• Prepare briefings, stakeholder analyses, and recommendations for management. ‎

Education

Experience

- Demonstrated experience working with government institutions, particularly those ‎involved in recovery, reconstruction, regional development, infrastructure, social ‎policy, or public investment processes. (experience with Ukrainian government is ‎advantage)‎
- Proven track record of developing strategic partnerships and mobilizing resources ‎from government, donors, development finance, private sector, or other financing ‎sources. ‎
- Experience working in humanitarian, development, recovery, or resilience-building ‎programmes, preferably within large national or international organizations, is an ‎advantage. ‎
- Strong understanding of stakeholder coordination and partnership management ‎within complex, multi-actor environments.‎

**Preferred** ‎

- Experience supporting the design or implementation of national, regional, or local ‎recovery and reconstruction initiatives is highly desirable.‎

Knowledge, Skills and Languages

jobs.title: Climate Resilience and Adaptation Advisor
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

**Summary:**

Position Summary

The Climate Resilience Advisor provides technical and advisory support to strengthen climate resilience of Habitat for Humanity’s housing and settlement work across Asia Pacific programs. The Advisor will work with the Asia-Pacific regional team to support Country Offices. This will include the implementation of strategic guidance, provision of technical assistance, design and delivery of capacity strengthening, supporting research, evidence-based implementation and knowledge management, advocacy and partnership development. This will include coordination with HFHI Global Program Operations, and specifically the Director-Climate Resilience (e.g., on development and implementation of the Global Climate Approach). The Advisor will work to ensure the integration of climate adaptation and mitigation into housing and settlement work and community development initiatives.

The Advisor will serve as the regional focal point for climate action, and in this capacity will support Country Offices to understand climate risks, and options to address/mitigate these risks to reduce vulnerability and build resilience of low- and middle-income households and communities across the Asia Pacific region.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Key Result Areas and Responsibilities**

**1. Strategic Alignment and Stakeholder Engagement (30%)**

Provide technical thought leadership to ensure climate resilient housing and settlement programming is aligned with the Global Climate Approach, with contextualized implementation across Country Offices in Asia Pacific region.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide technical leadership to support contextualized/localized implementation and monitoring of HFHI’s Global Climate Approach within the Asia Pacific region.
- Advise on current/recent sources of climate risk data and analyses, and options for integrating climate these risks into housing/settlement-focused project design, implementation and monitoring.
- Facilitate alignment and promote integration between climate resilience programming and broader disaster risk reduction/humanitarian programming.
- Serve as a technical resource and thought partner to Habitat Country Offices, supporting program design, implementation and learning.
- Engage with external stakeholders (HFHI’s global and regional partners, research institutions, NGOs, and networks) to strengthen technical positioning and partnerships opportunities around climate resilience and DRR.
- Represent HFHI and contribute to relevant regional and global forums, working groups, and coordination platforms, as required.
- Support strategic partnerships and collaboration opportunities that advance Habitat's climate resilience agenda.

**2. Capacity Building and Technical Support (25%)**

Strengthen the technical capacity of Country Offices and partners to design, implement, and scale high-quality climate resilience housing/settlement programming

**Key Responsibilities**

Assess in-country capacity, design and facilitate targeted capacity building initiatives (e.g., structured training, workshops, coaching) for National Organization staff on climate resilience.

Develop and maintain technical resources, tools, guidance documents, and learning materials.

Facilitate communities of practice, peer learning, and regional exchanges.

Promote organizational learning across countries, programs and operations.

**3. Technical Program Oversight (25%)**

Provide advisory support to Country Offices to help ensure the quality of climate-related program design, implementation and monitoring. considerations into program designs, projects—supporting Country Offices to scale impact, and cross-learning across the Asia Pacific Region.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Provide technical input and advisory support to Country Offices to strengthen integration of climate risk data/analyses and evidenced-based approaches into climate resilient housing/settlements project design, implementation and monitoring.
- Advise Country Offices on context specific adaptation measures, including resilient construction techniques, site selection, safer land use, and community-based approaches.
- Where feasible, advise Country Offices on context appropriate mitigation measures, where feasible,
- Contribute technical input to concept notes, program proposals, and donor reports related to climate resilience (e.g., adaptation and mitigation).
- As requested, support donor engagement resource mobilization efforts.
- Collaborate with other Subject Matter Experts (SMEs) and technical teams to ensure climate considerations are integrated into cross-sectoral programming.

**4. Research, Innovation, Learning and Knowledge Management (15%)**

Strengthen evidence generation, cross-learning and innovation, to improve climate resilient housing/settlement programming and support scaling of effective approaches.

**Key Responsibilities**

- Support research design and implementation, the generation and synthesis of evidence, and institutional learning specific to climate resilient housing.

- Contribute to integration of climate and DRR indicators into MEAL systems and contribute to regional and global learning agendas.
- Contribute to research, support innovation pilots, and partnerships related to climate resilient housing and settlements.
- Develop and disseminate technical resources, and guidance materials.
- Provide subject matter expertise and technical advisory support to other departments and initiatives within HFHI.

**5. Disaster Preparedness, Response and Recovery Support (5%)**

Provide advisory support to integrate climate risk reduction and resilience into disaster preparedness, response and recovery efforts

**Key Responsibilities**

Work with the Housing Disaster Risk and Resilience (HDRR) team on climate risk reduction measures in response and recovery

Provide technical input on risk-informed approaches to recovery planning and implementation

Support alignment of recovery interventions with long-term resilience objectives

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- Master’s degree in Climate Change, Environmental Sciences, Disaster Risk Reduction, Urban Planning, Engineering, Development Studies, or a related field
- Minimum 5–7 years of relevant experience in climate resilience, DRR, or risk-informed programming, preferably in the Asia-Pacific region
- Demonstrated experience supporting multi-country programs and working with decentralized teams
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, and resilience approaches in housing, settlements, or community development
- Strong understanding of climate risks, adaptation, resilience, and mitigation approaches in housing, settlements, infrastructure, or community development.
- Experience in humanitarian, recovery, or nexus programming is an asset
- Experience in donor engagement, proposal development, or climate finance is an advantage

**Key Skills & Competencies**

- Strong technical expertise in climate adaptation and the built environment
- Sound understanding of climate mitigation, with the ability to understand where synergies and tradeoffs exist between mitigation and adaptation (especially where these impact affordability)
- Ability to translate technical concepts into practical, field-oriented guidance
- Proven advisory, facilitation, and capacity-building skills
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills in English (regional languages an asset)
- Strong cross-cultural collaboration skills and ability to work in matrixed environments
- Willingness and ability to travel within the Asia-Pacific region

**Core Behavioral Competencies**

- Commitment to HFHI’s mission, values, equity, and safeguarding principles
- Collaboration and partnership mindset
- Learning oriented and solution focused
- Accountability and integrity

**Working Conditions**

- Regional role with frequent collaboration across multiple countries and time zones.
- Periodic travel to Country Offices and Country Offices, including fragile, climate-vulnerable, and disaster-affected contexts.
- Ability and willingness to travel within the Asia-Pacific region as required.

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Appel à candidature pour le poste de Directeur (trice) National(e)
jobs.description:
**Appel à candidature pour le poste de Directeur (trice) National(e) basé (e) à Abidjan**

**A propos de l’Organisation**

Présente en Côte d’Ivoire depuis 1971, l’Association Nationale SOS Villages d’Enfants en Côte d’Ivoire est une Organisation nationale de développement social qui œuvre pour la satisfaction des besoins et la protection des droits des enfants vulnérables. A ce jour, SOS Villages d'Enfants en Côte d'Ivoire dispose de trois villages (Abobo, Aboisso et Yamoussoukro) et intervient au NORD dans le Poro et Tchologo à travers un financement de SOS Villages d’enfants Norvège.

Pour la coordination des interventions, la gestion des équipes et la gestion des partenariats stratégiques et la représentation, l’Association Nationale SOS Villages d’Enfants en Côte d’Ivoire recrute un(e) Directeur(trice) National(e)

**Mission de la position:**

Sous l’autorité du Président du Conseil d’administration, le / la directeur (trice) national(e ) dirige, gère et développe l'Association Nationale (AN) en tant que chef de l'exécutif. Il/elle veille à la mise en œuvre efficace des programmes et des services de qualité aux enfants et aux jeunes, aux familles et aux communautés, dans le cadre de la vision, de la mission, des valeurs et de la stratégie de l'organisation internationale SOS Villages d'Enfants. En recherchant des subventions et des financements gouvernementaux, des subventions internationales/nationales ainsi qu'en collectant des fonds, il/elle maximise l'autosuffisance financière de l'association nationale (et la capacité à soutenir financièrement d'autres associations nationales) en fonction du potentiel du pays.

**Objectifs généraux du poste :**

- Mettre en œuvre la stratégie et les décisions des organes de gouvernances notamment le Conseil d’administration
- Diriger les processus de planification stratégique afin de garantir la durabilité et la pertinence du travail de l'AN.
- Assurer l'efficacité opérationnelle de tous les programmes et garantir la qualité de la prise en charge des enfants conformément aux normes définies par l'organisation.
- Assurer la mise en œuvre des principes de protection de l'enfance au sein de l'AN.
- Assurer une gestion efficace et durable des ressources financières et autres de l'AN
- Assurer la gestion des risques et la continuité des activités de l’AN
- Renforcer les capacités humaines de l'association nationale afin d'assurer sa croissance et sa stabilité à long terme.
- Assurer un enracinement local solide en promouvant l'intégration locale de l'association et en la faisant reconnaître à tous les niveaux dans le pays. Renforcer l'affiliation à la Fédération internationale en participant et en contribuant aux processus internationaux.
- Promouvoir et gérer une image appropriée de l'organisation, tant en interne qu'en externe, en utilisant les valeurs et les normes de SOS Villages d'Enfants comme base pour façonner la marque.
- Veiller à la mise en œuvre des normes internationales de SOS Villages d'Enfants.

**Principaux clients** :

- Conseil d'administration (ou administrateurs)
- Équipe de Management National
- Directeur de l’équipe IDS siège
- Points focaux des Associations ou Fondations partenaires
- Partenaires centraux et régionaux de l’Etat
- Parties prenantes externes de la société civile nationale et internationale

**Domaines de performance clés et principales responsabilités** :

**Planification stratégique**

- Facilite le processus de planification stratégique sous la direction du conseil d'administration (ou guidé par le conseil d'administration), en impliquant l'équipe de gestion nationale et d'autres membres clés du personnel dans l'identification des domaines prioritaires et la définition des objectifs.
- Communique et suis les plans pour garantir une mise en œuvre efficace des projets
- Présente les plans, les rapports et les propositions lors des réunions du conseil d'administration. Veille, en coopération avec le président, à la légalité de l'organisation nationale, dans le respect de la législation nationale applicable.
- Veille à ce que les décisions du conseil d'administration se traduisent par des actions claires.

**Développement de la marque**

- Applique le concept de développement de la marque convenu au niveau international dans la stratégie, la planification et la mise en œuvre au niveau national.

**Gestion des ressources humaines et développement de l'organisation**

- Veille à ce que les bonnes personnes soient employées aux bons postes afin que les collaborateurs et les partenaires extérieurs soient toujours traités avec le professionnalisme voulu et conformément aux principes de la culture organisationnelle.
- Veille à la mise en place d'un système efficace de gestion des performances et de développement des ressources humaines qui garantisse le développement des collaborateurs et l'identification des talents. Il/elle encourage la responsabilisation à tous les niveaux de l'association nationale.
- Dirige et gère l'équipe nationale,
- Assure le fonctionnement efficace du bureau national.

**Elaboration, gestion et suivi des programmes**

- Veille à ce que les ressources soient concentrées sur la mise en œuvre de programmes et de services adaptés et efficaces.
- Veille à l'examen et à l'évaluation des programmes afin de s'assurer que les plans et les politiques convenus sont mis en œuvre et fournit un renforcement des capacités et un soutien technique si nécessaire.
- Promeut l'interaction et l'échange d'expériences pertinentes entre les programmes.
- Vise l’atteinte de standards de haut niveau pour les projets et programmes.

**Finances et gestion des fonds**

- Assure la planification et la budgétisation
- Met en œuvre et surveille le système de contrôle interne, examine les chiffres clés et les rapports financiers
- Veille à la réalisation de l'état financier annuel et du rapport d'audit externe.
- S’assure de la conformité dans la gestion des ressources.
- S’assure de la gestion des risques et de la continuité des activités.

**Recherche de fonds et relations publiques**

- Promeut la stabilité à long terme et l'autosuffisance financière en recherchant le soutien de sources gouvernementales et privées dans le but de maximiser le potentiel de collecte de fonds.
- Soutient l'élaboration et la mise en œuvre de stratégies durables de collecte de fonds et de demandes de subventions.
- Soutient les activités de relations publiques/marketing selon les besoins et veille à ce que l'image de l'organisation soit appropriée.
- S’assure de la bonne mise en œuvre de toutes les initiatives de collecte de fonds

**Création** **de partenariats, plaidoyer et coopération avec les parties prenantes externes**

- Établit des relations solides avec les autorités gouvernementales compétentes, assure une représentation appropriée des points de vue de l'organisation et recherche la reconnaissance et le soutien du gouvernement pour le travail de SOS Villages d'Enfants.
- Etablit des partenariats avec des organisations non gouvernementales qui défendent les droits des enfants
- Poursuit des objectifs de plaidoyer dans les forums de protection de l'enfance et en partenariat avec d'autres ONG qui s'unissent pour donner vie à notre mission en faveur des enfants et des jeunes en situation de vulnérabilité.

**Coopération et rapports**

- Entretient des relations professionnelles et une coopération étroite avec le bureau des services IDS qu'avec d'autres unités du bureau international ;
- Fournit des rapports spécifiques aux parties prenantes et donne suite aux accords.
- Représente l'organisation auprès des autorités gouvernementales et d'autres parties prenantes externes.

**Sauvegarde de l'enfant (CS)**

- Responsable de la mise en œuvre et de la gestion de la politique de sauvegarde au sein de l’Association Nationale
- Veille à ce que tous les collaborateurs, partenaires et associés signent toutes les politiques de l’organisation
- Rapporte aux autorités compétentes toute préoccupation de l'organisation concernant la sauvegarde des enfants dans le cadre de ses programmes ;
- Veille à ce que la sauvegarde des enfants ne soit pas compromise par des activités dans le domaine de la collecte de fonds ou des relations avec les donateurs.
- S’assure que tous les partenaires/donateurs sont informés de la politique de la sauvegarde de l’enfant de l’organisation et sont invités à la respecter.
- Est responsable de la commande d'enquêtes internes en cas de besoin
- Veille à ce que les incidents de la sauvegarde de l’enfant qui répondent aux critères des incidents graves soient signalés dans les délais au bureau international.

**Qualification et Compétences requises**

- Le ou la candidat (e) doit avoir le niveau de BAC +5, MBA, Maitrise en Sciences sociales, économiques ou toute autre filière pertinente.
- Avoir une expérience d’au moins 10 ans dans la gestion des projets et programmes et des partenariats.
- Avoir au moins 5 ans d’expérience à un poste similaire ou de senior leadership dans une organisation humanitaire ou une institution de développement.

**Ce que nous défendons :**

SOS Villages d’Enfants Côte d’Ivoire est engagé à créer et à maintenir un environnement chaleureux et protecteur. Elle promeut ses valeurs fondamentales, prévient et traite les abus et l’exploitation des enfants. Nous condamnons fermement toutes les formes de maltraitance et d'exploitation des enfants, que ce soit au sein ou à l'extérieur de notre organisation. Nous répondons toujours à tout cas de maltraitance avérée, allégation ou tentation d’abus dans notre sphère d'influence selon sa nature. Nous veillons à ce que des mécanismes soient en place pour sensibiliser, aider à la prévention, encourager les signalements et faciliter les réponses. Ces mécanismes vont des actions de développement des ressources humaines telles que la formation et le conseil aux mesures telles que la suspension, le licenciement et l'action en justice.

jobs.title: Chief of Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch, D1
jobs.company: UN Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs
jobs.description:
This position is located in the Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch (SPPB), Humanitarian Sector Division, Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), in Geneva. OCHA is the part of the United Nations Secretariat responsible for bringing together humanitarian actors to ensure a coherent response to emergencies. OCHA also ensures there is a framework within which each actor can contribute to the overall response efforts. OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. This temporary job opening is being advertised for the position of Chief of Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch in Geneva. With delegated authority of the Humanitarian Sector Division Director, the Chief of Branch will be responsible for leading the reform of the humanitarian programme cycle and strengthening and streamlining humanitarian coordination in line with the Humanitarian Reset; the training of OCHA and IASC personnel; the documentation and sharing of best practice; shepherding interagency negotiations; spearheading cash coordination; enhancing humanitarian-development collaboration; and the provision of technical support to Humanitarian Coordinators, Humanitarian Country Teams and OCHA Country/Regional Offices. The Branch is responsible for the production of the Global Humanitarian Overview. The Chief of Branch will also oversee support from her/his teams to effectively contribute to the implementation of OCHA's Strategic Plan. The incumbent of this post reports to Director, Humanitarian Sector Division.

## **Responsibilities**

With delegated authority, the Chief of Branch will be responsible for the following duties: MANAGEMENT/REPRESENTATION: - Streamlines the functions of the Branch to ensure cohesion and 'fit-for-purpose' structures designed to effectively implement its responsibilities under the OCHA Strategic Plan and the Humanitarian Reset. - Drives change management to implement the reform of the humanitarian programme cycle and transform humanitarian coordination in line with the Humanitarian Reset’s four ‘D’s – Define, Devolve, Deliver, Defend. - Promotes localization of humanitarian action and coordination, accountability to affected people (AAP), gender, age and disability-sensitivity, and cross-cultural responsiveness. - Fosters and strengthens collaboration and consultation with all functions of OCHA HQ and Country and Regional Offices. - Provides strategic vision and leadership on each area of the humanitarian programme cycle: coordinated needs assessment, analysis and prioritization; joint strategic response planning; resource mobilization and joint response monitoring. - Guides and coordinates the establishment of a work plan for the Branch, the determination of priorities, and the allocation of resources to ensure timely delivery of agreed outputs. - Ensures regular and effective supervision of staff, particularly by leading, managing, developing and training staff. - Fosters teamwork and communication among staff, and strengthens the linkages between staff in country operations, regional offices and headquarters offices. - Undertakes or oversees the programmatic and administrative tasks necessary for the functioning of the Branch, including preparation of budgets, reporting on budget and programme performance, evaluation of staff performance, interviews of candidates for job openings, and evaluation of candidates. - Promotes OCHA's mandate, objectives and tools in terms of the humanitarian progamme cycle and humanitarian coordination through contacts with governments, diplomatic missions, UN entities, non-governmental organizations and the media. - Represents OCHA in the IASC in all matters related to the humanitarian programme cycle and humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration); and coordinates the development of relevant IASC policies and tools. - Leads efforts to raise awareness of the humanitarian programme cycle and humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration) and efforts to strengthen and reform these among Member States, Regional Organisations and other stakeholders. - Ensures close and regular engagement with the Development Coordination Office in support of humanitarian-development collaboration and guidance as well as leading OCHA's secretariat support to the Joint Steering Committee and OCHA’s work on transition. GUIDANCE AND COUNTRY SUPPORT: - Leads the development and maintenance of normative guidance, procedures and tools that enable Resident/Humanitarian Coordinators and Humanitarian Country teams, with the support of OCHA Country/Regional Offices, to effectively manage all aspects of the humanitarian programme cycle and the coordination architecture in-country, including relationships with development partners, to drive forward the Humanitarian Reset. - Facilitates the documentation and dissemination of best practice and drives innovation and reform around the humanitarian programme cycle and the coordination architecture, ensuring processes and tools evolve and are adaptable to different contexts, in line with the Humanitarian Reset, including with respect to localization and AAP. - Oversees and ensures coherence of efforts to strengthen the role of humanitarian coordination mechanisms in guiding humanitarian action. CAPACITY BUILDING AND TRAINING: - Works with the Crisis Response Division and OCHA Heads of Country/Regional Offices to identify and fill technical support requirements through coordinated missions. - Oversees the development and implementation of a plan for providing comprehensive training to OCHA headquarters and country/regional presences on the humanitarian programme cycle and humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration) and using online tools and platforms to support planning and response monitoring. - Supports and complements on-going efforts by OCHA Country/Regional Offices, Resident/Humanitarian Coordinator Offices and IASC subsidiary bodies' to reach out to, partner with and build capacities within Governments, national entities, regional organisations and other stakeholders on humanitarian programme cycle components and humanitarian coordination in crisis-prone areas. CONTRIBUTION TO CORPORATE LEADERSHIP: - Contributes, as a member of OCHA's General Management Team (GMT), OCHA Management Committee and other bodies, to policy development at corporate level that enhances OCHA's overall effectiveness. - In support of the Director, Humanitarian Sector Division, OCHA Geneva, advises the ERC and other Senior Leadership Group members all issues of policy and practice related to the humanitarian programme cycle, humanitarian coordination (including cash coordination and humanitarian-development collaboration) and accountability to affected people. - Provides leadership and oversight to ensure Strategic Prioritization and Practices Branch adherence to relevant areas of OCHA's Strategic Plan and its results framework.
