jobs.title: Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead - MENAU
jobs.description:
The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solutions-driven, passionate change-maker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people world-wide for a better future.

**This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in Jordan and Lebanon.**

**CONTEXTUAL BACKGROUND:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) has worked across the Middle East, North Africa, and Ukraine (MENAU) region for more than forty years, responding to some of the world’s most complex and protracted humanitarian crises.

Today, more than 75 million people across the MENAU are in need of humanitarian assistance, as conflict, displacement, climate change, and economic instability continue to disrupt lives and limit access to essential services. Vulnerable groups—especially women, children, and people on the move—remain most at risk.

With more than 1,000 staff working across Jordan, Lebanon, Libya, Syria, Yemen, and Ukraine, the IRC delivers integrated programs that meet both immediate and long-term needs—improving access to health, safety, education, and economic wellbeing, and helping those affected by crisis to survive, recover, and rebuild their lives.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead for MENAU is a key member of IRC’s Regional Management Team, ensuring a strategic approach to policy and advocacy engagement across the region. The role aims to influence the policies and practices of key national, regional and global decision-makers while translating the experience and expertise of IRC programmes and partners into influence at national, regional and global levels.

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead provides strategic leadership and support to country programmes, while leading on policy and, advocacy and managing in partnership IRC’s communications efforts across the region. S/he leads the development of regional policy positions and ensures that MENAU advocacy products are strategically aligned, evidence-based and meet the quality and standards expected by the organisation.

The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead represents IRC on regional policy and advocacy platforms, helping to shape debate and ensuring the perspectives and priorities of country programmes and partner organizations are at the forefront of humanitarian and development decision-making. Working closely with global colleagues, s/he also ensures that regional realities shape the IRC's wider policy and advocacy positions.

Reporting to the MENAU Regional Vice President, with a management in partnership to Global Policy and Advocacy team, namely the Global Director of Program Advocacy and Engagement, Director – Policy and Advocacy and works closely with global Policy and Advocacy, while supervising and supporting regional and country level policy, advocacy and communication staff. The Regional Policy and Advocacy Lead is based in Amman or Beirut with frequent travel in the region, and as needed to New York, Washington D.C., London, Brussels, Geneva and other capitals.

**SPECIFIC RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Overall Strategy and Team Management:**

- In close coordination with the Regional Vice President, leads the development, alignment and implementation of policy and advocacy strategy for the region.
- In close coordination with the global Policy and Advocacy team, contributes to and supports the implementation of organizational strategies.
- Builds and maintains relationships with diverse MENAU organizations and individuals to develop networks and increase collective impact.
- Maintains overall accountability for regional and country-based policy, advocacy and communications team cohesion, product delivery and ensures all products meet the quality and standard set by the organization.

**2. Advocacy and Policy:**

- Works in close collaboration with country-level and global policy and advocacy colleagues, to develop and drive policy and advocacy products for in-country, regional and international policymakers, ensuring that field priorities and perspectives are integrated.
- Coordinates and supports the work of country-level policy and advocacy staff and ensures that country-focused information and materials are widely disseminated internally and externally.
- Supports the development of policy and advocacy material for national, regional and global use including talking points, briefing notes, position papers and advocacy reports.
- Supports IRC’s efforts to scale the most impactful programmatic interventions by crafting strategies to overcome political and policy barriers to their deployment nationally, regionally, while informing global debates.
- Provides policy review for organizational positions and materials related to key issues in MENAU.
- Represents IRC in regional advocacy, policy and coordination forums, as well as at key lobbying meetings in global capitals, the UN and where necessary.
- Provides analysis and produces content for executive and regional leadership and ensures the Regional Vice President is briefed on all relevant policy developments.

**3. Communications and Media:**

- Provide day-to-day management of the Deputy Director of Public Affairs and Communications, MENAU to ensure regional alignment of the regional public affairs and communications strategy.
- Support the expansion of IRC’s reach and visibility in the region, acting as an IRC spokesperson with regional and international media.
- Ensures consistent advocacy messages, calls to actions and policy asks in external communications products, including press releases, talking points, and spokesperson briefings.
- Collaborates with Deputy Director on polished and accessible external communications materials to inform key audiences and influence policy decisions.

**SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES:** Management in Partnership of the MENAU Deputy Director of Public Affairs and Communications and their team. Management in Partnership of the ECD Policy, Advocacy and Communications Lead, as well as Management in Partnership of country-level policy and advocacy staff.

**KEY WORKING RELATIONSHIPS:**

**Internal:** Regional Vice President; MENAU Regional Management Team; MENAU Country Directors; global policy and advocacy staff and Vice President for Global Policy and Advocacy with Management in Partnership with the Director of Program Advocacy and Engagement, global communication staff with close coordinate with the Director of Global Public Affairs and Communication; country and regional based staff as appropriate.

**External:** Regional and national advocacy fora, international and national NGOs, UN agencies, public and private donor agencies, national governments/authorities, regional and international media representatives.

**REQUIREMENTS**

- University Degree in Communications, International Affairs, Policy & Advocacy, Political Science, or any other relevant field. Master’s degree is preferable.
- At least ten years of increasingly responsible professional experience responding to complex humanitarian crises and/or post-conflict situations, with a track record of delivering change through highly impactful policy, advocacy and communications strategies
- A keen understanding of political complexities in the MENAU region is required; previous experience working in the Middle East is required
- Solid communications and media relations experience required
- Fluency in English and Arabic (written and spoken) is required, with demonstrated outstanding writing skills.
- Proven ability to persuade and influence diverse audiences
- Excellent analytical, presentation, communication and reporting skills
- Ability to navigate interpersonal and inter-departmental organizational dynamics to keep focus on goals and products
- Must be willing and able to travel regularly within the region and occasionally internationally
- Culturally sensitive, able and interested in working with a multi-ethnic team
- Arabic Speaking candidates from the Middle East region are strongly encouraged to apply.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in [IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct](https://www.rescue.org/page/our-code-conduct). Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on [Safeguarding](https://www.rescue.org/page/safeguarding), Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Accounting Assistant
jobs.description:
**Purpose and Objectives:**

Asian Disaster Preparedness Center (ADPC) is an autonomous international organization for cooperation in and implementation of disaster risk reduction and building climate resilience in Asia and the Pacific. It was established in 1986 as a regional disaster preparedness center (DMC). ADPC has grown and expended its role to be for scientific, educational, developmental, and humanitarian purposes. ADPC employs a wide range of professional expertise typically required for Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and Climate Resilience (CR) in and effective manner.

The Finance and Accounting Unit is one of the ADPC’s Program Support Service Units with interlinked responsibilities with the Human Resource and Administration Unit and Procurement Unit and solely or jointly responsible for:

- Ensure compliance with statutory, legislative, and donor requirements.
- Safeguard ADPC’s cash, resources, and financial assets through effective internal control procedures.
- Monitor the effectiveness of the key control framework to minimize the risk of fraud and irregularities across ADPC.
- Ensure the availability of accurate and timely financial information for management decision-making.
- Develop and utilize appropriate financial tools to capture, store, and analyze financial data effectively and efficiently.
- Ensure the accuracy of budgetary information by promoting accountability and ownership among budget owners and facilitating budget monitoring.
- Allocate resources based on the priorities outlined and approved in the annual work plan.
- Administer institutional and donor audits in accordance with established guidelines.

**Purpose for the Assignment:**

ADPC is seeking a Finance and Accounting Assistant under a consultant contract to support its financial operations as the organization adopts International Public Sector Accounting Standards (IPSAS) from 1 January 2027. The assignment will focus on reviewing supporting documents, assisting with payment processing, preparing accounting entries, and maintaining financial records. The Assistant will help ensure timely and accurate transaction processing, contributing to the Finance Unit’s capacity to meet new accounting and reporting requirement.

**Expected Outputs:**

The Accounting Assistant will provide support throughout the assignment in reviewing financial documents, assisting with payment processing, and preparing accounting entries and supporting records. Tasks will be assigned by the supervisor according to the Finance Unit’s operational needs and accounting and reporting requirements.

This position will be based in Headquarters in Bangkok, Thailand.

Note:

*It is not the intent of this Terms of Reference to cover every aspect of the position requirements, rather to highlight the most important areas of personal and joint responsibilities.*

**Responsibilities and Tasks:**

Under the supervision of the designated Finance supervisor, the Accounting Assistant will perform the following tasks :

**Document examination**

- Review payment and advance requests to ensure they are properly authorized, fully supported with required documentation, and in compliance with ADPC policies and procedures.
- Review liquidation of cash advance to ensure that reported expenditures are adequately supported and comply with established policies and procedures.
- Follow up with relevant staff on missing documents, discrepancies, and outstanding liquidations, and notify them by email of the completion of liquidations and the corresponding settlement amounts
- Ensure that project codes, activity codes, and account codes are accurate and consistent with the nature and purpose of each transaction
- Calculate withholding tax on payment to vendor, supplier, consultant as applicable, as per Thai Revenue Code.

**Payment Processing Support**

- Ensure that all payment requests are processed within the required deadlines.

**Accounting**

- Prepare accounting entries for review, ensuring accuracy, completeness, and consistency with ADPC’s accounting policies
- Maintain supporting records in an orderly manner and compile transaction information for financial reporting and audit purposes

**Others**

- Perform any other related duties and responsibilities as may be assigned by the supervisor, consistent with the purpose and scope of this assignment

**Corporate Responsibilities**

- Ensure that all duties and responsibilities are carried out with a commitment to gender equality, diversity, social inclusion.
- Create a working environment at ADPC and ensure the protection and safety of all beneficiaries in accordance with ADPC’s PSEA and child protection policies.
- Contribute to environmentally sustainable practices, minimize waste, and ensure do no harm to people or the environment is observed.
- Ensure fraud is prevented, detected and dealt with promptly in their area of work. Be responsible for safeguarding resources entrusted to ADPC and for upholding and protecting its reputation.

**Working Principles:** The consultant will work in close collaboration with the Finance and Accounting Unit. The role requires adherence to accounting policies and key operational guidelines to ensure smooth workflow and compliance with ADPC policies.

**Qualifications:** The candidate should hold:

**Required Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree, preferable in accounting, finance, business or related field.
- Fresh graduates are encouraged to apply. Working/Internship experience in finance and accounting, particularly within an international non-profit or non-governmental organization, would be an advantage.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel, MS Office applications, and Google Sheet. Experience in accounting software (preferable SUN systems) and database would be advantage. Knowledge on basic accounting principles and practices, familiar with international Accounting Standards would be an advantage.
- Knowledge on relevant tax laws and regulations would be an advantage.
- Attention to detail with excellent organizational skills.
- Good command of English, both written and spoken.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Excellent interpersonal skills
- Ability to work in a team and across teams, in a multi-cultural environment
- Strong motivation, desire to learn; undertake new challenges
- Self-confidence, commitment and willingness to work hard
- Ensure confidentiality in all sensitive information

**Duty Station:** ADPC Bangkok office, Thailand

**Duration:** Twelve months consultancy contract January – December 2027

**Itinerary:** N/A

**Condition of payment:**

The payment will be based on a monthly basis, supplemented with a monthly timesheet submitted and approved by designated supervisor.

jobs.title: Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager
jobs.description:
**Description**

The **Pacific Community** (SPC) is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our unique organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health surveillance, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Fisheries, Aquaculture and Marine Ecosystems (FAME)** division is composed of three programmes: the Coastal Fisheries and Aquaculture Programme (CFAP); the Oceanic Fisheries Programme (OFP); and the Marine Ecosystems Programme (MEP). The Director’s Office provides implementation support and strategic direction across the three programmes and cross-cutting projects. Working with all 22 PICTs, SPC FAME has strong partnerships with regional, sub-regional and national entities working in the marine sector. SPC FAME staff are based in New Caledonia, Fiji, Federated States of Micronesia, Solomon Islands, and Tonga, with most of the staff being based in New Caledonia.

The **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** will provide strategic and technical expertise in the design, development, governance, and deployment of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data systems, including databases, digital platforms, and AI-enabled solutions. Support evidence-based management and strengthen capacity across Pacific Island countries through innovative, standardised, and sustainable data systems.

The key responsibilities of the role include the following:

**Develop and maintain high-quality regional and national coastal fisheries and aquaculture databases and information systems and provide training in their use**

- Develops, maintains and updates the regional coastal fisheries (science, management and development) and aquaculture databases including training in the use of databases, data extraction and analysis
- Develops new web and mobile applications for the regional and national databases in line with country needs and the needs of the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff
- Develops and assists in maintaining national databases based on the regional databases and additional modules.
- Develops specific queries for data extraction and analysis as required by countries or the coastal fisheries and aquaculture programme staff.
- Promotes and encourages the use of standard databases and information systems across the region for coastal fisheries and aquaculture data, and countries to providing the data they collect for back-up and storage at SPC.
- Identifies and develops linkages between the coastal fisheries and oceanic fisheries databases in collaboration with oceanic fisheries statistics and data collection section.
- Identifies ways to better use GIS and remote sensing products in relation to the analysis of coastal fisheries and aquaculture data.

**Practical assistance to members in the designing and targeting of appropriate awareness raising and educational information**

- Develops training materials on data entry, cleaning and extraction.
- Assists with developing and maintaining the website for the CFAP with the Information Unit to assist with the dissemination of information in general.
- Provides input to awareness raising and educational materials focused on coastal fisheries science and/or management or livelihoods and aquaculture

**Develop Artificial Intelligence based tools and models for data collection**

- Improves coastal fisheries and aquaculture data collection using photos and videos automatically processed by computer vision and artificial intelligence
- Develops and trains models to calibrate and reproject pictures for measurement from picture
- Develops and trains models to automate measurements of fishes and invertebrates for the various types of measurements
- Develops and trains models for species identification

**Promote inter-agency networking and cross-sectoral collaboration in coastal fisheries and aquaculture**

- Develops links with other CROP agencies and NGOs in regard to database needs and design for coastal fisheries and aquaculture
- Advocates at global forums on behalf of the Pacific region sectoral interests
- Develops and promotes collaborations within the CFAP on issues such as food security, small-scale livelihoods, climate change adaptation, etc.
- Works closely with other sections of CFAP to ensure smooth implementation of projects.

**Administration and communication**

- Assists the CFAP Deputy Director and Section heads, to include information and database needs in the annual work plans and work plan reports for each Section, consistent with the strategic plan.
- Maintains up to date corporate and administrative procedures for all activities undertaken.
- Contributes where applicable to Programme, Divisional and Corporate publications, such as Fisheries Newsletters, annual reports, and Divisional reports for CRGA.
- Produces reports for all activities undertaken in the appropriate format for the activity including technical reports and trip reports, and input to funding proposals, donor reports.
- Manage, develop and train direct report.
- Fills in for senior staff when they are on leave or duty travel, when required

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

**Key selection criteria**

**Qualifications**

- Master’s in computer science, database development or a related field/discipline or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 12 years’ of demonstrated experience in database management, project management and software development associated with the successful implementation of medium- to large-scale web and desktop application systems.
- At least 8 years’ of demonstrated experience in the use of Microsoft products, both as a user and developer, in particular, (i) experience in software engineering, (ii) programming in client-server environments in C# with MS Visual Studio, (iii) ASP.NET Core and single page web applications with MS Visual Studio (C#, JavaScript and angularjs), (iv) database technologies (preferably SQL Server) and other database formats, (v) development of mobile application in C# (.NET MAUI).
- Demonstrated experience with (i) producing system and user manual documentation, (ii) user training and (iii) ongoing technical support for deployed applications.
- Demonstrated problem solving skills, detail orientation, and ability to multi-task.

**Language skills**

- Excellent communication skills (oral and written).

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Excellent interpersonal skills, ability to work in team as well as undertake unsupervised work, and negotiate with people from different ethnic, cultural and educational backgrounds.
- Willingness to travel and undertake overseas assignments in SPC member countries.

**Salary, terms and conditions**

**Contract Duration** – This contract is budgeted for 3 years and is subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – the **Coastal Fisheries Information and Database Manager** is a band 12 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of SDR (special drawing rights) 5,012-6,169 per month, which converts to approximately XPF 723,251-890,185 (USD 6,717-8,267; EUR 6,061-7,460). SPC salaries are not presently subject to income tax in New Caledonia. An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews.

**Benefits for Staff in a position advertised internationally (EPAI) whose duty station is Noumea** – SPC provides housing support in Noumea. Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Languages** – SPC’s working languages are English and French.

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilinguism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will begiven to the **Pacific Islander**. Applicants will be assured of complete confidentiality in line with SPC’s private policy.

jobs.title: Adviser – Human Rights and Social Development
jobs.description:
## Description

The **Pacific Community (SPC)** is the principal scientific and technical organisation in the Pacific region, supporting development since 1947. We are an international development organisation owned and governed by our 27 country and territory members. In pursuit of sustainable development to benefit Pacific people, our organisation works across more than 25 sectors. We are known for our knowledge and innovation in such areas as fisheries science, public health, geoscience, and conservation of plant genetic resources for food and agriculture.

The **Human Rights and Social Development Division** has a vision for just, equitable and resilient Pacific societies and it aims to achieve this by advancing human rights, equality and social inclusion for all Pacific people, grounded in cultural values and principles. The work of this Division includes work previously undertaken by the Regional Rights Resource Team (RRRT) in the area of human rights and the Social Development Programme (SDP) in the areas of gender equality and social inclusion, culture and youth development.

In line with its vision, the work of the Division will encompass the following focal areas:

- **Objective 1:** Pacific institutions are strong, transparent, and responsive for upholding and promoting human rights and implementing inclusive, gender sensitive and culturally respectful development.
- **Objective 2:** Pacific Civil Society understand and can advocate for their rights and uphold cultural values.
- **Objective 3:** Pacific culture is protected, preserved, and promoted and culturally relevant and appropriate knowledge and systems are integrated across all work.
- **Objective 4:** All PSC programs and operations are grounded in people centered approaches and consider the rights and cultural values of diverse groups including women, children, youth and persons with disabilities.
- **Objective 5:** HRSD Division teams work collectively, coherently, and efficiently and to a high standard to achieve shared success for Pacific societies.

The role – **Adviser – Human Rights and Social Development** will provide technical advice, assistance and capacity building under the HRSD work programme. As the role requires working across the objectives of the HRSD work programme, the Adviser will have a matrix reporting relationship with other Team Leaders in this regard.

The key responsibilities of the role include:

**Provide technical assistance and support on human rights and GESI**

- Support governments and civil society organisations in Pacific Island Countries and Territories (PICTs) to implement and deliver on human rights and GESI commitments, including through human rights mechanisms.
- Support governments and civil society organisations in PICTs to implement and deliver on climate change and human rights priorities, with a particular focus on implementing and progressing the *International Court of Justice Advisory Opinion (ICJAO) on Climate Change and Human Rights.*
- Support Pacific Island Countries in the establishment and strengthening of their National Human Rights Institutions (NHRIs).
- Conduct research, legal and policy analysis on key and emerging regional human rights, gender and social inclusion issues in line with PICTs’ priorities.

**Human rights and GESI capacities and skills development**

- Identify needs for development of capacities and skills for PICTs and other stakeholders.
- Develop and deliver capacity building on human rights and GESI through multiple modalities.
- Develop and deliver capacity building material on Climate Change, Environment and Human Rights.
- Support capacity strengthening needs of PICTs to engage with human rights mechanisms.

**Stakeholder engagement, networking and coordination**

- Support stakeholder engagement, networking and coordination to advance divisional objectives at national, regional and institutional levels.
- Engage in working groups, task forces and other technical committees.
- Represent SPC at national, regional and international forums as delegated by the Director.

**Project management and people management**

- Manage and report on the delivery of projects, programmes and activities.
- Collaborate with in country staff to develop implement, monitor and report against project, programmes and activities work plans and budgets.
- Manage the leave approvals, management plans and performance appraisals of Country Focal Officers (CFOs) as required.
- Collaborate with CFOs and in country focal points to develop, implement, monitor and report against CFOs’ work plans and budgets.

For a more detailed account of the key responsibilities, please **refer to the online job description**.

## Key selection criteria

**Qualifications**

- A postgraduate qualification in development, human rights, law, gender, international relations or other relevant social science from a recognised university or equivalent work experience or equivalent body of knowledge and experience.

**Technical expertise**

- At least 7 years of development experience in human rights, gender equality and social inclusion, and/or youth development, including at least 5 years of experience working in the Pacific.
- Proven track record in quality programming, including developing, delivering and reporting against work plans.
- Experience in developing capacity building resources and delivering sessions to diverse government and non-government audiences.
- Practical experience and understanding of the nexus between climate change, the environment and human rights, including relevant Pacific and international convenings.

**Language skills**

- Excellent English communication skills (oral and written) with a working knowledge of French being an advantage.

**Interpersonal skills and cultural awareness**

- Ability to work in a multicultural, inclusive and equitable environment.

## Salary, terms and conditions

**Contract Duration** – **3 years** – subject to renewal depending on funding and performance.

**Remuneration** – The **Adviser – Human Rights and Social Development** is a band 11 position in SPC’s 2026 salary scale, with a starting salary range of 3,245‒4,057 SDR (special drawing rights) per month, which currently converts to approximately FJD 10,028–12,535 (USD 4,349–5,436; EUR 3,924–4,905). An offer of appointment for an initial contract will normally be made in the lower half of this range, with due consideration given to experience and qualifications. Progression within the salary scale will be based on annual performance reviews. Remuneration of expatriate SPC staff members is not subject to income tax in Fiji; Fiji nationals employed by SPC in Fiji will be subject to income tax.

Establishment and repatriation grant, removal expenses, airfares, home leave travel, health and life and disability insurances and education allowances are available for eligible employees and their eligible dependents. Employees are entitled to 25 working days of annual leave per annum and other types of leave, and access to SPC’s Provident Fund (contributing 8% of salary, to which SPC adds a 10% contribution).

**Recruitment principles** – SPC’s recruitment is based on merit and fairness, and candidates are competing in a selection process that is fair, transparent and non-discriminatory. SPC is an **equal-opportunity employer**, and is committed to cultural and gender diversity, including bilingualism, and will seek to attract and appoint candidates who respect these values. Due attention is given to gender equity and the maintenance of strong representation from Pacific Island professionals. If two interviewed candidates are ranked equal by the selection panel, preference will be given to the **Pacific Islander**. jobs.title: Press Attaché & Senior Advisor to the Judicial Communication Unit
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/211**
- **Position Title**: Press Attaché & Senior Advisor to the Judicial Communication Unit
- **Duty Station:** Beirut.
- **Duration:** 6 months (without exceeding 12 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 01 November 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 08 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link:

[https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a90xr5GZdIL87Ql2u97GNfjeoHI4DLsh/view?usp=sharing](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a90xr5GZdIL87Ql2u97GNfjeoHI4DLsh/view?usp=sharing)

**BACKGROUND**

In line with the strategic objective of enhancing the transparency, efficiency, and public accessibility of judicial institutions in Lebanon, efforts are underway to establish a permanent, professionally staffed Communication and Media capacity specifically serving the Higher Judicial Council (HJC).

The Lebanese judiciary operates in a highly complex, fast-paced, and politically sensitive environment where the absence of structured institutional communication has frequently eroded public trust, compromised the authority of judicial decisions, and allowed misinformation to destabilize the perception of justice. Establishing a professional, proactive media presence is not merely an administrative addition, but a core requirement for safeguarding judicial independence, upholding procedural confidentiality, and positioning the HJC as a transparent and trusted institution.

UNDP is seeking a Press Attaché & Senior Advisor to the Judicial Communication Unit to support the President and members of the Higher Judicial Council in managing external media relations, developing proactive communication strategies, mitigating media crises, and rolling out strategic public trust initiatives.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the overall guidance of the UNDP Rule of Law and Governance Chief Technical Advisor and in close coordination with the Higher Judicial Council and designated Spokesperson Judges, the Consultant will manage day-to-day media operations and strategic communications. All duties must be performed while strictly respecting judicial independence, procedural confidentiality, and the sensitivity of court cases.

The role is structured around four primary operational and strategic pillars:

**2.1. Strategic Support to the establishment of the Judicial Communication Unit**

- Establish and operationalize the HJC Judicial Communication Unit (structure, workflows, and coordination protocols with spokesperson judges and external media).

**2.2. Strategic Communication & Proactive Media Planning**

- Develop a general media communication approach for the HJC in line with Council priorities and key judicial milestones.
- Identify key media messages and adapt complex legal/judicial rulings into accessible, concise language for dissemination to journalists and civil society.

**2.3. Media Relations and Press Operations:**

**BACKGROUND**

In line with strategic initiatives to enhance the transparency, efficiency, public accessibility, and independence of judicial institutions in Lebanon, UNDP provides multi-faceted support to the Higher Judicial Council (HJC). In a complex institutional and media environment, providing accurate, timely, and accessible information is essential for building public trust, safeguarding judicial authority, and combating misinformation. The modernization of the HJC’s digital presence, centered around its official website and complemented by strategic social media channels, serves as the primary public gateway for judicial decisions, official announcements, news, and institutional updates.

To ensure that the HJC’s digital platforms are regularly updated and visually engaging, UNDP is seeking a Digital Communications & Media Officer. The Consultant will be responsible for managing web content, producing digital media (graphics, photo, and video), and regulating online communications to strengthen the Council’s public outreach and transparency.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the overall guidance of the UNDP Rule of Law and Governance Chief Technical Advisor and in close coordination with the designated HJC focal point, the Consultant will manage, create, and regulate content across all official HJC digital platforms, while strictly adhering to judicial communication standards, procedural confidentiality, and data protection rules.
