jobs.title: Digital Transformation and IT Officer and Junior Civil Engineer – Infrastructure Coordination
jobs.description:
**POSITION INFORMATION**

- **Organization:** UNDP Lebanon Through Stars Orbit Consultants and Management Development
- **VA No.: UNDP/LBN/VA26/209**
- **Position Title**: Digital Transformation and IT Officer and Junior Civil Engineer – Infrastructure Coordination
- **Number of Positions:** 2 (one consultant per position)
- **Duty Station:** Beirut
- **Duration:** 3 months each consultant (without exceeding 18 working days per month)
- **Vacancy Date of Issue: 01 November 2026**
- **Vacancy Closure Date: 08 November 2026**
- **National or International consultancy:** National consultancy

To review the full Terms of Reference (TOR), please follow link: [https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eR_CEeQQTBFs-Hk5sKba0YS_bSjKqsGo/view?usp=drive_link](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eR_CEeQQTBFs-Hk5sKba0YS_bSjKqsGo/view?usp=drive_link)

**BACKGROUND**

For over six years, Lebanon has been facing a prolonged economic, financial, and social crisis. The country experienced multiple shocks, including economic and financial collapse, the COVID-19 pandemic, the Beirut Port explosion, and, most recently, more than a year-long armed conflict that caused extensive damage and losses. These developments led to a severe economic contraction, depreciation of the Lebanese Pound, soaring inflation, fiscal imbalances, and a sharp decline in the real value of income, particularly affecting public sector employees. As a result, state institutions have been struggling to deliver on their mandates due to lack of financial resources and a significant loss of skilled professionals in the public sector. Against this backdrop, the capacity for evidence-based policymaking, regulation, and the delivery of priorities has been severely constrained by the crises.

The state continues to face major resource and capacity constraints in responding to the crisis, supporting post-conflict recovery, and addressing structural challenges. At the same time, there is limited visibility over development aid directed to Lebanon. Since the 2019 collapse, most donors have made funding conditional on broad reforms and progress toward an IMF agreement. As a result, only a small share of aid has been channeled through government systems. Most grants and loans remain off-budget, creating a disconnect between aid inflows and national public finance management.

The Ministry of Public Works and Transport (MoPWT) is one of Lebanon’s key line ministries, with a mandate covering roads and public buildings, land and maritime transport, civil aviation and urban planning. Through its General Directorates, the Ministry plays a central role in planning, implementing and overseeing public infrastructure, regulating the transport sector and managing major national assets such as ports, airports and the road network.

Over recent years, the Ministry has operated under exceptionally difficult conditions. The prolonged economic and financial crisis, the Beirut Port explosion and the impact of recent hostilities have placed significant pressure on the country’s infrastructure and on the Ministry’s institutional capacities, while at the same time increasing the volume and complexity of rehabilitation, reconstruction and modernization needs. The Ministry is also increasingly engaged with development partners, international financial institutions and bilateral donors in the preparation and follow-up of infrastructure and transport programmes.

In this context, the Office of the Minister requires dedicated support to strengthen its capacity to lead policy and institutional reform, coordinate with development partners, advance the digital transformation of its work, and monitor infrastructure programmes in close coordination with the Ministry’s technical Directorates. The Minister’s Office, however, continues to face significant staffing shortages, particularly in specialized policy, digital and technical functions.

Based on the Ministry’s needs and priorities, UNDP is seeking to contract a support team of two (2) junior professionals to work directly under the Office of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, as follows:

- Position 1: Digital Transformation and IT Officer — 1 consultant.
- Position 2: Junior Civil Engineer – Infrastructure Coordination — 1 consultant.

**SCOPE OF WORK, RESPONSIBILITIES AND DESCRIPTION OF THE PROPOSED ANALYTICAL WORK**

Under the general supervision of the UNDP Senior Economist and LPARD-P Project manager, and in close coordination with the Office of the Minister of Public Works and Transport, the support team will work directly under the Minister’s Office to support policy, institutional development, international cooperation, digital transformation and infrastructure coordination functions. Each consultant will be responsible for the tasks outlined under their respective position below.

**Position 1: Digital Transformation and IT Officer**

Purpose: Support the digital transformation of the Minister’s Office and provide technical support for programme management, data and information systems.

**Task 1: Databases, Dashboards and Monitoring Tools**

- Develop and maintain programme and project databases for the Minister’s Office.
- Design dashboards and monitoring tools to track programmes, projects, correspondence and follow-up actions.
- Ensure the accuracy, consistency and regular updating of data, and produce periodic data summaries and reports as requested.

**Task 2: Digital Document Management and Digitalization**

- Support the set-up and operation of digital document management and filing systems within the Minister’s Office.
- Assist the Ministry’s Directorates with digitalization initiatives, including the mapping and automation of administrative workflows.
- Test digital tools and workflows before roll-out, document issues and follow up on their resolution.

**Task 3: IT Support and Cybersecurity**

- Provide day-to-day IT support to the Minister’s Office, including troubleshooting of hardware, software and connectivity issues.
- Promote cybersecurity good practices, including access management, data protection and safe use of digital tools.
- Prepare simple user guidance and provide basic training to staff on the tools introduced.
- Perform other related duties as required by the Minister’s Office.

**Position 2: Junior Civil Engineer – Infrastructure Coordination**

Purpose: Provide technical engineering support to the Minister’s Office in monitoring infrastructure programmes and coordinating with the Ministry’s technical Directorates.

**Task 1: Technical Review**

- Review technical reports, engineering drawings, bills of quantities and project documentation submitted to the Minister’s Office.
- Assist in reviewing feasibility studies and donor-funded infrastructure projects, and flag technical issues for the attention of the Minister’s Office.

**Task 2: Infrastructure Monitoring and Coordination**

- Monitor the progress of infrastructure projects and programmes, including through site visits when required, and maintain a project tracking overview.
- Support coordination between the Ministry’s technical Directorates and follow up on pending technical matters.
- Use GIS and project management tools, where relevant, to map and track infrastructure projects.

**Task 3: Engineering Briefs and Reporting**

- Prepare engineering briefs, technical notes and presentations for the Minister’s Office.
- Prepare progress and close-out summaries ensuring accuracy and quality of technical documentation.
- Perform other related duties as required by the Minister’s Office.

**EXPECTED OUTPUTS AND DELIVERABLES**

Each Consultant is expected to complete the above tasks and activities under their respective position, noting that the total duration should not exceed 3 months (without exceeding 18 working days per month). On a monthly basis, each Consultant shall submit:

- A monthly timesheet, endorsed by the Minister’s Office; and
- A brief monthly progress report summarizing the tasks undertaken and outputs produced (e.g. briefs, reports, databases/dashboards, technical notes) during the month.

**INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS**

- With day-to-day management by the Minister of Public Works and Transport and/or the Minister’s Office (Chief of Staff or designated focal point).
- UNDP will be responsible for providing the contractor with all necessary materials related to the project in a timely, thorough and transparent manner. UNDP will also be responsible to provide clarifications and facilitation of the work.
- Day-to-day transportation from home to office (and vice versa) shall be covered by the Consultant’s own means. The Consultant will rely on his/her own means of communication and transportation.

**DURATION OF WORK**

The assigned duration for this consultancy is 3 months per consultant without exceeding 18 working days a month.

The mission of each consultant is expected to commence immediately after contract signature, and to be completed by end of December 2026.

The time needed to review/comment/approve deliverables and outputs is (5) five working days.

**DUTY STATION**

The Consultants will be based in Beirut, at the premises of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport, working directly within the Office of the Minister.

**STANDARD MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS**

**Position 1: Digital Transformation and IT Officer**

- **Education:** A Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical and Computer Engineering, Information Technology, Information Systems, Data Science or a related field.
- **Experience:** A minimum of 1 year of experience in software development, software testing/quality assurance, data management, IT systems or technical support (internships and project-based assignments are considered).

**Position 2: Junior Civil Engineer – Infrastructure Coordination**

- **Education:** A Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering.
- **Experience:** A minimum of 2 years of experience in engineering, including but not limited to technical quality assurance/control, engineering design and drafting, quantity take-off and bills of quantities, site inspection and construction progress follow-up, and technical documentation.
- **Language for both positions:** Fluent in Arabic and English.

**“The Personnel will be covered with Health insurance and Personal accident insurance; the fees shall be deducted from personnel's monthly payment”.**

jobs.title: Finance & HR Manager
jobs.description:
**MSF is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. We are a non-profit, self-governed worldwide movement of more than 63,000 people.**

**We provide emergency medical assistance during armed conflict, natural disasters, outbreaks of deadly diseases and assist those who are excluded from healthcare. MSF delivers care based on need and when we see injustice, we speak out. We are an organization that remains impartial, knowledgeable, and effective, and this is what makes the difference between life and death.**

**People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect.**

**Finance & HR Manager - Country Programmes**

**French speaker**

**Based in country programmes of MSF-OCA**

The Fin/HR Manager is responsible for the implementation of Human Resources policies in the project and the Administrative Management of all staff working in the project (including those recruited locally and internationally), along with the proper implementation of financial administration, management and control in the project.

This job description provides a framework for the main responsibilities and primary activities of the position, it is not all-encompassing. Therefore, the responsibilities and activities of the position may differ from those described in this job description due to organizational and operational needs.

**Objectives and responsibilities of the position**

- In close coordination with the Project Coordinator and the HR Coordinator, calculate the HR operational needs and the associated budget to efficiently ensure the project's required sizing and capabilities and facilitate budget follow-up.
- Plan, supervise and ensure the implementation of the staffing processes (including recruitment, training, briefing, induction, evaluation, development and communication) of the project staff, in close coordination with the HRCo.
- Take ownership of recruitment processes by ensuring effective hiring practices, integrating safeguarding measures at every stage, and strengthening staff capabilities, engagement, contribution to mission objectives, and commitment to MSF values.
- Supervise, coach and develop the Finance and HR team, ensuring appropriate delegation, performance follow-up and capacity building.
- Advise on set-up and updating the project's organizational chart and job descriptions and assisting the Project Coordinator, and/or team leaders and supervisors to draw up annual holiday planning and staff shifts in order to forecast HR needs and to ensure HR availability for the project activities.
- Ensure hiring, carry out amendments and contract termination formalities for employees at project level, according to labour local laws, managing individual employee files, informing them on their rights and preparing all mandatory tax declarations, in order to ensure legal compliance of the project activities.
- Supervise/perform payroll procedures, ensuring correct entry of all data related to monthly salary calculation of employees of the project.
- In close collaboration with the Project Coordinator and HRCo, look for options to avoid/solve possible labour conflicts in the project.
- Is responsible for all movements and/or accommodation of staff in the project.
- Ensure that MSF staff who have financial responsibilities are aware of and comply with local finance procedures, including those related to security.
- Ensure that project finance activities are carried out in line with OCA and mission finance policies & procedures, for example cash & safe management, advances management, authorizations (expenses and payments), payments (cash, bank & cheque), cash flow management, etc.
- Is responsible for assessing and suggesting mitigation measures of the financial risks of the project.
- Ensure that reliable internal control systems are in place, and financial ethics are respected within the project.
- Ensure proper and timely day-to-day bookkeeping takes place in the accounting software per MSF OCA Chart of accounts
- Ensure proper bookkeeping support documentation (hardcopy invoices/receipts, PO/PL/contract as applicable) is available for each bookkeeping entry.
- Ensure that daily and monthly bookkeeping closure takes place in line with the standard procedure, with due quality and on time.
- Support Project Coordinator and the Finance Coordinator with budgeting and monthly budget control activities, in order to ensure that funds are used in line with last approved budgets.

**Requirements**

- A degree in finance, management (business, HR) or administration is desirable.
- Essential working experience of at least five years in relevant and similar jobs.
- MSF or other NGO experience is desirable.
- Working proficiency in English and French (minimum B2 or equivalent) are required.
- Computer literacy (word, excel, internet) is essential.
- Knowledge of HR and Financial (MSF) software or willingness to learn.
- Availability for project durations of 6-9-12 months depending on operational needs.
- Willingness and ability to work in high insecurity zones and emergency responses.

**Assets**

- A good command of Arabic and/or Spanish language.

**Information and Application**

If you recognise yourself in this profile and meet the requirements, we encourage you to apply directly via the Apply button on this page and upload the following documents:

- Your most recent CV (in English) not exceeding 3 pages
- A cover letter explaining your motivation to work with MSF

***Female candidates who meet the requirements are strongly encouraged to apply.***

If you are interested and would like to have additional information, please contact Recruitment, recruitment@amsterdam.msf.org.

jobs.title: ERL Program Manager
jobs.description:
## General Information

- **Department:** ERL/FSL Program
- **Job Title:** ERL Program Manager
- **Duty Station**: Aleppo

### Overview of Bonyan Organization

Bonyan is an independent non-profit organization established in 2004 in Aleppo, Syria, and officially licensed in Turkey in 2014. Our response program focuses on three main areas: **Education, Protection, and Livelihoods**.

### Vision

We envision a developed and responsible population capable of contributing to the rebirth of Syrian society and the development of its civilization.

### Mission

To improve the quality of education and instill core values that contribute to the rise of Syrian society.

### Our Values

- Proficiency
- Initiative
- Welfare
- Abundance

## Job Purpose

Under the direct supervision of the Head of Programs, the Early Recovery Program Manager will be responsible for the successful strategic planning, implementation, and overall oversight of all Early Recovery projects within Bonyan's operations. This includes projects focused on shelter, livelihoods, and critical infrastructure that contribute to early recovery.

The role involves managing the program team, ensuring proper integration and achievement of projects in line with organizational strategies, and collaborating closely with other departments to ensure all activities are properly executed. The Program Manager will also play a crucial role in leading business development activities, representing Bonyan in coordination meetings with donors and other relevant bodies, and ensuring financial sustainability and compliance of the program.

## Duties and Responsibilities

**I. Program Management & Leadership:**

- Lead the development of a comprehensive work plan for the implementation of the Early Recovery program.
- Drive strategy development and articulate the vision for the Early Recovery program within Bonyan's broader strategic framework.
- Oversee the successful implementation and monitoring of all Early Recovery program projects, ensuring adherence to project timelines, objectives, and quality standards.
- Lead monthly program follow-ups, including active participation in grant management meetings, thorough review of procurement plans, analysis of budget forecasts, and assessment of progress against contractual indicators.
- Lead the financial management of the Early Recovery programs, encompassing comprehensive budget development, meticulous expenditure, tracking, and rigorous adherence to donor financial regulations and Bonyan's internal policies. This includes identifying needs for budget revisions and proactively working to secure funding for project sustainability.
- Directly manage and supervise program staff, which includes preparing and monitoring staff performance plans, developing tailored training plans for staff capacity building, and providing constructive feedback.
- Provide technical management, support, and expert advice to staff and project managers who implement Early Recovery activities.
- Develop and conduct necessary training sessions for both Bonyan staff and partner organizations to enhance program delivery.
- Supervise, motivate, and mentor the staff under their responsibility, ensuring clarity of objectives and strong team performance.
- Conduct initial data analysis and prepare early drafts of reports for surveys and studies conducted as part of the program.
- In collaboration with the related department, participate in developing comprehensive program plans, including detailed Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) frameworks, recruitment plans, procurement schedules, and accurate budget forecasts.
- Represent Bonyan in Clusters, technical working groups, and donors’ meetings.

**II. Strategic Development & External Relations:**

- Oversee the planning and achievement of business development activities related to the Early Recovery program, identifying new opportunities and partnerships.
- Represent Bonyan professionally in coordination meetings, relevant program meetings, and engagements with donors and other coordination bodies.
- Build and maintain strong relationships with key stakeholders, including local authorities, community leaders, NGOs, and UN agencies.
- Contribute to the development of concept notes and proposals to secure new funding for Early Recovery initiatives.

**III. Capacity Building & Quality Assurance:**

- Ensure that all ERL projects are implemented in strict alignment with Bonyan's policies and comply with all donor regulations and international standards.
- Play a key role in adapting Bonyan's policies to the specific contextual realities of Syria, ensuring they are culturally sensitive and effective.
- Lead initiatives for gathering systematic feedback from beneficiaries and communities to inform program design and adaptation.
- Ensure the planning and implementation of Humanitarian Principles, meticulously ensuring adherence to "Do No Harm" principles and appropriate sensitization across all activities.
- Lead staff capacity development initiatives, including the design and delivery of training programs, assessment tools, and monitoring frameworks related to protection issues.
- Stay continuously updated on new donors’ requirements, trends, legal frameworks, and best practices relevant to the Syrian context, integrating this knowledge into program design and implementation.

## Academic Qualifications, Requirements, and Skills

**Academic Qualifications:**

Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering, Architecture, Urban Planning, Disaster Management, International Development, Humanitarian Studies, or a closely related field.

A Master’s degree in a relevant field is highly preferred.

**Requirements:**

- Minimum of 5 years of progressive professional experience in managing early recovery and livelihood projects, including those related to shelter and critical infrastructure, within a humanitarian or development context.
- Demonstrated ability to represent the organization's image in a professional and effective manner.
- Profound commitment to humanitarian relief standards, Sphere standards, and other relevant international humanitarian principles.
- Strong understanding of early recovery principles, durable solutions, and humanitarian-development-peace nexus (HDPN) approaches.
- PMP (Project Management Professional) certification or equivalent project management qualification is highly preferred.
- Proven ability to engage effectively with donors and meticulously review narrative and financial reports.
- Prior experience working in Syria or similar complex humanitarian contexts is a significant advantage.

**Skills:**

- Communication: Excellent interpersonal skills, highly effective verbal and written communication, and comprehensive report writing skills.
- Management: High managerial skills, including strong remote management capabilities, and a proven ability to build, lead, and motivate high-performing teams.
- Financial Acumen: Strong knowledge of financial follow-up matters, budgeting, and financial reporting.
- Problem-Solving: Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to navigate complex challenges and make sound decisions in dynamic environments.
- Teamwork: Strong commitment to teamwork and collaborative approaches.
- Innovation: Innovative mindset and proven ability to work effectively under pressure and tight deadlines.
- Leadership: Strong delegation skills and the ability to empower and develop staff.
- Adaptability: High ability to learn, adapt, and develop in a rapidly changing operation
- Language: Fluency in both Arabic and English (written and spoken) is essential.

## General Principles

Bonyan Organization is committed to the highest standards of integrity and social responsibility, and maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward any form of sexual exploitation, abuse, or child maltreatment. We take all concerns and complaints related to such matters seriously, whether they involve our staff members or individuals associated with the organization. Bonyan is dedicated to safeguarding children and vulnerable adults engaged through our activities by ensuring a safe environment free from any actions or negligence that may expose them to abuse, exploitation, or harm. As part of this commitment, we conduct thorough background checks and reference verifications for all candidates throughout the recruitment process. Bonyan is also committed to gender equality and promoting diversity within its workforce. We strongly encourage qualified women, persons with disabilities, and individuals from underrepresented groups to apply for available opportunities. We believe that achieving the highest standards of competence, capability, and integrity must go hand in hand with fostering diversity and inclusion in the workplace.

jobs.title: Advocacy Advisor Multi Country (Nairobi Based, Open for Kenyans only)
jobs.description:
**Background:**

The humanitarian situation in Somalia and Kenya in 2026 remains among the most severe and protracted, driven by conflict, economic pressures, climate shocks, disease outbreaks, mass displacement, and shrinking humanitarian funding.

Conflict and climate shocks in Somalia fuel internal displacement, placing additional pressure on already overstretched services and humanitarian systems.

NRC works in Somalia to protect the rights of displaced and vulnerable people during crisis and meet immediate humanitarian needs, prevent further displacement, and contribute to durable solutions. Access remains a significant operational challenge due to active conflict, insecurity and bureaucratic impediments, making it difficult for aid organisations to reach those in need. Our programmes primarily include rapid response to emergencies, multipurpose cash assistance, legal protection, education, shelter, and water, sanitation and hygiene. Beyond this, NRC co-leads or supports coordination structures in both countries, including Shelter, CCCM and Protection clusters and the HLP and Durable Solutions Working Groups.

**What you will do:**

The Advocacy Advisor plays a pivotal role in shaping NRC’s policy influence and public positioning in Somalia and Kenya, two of the most complex humanitarian contexts globally. Operating at a senior level, the role leads the design and implementation of advocacy and communications strategies, ensuring coherence with country programme priorities and global standards. It provides expert analysis, develops evidence based advocacy products, and represents NRC in key fora, while also building the capacity of staff and partners to amplify the voices of displaced communities. By bridging operational realities with policy engagement, the Advocacy Advisor ensures NRC’s responses are not only impactful on the ground but also contribute to systemic change at national, regional, and international levels.

General Responsibilities:

1. Identify and coordinate NRC’s advocacy response to prioritised issues both within the country and internationally
2. Develop and implement an impactful advocacy and communications strategy, aligned with the overall country strategy.
3. Develop CO media plan and lines, ensuring risk analyses are made regarding public positions or statements and sign-off procedures are adhered to
4. Line management of communications teams, including development of staff if applicable, budget planning and execution, and other administration
5. Ensure systematic training on advocacy and communication to develop capacity of all relevant staff (within and beyond the advocacy and media department) and ensure compliance with NRC policies, e.g. informed consent, data protection, social media standards

Specific responsibilities:

1. Strategically and ethically raise issues and voices of displaced people in Somalia and Kenya to the attention of decision-makers, duty-bearers, and the public, through both traditional and innovative means
2. Increase accountability of NRC Somalia and Kenya through providing regular and consistent information publicly, about the situations we are responding to and the state of our response (or contributions to coordinated responses)
3. Contribute to Country Office and Area Office problem, protection, and programme analyses and ‘systems thinking’ with a policy lens and a public interest lens, and subsequently promote that relevant policy, advocacy, and communications elements are integrated when designing responses and strategies
4. Coordinate and monitor implementation and impact of NRC Somalia, Kenya, etc. advocacy and media plans and strategies
5. Prepare high quality briefings, reports, press statements, letters, and other communications materials (including visual, digital, and social media) for internal coordination and external use

**Please read the** [**full Job Description**](https://norwegianrefugeecouncil.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/JDsforNRCPeople/IQCTQMUUk7ptS4YRhDoAd2svASLS69XHBdPcOta_N73QWUg?e=cMfDfW) **as the above-mentioned responsibilities are just a snapshot.**

**What you will bring:**

**Generic professional competencies:**

- Post-graduate with minimum five years of relevant experience within the humanitarian field or international media/organisations
- Must have humanitarian advocacy experience and policy management from different contexts.
- Relevant experience in advocacy, communications, media, or humanitarian policy
- Experience working in complex and insecure contexts, preferably in the Horn of Africa
- Strong understanding of humanitarian coordination architecture and donor environments
- Proven experience engaging media and managing sensitive external communications
- Experience producing high-level advocacy products and policy analysis.
- Documented results related to the position’s responsibilities
- High levels of flexibility and creativity
- Documented professional experience of working in or with international media
- Strong managerial and interpersonal skills
- Fluency in English with strong verbal and written communications skills

**Context/ Specific skills, knowledge and experience:**

- Knowledge of international legal and policy processes and instruments relating to displacement, protection, peace/conflict, and humanitarian action
- Cogent communication skills, both written and verbal
- Aptitude to think creatively and boldly, to engage (potentially hostile) protection and access advocacy targets

**What we offer:**

- Duty station: Nairobi **(national contract)**
- Contract: 24 Months (renewable based on funding and performance)
- Travel: *70% of dedicated time to the Somalia country office, including regular visits to Somalia (once every 3 months); 10% dedicated time to the Kenya country office; and 20% travel to other countries in East Africa to be identified.*
- Salary/benefits: grade 9 on NRC’s **national** salary scale
- NRC is an equal opportunities employer. We are committed to diversity without distinction to age, gender, religion, ethnicity, nationality, and physical ability.
- We think outside the box, encourage ideas, and give responsibility to all employees at all levels. You will have many opportunities to be heard and take the initiative.

[Find out more about the benefits of working for NRC](https://www.nrc.no/career/what-we-offer/)

Important information about the application process

- *For Internal candidates: To apply as an internal candidate, log in with your official email or click on Opportunity MarketPlace.*
- When creating your profile, include your full name as given on your passport. Complete all the system-required fields for experience, employment history and education.
- Applicants who do not fill in the required information will not be considered for the role.
- Submit your application and CV in English, taking care to attach your latest CV.
- Applications that do not meet the minimum standards in terms of experience or qualifications will generally not be considered. Unsolicited applications not related to this specific job advertisement will not be considered.
- Mandatory to submit the below when applying:
- **Your most updated English CV and remove all previous outdated CVs.**
- **Your most updated Cover Letter**
- **Applicants should include to their Cover Letter, links to their three most compelling advocacy, media & communications production in their cover letter, ideally one text, one video, one TV/radio interview.**
- **Do not attach certificates or any other documents from the two mentioned above.**
- **Incomplete applications will not be considered.**
- This position is open for national candidates who have the legal right to work in Kenya. NRC will not sponsor visa nor residency permits.
- We receive many applications for each vacant position and so only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
- If you have any questions about this role, please email **esa.recruitment@nrc.no**with the job title as the subject line.

**Why NRC?**

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is an independent humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee. Our 15,000 staff work in crises across 40 countries, providing life-saving and long-term assistance to millions of people every year.

[Watch this short video](https://vimeo.com/736782633) to see NRC in action.

We are looking for people who are passionate about helping refugees and people forced to flee. Are you one of those people? If you are, NRC offers you the opportunity to:

- do demanding and professional work, often in challenging contexts.
- join a work culture that empowers every employee to share ideas and take responsibility.
- be part of a welcoming and supportive community committed to human dignity.
- [Learn more about NRC](https://www.nrc.no/)

## About Us

The Norwegian Refugee Council (NRC) is a global humanitarian organisation helping people forced to flee.

Join us in assisting millions of people in areas where others cannot, tackling some of the world's most dangerous and difficult crises. Bring your skills and dedication to an organisation recognised for providing high quality aid and for defending the rights of refugees and internally displaced people.

At NRC, we give responsibility to employees at all levels and foster professional growth and innovative teams. You can expect a supportive culture and an open dialogue with management. We are committed to diversity, equity and inclusion.

Together, we save lives and rebuild futures.

Safeguarding is central to NRC’s work. We expect all employees to:

• treat everyone with respect and dignity

• contribute to building a safe environment for all

• never engage in any form of exploitation, harassment and specifically sexual exploitation, abuse and sexual harassment (SEAH)

• always report. NRC has a zero-tolerance approach to inaction against exploitation, abuse and SEAH

jobs.title: Policy Consultant -ميسر ورشات العمل المشاورات حول مشروع قانون مراكز التنمية المجتمعية -Damascus
jobs.description:
**Background/IRC Summary:** The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises, helping to restore health, safety, education, economic wellbeing, and power to people devastated by conflict and disaster. Founded in 1933 at the call of Albert Einstein, the IRC is one of the world's largest international humanitarian non-governmental organizations (INGO), at work in more than 40 countries and 29 U.S. cities helping people to survive, reclaim control of their future and strengthen their communities. A force for humanity, IRC employees deliver lasting impact by restoring safety, dignity and hope to millions. If you're a solution-driven, passionate changemaker, come join us in positively impacting the lives of millions of people worldwide for a better future.

**Job Overview/Summary:**

The Workshop Facilitator will prepare and facilitate five regional consultations on the draft Community Development Centers Law in Syria and document the findings. The consultations will bring together government directorates, community representatives, the private sector and civil society organizations to develop recommendations for consideration by the Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour (MoSAL).

The facilitator will use technical materials and consultation questions provided by IRC and MoSAL. IRC will provide technical analysis and recommendations through its country team and relevant technical advisers, coordinated by the Integrated Protection Lead. MoSAL will lead the review of consultation recommendations and revisions to the draft law.

The facilitator will report to the IRC Integrated Protection Lead, with oversight from the Deputy Director of Programs, and coordinate with the designated MoSAL focal point. IRC and MoSAL will confirm the workshop locations and coordinate participant invitations and logistics.

The estimated duration is **22** working days, comprising **3** days for preparation, **15** days for travel, workshop consultation and feedback and validation, and **4** days for consolidated reporting and revisions. This includes 3 working days per location, depending on the itinerary. The final schedule and level of effort will be specified in the contract.

The workshops will be facilitated in Arabic. Reports will be submitted in Arabic, with a concise English executive summary of the final report. The contract will specify coverage of travel and accommodation costs.

**Key Responsibilities**

**Preparation and Consultation Design**

- Review the draft law and technical materials provided by IRC and MoSAL to inform workshop preparation.
- Prepare a workplan covering workshop preparation, travel, delivery and reporting, for approval by IRC in coordination with MoSAL.
- Develop workshop agendas, discussion guides and participatory exercises based on the consultation objectives. Prepare group feedback forms and templates for documenting recommendations during the sessions.
- Incorporate arrangements for the participation of women, persons with disabilities and marginalised groups, including accessible materials and appropriate small-group discussions.

**Workshop Facilitation**

- Facilitate five workshops in Arabic, covering the agreed provisions and consultation questions within the scheduled time.
- Ensure balanced participation across stakeholder groups and facilitate sensitive discussions impartially and respectfully.
- Guide participants in examining the practical implications of draft provisions and formulating recommendations linked to the relevant articles.
- Validate session summaries with participants and document areas of agreement, differing positions and unresolved issues.

**Documentation and Reporting**

- Document each workshop through structured notes and written participant feedback, recording the groups represented, key findings, recommendations and follow-up actions.
- Consolidate participant recommendations in an article-by-article matrix recording the issue, proposed change, rationale, consultation source and differing positions.
- Prepare a consolidated report identifying common priorities, differences between locations and matters requiring further technical review. Attribute participant recommendations, IRC technical inputs and MoSAL decisions accurately.
- Present the findings to IRC and MoSAL and finalise the report and recommendations matrix following one consolidated round of feedback.
- Maintain the confidentiality of consultation records and collect only the personal information required for workshop administration and reporting.

**Coordination and Deliverables**

- Provide progress updates to the IRC Integrated Protection Lead and coordinate workshop requirements with the designated IRC and MoSAL focal points.
- Submit workshop agendas, discussion guides and documentation templates for approval before the consultations begin.
- Deliver five workshop reports, the consolidated consultation report, recommendations matrix and English executive summary in editable formats within the contractual deadlines.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

- University degree in social sciences, public administration, law, development studies or a related field, or equivalent relevant professional experience.
- At least five years of relevant experience in workshop facilitation, stakeholder consultation or participatory dialogue involving government institutions, civil society and communities.
- Familiarity with the Syrian context and experience working with government institutions and community representatives. Experience facilitating legislative consultations is desirable.
- Demonstrated ability to facilitate inclusive discussions impartially, manage differing views, and produce accurate consultation reports and recommendations matrices.
- Understanding of community participation, gender equality, disability inclusion and protection-sensitive consultation approaches.
- Fluency in spoken and written Arabic, with good working English for coordination and preparation of the English executive summary.
- Availability to travel to the consultation locations and complete the assignment within the contracted
- **نبذة عن لجنة الانقاذ الدولية**
- تستجيب **لجنة الانقاذ الدولية** لأشد الأزمات الإنسانية في العالم، وتعمل على استعادة الصحة والسلامة والتعليم والرفاه الاقتصادي والقدرة على اتخاذ القرار للأشخاص المتضررين من النزاعات والكوارث. تأسست المنظمة عام 1933 بدعوة من ألبرت أينشتاين، وتُعد واحدة من أكبر المنظمات الإنسانية الدولية غير الحكومية، حيث تعمل في أكثر من 40 دولة و29 مدينة في الولايات المتحدة، لمساعدة الأفراد على البقاء واستعادة السيطرة على مستقبلهم وتعزيز مجتمعاتهم. ويعمل موظفو المنظمة على تحقيق أثر مستدام من خلال استعادة الأمان والكرامة والأمل لملايين الأشخاص حول العالم**.**
- **ملخص الوظيفة**
- سيتولى **ميسر ورشات العمل** إعداد وتيسير خمس مشاورات إقليمية حول مشروع قانون **مراكز التنمية المجتمعية** في سوريا، بالإضافة إلى توثيق النتائج والمخرجات. وستجمع هذه المشاورات ممثلين عن المديريات الحكومية والمجتمعات المحلية والقطاع الخاص ومنظمات المجتمع المدني بهدف تطوير توصيات تُعرض على **وزارة الشؤون الاجتماعية والعمل** للنظر فيها**.**
- سيعمل الميسر استناداً إلى المواد الفنية والأسئلة الإرشادية المقدمة من اللجنة الدولية للإنقاذ ووزارة الشؤون الاجتماعية والعمل. وستوفر اللجنة التحليل الفني والتوصيات من خلال فريقها القطري ومستشاريها الفنيين المختصين، بإشراف قائد الحماية المتكاملة. وستتولى الوزارة مراجعة توصيات المشاورات وإجراء التعديلات اللازمة على مشروع القانون**.**
- سيكون الميسر مسؤولاً أمام قائد الحماية المتكاملة في اللجنة الدولية للإنقاذ، مع إشراف من نائب مدير البرامج، كما سيقوم بالتنسيق مع نقطة الاتصال المحددة من قبل وزارة الشؤون الاجتماعية والعمل. وستتولى اللجنة والوزارة تحديد مواقع الورشات والتنسيق بشأن دعوات المشاركين والجوانب اللوجستية**.**
- تُقدّر مدة المهمة بـ **22 يوم عمل**، تشمل**:**
- **ثلاثة** للتحضير**.**
- **15** أيام للسفر وتنفيذ الورشات وإعداد تقاريرها الفردية**.**
- **4** ايام لإعداد التقرير الموحد النهائي وإجراء المراجعات**.**
- ويشمل ذلك **ثلاثة أيام** عمل في كل موقع، وفقاً لجدول التنقلات. وسيتم تحديد الجدول النهائي ومستوى الجهد المطلوب في العقد**.**
- ستُنفذ الورشات باللغة العربية، وتُقدَّم التقارير باللغة العربية مع **ملخص تنفيذي موجز باللغة الإنجليزية** للتقرير النهائي. كما سيحدد العقد آلية تغطية تكاليف السفر والإقامة**.**
- **المسؤوليات الرئيسية**
- **أولاً: التحضير وتصميم المشاورات**
- مراجعة مشروع القانون والمواد الفنية المقدمة من اللجنة الدولية للإنقاذ ووزارة الشؤون الاجتماعية والعمل لدعم التحضير للورشات**.**
- إعداد خطة عمل تشمل التحضير والتنقل والتنفيذ والتقارير، والحصول على موافقة اللجنة بالتنسيق مع الوزارة**.**
- إعداد أجندات الورشات وأدلة النقاش والأنشطة التشاركية بما يتوافق مع أهداف المشاورات، وتطوير نماذج التغذية الراجعة وأدوات توثيق التوصيات**.**
- ضمان دمج ترتيبات تيسر مشاركة النساء والأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة والفئات المهمشة، بما في ذلك توفير المواد الميسرة ومجموعات النقاش المناسبة**.**
- **ثانياً: تيسير ورشات العمل**
- تيسير خمس ورشات عمل باللغة العربية وفق البنود المتفق عليها وأسئلة المشاورة ضمن الوقت المحدد**.**
- ضمان مشاركة متوازنة لجميع فئات أصحاب المصلحة وإدارة النقاشات الحساسة بطريقة حيادية ومحترمة**.**
- توجيه المشاركين لدراسة الآثار العملية للمواد المقترحة في مشروع القانون وصياغة توصيات مرتبطة بالمواد ذات الصلة**.**
- مراجعة وتأكيد ملخصات الجلسات مع المشاركين وتوثيق نقاط الاتفاق والخلاف والمسائل غير المحسومة**.**
- **ثالثاً: التوثيق وإعداد التقارير**
- توثيق كل ورشة من خلال ملاحظات منظمة ونماذج التغذية الراجعة المكتوبة، مع تسجيل الجهات المشاركة والنتائج الرئيسية والتوصيات وخطوات المتابعة**.**
- تجميع توصيات المشاركين ضمن مصفوفة منظمة حسب مواد القانون، تتضمن القضية المطروحة والتعديل المقترح ومبرراته ومصدر التوصية والآراء المختلفة**.**
- إعداد تقرير موحد يوضح الأولويات المشتركة والاختلافات بين المناطق والقضايا التي تحتاج إلى مراجعة فنية إضافية، مع التمييز الواضح بين توصيات المشاركين والمدخلات الفنية للجنة الدولية للإنقاذ وقرارات الوزارة**.**
- عرض النتائج على اللجنة الدولية للإنقاذ ووزارة الشؤون الاجتماعية والعمل، واستكمال التقرير النهائي ومصفوفة التوصيات بعد جولة مراجعة موحدة**.**
- الحفاظ على سرية سجلات المشاورات وعدم جمع أي بيانات شخصية غير ضرورية لأغراض إدارة الورشات وإعداد التقارير**.**
- **رابعاً: التنسيق والمخرجات**
- تقديم تحديثات دورية لقائد الحماية المتكاملة في اللجنة الدولية للإنقاذ والتنسيق مع نقاط الاتصال المعتمدة من اللجنة والوزارة**.**
- تقديم أجندات الورشات وأدلة النقاش ونماذج التوثيق للمراجعة والموافقة قبل بدء المشاورات**.**
- تسليم**:**
- خمسة تقارير ورشات عمل**.**
- التقرير الموحد للمشاورات**.**
- مصفوفة التوصيات**.**
- الملخص التنفيذي باللغة الإنجليزية**.**
- وذلك ضمن المهل الزمنية المحددة في العقد وبصيغ قابلة للتحرير**.**
- **المؤهلات والخبرات المطلوبة**
- شهادة جامعية في العلوم الاجتماعية أو الإدارة العامة أو القانون أو دراسات التنمية أو أي مجال ذي صلة، أو خبرة مهنية مكافئة**.**
- خبرة لا تقل عن خمس سنوات في تيسير ورش العمل أو المشاورات مع أصحاب المصلحة أو الحوارات التشاركية التي تشمل المؤسسات الحكومية ومنظمات المجتمع المدني والمجتمعات المحلية**.**
- معرفة جيدة بالسياق السوري وخبرة في العمل مع المؤسسات الحكومية وممثلي المجتمعات المحلية. وتُعد الخبرة في تيسير المشاورات التشريعية ميزة إضافية**.**
- القدرة المثبتة على إدارة الحوارات الشاملة والمحايدة والتعامل مع الآراء المختلفة وإعداد تقارير دقيقة ومصفوفات توصيات واضحة**.**
- فهم جيد لمبادئ المشاركة المجتمعية والمساواة بين الجنسين وإدماج الأشخاص ذوي الإعاقة ومقاربات الحماية الحساسة**.**
- إجادة اللغة العربية كتابةً وتحدثاً، مع مستوى جيد من اللغة الإنجليزية لأغراض التنسيق وإعداد الملخص التنفيذي باللغة الإنجليزية**.**
- الاستعداد للسفر إلى مواقع المشاورات المختلفة وإنجاز المهمة خلال الفترة التعاقدية المحددة**.**

jobs.title: Logistics and Procurement Manager - Kenyan Nationals only
jobs.description:
**Overall Job Purpose**

The Procurement and Logistics Manager is responsible for leading and coordinating procurement and logistics operations across the programme portfolio, ensuring that goods, services and logistical support are delivered in a timely, compliant and cost-effective manner. The postholder provides operational oversight of procurement planning, supplier management, logistics systems, fleet, warehousing, assets and facilities, while ensuring compliance with Johanniter and donor policies and procedures. The position works closely with programme, finance and other support teams and provides guidance and support to logistics staff and relevant colleagues.

**Strategy and Vision**

- Actively supports the values of Johanniter and shapes his/her work according to these values
- Contributes to the development and implementation of the global strategy of Johanniter International Assistance in his/her area of responsibility
- Supports the implementation of the country strategy in his/her area of responsibility in line with the global JIA strategy

**Leadership**

- Actively leads by example, upholding the Johanniter leadership principles and creating a culture where the leadership mindset can emerge and thrive, actively empowering and guiding team members towards an inclusive, accountable work environment
- Supports the development of an organisational culture and leadership that addresses power relations and privilege, promotes diversity and inclusion, encourages continuous self-reflection, embraces change and works towards shared goals
- This is reflected in day-to-day activities in line with the Code of Conduct and related policies to achieve our goals

**Procurement Management**

- Coordinates procurement activities with programme and finance teams and provides procurement input to programme planning and budget development
- Leads the development and implementation of procurement plans in coordination with partners and the programmes team, ensuring alignment with programme timelines and donor compliance requirements
- Maintains accurate procurement trackers and ensures procurement documentation is complete, properly authorised and audit-ready
- Ensures full adherence to organisational and donor procurement policies and regulations and oversees the end-to-end procurement process
- Manages and monitors procurement activities, including bidding, tendering, supplier selection, contracting and supplier performance, ensuring value for money both for Johanniter and with partners
- Develops and maintains supplier databases, conducts market surveys and monitors supplier performance

**Operations and Logistics Management**

- Implements logistics functions in accordance with Johanniter and donor guidelines while ensuring adherence by programme, support and partner staff
- Engages with programme staff to provide timely delivery of logistics support and contributes logistics input to project design and planning
- Ensures the proper management, scheduling, use and maintenance of Johanniter generators and other office equipment, including fuel consumption and monitoring
- Ensures appropriate management of assets, equipment, communication, IT and power systems and that resources are operated in the most cost-efficient manner
- Supports the proper management of offices and ensures repairs and maintenance are completed in a timely manner
- Supports the effective management of communications and other operational equipment and ensures they are available and functional when required
- Manages team transport during field trips which includes booking of vehicles and flights for staff

**Asset and Inventory Management**

- Oversees logistics store rooms ensuring proper record keeping, storage and issuing of items, appropriate storage conditions and security
- Ensures regular physical inventory checks are conducted and discrepancies, impairments or stock deterioration are identified and addressed
- Ensures effective internal controls for asset and inventory management and that assets are properly allocated, labelled, tracked and maintained
- Ensures that the goods, services and works procured are of the right quality, right quantity, right price, delivered to the right place at the right time (5 Rs) and that the appropriate documentation of goods received, stored and dispatched, including relevant waybills and inventory records
- Ensures damaged, obsolete or unusable items are appropriately documented and disposed of in accordance with procedures
- Maintains accurate and up-to-date asset, inventory and warehouse records and ensures they are available for audit purposes

**Procedures, Documentation and Reporting**

- Maintains accurate filing systems with documented and supported records of procurement and logistics transactions for audit purposes, both manually and electronically
- Ensures procurement and logistics procedures, systems and documentation are implemented consistently across the programme
- Compiles monthly logistics reports in accordance with Johanniter policies and procedures
- Follows up on audit findings, compliance gaps and agreed corrective actions relating to procurement and logistics
- Identifies opportunities to improve transparency, efficiency and internal controls within procurement and logistics processes

**Quality Management**

- Promotes the use of Johanniter’s quality management tool Consense and ensures that relevant staff are able to access and use it
- Implements systems to improve transparency and ensures adequate anti-fraud, conflict of interest and ethical procurement procedures are in place
- Carries out regular inspections and spot-checks to ensure the best use of Johanniter assets and resources
- Ensures that procurement and logistics activities effectively support projects in line with donor budgets, guidelines and organisational requirements
- Undertakes field visits to project sites on a regular basis to follow up on the quality of logistics and procurement procedures of partners and / or JUH staff
- Proactively engages with line managers in areas where there are needs for improvement, ensure good coordination and adequate information sharing and address common concerns/ problems with a goal to seek solutions

**People Management**

- Manages staff with integrity and in accordance with HR policies and procedures, ensuring high standards of accountability, professionalism and performance
- Conducts performance management processes, including objective setting, regular reviews and annual appraisals
- Develops and implements measurable staff development plans, including on-the-job learning, mentoring and targeted capacity strengthening
- Promotes knowledge sharing within the team and ensures systematic exchange of technical expertise
- Provides guidance on career development and succession planning to strengthen long-term staff capacity within the function

**Capacity Building**

- Provides guidance and technical support to programme, support and partner staff on procurement and logistics procedures where required
- Leads capacity development activities in procurement and logistics procedures and compliance for field-level staff and relevant colleagues
- Identifies capacity gaps and supports the development of appropriate learning and training activities
- Promotes learning and good practice within the procurement and logistics function and supports consistent application of organisational procedures

**Safety and Security**

- Oversees the implementation of logistics-related safety and security measures in accordance with Johanniter policies and relevant security guidance
- Ensures that vehicles, facilities, equipment and other logistics resources are maintained and used in accordance with applicable safety requirements
- Supports the implementation and updating of logistics aspects of the security plan and ensures resources and facilities are ready for hibernation or evacuation
- Ensures safety and security incidents affecting logistics operations are reported, followed up and addressed through appropriate corrective and preventive actions

**Safeguarding**

- Applies and upholds the organisation’s safeguarding policies and Code of Conduct in daily work, including taking responsibility for immediately reporting concerns related to Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH)
- Applies safeguarding principles in procurement and supplier management processes, ensuring fair and safe practices that prevent exploitation and abuse

**Communication and Representation**

- Represents Johanniter International Assistance in a positive and professional manner, contributing to the continuation of a positive image and overall credibility of the organisation
- Builds and maintains professional relationships with suppliers, service providers and relevant external stakeholders
- Represents Johanniter in relevant coordination meetings and networks, including logistics coordination forums and the Logistics Cluster where appropriate
- Proactively engages with programme, finance and senior management on areas requiring improvement, ensuring good coordination, information sharing and effective solutions

jobs.title: Finance Assistant - Kenyan Nationals only
jobs.description:
**Overall Job Purpose**

The finance assistant manages and records transactions into the SUN field upload template and ensures payments to all suppliers based on invoices generated from Logistics and Administrative Offices. position holder processes all Payment Vouchers, ensuring that all necessary supporting documentation is available, appropriately signed by the relevant authorities, and that all documents are scanned, properly arranged and uploaded to SharePoint.

The position supports the effective management of cash and bank transactions, financial documentation, payment processing and compliance with Johanniter financial procedures and guidelines.

**Strategy and Vision**

- Actively supports the values of Johanniter and shapes his/her work according to these values

**Leadership**

- Actively lives the Johanniter’s leadership principles by fostering trust, embracing diversity, communicating openly, supporting wellbeing, and taking responsibility to contribute to a positive, inclusive, and adaptable work environment
- This is reflected in the day-to-day activities in line with the Code of Conduct and related policies to achieve our goals

**Accounting & Financial Reporting**

- On a daily basis, records transactions in the SUN upload template on a daily basis, ensuring that booking texts conform to organisational financial guidelines and required L-codes are completed
- Maintains the cash and bank books in the specified SUN upload template, ensuring that transactions are accurately and completely recorded
- Ensures that booking text descriptions and L-codes, including project code, JUH and donor budget lines, source of funds, country, partner, person and Fibu code, are correctly allocated
- Ensures the accuracy and completeness of cash and bank books and the proper filing of supporting financial documentation
- Assists with the preparation, scanning and uploading of monthly closing documents to the sharepoint or approved sharing platform after review by the Finance Coordinator
- Provides accurate and timely financial information and documentation to the Senior Finance Officer and other authorised finance staff

**Budgeting & Financial Planning**

- Ensures transactions are recorded against the correct project, budget line, source of funds and other relevant L-codes in accordance with organisational financial guidelines
- Supports the Finance Coordinator and Senior Finance Officer by providing accurate transaction information required for budget monitoring and financial reporting
- Raises any apparent coding or budget allocation issues to the Senior Finance Officer before payment or recording of transactions

**Cash & Treasury Management**

- Responsible for the management of cash/bank books and ensures proper filing of all financial documents
- Ensures the safety of the safe and performs cash counts every friday in the presence of the finance manager and senior finance officer, and files the cash count reports appropriately
- Ensures the accuracy and completeness of cash and bank records
- Ensures the management of cash boxes, including following up advances and maintaining the advances register, physical inventories and expenditure reconciliations
- Assists with banking-related activities and ensures that cash and bank transactions are properly recorded and supported
- Reports any cash or bank discrepancies immediately to the senior finance officer or finance manager
- Ensures cash is handled and stored securely and in accordance with organisational procedures

**Payments & Supplier Management**

- Receives payment requests from Logistics and HR& Admin and prepares Payment Vouchers for submission to the Senior Finance Officer for review and approval by authorised signatories
- Ensures that all payment documentation is properly completed, signed and dated by the relevant authorities before payment is processed
- After approval, releases payments as authorised and records the transactions in the SUN budget/upload template
- Ensures that all receipts are stamped using the Johanniter Approval/Paid stamp and that all invoices and/or receipts are signed by the suppliers
- Ensures that invoices are arranged in chronological order and scanned and filed accordingly in the various files for each cashbook
- Ensures that all bank transfers to suppliers are processed when necessary and assists the Senior Finance Officer with banking-related issues
- Ensures that payments are made only after the required approvals and supporting documentation have been obtained
- Maintains confidentiality and integrity in relation to supplier and payment information

**Financial Compliance & Internal Controls**

- Checks that purchasing procedures are followed and that RFPs, Purchase Authorisations (PA) and Payment Vouchers are systematically signed by authorised persons
- Checks that expenditures are validated by management, taking into consideration all applicable Johanniter validation thresholds
- Checks supporting documents and their conformity for all transactions before payments are made, including requisition forms, quotation analyses, invoices, inventories and other relevant documentation
- Ensures that all financial documents are properly filed and that the filing system is updated, complete and accurate
- Ensures all payment vouchers contain the required supporting documentation before submission for approval
- Ensures financial documents are scanned and uploaded to the approved sharing platform in accordance with established procedures
- Immediately reports any suspected irregularities, fraud, corruption, misuse of funds or other financial concerns to the appropriate supervisor
- Supports internal and external audit processes by ensuring that requested financial documents are properly filed and readily available

**Partner Financial Management & Capacity Building**

- Supports the Finance Coordinator/Senior Finance Officer in maintaining complete and accurate financial documentation relating to partners, where applicable
- Ensures that partner-related financial documents received by the office are properly recorded, filed and made available to authorised finance staff
- Raises any missing or incomplete financial documentation to the Senior Finance Officer/Manager or relevant supervisor

**Team Support & Capacity Building**

- Works closely with the Finance Manager, Senior Finance Officer and other finance staff to ensure the smooth running of finance activities
- Supports colleagues in maintaining proper financial filing and documentation systems
- Participates in finance meetings, trainings and capacity-building activities as required
- Maintains a good team spirit and supports other team members when required, while ensuring that assigned responsibilities are completed accurately and on time

**Administrative Responsibilities**

- Receives, distributes, circulates and files all documents that come into the office
- Distributes documents to other agencies as required
- Maintains proper filing of finance and administrative documents
- Ensures that confidential financial documents are stored securely and that access is limited to authorised personnel
- Performs other finance and administrative duties as assigned by the supervisor

**Safeguarding**

- Applies and upholds the organisation's safeguarding policies and Code of Conduct in daily work, ensuring respectful behaviour and taking responsibility for immediately reporting any concerns related to Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH)
- Maintains confidentiality and integrity in financial processes while raising awareness of safeguarding risks linked to fraud, corruption or misuse of funds
- Ensures that financial transactions and payments are processed transparently, accountably and in accordance with approved procedures
- Immediately reports any concerns relating to fraud, corruption, aid diversion, exploitation, abuse or misuse of organisational resources through the appropriate reporting channels
- Ensures that financial documentation and information relating to beneficiaries, staff, suppliers and other stakeholders are handled confidentially and responsibly

**Safety & Security**

- Complies with organisational safety and security procedures and instructions
- Maintains awareness of safety and security requirements when handling cash, undertaking banking activities or carrying out other finance-related duties
- Ensures cash and financial documents are handled and stored safely and securely
- Immediately reports safety or security concerns, incidents or risks that may affect staff, financial assets or office operations to the appropriate supervisor
- Follows established procedures for safe movement and handling of cash and financial documents

**Person Specification**

**Professional Qualification and Experience**

*Essential:*

- Relevant training from a recognized institution or two (2) years’ work experience in finance, accounting, business administration or relevant discipline in an NGO/ INGO setting
- At least CPA level I qualification
- Experience maintaining financial documentation

*Desirable:*

- Experience working with NGOs or international organizations
- Familiarity with accounting systems or financial templates
- Experience using the SUN System is an advantage

**Skills**

- Professional in Excel and computerised accounting
- Knowledge of the SUN System or any accounting software is essential
- Honest and of high integrity
- Able to multi-task while maintaining a stringent eye on detail
- Excellent interpersonal, communication, negotiation and representation skills
- Accurate and precise work style
- Able to organize, plan ahead and prioritize multiple tasks and meet deadlines
- Flexibility, ability to adapt, good team player, discrete, responsible and innovative
- Fluency in English and Swahili (knowledge of local languages will be an added advantage)

The gross monthly salary for this position ranges from KES 89,000/- to KES 92,000/-. The actual salary offered will be determined based on the successful candidate’s relevant years of professional experience and corresponding placement within the organization’s salary scale.

jobs.title: Partnerships Development Specialist
jobs.description:
## **Job Highlight**

The Partnerships Development Specialist (IICA-2) will support the strengthening of strategic partnerships between the United Nations, International Financial Institutions, the European Union and Government counterparts. The position will contribute to advancing joint programming, identifying investment opportunities and developing innovative financing solutions aligned with national development and peacebuilding priorities, with a focus on conflict prevention, sustainable peacebuilding and evidence-informed decision-making.

## **About the Region**

The UNOPS Global Portfolios Office (GPO) brings together diverse expertise to help partners deliver impact worldwide. With hubs in New York, Geneva, and Vienna, and expert teams operating globally, GPO leads multi-regional initiatives that advance sustainable development, climate action, and peacebuilding - including in some of the world’s most challenging environments. By leveraging our collective expertise and global networks, GPO supports UNOPS’ strategic priorities and the Sustainable Development Goals across more than 130 countries. We work closely with major global partners - including governments, international financial institutions, and UN agencies - to deliver a wide range of services, such as project management, fund management, hosting services, and HR support.

## **About the Country/Multi-Country Office**

UNOPS Development and Special Initiatives team works with UN partners and Member States. This portfolio offers support for various initiatives and priorities of the UN Secretary-General in pursuit of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. Additionally, it helps the UN Secretariat in implementing global programs in areas such as political affairs, climate, counterterrorism and peacebuilding, among others.

## **Job Specific Context**

UNOPS has an agreement with the Peacebuilding and Peace Support Office (PBPSO) to implement the Partnership Facility activities. The Partnership Facility supports strategic collaboration between the United Nations and peace finance ecosystem including International Financial Institutions (IFIs), innovative financing actors, private sector and peace tech partners in crisis-affected settings through dedicated capacities, shared analysis and stronger alignment of planning, financing and programming.

The Central African Republic (CAR) is implementing the Plan National de Developpement (PND 2024-2028) and the PBF-EU-IFI Strategic Results Framework (SRF 2025-2028). The SRF provides a common reference for conflict-sensitive programming, joint monitoring and alignment among the Government, United Nations, IFIs and the European Union.

The project establishes dedicated liaison capacity in the Resident Coordinator Office (RCO) through 31 December 2027 to strengthen operational alignment, joint planning, pipeline development and strategic collaboration among the United Nations, the World Bank, the African Development Bank (AfDB), the IMF, the European Union and Government counterparts. The function is intended to deepen strategic and programmatic collaboration, with particular attention to the World Bank Country Partnership Framework and PRA eligibility process, joint programming and prevention financing in the context of the AfDB 2026-2031 Country Strategy Paper, continued strategic engagement with the European Union, the growing partnership with the IMF, and knowledge generation and evidence-informed decision-making.

The incumbent of the position will be personnel of UNOPS under its full responsibility.

## **Role Purpose**

The assignment will provide strategic partnership, financing and analytical support to translate the SRF into implementable, evidence-informed collaboration with IFIs, European Union and Government counterparts in support of nationally owned peacebuilding priorities. The role will place greater emphasis on upstream partnership development, joint investment design, prevention financing, partner-specific strategic processes and knowledge products, while supporting the continuity of SRF implementation and coordination mechanisms.

The incumbent will work under the UNOPS Senior Programme Manager supervision and within the RCO and PBPSO coordination arrangements established for the project, in close collaboration with the UN Country Team, PBF Secretariat and relevant external partners.

## **Functions / Key Results Expected**

**A. Strategic partnerships and partner-specific engagement**

- Support substantive engagement around the World Bank Country Partnership Framework and contribute analysis and coordination inputs relevant to the PRA eligibility process and prevention priorities.
- Deepen collaboration with AfDB on joint programming, prevention financing, catalytic approaches and collaborative analytical work, identifying concrete entry points for aligned or co-financed initiatives.
- Support the growing partnership with the IMF by preparing analytical inputs, mapping areas of complementarity with peacebuilding priorities, and facilitating relevant technical exchanges.
- Engage Government and partner teams to test interest in specific opportunities and establish the steps needed to advance them.

**B. Joint programming, investment pipelines and financing solutions**

- Map and prioritize investable opportunities emerging from the SRF and PND, including opportunities where PBF resources can catalyze, sequence or complement larger IFI or EU financing.
- Coordinate or substantively contribute to concept notes, investment briefs, terms of reference, joint proposals and programming matrices for aligned or co-financed initiatives.
- Analyze financing options, sequencing, targeting and implementation dependencies and provide recommendations to support conflict-sensitive and gender-responsive investment design.
- Facilitate technical exchanges needed to move priority concepts from identification toward partner review, approval or financing decisions.

**C. Evidence, results and knowledge for partnership decisions**

- Develop and maintain decision-oriented mapping of UN, PBF, IFI, EU and relevant Government investments linked to SRF priorities, including pipeline status and potential complementarities.
- Produce concise analytical and strategic products, including alignment briefs, financing notes, risk and opportunity analyses, pipeline overviews and inputs to joint assessments.
- Support conflict-sensitive and gender-responsive analysis, including attention to populations at risk, women and young people, as relevant to joint programming and investment decisions.
- Document lessons, good practices and recommendations on UN-IFI-EU collaboration and prevention financing and support their dissemination through appropriate country and global knowledge channels.

**D. SRF implementation, coordination and follow-up**

- Facilitate technical and programmatic coordination among the United Nations, IFIs, European Union and Government where this adds value to SRF implementation and partnership decisions.
- Support preparation and follow-up for SRF governance mechanisms, including concise materials, action tracking and partner inputs, in collaboration with the PBF Secretariat.
- Support collection and synthesis of partner information needed to track SRF indicators and connect reported results with active or planned programmes.
