jobs.title: Project Director – CDC Capacity Building for Global, Regional, and National Immunization Programs (Global)
jobs.description:
***About Corus:*** Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. Our more than 800 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world's most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives. Further details about the organization can be found at: [https://corusinternational.org](https://corusinternational.org/)

Today, IMA offers extensive expertise in managing and implementing highly successful and complex donor-funded programs in global health security, vaccine-preventable disease immunization, nutrition, maternal and child health, health systems strengthening (HSS), malaria, HIV/AIDS, and neglected tropical diseases (NTDs). IMA has managed an average of $100 million annually over the last four fiscal years, through grants and contracts from the United States Government (including CDC, DoS, and others), FCDO, World Bank, the Global Fund, UNDP, and private donors.

***About the job:***

IMA World Health, a member of Corus International, is seeking a **Project Director** to lead an anticipated 5-year CDC-funded project titled **- Capacity Building for Global, Regional, and National Immunization Programs**.

The program's goal is to strengthen immunization programs in priority countries so they can better prevent, control, and eliminate/eradicate vaccine-preventable diseases (VPDs) like polio, measles, and rubella, reduce illness and death from these diseases, and respond to emerging global health threats. will build stronger systems in priority countries to prevent, detect, and respond to VPDs. This includes improving immunization services, strengthening VPD surveillance, and expanding the capacity to prepare for and manage outbreaks. The Recipient will also create and carry out targeted approaches to reach high-risk groups who are un- or under-immunized. Additionally, the Recipient will promote long-term sustainability of immunization programs-such as supporting evidence-based decisions through National Immunization Technical Advisory Groups (NITAGs)-and enhance program evaluation to increase impact.

The Project Director will lead the technical approach of the project and serve as the primary liaison with CDC, country governments, and other implementing development partners on the progress and reporting of all activities under the award. S/he will ensure the project's goals, objectives, and strategy are achieved and that contractual requirements are met on time and within budget. S/he is responsible for directing the project team with an integrated vision, applying effective leadership and strategic planning skills, management experience, outstanding interpersonal skills, and strong written and oral communication skills. The Project Director supervises the day-to-day work of staff and oversees project implementation to ensure quality programming.

The Project Director also ensures that all management systems, from technical to MEL to finance, actively support timely and accurate project reporting and cost effectiveness for successful implementation of the project. The Project Director is also responsible for ensuring compliance with Corus's policies and procedures and CDC rules and regulations, including responsibility for ensuring sub-awardee compliance and monitoring the quality of program implementation.

The competencies required to be successful in this position include a theoretical and practical understanding of global health systems and integration strategies to address prevention, early detection, and response to infectious disease threats; programming in conflict and fragile settings; personnel and project management skills; the ability to motivate and lead teams; and the demonstrated ability to operate at advanced levels of authority and accountability for achieving results. The candidate must demonstrate proven experience in coordinating public health systems and resources in fragile settings. The position will report to the Program Director, Global Health Security and Immunization. The Project Director will be expected to visit project sites periodically.

**The Project Director will report to Corus HQ and may be remote, depending on circumstances.**

**Key Responsibilities:**

- Provide overall management, strategic direction, and technical leadership to the project to achieve expected project results within budget and timeframe.
- Serve as principal liaison to CDC and the country governments, ensuring high levels of coordination, while nurturing relationships with all key stakeholders (including partner organizations at the national and subnational level) on administrative, financial, and programmatic matters related to the project.
- Liaise with CDC, other donors, and implementing partners and stakeholders, to ensure coordination of and harmonization with other relevant public health mechanisms, private sector engagement, and USG activities globally.
- Ensure results-oriented technical components and high-quality and timely deliverables and reports.
- Oversee implementing partners and advise on technical issues.
- Lead project teams (e.g., technical, program, finance, and operational staff) to ensure program tasks, deliverables, and responsibilities are met; staff management includes hiring, supervising, and mentoring project staff.
- Oversee project deliverables, including ensuring programmatic and financial report preparation and high-quality timely submission, and ensuring cross-cutting issues are effectively integrated into project implementation.
- Direct preparation of annual work plans, project activity updates, and other project-related communication and reporting materials.
- Represent the project in all technical, policy, and programmatic forums at all levels (country, national, and international). Identify lessons learned and best practices for external dissemination.
- Oversee implementing partners and advise on technical issues.
- Ensure compliance with CDC rules and regulations, working with the headquarters grants and contracts team.

**Qualifications:**

- Advanced graduate degree in public health, medicine/nursing, international development, or related field experience. Doctoral degree or MD/MPH an asset.
- Minimum of 10 years' experience in the implementation and management of international donor/CDC funded health projects, with substantial knowledge and experience related to immunization systems and vaccine preventable disease surveillance highly preferred.
- Proven technical expertise using new approaches to build capacity in national immunization and VPD surveillance programs.
- Knowledge of USG framework of global health security and its immunization related implications and priorities, especially in fragile contexts, and familiarity with CDC policy and strategies.
- Knowledge of and experience with CDC rules and regulations required.
- Demonstrated experience in developing and maintaining strong relationships with government agencies, international donor agencies, and private sector stakeholders.
- Experience collaborating and coordinating with local and national host government agencies and aligning program activities and results with national strategies.
- Demonstrated leadership qualities, including technical, management, and evaluation expertise for complex programs in resource-constrained countries; prior experience as a Project Director/Chief of Party for CDC-funded projects similar in scope and size is required.
- Strong staff supervision skills and demonstrated ability to coordinate programs with partners from a broad range of backgrounds and experiences; demonstrated ability to lead multi-disciplinary teams.
- Experience building the capacity of national non-government partner organizations and government systems to achieve CDC's goal of strengthening national ownership for future funding.
- Strong communication skills, including both written and oral presentation skills; proven ability to develop and communicate a common vision among diverse public and private partners.
- English fluency with professional proficiency in writing required
- Working fluency or better in other language an asset, especially French, also potentially Spanish, Arabic, etc.
- Experience working fragile contexts preferred.
- Ability to travel to project sites as needed.

jobs.title: Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)
jobs.description:
The **International Rescue Committee (IRC)** responds to the world’s most pressing humanitarian crises and helps people whose lives and livelihoods have been shattered by conflict and disaster. In Poland, IRC is supporting refugees and host communities with economic recovery, livelihood programs, and social protection initiatives to foster resilience and self-reliance.

**JOB OVERVIEW:**

REAL Talk is a two-year, EU-funded project that prevents gender-based violence (GBV) and cyber GBV among adolescents aged 11–16 in Poland, Italy and Estonia. It works with adolescents and with the adults around them: caregivers, especially fathers and male caregivers, and school staff and educators. IRC Poland leads the project’s work with caregivers and delivers all activities in Poland, together with IRC Italia (coordinator), Una Casa per l’Uomo, the University of Tartu and the International Child Development Initiatives (ICDI).

The **Education and Child Protection Officer (Training Facilitator)** is IRC Poland’s facilitator for REAL Talk. Working in tandem with another facilitator, the post holder delivers sessions of the project’s Cross-Cultural Socio-Emotional and Relational Education Model: dedicated sessions for adolescent boys, the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood” workshops for fathers and male caregivers, and training for teachers and educators. The post holder also takes part in the project’s mandatory transnational training for facilitators, which starts on 12 November 2026.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**1. Facilitation and delivery**

- Facilitate sessions of the Model with adolescents aged 11–16 at the partner school: dedicated sessions for boys, and mixed-gender groups co-facilitated with the female facilitator. Groups have 10–15 adolescents and follow a series of 5–8 sessions of 100–120 minutes, reaching around 40 adolescents in Poland.
- Deliver the “Cycle of Aware Fatherhood”: a series of 4–6 workshops of 60–90 minutes for small groups of 3–8 fathers and male caregivers (around 15 in total), on masculinity, emotional literacy, non-violent role modelling and parenting in the digital age.
- Co-facilitate, with the female facilitator, mixed-gender information sessions for parents and caregivers on adolescent relationship violence, social media and online safety (around 80 caregivers).
- Co-deliver training for school staff (around 30 teachers, in groups of about 10) and online basic training sessions for educators across Poland (around 80 participants).
- Create a safe, trauma-informed and non-judgmental space in every session. Respond to disclosures following IRC procedures and refer participants to support services through the agreed referral pathways.

**2. Preparation and learning**

- Take part in, and prepare for, the mandatory transnational capacity-building sessions for facilitators (online, in English). The first session is on 12 November 2026, and further sessions follow through January 2027.
- Study the Model and adapt session plans and materials to the Polish context and to participants with migrant or refugee backgrounds, together with the female facilitator and the project lead.
- Prepare sessions, materials and logistics, and stay in contact with participants, especially fathers, in line with the project’s engagement and retention strategy for caregivers.
- In November 2026, support colleagues, where needed, in focus group discussions and key informant interviews for the project’s research on online masculinity norms.

**3. Partnerships and coordination**

- Coordinate with the partner school (leadership, teachers and school counsellors) on schedules, venues, consent procedures and the recruitment of participants.
- Plan, deliver and debrief sessions jointly with the female facilitator, and exchange practice with facilitators from the project’s partner organizations in Italy and Estonia.
- When requested, support other REAL Talk activities in Poland, such as consultations with adolescents and caregivers, the Champions workshop, the national webinar and the study visit to Poland.

**4. Monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL), safeguarding and compliance**

- Administer pre- and post-session questionnaires and feedback tools, and collect signed attendance lists and consent forms, following MEAL guidance and data protection (GDPR) requirements.
- Record sex-disaggregated session data and write short session reports. Contribute lessons learned to the project’s deliverables and donor reports.
- Apply the IRC Child Safeguarding Policy, the IRC Poland Child Protection Response Procedure and the IRC Way standards at all times. Report any concern immediately to the Protection and Safeguarding Coordinator.
- Make sure session materials carry the EU funding acknowledgement required by the donor.
- Mainstream gender equality, inclusion and a Do No Harm approach in all activities.
- Carry out other duties assigned by the supervisor, within the scope of the project.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

- **Working time:** part-time. The indicative workload is around 230 hours over the assignment; the exact working time is confirmed in the offer.
- **November 2026 – January 2027:** onboarding, five online transnational training sessions of about two hours each (the first on 12 November 2026) and, if needed, support to the research activities. The successful candidate must be able to start in time for the first session.
- **February – May 2027 (dates to be confirmed):** delivery of sessions with adolescents, fathers, parents, teachers and educators, as the partner school is confirmed and the school semester allows. The rest of the assignment covers follow-up and reporting.

**JOB REQUIREMENTS**

**Education**

- Bachelor’s degree (Master’s preferred) in education, pedagogy, psychology, social work, sociology, gender studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Additional training in facilitation, child protection or trauma-informed practice is an asset.

**Experience**

- At least 2 years of experience facilitating group sessions or workshops with adolescents and/or adults (such as parents or teachers) in a school, NGO, youth or community setting.
- Experience addressing sensitive topics, such as relationships, consent, violence, masculinity or online risks, in a participatory and non-judgmental way.
- Experience in gender equality, GBV prevention, engaging men and boys, positive parenting or child protection is strongly preferred.
- Familiarity with approaches such as Engaging Men through Accountable Practice (EMAP), Engaging Adolescent Boys in Accountable Practice (EABAP) or My Safety, My Wellbeing is an asset.
- Experience working with refugee or migrant communities, or in EU- or donor-funded projects, is an asset.

**Skills and competencies**

- Strong facilitation skills: able to build trust quickly with adolescent boys, fathers and teachers, and to manage group dynamics.
- Commitment to gender equality, an anti-racist and Do No Harm approach, and to modelling respectful behaviour. Ability to work in close tandem with a co-facilitator and in an international team.
- Good planning and organizational skills, attention to detail and reliable record keeping.
- Good digital skills: Microsoft Office, Teams, Zoom or Google Meet, confidence delivering online sessions, and an understanding of social media and online safety.
- Languages: Polish (fluent or native) and English (upper-intermediate or higher, as the transnational training is delivered in English). Ukrainian and/or Russian is an asset.
- Willingness to travel within Poland, and to deliver some sessions in the late afternoon or evening.
- Right to work in Poland.

Appointment is subject to the safeguarding screening for work with minors required by Polish law and IRC policy, including a certificate from the National Criminal Register, a check in the Register of Sexual Offenders and, where applicable, certificates from other countries of residence.

*We encourage male candidates to apply as the sessions are to be delivered to adolescent boys.*

jobs.title: Travel Agency Services (North Africa) for Journalists under the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices Project
jobs.description:
Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) invites travel agencies legally registered and licensed in Tunisia to submit offers for booking round-trip flights to Tunis for fellows from Libya, Algeria and Morocco under its “MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices 2026–2027” programme. This will be a service contract running from 9 November 2026 to 30 June 2027. Interested agencies are invited to apply by 6 November 2026.

**1. Introducing MiCT**

Media in Cooperation and Transition (MiCT) is a non-profit organisation that delivers expert media services in complex and challenging contexts with passion, precision, and agility. Through our collaborative work with our partners, we foster transparent, inclusive, and fair dialogue, supporting resilient societies that thrive.

Across three continents and 15 countries, MiCT facilitates the training of journalists and media producers, programme and content development, radio and film production, magazine and book publishing, media research and monitoring, and supporting our partners’ financial viability.

**2. The MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices Programme**

Since 2022, the MiCT Fellowship for Critical Voices has supported at-risk journalists and media professionals from conflict regions, enabling them to continue their essential work in safety. The programme is part of the Hannah Arendt Initiative and a member of the Journalists in Distress Network. It offers stipends, security and equipment support, (mental) health services, legal aid, relocation, and professional development through regional hubs.

**3. Services required**

The fellowship brings participants from North Africa to Tunis for stays of typically two to three months. MiCT is seeking a reliable, transparent and cost-effective travel agency for the 2026 and 2027 fellow groups. The expected volume is small, about 8–9 round-trip tickets per year (maximum 10), mostly from Libya, followed by Algeria and Morocco.

The tender documents, including the Terms of Reference and Annex 1 – Bidder Application Form, are available without registration in a read-only online folder at: [CfP-FCV-NorthAfrica-2026-02](https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1f_ub_P1UK_vNiAqvToATGjC-K0vIYvUg?usp=sharing)

jobs.title: Venezuela: Auxiliar de Logística en Terreno (Caracas)
jobs.description:
La Cruz Roja Venezolana (CRV) es una organización humanitaria cuyo mandato es salvar vidas y mejorar las condiciones de las personas en situación de vulnerabilidad. Como parte del Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y la Medialuna Roja, brinda asistencia oportuna en emergencias, desastres y contextos de necesidad humanitaria.

Guiada por sus Principios Fundamentales (Humanidad, Imparcialidad, Neutralidad, Independencia, Voluntariado, Unidad y Universalidad) la CRV actúa como auxiliar de los poderes públicos en el ámbito humanitario, trabajando para reducir el sufrimiento humano sin distinción de raza, género, religión o ideología. Su labor abarca la atención médica de emergencia, el fortalecimiento de la resiliencia comunitaria, la capacitación en primeros auxilios, la respuesta a desastres y la promoción de la salud y el bienestar.

A través de una red de voluntarios altamente comprometidos, la CRV moviliza recursos de manera eficiente y eficaz para estar presente donde más se necesita, cuando más se necesita. Su labor se fundamenta en la solidaridad, el respeto a la dignidad humana y el compromiso con la protección de la vida en todas sus formas.

**Compromiso con la Salvaguarda**

La Cruz Roja Venezolana está comprometida con la creación y mantenimiento de entornos seguros y respetuosos para las comunidades, el personal y el voluntariado y con la prevención de la explotación, el abuso y el acoso sexual.

Las personas seleccionadas deberán cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas y estándares de Salvaguarda aplicables. Como parte de su proceso de contratación segura, la CRV podrá realizar verificaciones de referencias profesionales y solicitar información pertinente sobre antecedentes de conducta profesional y Salvaguarda, de acuerdo con sus procedimientos y la normativa aplicable.

**Responsabilidad general de Salvaguarda**

La persona titular del puesto deberá promover y respetar los estándares de Salvaguarda de la Cruz Roja Venezolana, cumplir el Código de Conducta y las políticas aplicables, mantener límites profesionales apropiados, contribuir a prevenir daños y reportar de forma inmediata cualquier preocupación de Salvaguarda a través de los mecanismos establecidos.

**Adición para puestos de riesgo elevado**

Debido a la naturaleza de sus funciones, la persona deberá identificar y mitigar activamente riesgos de Salvaguarda asociados a sus actividades, mantener estándares reforzados de conducta y límites profesionales y asegurar que su interacción con comunidades y personas en situación de vulnerabilidad se desarrolle de forma segura, digna, inclusiva y respetuosa.

Si deseas formar parte del equipo y hacer la diferencia, te invitamos a sumarte.

*¿Cómo puedes hacer la diferencia? Funciones claves / Responsabilidades*

El/La Auxiliar de Logística en terreno brindará apoyo operativo y logístico para el desarrollo de las jornadas de salud en terreno, especialmente aquellas realizadas a través de las unidades móviles de salud de la Cruz Roja Venezolana. Será responsable de apoyar la preparación, movilización, organización y disposición de los medicamentos, insumos, materiales, mobiliario y equipos necesarios para garantizar el adecuado funcionamiento de las jornadas, de acuerdo con la planificación operativa y los procedimientos establecidos.

Asimismo, participará activamente en el alistamiento de las unidades móviles, las actividades de cargue y descargue, el montaje y desmontaje de los espacios de atención y el control de los suministros utilizados durante cada jornada. Apoyará la verificación, organización y reposición de los materiales y equipos al finalizar las actividades, asegurando que las unidades móviles queden debidamente acondicionadas para su siguiente despliegue. El cargo requiere disponibilidad para adaptarse a los horarios y necesidades operativas de las jornadas, así como para desarrollar actividades logísticas en diferentes condiciones de terreno, conforme a los procedimientos de la Cruz Roja Venezolana y los lineamientos de la Cruz Roja Alemana.

*Reporte*

El/La Auxiliar de logística en terreno reportará al Oficial de Cadena y Suministro.

*Lugar de trabajo*

Caracas, con disponibilidad para viajar a los sitios de implementación de proyecto.

*Para calificar como un constructor del sistema humanitario venezolano deberás cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:*

Será el/la encargado(a) de:

- Apoyar al responsable de cadena de suministro en el alistamiento logístico de las actividades de salud, preparación para desastres y respuesta a emergencias, de acuerdo con la planificación operativa.
- Recibir, contar y verificar los medicamentos, insumos, materiales y equipos que ingresen a la bodega, contrastándolos con los documentos de entrega y reportando cualquier diferencia o daño.
- Clasificar, ubicar y almacenar los bienes de forma ordenada y segura, siguiendo los procedimientos establecidos y las indicaciones del personal responsable para el manejo de medicamentos.
- Mantener actualizados los registros de inventario, incluidas entradas, salidas, traslados, devoluciones, existencias y ubicación de los bienes.
- Realizar conteos físicos periódicos y reportar diferencias, pérdidas, daños, productos próximos a vencer o necesidades de reposición.
- Preparar y verificar los bienes requeridos para jornadas de salud, actividades de preparación, despliegues y operaciones de respuesta, utilizando las solicitudes aprobadas y listas de comprobación.
- Apoyar el cargue, descargue y despacho de bienes, verificando sus cantidades y condiciones físicas. Organizar la carga dentro del vehículo para protegerla durante el traslado, en coordinación con el conductor.
- Registrar y archivar los movimientos de bienes mediante actas de entrega y recepción, notas de salida, formularios de inventario y demás soportes requeridos.
- Verificar los bienes y equipos que regresen de las actividades en terreno, registrar las devoluciones y organizar su almacenamiento o reportar las necesidades de reposición.
- Apoyar el montaje y desmontaje logístico de jornadas y operativos, incluida la organización de espacios, mobiliario, carpas, señalización, materiales y equipos.
- Mantener ordenados y disponibles el archivo físico y digital de los soportes logísticos para seguimiento, rendición de cuentas y auditoría.
- Cuidar los bienes, equipos e insumos bajo su responsabilidad y reportar de inmediato pérdidas, daños, incidentes de seguridad o incumplimientos de los procedimientos logísticos.
- Realizar otras tareas de bodega y apoyo logístico relacionadas con el cargo, según las necesidades de las actividades.

**Para calificar como constructor(a) del sistema humanitario venezolano, deberá cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:**

- Educación secundaria completa (bachiller). Formación técnica o estudios en logística, administración, gestión de almacenes o áreas afines (deseable).
- Experiencia comprobable en labores operativas de bodega, almacenamiento, organización, control de inventarios, preparación, movilización y despacho de suministros.
- Experiencia en actividades de cargue, descargue, organización de mercancías, equipos y materiales, así como en el mantenimiento del orden y las condiciones adecuadas de almacenamiento.
- Experiencia o conocimientos básicos en el manejo de medicamentos, insumos médicos o suministros humanitarios (deseable).
- Capacidad para organizar y mantener actualizados inventarios, registros de entradas y salidas, actas de entrega y recepción y otros soportes logísticos.
- Manejo básico de hojas de cálculo y otras herramientas informáticas para el registro y reporte de información (deseable).
- Capacidad y disposición para realizar actividades de alta exigencia física, incluyendo la movilización frecuente de equipos, mobiliario y suministros, cargue, descargue, instalación y desmontaje de espacios de atención, siguiendo las medidas de seguridad correspondientes.
- Disponibilidad para trabajar en terreno y adaptarse a los horarios operativos de las jornadas de salud, incluyendo actividades de alistamiento previo y posterior, horarios extendidos y fines de semana, cuando las necesidades operativas lo requieran.
- Capacidad para trabajar de forma independiente y en equipo, siguiendo instrucciones, procedimientos establecidos y medidas de seguridad.
- Experiencia en contextos de emergencia, jornadas de salud, actividades comunitarias o trabajo con voluntariado (deseable).
- Experiencia con el Movimiento Internacional de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja (deseable).
- Compromiso con los Principios Fundamentales de la Cruz Roja y de la Medialuna Roja.
- Fluidez oral y escrita en español.

jobs.title: Grants and compliance coordinator (F/M) - Yemen
jobs.description:
Do you want to join a committed, activist-driven organization and take meaningful action for social justice?
For over 40 years, Médecins du Monde has been delivering healthcare to the most vulnerable, challenging barriers to access, and driving long-term change in health policies.

In France and across nearly 30 countries, our work is built around six core missions:

- Sexual and reproductive health and rights (including access to safe abortion)
- Migration, exile, human rights and health
- Harm reduction
- Health and the environment
- Healthcare systems
- Humanitarian spaces

**MdM in Yemen**

Yemen remains one of the world's most severe humanitarian crises, after more than a decade of conflict, economic decline, climate shocks, and political instability. In 2026, over two-thirds of the population require humanitarian assistance, including 9.4 million people identified as most in need of life-saving support.

The health system is under extreme strain, with only 59.3% of health facilities fully operational and 19.3 million people requiring healthcare services, including more than 660,000 pregnant women in need of urgent care. Cholera continues to pose a major public health challenge, adding pressure to an already weakened system.

The operational environment remains highly volatile, marked by security incidents, service disruptions, funding cuts, and economic challenges that regularly affect humanitarian activities.

Médecins du Monde operates across northern and southern Yemen, with a coordination office in Sana’a and field offices in Aden and Marib. Its interventions focus on two strategic priorities:

- Supporting 29 health facilities to deliver primary healthcare services, including outpatient care, vaccination, nutrition, and reproductive health.
- Providing mental health and psychosocial support (MHPSS) through healthcare facilities and community-based networks trained in identification, referral, and awareness-raising activities.

**About the role**

You will be responsible for providing technical expertise on grants and compliance while playing an essential coordination lead role amongst all departments. You are a key in ensuring all departments have a clear understanding of their role and responsibilities as regards to grants and compliance aspects.

You are actively involved in the country strategy and the overall project cycle management, especially through contracts management (including partnerships), reporting, donor communication, fundraising and compliance.

**Who you’ll work with**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator in charge of programs and the technical management of the HQ program officer, you will work in close collaboration with the general coordinator, the deputy general coordinator in charge of support services, along with other key departments when relevant (MEAL, field coordinators, etc.).

**What you’ll do**

Under the supervision of the deputy general coordinator in charge of programs, your main responsibilities are the following:

- Support country strategy development through donor mapping, strategic opportunity identification, and donor engagement
- Lead fundraising efforts, identify funding opportunities, and build relationships with donors and key stakeholders
- Coordinate the development of grant proposals, budgets, and project design processes with technical and support teams
- Ensure effective grant management, donor compliance, contract follow-up, and timely donor communications
- Oversee the preparation and submission of high-quality donor reports and visibility materials
- Manage partnerships, including partner identification, due diligence, agreements, and performance monitoring
- Ensure compliance with donor requirements and MdM procedures, while supporting audits and risk management processes
- Facilitate coordination between departments and represent MdM in relevant meetings, forums, and donor engagements

**You are the right match if you...**

- Hold a master’s degree in one of the related fields or project management
- Have 5 years of proven experience in humanitarian and/or development contexts, with at least 2 years in a similar role
- Demonstrate strong knowledge in partnerships, multi-sectoral, regional and/or co-funded programming management
- Are skilled in developing high-quality funding proposals, reports and have experience working with institutional donors
- Experience /knowledge of the region
- Speak English fluently. Arabic is highly appreciated.

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Are uncomfortable working in complex, unstable, or rapidly evolving humanitarian contexts that require flexibility, resilience, and adaptability
- Prefer close supervision and highly structured processes rather than taking initiative, anticipating needs, and working independently
- Do not have strong written English skills or experience producing donor proposals, narrative reports, and other high-quality programme documentation
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 392 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting in December 2026
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Aden
- Frequent visits to Sanaa and to the field, depending the security conditions.

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

- Demonstrate strong knowledge in partnerships, multi-sectoral, regional and/or co-funded programming management
- Are skilled in collaborating with authorities
- Experience /knowledge of the region
- Speak English fluently. Arabic is highly appreciated

**This role may not suit you if you...**

- Are uncomfortable working in complex, unstable, or rapidly evolving humanitarian contexts that require flexibility, resilience, and adaptability
- Prefer close supervision and highly structured processes rather than taking initiative, anticipating needs, and working independently
- Do not have strong leadership skills and a supportive management style (experience managing national and expatriate staff)
- Are not aligned with MdM’s values and activist approach

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

**Contract & status:**

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract for 6 months starting in December 2026
- Single posting

**Work environment:**

- Position based in Aden
- Frequent visits to Sanaa and to the field, depending the security conditions.

**Benefits:**

- 13th-month salary (for employees with more than 6 months’ seniority)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Accommodation: guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

**Essentials:**

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know.

jobs.title: Stagiaire comptabilité siège
jobs.description:
## Rejoignez MSF OCG en tant que Stagiaire comptabilité siège !

**Nous cherchons des personnes passionnées et prêtes à contribuer à notre mission humanitaire.**

**Découvrez ci-dessous les détails du poste et les qualifications que nous recherchons.**

Ce stage s'inscrit dans le cadre d'un programme de formation académique, professionnelle ou d'insertion socioprofessionnelle, et doit répondre aux [conditions](https://www.ge.ch/engager-personne-stage/stages-formation-insertion-reconnus) fixées par le Conseil de surveillance du marché de l'emploi (CSME). La durée du stage, fixée par la convention tripartite, est de 6 à 9 mois à 100 %.

### Inclusivité et Diversité chez MSF

Vos qualifications et votre expérience ne correspondent pas exactement à toutes les exigences ?

À MSF OCG, nous nous engageons à promouvoir une culture inclusive qui soutient et amplifie les voix diverses de nos collaborateurs. Nous nous efforçons de créer des environnements de travail où des équipes de personnes aux parcours, caractéristiques, perspectives, idées et expériences variés collaborent pour faire avancer la mission sociale de MSF et améliorer les résultats pour nos patients et les communautés avec lesquelles nous travaillons.

Nous comprenons que certaines personnes peuvent hésiter à postuler si elles ne répondent pas à toutes les exigences du poste. Les recherches montrent que cela est particulièrement vrai pour les femmes. Si vous pensez que votre profil correspond bien à ce poste, nous vous invitons à postuler, même si vous ne remplissez pas toutes les qualifications listées.

Nous encourageons les candidatures de personnes de tous genres, âges, orientations sexuelles, ethnies, origines, religions, croyances, situations de handicap et toutes autres caractéristiques de diversité.

MSF ne tolère aucune exploitation ou abus sexuels, aucune forme de discrimination ou de harcèlement, y compris le harcèlement sexuel. Tous les candidats sélectionnés feront l’objet de vérifications de références

### Contexte & Mission

Médecins Sans Frontières est une organisation médicale et humanitaire internationale indépendante qui fournit des soins aux personnes dans le besoin, aux personnes touchées par des catastrophes naturelles ou causées par l'homme et aux victimes de conflits armés, sans discrimination et sans tenir compte de la race, de la religion, des croyances ou de l'appartenance politique (Charte de MSF).

Le service de la comptabilité à Genève est composé de deux unités, l’une ayant la charge des activités comptables HQ (fournisseurs, trésorerie, taxes) et l’autre assurant le suivi comptable des missions dans les pays d’intervention de MSF (comptabilité terrain). Le·la stagiaire sera intégré·e à l’équipe comptabilité HQ et collaborera principalement avec le·la comptable fournisseurs. Il·elle pourra ponctuellement appuyer le reste de l’équipe comptable, HQ et/ou terrain.

### Principales responsabilités

L’intervention du·de la stagiaire est orientée sur l’apprentissage autour de projets précis récurrents, et en priorité autour du traitement complet du cycle des factures fournisseurs, dont notamment :

- Réception, vérification (aspects légaux et fiscaux) et comptabilisation (comptabilité générale et analytique) des factures fournisseurs via le logiciel de traitement des factures et l’ERP comptable (MS Dynamics D365).
- Justification des comptes fournisseurs via la réalisation de certains contrôles clés mensuels/trimestriels (fournisseurs débiteurs, analyse de la balance âgée, etc.).
- Participation aux travaux de clôture annuelle et préparation des audits selon les périodes.

Le·la stagiaire pourra par ailleurs, selon les besoins, être impliqué·e dans diverses tâches comptables (analyses ponctuelles, appui au traitement des notes de frais, documentation du contrôle interne).

### Profil recherché

- En cours d’études supérieures ou en fin de cycle d’études supérieures.
- Être éligible à une convention de stage avec un tiers.
- Français courant à l’écrit et à l’oral, bon niveau d’anglais à l’écrit, allemand un plus.
- Connaissance des outils bureautiques usuels.
- Connaissance d’un ERP, un atout.
- Organisé·e et rigoureux·se.
- Proactivité et dynamisme.
- Capacité à gérer plusieurs activités.
- Esprit de synthèse.
- Intérêt ou engagement pour la solidarité internationale.
- Expérience préalable dans un département financier/comptable, un atout.

### Conditions de stage

- Convention de stage tripartite obligatoire
- Stage de 6 à 9 mois (en fonction de la convention de stage)
- Stage à 100% (40h par semaine)
- Basé à Genève
- Date d’entrée en fonction : fin mars 2027
- Rémunération mensuelle brut : CHF 2’000.-

jobs.title: Instructional Design and E-Learning Consultant
jobs.description:
**Background**

Medair is seeking an experienced **Instructional Design and E-Learning Consultant** to develop an engaging, learner-centered online course for humanitarian health and nutrition staff.

Medair's International Department Advisor Team works to strengthen the capacity of field health and nutrition staff and increase knowledge and use of sector-specific evidence-based approaches. Rapid changes in health and nutrition interventions, together with the need for greater standardization and effective onboarding of new and experienced staff, have increased the need for updated, user-friendly online training.

The assignment involves developing **one online course with two main sections: Health and Nutrition**:

- **Health:** Review, update and improve an existing unpublished Articulate 360 course section of approximately eight hours of learner seat time.
- **Nutrition:** Transform an existing PowerPoint-based training of approximately 170 slides into an interactive Articulate 360 course section.

**Purpose of the Consultancy**

The purpose of this consultancy is to produce a **SCORM-compliant, learner-centered e-learning course** aligned with adult-learning principles and humanitarian health and nutrition training needs.

The course is intended to equip new Medair health and nutrition staff with knowledge relevant to the technical implementation of Medair's health and nutrition programmes.

**Scope of Work**

Working in close collaboration with Medair's Health and Nutrition Advisors, the consultant will develop:

**Content analysis and instructional design**

- Review existing Health Articulate 360 and Nutrition PowerPoint materials.
- Assess alignment between course content, learning objectives and assessments.
- Identify redundancies, gaps and opportunities to improve learner engagement.
- Recommend instructional-design improvements to support knowledge retention and practical application.

**Storyboarding and course structure**

- Develop or update the course storyboard/course map.
- Review and refine learning objectives.
- Establish an appropriate module structure and sequencing.
- Define screen flow, interactions, activities and assessment approaches.
- Ensure appropriate pacing for self-directed learning.

**E-learning development**

- Update and improve the existing Articulate 360 Health section.
- Convert the approximately 170-slide Nutrition PowerPoint into an interactive Articulate 360 course section.
- Use Articulate Storyline 360 and/or Rise 360, as appropriate.
- Apply adult-learning principles and instructional-design best practices.
- Incorporate engaging and appropriate interactive learning elements.
- Apply consistent organizational branding and visual-design standards.
- Apply responsive design where appropriate.

**Assessment development**

- Review existing assessment questions.
- Revise and/or develop assessments as required.
- Ensure assessments are aligned with learning objectives.
- Incorporate appropriate knowledge checks and interactive learning activities throughout the course.

**Review, quality assurance and testing**

- Support up to two stakeholder review and revision cycles.
- Incorporate agreed technical and instructional-design feedback.
- Conduct functionality, navigation and usability testing.
- Resolve identified technical issues.
- Verify LMS compatibility and successful SCORM export.
- Conduct appropriate cross-browser testing.

**Accessibility and user experience**

Apply accessibility and usability principles where feasible, including:

- Clear navigation
- Readable typography
- Appropriate color contrast
- Alternative text for graphics
- Keyboard accessibility where applicable.

**Key Deliverables**

The consultant will provide:

1. Course review and instructional-design recommendations.
2. Updated storyboard/course map.
3. Updated Health section in Articulate 360.
4. New Nutrition section developed from the existing PowerPoint materials.
5. Interactive learning elements and assessments.
6. Draft integrated Articulate 360 course for stakeholder review.
7. Revised course following stakeholder feedback.
8. Final editable Articulate 360 source files.
9. SCORM/xAPI package ready for LMS upload.
10. Quality assurance and testing report.
11. All multimedia assets developed or used under the assignment.

**Tools and Technical Standards**

The consultant should be able to work with:

- Articulate Storyline 360 and/or Rise 360
- Microsoft PowerPoint
- Microsoft Word and Excel as required
- Appropriate graphic-design software
- SCORM-compliant outputs
- Learning Management Systems
- Responsive e-learning design where appropriate.

All agreed editable source files and other final deliverables must be provided to Medair upon completion.

**Timeframe and Availability**

The assignment is expected to commence in **November 2026**, with the final completed course due by **21 December 2026**.

The consultant should be available for at least **50% capacity, approximately 20 hours per week**, to support timely collaboration, review and feedback.

The consultant should propose the estimated number of working days required for:

- Reviewing existing materials and providing recommendations
- Updating content and developing/updating the storyboard
- Converting the Nutrition PowerPoint to Articulate 360
- Developing interactive learning elements
- Assessment review and development
- Quality assurance, testing and SCORM validation
- Incorporating stakeholder feedback and finalizing the course for LMS deployment.

**No travel is required. The consultancy is remote.**

**Required Experience and Competencies**

Applicants should demonstrate:

- Strong professional experience in **instructional design and e-learning development**.
- Demonstrated experience developing interactive online learning using **Articulate Storyline 360 and/or Rise 360**.
- Strong knowledge and practical application of **adult-learning and learner-centered instructional-design principles**.
- Experience converting PowerPoint or other existing training materials into interactive digital learning.
- Experience reviewing and improving existing e-learning courses.
- Experience developing interactive learning activities and assessments.
- Ability to transform complex technical information into clear, engaging and accessible digital learning.
- Experience producing **SCORM-compliant** courses suitable for LMS deployment.
- Strong quality-assurance and attention-to-detail skills.
- Ability to collaborate remotely with technical subject-matter experts and incorporate stakeholder feedback.

**Highly desirable**

- Instructional-design experience in **humanitarian action, public/global health, nutrition or international development**.
- Experience developing technical learning for humanitarian or NGO staff.
- Experience designing learning for diverse international audiences.
- Experience applying accessibility and usability principles to online learning.

**Consultant Responsibilities**

The consultant will:

- Fill Medair Supplier Registration Form and provide RIB-Banking details
- Provide their own computer, software and other equipment necessary to undertake the assignment.
- Complete the agreed outputs within the established timeframe.
- Provide proof of registration as a consultant before contracting, where such registration is normal practice in the consultant's country of residence.
- Provide required progress information and documentation for invoicing.

**Medair Responsibilities**

Medair will:

- Provide access to existing training materials required for development of the course.
- Review agreed outputs and provide feedback and technical support at defined stages of the consultancy.

jobs.title: Finance Officer- Damascus- Capital
jobs.company: Agency for Technical Cooperation and Development
jobs.description:
**About Acted**

“We go the last mile. Founded in Afghanistan, against the backdrop of a forgotten crisis, Acted’s mission is to save lives and support people in meeting their needs in hard-to-reach areas. Millions of vulnerable people around the world need humanitarian assistance today, and hundreds of millions will need it tomorrow, in the face of the growing threat of climate change. We believe that our assistance must be conceptualised and delivered within the framework of people’s natural environments, and the territories on which they depend. Therefore, Acted pursues a triple mandate as a humanitarian, environmental and development aid actor, contributing to the relief, stabilisation, and recovery of crisis-affected people in fragile areas. This vision is guided by the motto “Think Local – Act Global” - reflecting the need to rely on a deep understanding of local territories and contexts to develop and implement actions based on local knowledge, structures and capacities. This local thinking contributes to a global response - running through all Acted programming and operations - as we work together towards the building of a 3ZERO world: a world with Zero Exclusion, Zero Carbon, and Zero Poverty”.

**Greening strategy:**

Acted’s greening strategy aims to tackle environmental degradation and climate change while meeting the needs of the most vulnerable who are often those most affected by the deepening environmental crisis. Each Acted employee will adhere to these principles through key green programming responsibilities:

• Contribute towards the adherence and development of the greening strategy plan.

• Explore innovative green programming opportunities and/or solutions within your realm of responsibilities and roles

• Encouraging and promoting environmental safeguarding processes and environmental programming standards in accordance with SOPs and technical guideline notes

**Acted PSEAH Policy**:

The Finance Officer has the responsibility to adhere to the PSEAH Policy (Protection against Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment). Finance Officer has the obligation to complete all mandatory trainings related to the Code of Conduct and the PSEA policy and report any safeguarding concern such as breaches of organisational policies or codes of conduct according to Acted’s procedures. Finance Officer carries out work duties in a way that does not harm children, vulnerable adults or other staff or volunteers.
**Location**: Damascus, Syria

**Start Date**: ASAP

**Chain of Command:** Under the authority of: Country Finance Manager.
**Working Relations**

**Internal:** Logistics, HR, compliance, and Expats

**External:** Suppliers, Banks
**Job Purpose:**

The Finance Officer is a key member of the finance team at Capital Level. S/he is responsible of the Accounting software, Procurement Control, Cash management including Banks and MTAs, Accounting, and Archiving.

Objectives

1. Procurement is validated as per acted Manual and procedure
2. Ensure that payments are made efficiently and on a timely manner as per ACTED internal rules and processes in terms of compliance and validation
3. Ensure that the capital accounting books are correctly maintained and updated for a smooth monthly reporting
4. Ensure that the allocation and information of the bank books are correct and compliant
5. Ensure that monthly bank reconciliations are matching
6. Ensure that all documentation is properly scanned and archived as per ACTED standards

**Duties & Responsibilities**

**Procurement review :**

1. Validate procurement of capital managed scenarios submitted by logistics, in respect to acted’s procedure and manual, SoPs, or Memo.
2. Update the Contracts Follow Up File.
3. Attend tenders opening.

**Cash & Payments Management**

1. Ensure sufficient cash in the banks to process payments, by the monthly cash request shared with HQ in coordination with the acted’s offices in the country.
2. Validate and process payments by banks, Cheques, or MTAs, ensure eligible supporting documents, and necessary approvals are maintained.
3. Ensure accurate monthly bank reconciliation prepared, signed, and archived, and report variances if any.

**Accountancy Management and control**

1. Register payments voucher once the payment is processed in your bankbooks
2. Validate the accountancy of each office in the country, the expenses paid by HQ, between missions, from Partners, and requests for allocations, and upload in the accounting software “*SAGA*”
3. Make sure that all information in the accountancy is in line with ACTED standards (accounting codes – harmonised description – third party codes, allocation, etc.)
4. Prepare and record vouchers for any exchange currency or transfer in the concerned bank books.
5. Do the necessary reconciliation in the accounting software *(Matching/Lettering),* and any other tasks associated with SAGA when requested, such as: *FS, Exchange rates, TPCs creation, etc…*

**Archiving Management**

1. Make sure the vouchers’ numbers and dates are matching the accounting records and they are stamped PAID
2. Make sure all payment vouchers and supporting documents are compliant to ACTED procedures, scanned, and archived as per ACTED policy
3. Validate and Provide samples to the compliance when required for the auditors

**Other Tasks:**

1. Collect and archive signed Time Sheets
2. Provide samples to compliance when requested
3. Any other tasks assigned by the line manager

## Key Performance Indicators

> - Monthly closure of SAGA
> - Number of accurate & timely submission of bank books for accounting
> - Liquidity sufficiency
> - Number of timely bank reconciliations
> - Number of archived scanned vouchers & missing
> - Number of complete & timely providing samples to the compliance
> - Timeline of procurement review and payments processing
> - Feedback from other departments and the area.
>
> ### QUALIFICATIONS
>
> - Bachelor’s degree in accounting or a related field
> - Fluent English and Arabic (written and spoken)
> - Excellent writing and communication skills
> - At least 3 years work experience with minimum 1 year as Finance Officer, INGO/NGO experience is preferrable.
> - Ability to work under pressure in a high-pace environment
> - Good organisational and prioritisation skills
> - Proficiency in Microsoft Excel
> - Strong interpersonal and analytical skills
> - Details oriented and control skills

jobs.title: Community Liaison focal person- MMC and Jere
jobs.description:
**JOB PURPOSE**

Under the supervision of the Livelihood Project Manager, the Community Liaison Focal Person is the project's day-to-day presence in each LGA. They are the trusted link between the project team, the facility committees, landowning families, traditional leaders and community members at the livelihood facilities in MMC, Jere and Mafa.

**RESPONSIBILITIES**

## Key responsibilities

### 1. Community entry, mobilisation and communication

- Introduce the project to traditional leaders (District Head, Lawans, Bulamas), religious leaders, landowning families, women and youth groups, and IDP and returnee representatives in the assigned LGA.
- Mobilise participants for consultations, dialogues, trainings, elections and General Assemblies. Make sure women, youth, persons with disabilities, IDPs and returnees are invited and able to attend.
- Explain project decisions, selection criteria, fees and agreements clearly in Hausa, Kanuri or other local languages.
- Share information on the Feedback and Complaints Response Mechanism (FCRM) in every meeting.

### 2. Support to ownership and social cohesion activities

- Support the Social Cohesion Officer in the ownership and tenure audit by locating documents, identifying landowners and arranging consultations.
- Organise and record landowner consultations, community dialogues, public validation of agreements, recognition events and community open days.
- Support the Peace and Grievance Committees: arrange meetings, take notes and follow up on agreed actions.
- Report any tension, dispute or rumour about the facilities to the Social Cohesion Officer the same day, and log it in the tension log.

### 3. Facility committee support

- Attend Facility Management Committee meetings and help with agendas, minutes and follow-up actions.
- Support transparent selection of members and supervised elections, and help committees apply their constitutions.
- Check that membership lists, plot allocations, fees and monthly accounts are publicly displayed.
- Remind committees of their reporting duties to the LGA Facility Oversight Committee, and support preparations for quarterly social audits.

### 4. Day-to-day enterprise facilitation

- Visit each facility in the LGA at least once a week.
- Coach treasurers and records keepers on the cash book, sales records, fee registers and stock records, following the Business Development Officer's tools.
- Check that maintenance logs, equipment logs and asset registers are kept up to date, and report faults to the relevant officer.
- Follow up on production plans, water schedules (irrigation), stocking and harvesting plans (fish farms) and order books (tailoring), and flag problems early.
- Support logistics for trainings, deliveries and commissioning events at the facilities.

### 5. Data collection and reporting

- Collect routine monitoring data using digital or paper tools from the MEAL Officer: attendance, facility days operational, sales, fees collected, maintenance and complaints.
- Submit a weekly activity report and photos, and contribute to monthly reports.
- Support baseline, endline and perception surveys.

### 6. Accountability and referrals

- Receive feedback and complaints from community members, record them accurately and pass them to the FCRM focal point within 24 hours.
- Refer protection and safeguarding concerns immediately and confidentially, only through the approved channels. Never investigate such cases personally.

### Cross-cutting duties

- Stay neutral and never make promises on behalf of the project, government or landowners.
- Follow PSEA, safeguarding, confidentiality and security procedures, and report any security incident immediately.
- Carry out any other reasonable duties related to the project, as assigned by the supervisor.

**Essential requirements:**

## Qualifications, experience and competencies

### Education

- **Essential:** an OND, NCE or HND in Social Sciences, Community Development, Agriculture, Business, Adult Education or a related field.
- **Desirable:** a B.Sc in one of these fields, or certificates in community mobilisation, facilitation, record keeping or peacebuilding.

### Experience

**Essential**

- At least 2 years of experience in community mobilisation, community development or field work with an NGO, UN agency or government programme.
- Experience organising and facilitating community meetings with mixed groups, including women, youth and displaced persons.
- Good knowledge of the assigned LGA, its communities, traditional structures and local dynamics. Residence in or strong ties to the LGA are a strong advantage.

**Desirable**

- Experience supporting community committees, cooperatives, VSLAs or Water User Associations.
- Experience with livelihoods, agriculture, aquaculture or tailoring activities.
- Experience collecting data with mobile tools such as KoBoToolbox or ODK.
- Experience with complaints and feedback mechanisms.

### Skills and competencies

- Excellent communication and listening skills; able to explain ideas simply and respectfully.
- Trusted by and able to relate well to leaders, elders, women, youth and vulnerable groups.
- Neutral, discreet and honest, with good judgement in sensitive situations.
- Organised and reliable; able to work independently in the field with little supervision.
- Basic numeracy and record keeping, and basic smartphone and MS Office skills.
- Commitment to inclusion, PSEA and humanitarian principles.

### Languages

- **Essential:** fluent Hausa and Kanuri; good written and spoken English.

jobs.description:
**A propos de la Chaîne de l'Espoir**

La Chaîne de l’Espoir est une ONG internationale fondée en 1994. Elle a pour vocation de renforcer les systèmes de santé pour donner à chacun et en particulier aux enfants les mêmes chances de survie et de développement.

Nous intervenons dans 25 pays par une approche globale, centrée sur l’enfant mais également sur les mères et les communautés défavorisées :

- Prévention et dépistage dès le plus jeune âge, notamment dans le cadre de programmes de santé à l’école.
- Soin et chirurgie, afin de répondre aux besoins les plus urgents des enfants et de leurs mères.
- Formation et transferts de compétences aux équipes locales grâce à notre réseau international d’experts dans tous les domaines de la chirurgie.
- Construction et équipement de structures hospitalières adaptées aux besoins locaux.

**Poste et missions**

Rattaché à la Directrice générale, vous pilotez l’audit, le contrôle interne et la gestion des risques au siège et dans les bureaux pays. Vous mobilisez les managers, faites aboutir les mesures correctrices et accompagnez les équipes sans vous substituer à elles.

Vous rendez compte à la Direction générale et au Comité d’audit et de contrôle interne (CACI). Vous exercez également, en toute indépendance, les fonctions de Délégué à la protection des données (DPO) et cogérez la cellule de signalement avec la DRH.

**Cartographie et gestion des risques**

- Actualiser les cartographies des risques de l’association et des bureaux pays avec leurs responsables ; suivre les mesures de maîtrise et alerter sur les risques majeurs.

**Audit interne**

- Définir les audits prioritaires, les conduire au siège et sur le terrain, puis formuler des recommandations hiérarchisées et opérationnelles.
- Piloter le suivi des plans d’action avec les managers, vérifier leur réalisation, faire remonter les blocages et appuyer, si besoin, les audits bailleurs.

**Contrôle interne, procédures et conformité**

- Faire évoluer les procédures et outils de contrôle interne avec les services et veiller à leur appropriation et application, au siège comme sur le terrain.
- Superviser la lutte contre le blanchiment et le financement du terrorisme (LAB/FT), le criblage des parties prenantes et la gestion des dérogations.

**Protection des données personnelles – fonction DPO**

- Conseiller les services et référents RGPD ; suivre la documentation des traitements, les demandes d’exercice des droits et les incidents de données personnelles.
- Contrôler la conformité RGPD, prioriser les recommandations, vérifier les actions mises en œuvre par les services et alerter la DG, dans le respect de l’indépendance du DPO.

**Éthique et cellule de signalement**

- Sensibiliser à la prévention de la fraude, de la corruption, des conflits d’intérêts et de l’exploitation, des abus et du harcèlement sexuels (PSEAH).
- Cogérer avec la DRH la cellule de signalement ; veiller au traitement confidentiel et impartial des alertes, au suivi des mesures correctrices et à un circuit indépendant en cas de conflit d’intérêts.

**Reporting, gouvernance et CACI**

- Fournir chaque mois à la DG un tableau de bord priorisé (risques, audits, contrôle interne, RGPD et plans d’action) ; alerter sur les risques critiques et proposer les arbitrages nécessaires.
- Préparer avec la trésorière, présidente du CACI, les réunions, rapports et comptes rendus ; suivre les décisions et recommandations.

## Profil recherché

**Formation et expériences**

- Bac+5 en audit, contrôle interne, gestion des risques, conformité, finance ou domaine comparable ; formations complémentaires en RGPD, enquêtes internes ou prévention de la fraude appréciées.
- Au moins 8 ans d’expérience en audit, contrôle interne, risques ou conformité. Une expérience en ONG internationale ou organisation comparable, au siège ou sur le terrain, est fortement souhaitée.
- **Expériences avérées :** cartographie des risques, audits, déploiement du contrôle interne et conduite de plans d’action transversaux avec des résultats démontrés.
- **Atouts supplémentaires :** expérience DPO, gestion de signalements et d’enquêtes sensibles, criblage, audits bailleurs et coordination avec des fonctions support et opérationnelles.

**Compétences et qualités requises**

- **Leadership transversal :** mobiliser sans autorité hiérarchique, responsabiliser les managers et obtenir des résultats concrets sans faire à leur place.
- **Analyse et décision :** hiérarchiser les risques, rédiger des recommandations claires et produire des tableaux de bord utiles aux arbitrages.
- **Intégrité et discernement :** traiter les situations sensibles avec indépendance, confidentialité, impartialité, diplomatie et fermeté.
- **Pédagogie et écoute :** convaincre, former, accompagner le changement et conduire des entretiens, y compris délicats.
- **Bailleurs :** connaître les exigences des partenaires français (AFD, CDCS), européens (ECHO, INTPA) et onusiens, ainsi que les contraintes du terrain.
