Senior Corporate Development Officer
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

JOB SUMMARY
Leads advanced fundraising projects and initiatives, ensuring effective donor engagement, grant identification, and proposal development.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Join a Global Mission That Changes Lives**

When you join Habitat for Humanity International (HFHI), you join a movement that believes every person deserves a safe and affordable place to call home. As our next **Senior Corporate Development Officer**, you will help build the partnerships that make this mission possible.

In this role, you will focus on cultivating and expanding relationships with corporate partners in the New York City market, with a particular emphasis on the banking and financial services sector. Your work will help generate critical revenue that fuels Habitat’s mission and supports families and communities around the world.

You will shape national and global corporate relationships that fuel Habitat’s work in more than 70 countries. Your creativity, strategy, and relationship-building skills will directly support families and communities around the world.

**Location and Travel**

This position is fully remote in New York or New Jersey. You will have the flexibility to work from home while collaborating with colleagues and partners across the country and around the world.

This role requires approximately 25 percent domestic travel for partner meetings, prospecting activities, events, and other key engagements.

**Role Purpose**

You will lead the development, cultivation, and stewardship of high-value corporate partnerships, primarily with Fortune 500 companies. You will manage a portfolio that generates between 5 and 10 million dollars annually and collaborate across HFHI’s global network to design innovative, mission-aligned partnerships that advance affordable housing worldwide.

**Key Responsibilities**

\*Develop and execute strategic, partner-centered plans that align corporate goals with Habitat’s mission.
\*Identify, cultivate, and secure new national and global corporate partnerships while strengthening existing relationships.
\*Create and deliver compelling proposals and presentations that inspire corporate engagement.
\*Negotiate complex, multi-year commitments in collaboration with legal, finance, and program teams.
\*Provide high-touch stewardship that ensures partner satisfaction and long-term growth.
\*Collaborate with HFHI affiliates and global teams to maximize partnership value and ensure seamless execution.
\*Track, analyze, and report on partnership performance using CRM systems and forecasting tools.

**Must-Have Qualifications**

\*Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience
\*5+ years of experience in fundraising, sales, or prospect development
\*Proven success securing six and seven figure multiyear commitments from Fortune 500 companies
\*Experience with international partnership strategy and development
\*Strong understanding of corporate social responsibility, sponsorships, and employee engagement
\*Exceptional relationship-building, communication, and negotiation skills
\*Highly proactive, solutions-oriented, and comfortable navigating a complex organization
\*Strong project management, analytics, and reporting capabilities
\*Commitment to HFHI values: Humility, Courage, Accountability, and safeguarding practices

**Nice-to-Have Qualifications**

\*Experience with Blackbaud CRM or similar platforms
\*Background in sales, marketing, or public relations
\*Knowledge of and passion for Habitat’s global mission

**Culture and Values**

At Habitat for Humanity International, you join a community that believes in:
**\*Humility:** We are part of something bigger than ourselves.
**\*Courage:** We do what is right, even when it is difficult.
**\*Accountability:** We take personal responsibility for Habitat’s mission.
**\*Safeguarding:** We protect the rights, dignity, and safety of all people we serve and work alongside.

**Ready to Build Something Bigger Than Yourself**

If you are excited to create partnerships that change lives and strengthen communities, we would love to hear from you. Your leadership can help families around the world build strength, stability, and self-reliance through shelter.

**Apply today and help us build a world where everyone has a decent place to live.**

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$97,300.00 USD

\-

$144,775 USD

/

Annual

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. We strive to build a culture rooted in learning, accountability and trust, attracting and retaining mission-driven talent reflective of the global communities we serve.

**Equal Opportunity Employer Statement:**

As an equal opportunity employer, we realize our success depends on courageously committing to being a workplace where all staff feel safe, welcome, visible, respected, supported and valued, and building a workforce that reflects a variety of lived experiences, backgrounds and perspectives, in which every person experiences dignity and respect.

jobs.title: Communications Officer
jobs.description:
## **About CBM**

CBM (registered as CBM Christoffel-Blindenmission Christian Blind Mission e.V.) is an international development organisation committed to improving the quality of life of persons with disabilities in the persons communities of the world. Based on our Christian values and more than 100 years of professional expertise, we address poverty as a cause and a consequence of disability. We work in partnership to create an inclusive society for all.

**About the role:**
We are looking for a Communications & Visibility Officer to support the implementation of communication and visibility activities across our programmes in Ukraine.
In this role, you will help ensure that CBM’s work is effectively communicated and visible, in line with donor requirements (including EU ECHO), while contributing to storytelling, content development, and stakeholder engagement.
**This position is fixed-term until 31.07.28 and only filled locally. With contractual conditions of the respective country. An expatriation is not intended.**

## **These are your responsibilities**

Communication Planning & Compliance

- Support the development and implementation of the country programme’s communication and visibility plan in line with CBM and donor requirements (including EU ECHO)
- Ensure all communication and visibility actions comply with EU ECHO guidelines (logos, disclaimers, funding acknowledgement)
- Contribute to communication approaches tailored to different stakeholder groups

Content Development & Storytelling

- Draft and edit communication materials such as briefing notes, situation updates, reports, and other internal and external content
- Develop and share content across CBM communication channels (website, social media, newsletters)
- Collect and develop human-interest stories, case studies, and testimonies, ensuring ethical storytelling and informed consent
- Capture and produce photo and video content, including basic filming and editing, in line with donor requirements

Visibility & Outreach

- Support the planning and implementation of visibility activities (events, campaigns, field visits, media engagement), primarily from Kyiv
- Assist in organising trainings, workshops, and outreach activities
- Contribute to communication and promotional activities across projects

Coordination & Partner Support

- Work with implementing partners to ensure appropriate visibility of EU funding at project sites
- Provide basic guidance and support to partners on EU ECHO communication and visibility standards

Monitoring, Reporting & Knowledge Management

- Monitor and document communication and visibility activities, ensuring proper archiving
- Support reporting requirements related to communication and visibility
- Collaborate with MEAL teams to develop communication products that support learning and accountability

## **These are your qualifications**

- A bachelor’s degree in communications, public relations, journalism, media studies, or a related field (or equivalent experience)
- Strong practical skills in content creation, including writing, photography, and basic video production/editing
- Proficiency in Adobe Creative Cloud (InDesign, Illustrator, Photoshop, Premiere Pro) and/or similar tools (e.g. Canva)
- A good eye for visual storytelling, including composition and lighting
- Familiarity with communication strategies, branding, and visibility guidelines
- Experience in using social media platforms and digital communication tools
- Ability to draft clear, engaging content for different audiences
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, particularly for compliance and reporting
- Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a team
- Professional proficiency in Ukrainian; English is an asset
- Experience with EU or other institutional donor-funded projects is an advantage
- Identification with the Christian values and mandate of CBM

## **What we offer**

- A meaningful position with a lot of creative freedom in the world's leading organisation in the field of Disability Inclusive Development
- A fair salary and other social benefits based on the local conditions in the country you apply for
- An approachable, agile organisation with self-reliant people in a diverse and collegial team and great team spirit

jobs.title: Referral Coordination Officer
jobs.description:
## I. Background

Raising Awareness of the Dangers of Irregular Migration II (RADIM II) is a migration-focused project implemented by Seefar. The project operates across six governorates in Federal Iraq including Baghdad, Basra, Dhi Qar, Babylon, Nineveh, and Al-Muthanna. RADIM II aims to reduce irregular migration by strengthening awareness at individual and community level, providing targeted psychosocial and practical support to at-risk youth, and connecting individuals to viable local and overseas alternatives.

A core element of RADIM II is offering young people one-to-one advisory calls to share information on irregular migration and connect those eligible to local alternatives or Seefar’s legal migration pathways service.

## II. Objective of the Position

Seefar is seeking a Referral Coordination Officer to connect young people with local service providers as well as Seefar’s legal migration pathway service “Dalil”, and to ensure they receive support that meets Seefar’s standards. This is a remote, part-time assignment, expected to run from mid-November 2026 to mid-April 2027

## III. Key Responsibilities

- Receive potential referrals from counsellors, prioritise cases and plan the monthly call schedule.
- Contact each young person to check whether their circumstances have changed since counselling and understand their current needs and aspirations.
- Explain the suitable support options available to them, whether a local service provider or a legal migration pathway, and support them to make an informed choice.
- Obtain informed consent and refer 100 young people to the chosen service provider in their governorate, or to Seefar’s legal migration pathways expert.
- Follow up to confirm whether they have accessed the service and, where they haven’t, understand what is holding them back.
- Identify and escalate any safeguarding concerns in line with Seefar’s procedures.
- Keep accurate records of all contacts and referral outcomes until each case is closed.
- Record every follow-up call and keep each person’s referral status up to date until the case is closed.
- Attend and lead weekly counselling status meetings, sharing referral updates, supporting counsellors with reaching targets, track progress, and discuss challenges.
- Attend \[monthly / quarterly\] review meetings with referral partner organisations and support the Project Manager in reviewing referral numbers, outcomes, challenges and any changes to services.

## IV. Remuneration

You will be paid GBP 800 (approx. USD1,000) per month for a maximum of five months, with an expectation that you work approximately 20 hours per week. The workload might vary from month to month depending on the number of referrals taking place.

## V. Qualifications and Experience

You should apply if you meet most or all of the following criteria:

### Essential

- Bachelor’s degree in social work, psychology, sociology, development studies or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.
- At least two years’ experience in case management, referrals, community outreach or similar roles, ideally with young people.
- Good knowledge of local services, NGOs and support organisations in the programme governorates.
- Strong communication skills, with the ability to build trust quickly over the phone and hold sensitive conversations.
- Fluency in Arabic and English.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to manage a caseload, prioritise cases and meet monthly referral targets.
- Accurate record-keeping and confidence using databases or spreadsheets to track calls and referral status.
- Understanding of confidentiality, informed consent and safeguarding principles.
- Reside in one of the project governorates.

### Desirable

- Experience working on migration, livelihoods, protection or youth programmes.
- Persistent and motivating, especially when encouraging young people to follow through on referrals.
- Able to work independently and remotely while staying in close contact with counsellors and the wider team.
- Experience supporting young people’s psychosocial wellbeing and motivating them to take positive steps
