jobs.title: Mozambique - Head of Finance and Administrative department (M/F) - PEMBA
jobs.description:
## About us

**Desired start date: 03/01/2027**
**Duration of the mission: 6 months**
**Location: Pemba**

**SOLIDARITES INTERNATIONAL (SI)** is an international humanitarian aid association which, since more than 40 years, has been providing assistance to populations affected by armed conflicts and natural disasters by meeting their basic needs for food, water and shelter. Particularly committed to the fight against diseases linked to unsafe water, the leading cause of death in the world, SI's interventions provide expertise in the field of access to drinking water, sanitation and hygiene promotion, but also in the essential area of food security and livelihoods. Present in 26 countries, the SI teams – 3200 people in total, made up of expatriates, national staff, permanent staff at HQ, and a few volunteers - intervene with professionalism and commitment while respecting cultural norms.

## About the mission

Solidarités International (SI) has been providing life-saving assistance in northern Mozambique since March 2019, initially responding to Cyclone Idai. As the crisis in Cabo Delgado escalated, SI began operations in Mueda in July 2021 and progressively expanded to other northern districts including Nangade, Muidumbe, Palma and, more recently, Mocímboa da Praia. By 2022, SI had established a coordination office in Pemba and operational bases in Mueda and Palma.
Following the closure of the Palma base, SI opened a new base in Mocímboa da Praia in July 2023 to support urgent returnee needs. Today, SI operates from Pemba, Mueda and Mocímboa da Praia, covering not only the northern districts (Mueda, Mocímboa da Praia, Nangade, Muidumbe and Palma) but also additional districts further south, such as Metuge, Chiúre, Mecúfi and Ancuabe.
In 2024–2025, SI Mozambique has prioritized integrated, multisectoral programming focused on the Rapid Response Mechanism (RRM), WASH, Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL), and Shelter/NFI. At the beginning of 2025, however, major BHA funding cuts forced a significant restructuring, reducing the mission from approximately 140 to around 50 staff and prompting a reorganization of operations to maintain essential activities.
This restructuring coincided with a deterioration of the security situation in Cabo Delgado, with renewed attacks, increased displacement, and unpredictable access since mid-2024, requiring continuous adaptation of SI’s strategies.
In 2026, despite these challenges, SI continues to deliver principled, needs-based assistance across Cabo Delgado with the support of key donors such as ECHO, SDC, CDCS, OCHA, IFSAN and UNICEF while exploring emergency and nexus funding opportunities with other donors such as DG INTPA, adapting its WASH strategy and stenghtening its FSL expertise,

## About the job

**GENERAL OBJECTIVE:**

The administrative coordinator will direct and coordinate all administrative, accounting and financial services associated with the mission.
He/she will take part in defining Solidarités International’s human resources policy and ensure that it is followed.
As coordinator, he is responsible for the mission’s financial balance.
He/she will monitor adherence to Solidarités administrative procedures and donor procedures as well as to the laws of the country in which intervention is taking place.
He/she is the point of reference for the mission, and the link between headquarters and the mission for all administrative matters.

**THE MAIN CHALLENGES:**

• Complex and evolving Mozambican legal and administrative environment
• Visa and work permit procedures for expatriates remain lengthy and restrictive
• Young mission with a relatively new team requiring training, coaching, and mentoring
• In 2025 and 2026, the mission went through rapid decline and growth of its budget which led to signfiicant delays in accounting closure, budget management and reporting.

**PRIORITIES FOR THE 2/3 FIRST MONTHS:**

• Stabilised the implementation of the shared costs policy

• Strengthen and build the capacities of the HR and Finance newly nationalised teams

• Ensure ongoing capacity building and follow-up with the local partner organizations.

• Support the development of new financial proposals, including budget preparation

• Implement SI's new financial software in Mozambique

• Streghten internal control, conduct internal audit and lead on the financial aspects of the external audits

**SECURITY CONSTRAINTS:**

Very limited security constraints in Pemba where the position is based ; with regular visits of one to two weeks visits in the different bases.
Mueda and Chiure – more restrictions; movement and activities depend on local conditions and Security Department guidance.

## Your profile

**DIPLOMA AND EXPERIENCE:**

Diploma : Minimumum Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Business Administration,Social sciences , Organization Development or related HR discipline

Experience in the humanitarian sector : 3/4 years

Experience on a similar position : 3/4 years

**SKILLS:**

TECHNICAL SKILLS

1. In-depth technical knowledge of the principles and concepts in HR administration (workforce and organizational planning,recruitment & selection , compensation and benefits , performance management, Training and development, employee relations, staff health and safety, and employee engagement), HR-good-practices, HR information systems and databases; / Knowledgeand experience working with SI HR procedures and tools is a major plus
2. Mastery of budget and accounting management, shared costs requirement, donors' financial requirements, audit management
3. Experience in capacity building and setting frameworks for staff development
4. Experience leading workplace investigation and supporting resolution of employee relations / Knowledge of Mozambique labout law is a plus

TRANSVERSAL SKILLS

1. coordination and management skills
2. training and facilitation skills
3. Diplomacy

**LANGUAGE:**

1. English mandatory
2. Portuguese is desirable
3. Spanish a plus if no portuguese

## SI will offer you

**A salaried position:**
**According to experience,** starting from EUR 2860 gross per month (2600 base salary + 10% annual leave allowance paid monthly) and a monthly Per Diem of USD 750.

SI also covers accommodation costs and travel expenses between the expatriate's country of origin and the place of assignment.

**Breaks:** During the assignment, a system of alternation between work and time off is implemented at the rate of 7 working days every three months (with a USD 850 break allowance, allocated by Sl). To these breaks periods, SI grants one (1) additional rest day per month worked.

**Insurance package:** Expatriates benefit from an insurance package which refunds all healthcare expenses (including medical and surgical expenses, dental care and ophthalmological expenses, repatriation) and a welfare system including war risks. Essential vaccination and antimalarial treatment costs are refunded.

**LIVING CONDITIONS:**

Pemba is a peaceful coastal city with beautiful beaches, seafood, and a wide range of restaurants and leisure activities. There is no curfew, and walking is allowed during the day for expatriates. Many international NGOs are present. The guesthouse offers comfortable living conditions for expatriates with stable water and electricity. Internet connectivity is reliable (4G). Both bases are reachable by UNHAS flight in less than one hour.

jobs.title: Warehouse Assistant - EVD Emergency Response (Consultant)
jobs.company: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies
jobs.description:
About Us

Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS) is a faith-based health solutions provider founded by an ecumenical partnership of the Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops (KCCB) and the Christian Health Association of Kenya (CHAK). The Organization’s core mandate is providing access to quality health products and technologies through Supply Chain, Quality Assurance and Health Systems Strengthening services. MEDS was established in 1986 and serves clients spread throughout Kenya, other regions in Africa and beyond.

Project Summary

MEDS is implementing the Dawa za Ubora Project, funded by the United States Government (USG) through the U.S. Department of State (DoS) under the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and other Global Health Programs, running until June 2028. Under this mandate, MEDS provides efficient, reliable, and accountable supply chain management services for the warehousing and distribution of health commodities across all 47 counties in Kenya, supporting the prevention, treatment and management of communicable diseases and other health priorities.

About the Role

The Warehouse Assistant (Consultant) for the Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) Emergency Response Initiative under Dawa za Ubora provides hands on operational and technical support to ensure rapid, secure, and fully compliant handling of emergency medical commodities.

Given the high-risk nature of EVD contingencies, this short-term role focuses on maintaining tight inventory control, cold chain integrity, and strict safety protocols to ensure life-saving health products and personal protective equipment (PPE) reach priority response zones without delay.

Key Responsibilities
Operational Responsibilities
a) Oversee receiving activities at Third-Party Logistics (3PL) facilities for all incoming emergency response products, ensuring proper material handling and precise, rapid system posting to protect inventory integrity.
b) Report on the status of inbounds and outbounds of Health Products and Technologies (HPTs) to guarantee strict adherence to established emergency protocols by 3PLs.
c) Execute proper stock rotation protocols (First-Expiring, First-Out / FEFO) to mitigate product spoilage, protect temperature-sensitive emergency assets, and maintain pristine inventory tracking.
d) Participate actively in the preparation of HPTs for rapid emergency shipment, confirming that 3PLs complete accurate labeling, thermal shielding, and secure packaging.
e) Verify all physical HPTs loaded onto transit vehicles against tally sheets and delivery notes during truck dispatch to eliminate field transit discrepancies.
f) Rapidly assemble, pack, and label emergency distribution kits according to dispatch orders destined for high-risk zones, isolation units, or partner facilities.
g) Participate in routine physical stock counts, emergency cycle counts, and reconcile floor records against system balances to guarantee zero stock leakage.
h) Comply fully with all institutional safety regulations, occupational health standards, and emergency hazard protocols to maintain a secure working environment.
i) Address complaints by conducting rapid, thorough investigations, implementing Corrective and Preventive Actions (CAPA), and resolving issues both physically on the floor.
Required Qualifications

Education and experience
• Diploma in a Business-related field, Diploma in Health Systems Management, or an Enrolled Diploma in Pharmacy.
• Recognized training/certificates in Warehouse Management, CIPS, Stores Management, Health Commodities, or Hazardous Materials Handling
• Minimum of 1 years’ hands-on experience with supply chain procedures, FEFO management, and rapid dispatch workflows.

Preferred Skills and competencies
• Working knowledge of supply chain procedures, good distribution practices, and cold-chain management.
• Clear communication, proactive problem solving, analytical mindset, cross-functional collaboration, and absolute professional integrity.
• Proficiency in stock inspection, high-velocity alphanumeric data entry, and MS Office Suite proficiency (specifically MS Excel).
• Strong organizational, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder-coordination skills.
• Strong attention to batch tracking, expiration monitoring, and audit-ready record keeping.

Preferred Attributes
• Ability to work independently under pressure and effectively manage multiple priorities in a rapidly changing environment.
• Willingness to travel to response locations and work outside normal working hours when required.

If you fit the profile of this position, please submit your application providing the following MANDATORY requirement:
i. Detailed CV stating your current or previous positions, expected salary, telephone number, Availability and email address
ii. Academic Certificate
iii. Copy of National Identity Card
iv. Copy of KRA PIN

The final consultancy fee will be determined by Dawa za Ubora based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

jobs.title: Medical Device UniQuality & Unidata Product Information Specialist
jobs.description:
**Location:** Any MSF office\*

**Contract:** Permanent contract at 100%

**Starting date:** 01.12.2026

**Deadline to apply:** The position will close once a suitable candidate has been selected

**Compensation and Benefits:** MSF practice is to offer the compensation and benefits package in line with the MSF entity offering the contract

*\*By default, the successful candidate will be offered a contract in the MSF office, able to issue a contract, of their country of residence at the time of application. If no MSF office exists in their country of residence, the successful candidate will be expected to relocate to a country where an MSF office can issue a contract, provided the local legislation allows for that.*

At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. The successful candidate will be expected to comply with the organisation’s safeguarding policies and standards of professional behaviour.

We are committed to removing barriers for people with specific accessibility needs. If you need an adjustment to the recruitment process to be considered for the role, please let us know from the beginning of the selection process.

**I. MSF International**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent, medical humanitarian organisation that delivers emergency aid to people affected by armed conflict, epidemics, healthcare exclusion and natural disasters. MSF offers assistance to people based only on need and irrespective of race, religion, gender or political affiliation. MSF International is the legal entity that binds MSF’s 24 sections, 28 associations and 19 branch offices together. Registered in Switzerland, MSF International provides coordination, information and support to the MSF Movement, as well as implements international projects and initiatives as requested.

**II. POSITION BACKGROUND**

Coordination and Source of Product Information (SPINCO) was created to maintain consistency in the choice of medical and non-medical articles between MSF sections in order to improve MSF interventions, while considering field realities.

SPINCO is the driver for effective collaboration across the movement to deliver a central source of trusted product information that enables continuous process improvements. SPINCO contributes to MSF’s social mission by enabling improvements in field operations through the provision of product information to all layers of the organization. This enables product quality and visibility for better quality of care, enables assortment management, improvement in supply chain performance and increases overall interoperability whilst reducing duplication of effort. SPINCO’s core role is coordinating the expression of the demand of articles (medical and non-medical) and ensuring it is properly translated for supply whose role is to fulfil that demand.

In 2018, UniQuality was implemented as the unique central quality assurance database of MSF, containing the quality assured drugs, medical devices and specialised food validated for use in MSF projects. It is used by the MSF International Pharmacist Network, International Specialised Foods Network, and International Medical Devices/In-vitro Diagnostics Network, and Supply Centres to allow access to the most up-to-date validated product-manufacturer information.

In 2022, the UniMed project was launched to connect UniQuality to the supply centres’ ERP systems and automate the dissemination of the information regarding medicines and specialized food, to ensure the accuracy and consistency of quality review information. This position will support the completion of UniQuality for Medical Devices and IVDs in preparation of the linkage of both systems for this category of products as well.

In 2024 the Medical Device Repository, a SharePoint library for regulatory, quality and technical documents, went live to facilitate importation procedures with a direct access for field teams, and to keep product validation documentation after assessment by IO and ESC QA referents.

In 2025, the NexSpin project was launched to replace the existing solutions including UniQuality and the MD repository by a new Product Information Management System aiming at improving operational efficiency, user experience and user interface. This requires cleaning of the existing solutions, providing input to the NexSpin team as key users and being involved in the implementation phase scheduled in 2027.

Medical Device UniQuality & Unidata Product Information Specialist open-end position (100%).

**III. PLACE IN THE ORGANISATION**

- The person reports to the SPINCO Product Information Specialists Coordinator with a functional reporting line to the Deputy Quality Assurance coordinator for Medical Devices.
- The person will closely coordinate with the Data-Owners in the International QA MD Coordination team and the European Supply Centres.

**IV. OBJECTIVES OF THE POSITION**

This position is focused on Medical Devices (MD). The objective of the position is to ensure that information related to Entities and Quality Review in UniQuality and the MD Repository is complete, accurate and available for the relevant MSF stakeholders. By guaranteeing the compliance with Quality Assurance processes, the Uniquality Data Steward’s role is to safeguard the quality of information in UniQuality and the MD repository, as well as the consistency between both tools.

They will act as primary point of contact for all stakeholders in case of questions about rules or non-conformity of information contained in UniQuality. They will develop a plan to gradually introduce a data quality and reporting plan to ensure that trust is maintained.

The Unidata Product Information Specialist role contributes to MSF social mission by ensuring the availability of trusted, standardized, and high-quality product information. This role supports field operations, supply chain performance, and interoperability through centralized data stewardship, product portfolio management, and collaboration with diverse stakeholders.

**V. MAIN RESPONSIBILITIES**

**A. UniQuality Data Steward**

**1. Management of Entities in UniQuality:**

- Currently close to 1300 MD international entities in UQ
- Create, validate and update MD entities according to the relevant SOP, more specifically:
- Create new entities upon request of ESCs QA referents and Spinco data stewards (creation of a new article code), by verifying the availability of documents in the MD Repository for manufacturers not existing in UQ
- Support the update/cleaning of the ESC database of entities.
- Approve the entities for MD International purchase by checking for completeness of data in relevant public database, e.g. Eudamed, FDA registration, Conformity Assessment Bodies database for ISO certificates
- Update the entities (name / address) according to new supplier information received from ESC and by regularly checking public database

**2. Management of ISO certificates**

- Close to 1000 ISO certificates in the MD repository
- Search for online information: manufacturer’s website, Conformity Assessment Bodies and Accreditation Bodies database
- Ensure that information related to ISO certificates in UQ and in the MD Repository are updated and consistent, especially for entities associated to quality reviews.
- Request updated documentation to the ESC referents or regulatory assistants.
- Update the list of the certification bodies in UQ and the related information: NB number, accreditation, link to online directories for certificates verification

**3. MD Repository**

- Currently around 9000 documents in total, will grow as quality reviews are completed
- Ensure that the rules set for the uploading and tagging of regulatory and quality documentation in the MD repository are followed by all stakeholders, i.e., IO MD QA Coordination, supply centers QA referents and regulatory assistants, RA Pharma, and field users.
- Check regularly recently uploaded documents: naming of file is correct, tagging is completed, certificates information in UQ (ISO and EU/CE certificate) is updated, duplicates are removed
- Assist the end-users with practical use of the MD Repository and report issues to the helpdesk if needed.

**4. Eudamed**

- Follow up the use of the different modules in Eudamed: changes of activities, new documentation and information available. Inform the QA referents of changes.
- Train the different groups (ESC QA referents, intersection pharmacists) in the practical use of Eudamed.
- Liaise with the Spinco development team for the possibilities to link with Eudamed in Uniquality

**5. General UniQuality / MD Repository**

- Propose improvements and updates of SOP for UniQuality and the MD Repository as necessary, in collaboration with the product owners and in agreement with the main stakeholders
- Propose an action plan to review and improve the quality of information aligned with the needs and work capacity of the stakeholders.
- Implement an annual report/control on data quality of UniQuality and the MD repository by defining the quality criteria and setting the KPI in collaboration with the MD QA coordination
- Train new UniQuality / MD Repository users by developing e-learning tools, and organizing training sessions in collaboration with the UQ product owner

**B. Unidata Product Information specialist**

**1. Product Information Management**

- Monitor, evaluate, and process requests for new, modified, or removed products in alignment with MSF guidelines, protocols and standards.
- Consolidate and validate information on product description, quality, pricing, field testing, and maintenance requirements for approval by the Medical Directors' platform.
- Ensure product availability and suitability for field use by collaborating with QA teams, buyers, and regional hubs.
- Owns the data product lifecycle and technical specifications
- Ensures the product meets user needs and use cases
- Prioritises improvements and manages changes over time

**2. Harmonization and Interoperability**

- Collaborate with intersectional platforms, supply centres and field operations to standardize products across MSF operations.
- Facilitate resource sharing and intersectional field operations by ensuring product harmonization.
- Promote responsible use of product data to balance efficiency, cost, and humanitarian mission.

**3. Data Stewardship**

- Ensure and maintain the high quality of product information in terms of accuracy, validity, consistency, completeness, uniqueness and accessibility of product information in the UniData tool, MSF central article database.
- Ensure UniData serves as the single source of truth for downstream systems (e.g., ERP, UniQuality, order tools).
- Govern the central database and ensure compliance with regulatory standards (e.g., EU norms, ISO standards, IATA transport regulations).
- Promote consistency and usability by maintaining aligned definitions (Knowledge database, KPIs) and making data fit for decision-making.
- Support continuous improvement by identifying data issues, proposing enhancements, and acting as a bridge between technical team and IT

**4. Data ownership: accessibility and visibility**

- Responsible and accountable for the accessibility and visibility of product information
- Publish product information on accessible platforms (web, intranet, offline tools) for global MSF staff.
- Act as the focal point for central database governance and user support.

**5. Process Design and Improvement**

- Responsible and accountable for data governance: how product information is defined, created and used
- Design, implement, and enhance processes related to data requirements, product codification, and multilingual labelling.
- Pushing data governance by setting the direction and objectives
- Actively promoting improved data governance practices (RACI).
- Ensure product information data supports reliable operational & strategic decision-making
- Publish annual summaries of medical product changes and updates to MSF catalogues.
- Publish monthly reports on medial product changes for the ESC referents and medical referents of the OC/OD’s
- Develop policies, guidelines, and training materials for approximately 1,700 database users.

**6. Collaboration and Stakeholder Engagement**

- Work closely with MSF field staff, headquarters, Quality Assurance teams, tactical buyers and intersectional platforms to ensure product standardization and quality of product information.
- Participate in international projects with NGOs and UN sectors, such as emergency health kits and medical device nomenclature initiatives.

**VI. SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE ROLE**

The incumbent commits to contribute to a safe, supportive, inclusive, equitable, diverse, respectful, and healthy workplace, free from abuse and other misconduct. They will not engage in any form of abuse including those detailed in MSF Typologies of Abuse and when an employee suspects or observes abuse, they will report it to protect others.

**VII. REQUIREMENTS**

- Master’s degree in scientific, engineering, pharmacy or paramedical sciences
- Detail-oriented, meticulous and organized for data entry/modification in database is essential
- Computer & analytical skills, including MS Excel are essential
- Knowlegde of Medical Devices regulatory environment (MDR/IVDR) and ISO standards is a plus
- Proficiency in English (both speaking and writing) and knowledge of French
- MSF field or Supply experience in a medical position is an asset
- Fast learner, able to adapt quickly to a changing environment
- Customer oriented, resilient, with good people and communication skills
- Self-motivated, with an interest in problem solving
- Excellent time management skills, with the ability to prioritise and multi-task depending on the needs.
- Technical writing capacities.

**Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.**

**At MSF, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, races, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.**

**MSF is committed to preventing abuse, inappropriate behaviour, lack of integrity and financial misconduct in its work and care spaces. MSF expects all staff to share this commitment and promote an environment where abuse and misconduct is not tolerated.**

jobs.title: Warehouse Officer – EVD Emergency Response (Consultant)
jobs.company: Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies
jobs.description:
About Us

Mission for Essential Drugs and Supplies (MEDS) is a faith-based health solutions provider founded by an ecumenical partnership of the Kenya Conference of Catholic Bishops (KCCB) and the Christian Health Association of Kenya (CHAK). The Organization’s core mandate is providing access to quality health products and technologies through Supply Chain, Quality Assurance and Health Systems Strengthening services. MEDS was established in 1986 and serves clients spread throughout Kenya, other regions in Africa and beyond.

Project Summary

MEDS is implementing the Dawa za Ubora Project, funded by the United States Government (USG) through the U.S. Department of State (DoS) under the President’s Emergency Plan for AIDS Relief (PEPFAR) and other Global Health Programs, running until June 2028. Under this mandate, MEDS provides efficient, reliable, and accountable supply chain management services for the warehousing and distribution of health commodities across all 47 counties in Kenya, supporting the prevention, treatment and management of communicable diseases and other health priorities.

About the Role

The Warehouse Officer coordinates the receipt, storage, inventory control, order verification, and dispatch of EVD emergency response commodities at MEDS and designated third-party logistics providers (3PLs). The Officer maintains stock visibility, product integrity, and audit-ready records, and escalates supply risks to support timely and accountable delivery against approved emergency allocations.
The role covers approved response supplies, including personal protective equipment (PPE), infection prevention and control (IPC) supplies, medical consumables, and other designated HPTs. Activities must comply with approved standard operating procedures, applicable good storage and distribution practices, manufacturer requirements, and relevant Ministry of Health guidance.
This role does not include clinical care, handling infectious specimens, managing contaminated returns, or undertaking specialist decontamination. These activities require authorized specialist arrangements.
Key Responsibilities
Receipt and inbound verification
• Coordinate the receipt of approved EVD response commodities, including applicable USG-funded products, at MEDS and designated 3PL warehouses.
• Verify quantities, product descriptions, batch or lot numbers, expiry dates, packaging condition, and supporting documentation.
• Record receipts promptly and escalate any discrepancies to the designated supervisor.
Storage, inventory control and stock visibility
• Maintain accurate stock locations, batch-level records, and inventory-system records for all emergency commodities.
• Apply first-expiry, first-out (FEFO) stock-rotation principles to expiry-dated commodities.
• Conduct risk-based cycle counts and scheduled physical stock counts; reconcile physical balances with system records, investigate variances, and submit adjustments for approval.
• Prepare and submit daily emergency stock-status reports covering receipts, dispatches, available and allocated stock, outstanding orders, consumption trends where available, and supply risks.
• promptly flag shortages, stockouts, near-expiry items, and replenishment needs to the designated supervisor.
Order fulfilment, kitting and dispatch
• Coordinate picking, packing, labelling, and staging of approved emergency orders and response kits.
• Verify kit contents against approved packing lists and support pre-positioning in line with authorized allocations and response priorities.
• Verify goods for loading against approved orders, packing lists, and delivery documentation; confirm quantities, batch details, destination, packaging integrity, and transport requirements.
• Coordinate with transport teams and response focal persons on urgent dispatches, daily warehouse priorities, and agreed emergency turnaround times.
• Retain signed handover and proof-of-delivery records for all dispatched consignments.
• Escalate capacity constraints, delayed deliveries, and other risks affecting timely dispatch.
Warehouse conditions, product quality and non-conformance
• Monitor warehouse cleanliness, organization, access control, pest control, and storage conditions at MEDS and 3PL facilities.
• Ensure temperature-sensitive commodities are handled only within validated storage and transport arrangements; escalate temperature excursions for quality assessment before release.
• Segregate damaged, expired, recalled, or suspect products and prevent their release pending authorized quality decisions.
• Verify compliance with approved quality-control and good storage and distribution procedures at 3PL facilities.
• Maintain traceability for emergency commodities and support authorized recalls, quality investigations, and disposition of non-conforming stock in liaison with the quality assurance team.
Occupational safety and infection prevention
• Implement approved occupational safety and warehouse IPC procedures, including task-appropriate PPE, safe material handling, and prompt incident reporting.
• Escalate suspected contamination or exposure to designated IPC and safety personnel.
• Do not accept potentially contaminated items into routine stock, manage contaminated returns, or undertake specialist decontamination; these activities require authorized specialist arrangements.
Discrepancy management and continuous improvement
• Investigate and document delivery discrepancies and client complaints.
• Reconcile associated physical and system records and identify root causes.
• Implement approved corrective and preventive actions (CAPA), track actions to closure, and provide feedback to the requesting team.
Required Qualifications

Education and experience
• Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Humanitarian Logistics, Public Health, Business Administration, Bachelor of Commerce or a related field.
• Relevant specialized Level 4 (and equivalent operational-tier) supply chain certifications such CPSP-K, APICS CPIM, APICS CLTD, CILT, CIPS, CHL, MLP (Medical Logistics in Pandemics & Outbreaks).
• Minimum of 3 years’ experience in logistics, supply chain management, humanitarian response, emergency response, or public health programs.
• Demonstrated experience in medical supply chains, pharmaceutical distribution, or cold-chain logistics emergency, disaster response, or other fast-paced operational environments preferred. Experience coordinating warehouse, transport, and distribution activities in emergency or health programs.
• Experience working with donors, government agencies, United Nations agencies, or humanitarian logistics partners.
• Prior experience in EVD, cholera, COVID-19, or other infectious disease emergency response.

Preferred Skills and competencies
• Working knowledge of medical supply chain procedures, good distribution practices, and cold-chain management.
• Familiarity with import, export, customs, and regulatory documentation requirements for health commodities.
• Proficiency in inventory management systems, supply chain tracking tools, and Microsoft Office applications.
• Strong organizational, problem-solving, communication, and stakeholder-coordination skills.
• Strong organizational, problem-solving, and stakeholder coordination skills.

Preferred Attributes
• Ability to work independently under pressure and effectively manage multiple priorities in a rapidly changing environment.
• Familiarity with Kenya’s health supply chain system, Ministry of Health structures, and humanitarian coordination mechanisms.
• Willingness to travel to response locations and work outside normal working hours when required.

If you fit the profile of this position, please submit your application providing the following MANDATORY requirement:
i. Detailed CV stating your current or previous positions, expected salary, telephone number, Availability and email address
ii. Academic Certificate
iii. Copy of National Identity Card
iv. Copy of KRA PIN

The final consultancy fee will be determined by Dawa za Ubora based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

jobs.title: MEAL Assistant – Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning
jobs.description:
## **1. Background**

Habibi Association was founded in Italy in 2013 to promote social justice and socio-economic inclusion, with a particular focus on refugee protection, humanitarian assistance and support for people experiencing poverty or affected by conflict. The Association is recognised as a Civil Society Organisation by the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation (*Agenzia Italiana per la Cooperazione allo Sviluppo – AICS*) and operates in several countries across the Middle East.

In 2018, Habibi Association registered with Jordan’s Ministry of Social Development and has since implemented projects supporting refugees and vulnerable members of host communities, with particular attention to women, young people and persons with disabilities.

Habibi Association is seeking a **MEAL Assistant** to support the implementation and development of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities across its projects in Jordan, ensuring the quality and effective use of project data.

## **2. Key Responsibilities**

Reporting to the MEAL Officer and working closely with Project Managers, the MEAL Assistant will be responsible for the following:

**A. Monitoring, Evaluation and Data Management**

- Support the implementation of projects’ MEAL plans and monitoring tools, including logical frameworks, project monitoring plans, indicator tracking tables and project databases.
- Support the design, adaptation and digitalisation of data collection tools, ensuring that data is systematically disaggregated by sex, age, displacement status, disability and other relevant vulnerability criteria.
- Conduct field visits to project implementation areas, currently including Amman, Zarqa, Maan, Mafraq, Madaba, Ader and Petra, to monitor progress, document challenges and verify reported results.
- Support baseline, midline and endline assessments, post-distribution monitoring and beneficiary satisfaction surveys.
- Contribute to data cleaning, validation and Data Quality Assessments (DQAs), ensuring that collected information is accurate, consistent and reliable.
- Analyse quantitative and qualitative data and contribute to the preparation of monitoring reports, donor reports and other project documentation.
- Support needs assessments and the development of new project proposals through data collection, analysis and the identification of relevant indicators.

**B. Accountability and Learning**

- Support the establishment and management of accessible Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs), ensuring the confidential recording, follow-up and analysis of feedback in accordance with established procedures.
- Contribute to the analysis of feedback and monitoring findings to identify trends, challenges and opportunities for improving project implementation.
- Support project reflection sessions and the documentation of lessons learned and success stories, ensuring that findings are evidence-based and contribute to organisational learning.
- Provide technical support to project teams and implementation partners on MEAL tools, data collection procedures and reporting requirements.

**C. Coordination and Organisational Support**

- Participate in internal project meetings and coordination meetings with consortium partners, as required.
- Collaborate closely with Project Managers and teams, implementation partners and relevant external stakeholders.

## **3. Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Degree in Social Sciences, Political Science, International Relations, International Cooperation, Statistics or a related field.

**Professional Experience and Technical Skills**

- At least two years of relevant professional experience in monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning activities, preferably within development or humanitarian projects.
- Practical experience with MEAL frameworks, indicator tracking tools, digital data collection and project databases.
- Knowledge of quantitative and qualitative data collection methods, data cleaning and validation, data quality assurance, and the preparation of analytical reports.
- Familiarity with Complaints and Feedback Mechanisms (CFMs) and accountability to affected populations.
- Good command of IT tools and standard office software. Experience with KoboToolbox or other digital data collection and management software will be considered an asset.
- Valid driving licence and ability to drive in Jordan.

**Languages**

- Advanced proficiency in Arabic, both written and spoken.
- Proficiency in English, both written and spoken.

**Personal and Interpersonal Skills**

- Excellent communication and interpersonal skills, including the ability to work constructively with people from diverse backgrounds.
- A proactive, solution-oriented approach and the ability to respond effectively to challenges.
- Strong organisational skills, attention to detail and commitment to meeting deadlines.
- Ability to handle sensitive information responsibly and maintain confidentiality.
- Commitment to social inclusion, child protection, gender equality and the rights and dignity of vulnerable and marginalised people.
- Willingness and availability to travel regularly to project locations outside Amman.

## **4. Contractual Conditions**

- **Duty station:** Amman, Jordan.
- **Contract duration:** 12 months.
- **Expected starting date:** December 2026 / January 2027.
- **Gross monthly salary:** JOD 850–950, depending on the candidate’s qualifications and relevant experience.

jobs.title: Mission France - Coordinateur.rice de projet adjoint.e F/H
jobs.description:
Médecins Sans Frontières, association médicale humanitaire internationale créée en 1971, apporte une assistance médicale à des populations dont la vie est menacée : principalement en cas de conflits armés, mais aussi d'épidémies, de pandémies, de catastrophes naturelles ou encore d'exclusion des soins.

La mission France recherche un.e Coordinateur.rice de projet adjoint.e pour son projet au Littoral Nord.

**Contexte :**

Médecins Sans Frontières intervient en France auprès des personnes exilées confrontées aux conséquences sanitaires, psychologiques et sociales des violences liées aux parcours migratoires et aux ruptures de protection. La Mission France combine soins, protection et témoignage pour répondre aux besoins des personnes les plus vulnérables.

Elle concentre aujourd’hui son action sur le Littoral Nord et en Île-de-France, tout en conservant une capacité de réponse rapide aux situations d’urgence. Portée par des équipes pluridisciplinaires, elle développe des activités médicales, psychologiques, sociales et de plaidoyer dans un contexte en constante évolution.

Dans un contexte de forte vulnérabilité des personnes exilées à la frontière franco-britannique, le projet Littoral Nord vise à améliorer l’accès aux soins et à la protection des publics les plus exposés, tout en documentant les impacts sanitaires, psychologiques et sociaux des politiques migratoires. Il constitue un axe stratégique de la Mission France, à l’interface entre opérations de secours et plaidoyer.

**Votre rôle :**

Aux côtés du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, vous participerez au pilotage des opérations, à l’organisation des activités et à l’accompagnement des équipes dans un contexte exigeant et en constante évolution. Vous contribuerez à l’analyse des besoins et des risques, à la coordination des interventions et à la qualité de la prise en charge. En l’absence du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, vous assurerez la continuité de la coordination.

Vous assisterez également le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet dans la planification, la coordination et le suivi des activités de MSF sur le Littoral Nord, afin de garantir une réponse cohérente, sûre et adaptée aux besoins des personnes exilées.

**Principales responsabilités :**

Favoriser une communication claire et respectueuse entre les personnes accompagnées et les équipes MSF, en atténuant les barrières linguistiques, les incompréhensions culturelles et les discriminations, afin de contribuer à un accès équitable à des soins et à un accompagnement adaptés.

**Vos principales responsabilités :**

**Contribuer à la coordination des opérations sur le terrain**

- Participer à la transition des projets de Calais et Dunkerque vers un projet Littoral Nord intégré.
- Contribuer à l’organisation et au suivi des activités sur les lieux de consultation, les lieux de survie et les plages ou zones de départ.
- En l’absence du ou de la coordinateur·rice de projet, assurer la coordination des activités et la continuité opérationnelle.
- Organiser, avec les responsables de pôle, la participation des équipes aux maraudes de prévention et de prise en charge des personnes lors des tentatives de traversée.
- Veiller à l’application des protocoles opérationnels et de sécurité, notamment les briefings et débriefings et les procédures liées aux distributions.
- En lien avec le ou la référent·e pluridisciplinaire du projet Migration, contribuer à la coordination entre les équipes et à la qualité de la prise en charge, dans le respect du secret médical partagé et des standards MSF.

**Analyser le contexte et contribuer à la représentation de MSF**

- Participer au suivi du contexte politique, humanitaire et sécuritaire à la frontière et faire remonter les évolutions susceptibles d’affecter les opérations.
- Contribuer aux missions exploratoires sur le littoral, notamment en dehors des zones d’intervention actuelles de Calais et Dunkerque, afin d’identifier les besoins et les priorités.
- Assurer le lien avec les acteurs du littoral et participer aux réunions de coordination.
- En collaboration avec le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet, contribuer à la représentation de MSF auprès des autorités, des services publics, des forces de l’ordre, des associations, de la société civile et des médias.
- Participer aux actions de communication et de plaidoyer liées aux interventions de MSF sur le littoral.

**Accompagner les équipes et veiller à la sécurité**

- Contribuer à l’organisation des ressources humaines, à l’intégration du nouveau personnel, au suivi quotidien des équipes et à l’identification des besoins de formation.
- Participer à l’analyse des risques et à la mise à jour des consignes de sécurité ; être le point focal sécurité lors des interventions selon les responsabilités définies pour le projet.
- Soutenir les équipes dans la mise en œuvre des activités et assurer la transmission des informations opérationnelles.
- Promouvoir les principes de safeguarding et veiller à leur compréhension et à leur application au sein de l’équipe et du projet.

**Assurer le suivi, la qualité et le reporting des activités**

- Superviser ou contribuer à la compilation et à l’analyse des données collectées, ainsi qu’au reporting des activités.
- Veiller au respect des standards MSF et à la qualité de la prise en charge pendant les interventions, notamment en matière de distributions et de safeguarding.
- En collaboration avec le ou la coordinateur·rice de projet, contribuer à l’accompagnement des équipes de support, notamment logistique et RH/finance.
- Participer à l’identification de pistes de plaidoyer en lien avec la présence de MSF lors des tentatives de traversée.

**Profil recherché**

**Formation et expérience :**

- Diplôme universitaire de niveau bac+3 minimum.
- Au moins deux ans d’expérience en gestion de projet, dans l’aide humanitaire, au sein de MSF, d’une autre ONG ou d’une association.
- Expérience en gestion d’équipe.
- Une expérience dans des contextes migratoires est souhaitée.

**Qualités :**

- Capacité d’analyse et vision stratégique.
- Leadership et aptitude à accompagner les équipes.
- Sens de l’organisation, de la planification et des priorités.
- Esprit d’équipe et capacité à coopérer avec des interlocuteurs variés.
- Gestion du stress, flexibilité et capacité d’adaptation à un environnement changeant et exigeant, y compris lors d’interventions de nuit.
- Maîtrise des outils informatiques de base, notamment Word, Excel et Internet.
- Permis B obligatoire.

**Langues et outils :**

- Maîtrise du français indispensable.
- Bonne connaissance de l’anglais souhaitée.
- La maîtrise d’autres langues est un plus.

**Conditions d'emploi**

**Mobilité exigée sur le Littoral Nord entre Calais et Dunkerque**

Statut non-cadre : **CDD de 12 mois renouvelable**

**Rémunération et avantages :**

- **3 598,40 € brut mensuel sur 13 mois** 22 jours de RTT par an
- Complémentaire santé prise en charge à 100 % par MSF·
- Titres-restaurant de 12 € (prise en charge MSF à 60 %)·
- Prise en charge à 50 % des transports en commun ou des kilomètres à vélo

**Poste à pourvoir :** 18 janvier 2027
