jobs.title: Program Manager I – Community Based Health Insurance
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Program Manager I - Community Based Health Insurance

**Reports to:** Program Manager II

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by November 6, 2026 no later than 11:59pm.

**Note:** CRS is recruiting in anticipation of an award – recruitment for all candidates is contingent upon successful award of the project.

**Job Summary**

CRS is seeking to hire for an anticipated five-year health systems strengthening project in Uganda. The project aims to support the sustainability and resilience of faith-based health services through strengthened institutional capacity, improved community health financing mechanisms, enhanced governance, and locally led solutions that contribute to improved health outcomes. As the **Program** **Manager I - Community Based Health Insurance (CBHI),** you will provide strategic technical leadership and support in the design, implementation, monitoring, learning, and scale-up of Community Health Insurance and other community health financing approaches. You will provide technical advice and support on a range of program design and implementation issues in line with CRS program quality principles and standards, donor requirements, and global best practices to advance the delivery of high-quality programming for poor and vulnerable communities. Your advice, knowledge, and support will contribute to determining how effective, adaptive and innovative CRS’ Community Health Insurance programming is across the globe.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Support the development and contribute to the implementation of CRS agency-wide strategies, technical standards, tools, and best practices in Community Based Health Insurance (CBHI) and community health financing ensuring alignment with donor requirements, government priorities, and global best practices. Help ensure a cross-sectoral approach integrating gender, safeguarding and protection mainstreaming, and local leadership.
- Provide technical leadership and guidance to project teams and partners on the design, implementation, monitoring, and adaptation of CBHI interventions. Work closely with partner staff to strengthen technical quality, facilitate joint problem-solving, and promote local ownership of project implementation and results.
- Provide technical solutions to CP and partner teams, remotely and on-site, for strategic planning and how to best apply standards, best practices, partnership principles, tools and M&E, helping to ensure high-quality implementation. Accompany local partners to strengthen their technical leadership, decision-making, and implementation capacity while fostering equitable partnerships and mutual accountability.
- Cultivate strong working relationships with local partner organizations and support partner-led implementation through regular engagement, joint planning, technical accompaniment, and learning. Contribute to partner capacity strengthening strategies and help ensure that principles of localization, mutual accountability, and local leadership are embedded throughout project implementation.
- Contribute to the development of the technical design for proposals. Support the process of preparation, design, submission and approval of project concepts and full-fledged proposals. As needed, act as a technical writer on proposal development teams. Advise project teams on integrating donor strategies, priorities and technical requirements into CRS’ approach.
- Support capacity strengthening initiatives in Community Based Health Insurance (CBHI) for community, and partners through helping develop learning and training strategies and agendas/curriculums, conducting trainings and workshops, and coaching. Promote partner-led learning, adaptation, and sustainability of project approaches beyond the life of the award.
- Collect and analyze program data, capture and share lessons learned and best practices for specific projects to facilitate improvements in decision-making and contribute to CRS’ learning agenda and technical excellence in community health financing.
- Contribute to maintaining relationships with donors, peer organizations, research and other institutions, participate in Health forums to collect and share best practices and promote CRS’ work.
- Represent CRS in technical working groups, professional networks, policy dialogues, conferences, and sector forums related to health financing, universal health coverage, and health systems strengthening.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in actuarial science, Development Studies, Social Science, Economics, Health Services Management, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field required.
- Minimum of five-eight relevant work experience with progressive responsibilities, ideally with an international NGO. At least two years of field-based experience in community health insurance, health financing, health systems strengthening, or related areas.

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master’s degree in actuarial science, Economics, Public Health, Health Financing, Health Systems Management, Business Administration, Development Studies, Social Sciences, or a related field is an advantage.
- Knowledge of Uganda's health financing, health insurance, and Universal Health Coverage (UHC) landscape
- Experience working in partnerships with local organizations and supporting partner-led implementation through technical accompaniment, capacity strengthening, coaching, and organizational development.
- Experience in an international NGO an advantage

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- Proficient in MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information and budget management systems, knowledge-sharing networks.
- Knowledge of technical principles and concepts in insurance Health financing. General knowledge of other related disciplines to ensure a proper cross-sectoral approach.
- Experience in project design and proposal development. Experience in writing content for proposals.
- Knowledge of capacity-strengthening best practices.
- Experience with program monitoring and evaluation and analysis.
- Experience and skills in networking and relations with donors, peer organizations, and faith-based civil society partners. Understanding of partnership principles.
- Strong relationship management skills with ability to influence and get buy-in from people not under direct supervision and to work with individuals in diverse geographical and cultural settings
- Good strategic, analytical, problem-solving and systems thinking skills with capacity to see the big picture and ability to make sound judgment
- Good technical writing skills
- Presentation, facilitation, training, mentoring, and coaching skills
- Proactive, resourceful and results-oriented

**Required Languages** - Fluency in English required

**Travel** - Must be willing and able to travel up to 40%.

**Supervisory Responsibilities -** Field Officers

**Key Working Relationships:**

Internal: CRS Country Representative, Head of Programs, Head of Operations, Uganda-based technical experts for MEAL, Gender, Youth and Social Inclusion (GYSI) and Partner Capacity Strengthening (PCS), technical health team, Regional and Headquarters technical staff.

External: Local partner staff, representatives from for-profit and other non-profit organizations and relevant national, district, sub-county, parish and other government stakeholders, community leaders.

*\*\*\*Our Catholic identity is at the heart of our mission and operations. Catholic Relief Services carries out the commitment of the Bishops of the United States to assist the poor and vulnerable overseas. We welcome as a part of our staff people of all faiths and secular traditions who share our values and our commitment to serving those in need. CRS’ processes and policies reflect our commitment to protecting children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.*

*Disclaimer: This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skill, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.*

**CRS' talent acquisition procedures reflect our commitment to protecting children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.**

**CRS is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.
- **Agency Leadership Competencies:**
- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

jobs.title: Gestor de casos de violencia basada en género (VBG) - Carúpano
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Gestor/a de Casos de Violencia Basada en Género (VBG)** altamente calificado con sede en **Carúpano, Sucre.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL CARGO**

Bajo la supervisión directa de la Gerencia de Protección de la base, el/la Gestor/a de Casos de VBG apoyará la implementación en terreno del componente de respuesta y atención a la Violencia Basada en Género (VBG) en el marco de las intervenciones humanitarias de DRC Venezuela. La persona seleccionada será responsable de brindar atención individualizada directa a personas sobrevivientes de VBG y personas en riesgo bajo el modelo de Gestión de Casos de VBG, garantizando el cumplimiento de los principios rectores (enfoque centrado en la persona sobreviviente, confidencialidad, seguridad, respeto y no discriminación).

Asimismo, integrará un enfoque diferencial de Edad, Género y Diversidad (AGD), interseccionalidad y derechos humanos, asegurando el adecuado mapeo, articulación y derivación con servicios especializados (salud, legal, protección infantil, apoyo psicosocial) y actores institucionales locales (Consejos de Protección de NNA, Defensoría del Pueblo, Ministerio Público, Centros de Salud), contribuyendo al fortalecimiento de los entornos de protección comunitarios y a la calidad de la información del programa.

**RESPONSABILIDADES**

- Implementar el ciclo completo del modelo de Gestión de Casos de VBG (evaluación, plan de atención, seguimiento y cierre), brindando Primera Ayuda Psicológica bajo principios de estricta confidencialidad y consentimiento informado.
- Elaborar planes de seguridad individualizados junto con las personas sobrevivientes para mitigar sus factores de riesgo.
- Gestionar derivaciones seguras y oportunas a servicios especializados (atención médica/atención postexposición, asesoría legal, atención en salud mental y apoyo psicosocial y/o alojamiento).
- Mantener actualizado el mapeo local de actores y rutas de atención (CPNNA, Fiscalía, Defensorías, centros de salud, etc.).
- Facilitar sesiones comunitarias de sensibilización sobre prevención de VBG, derechos humanos y rutas de atención, promoviendo la inclusión de mujeres, niñas, personas con discapacidad y población OSIEGD.
- Registrar de manera oportuna, segura y confidencial la información de los casos en las plataformas internas (KoBo, bases de datos), garantizando la entrega de insumos mensuales para reportes programáticos y donantes.
- Garantizar la aplicación transversal de la Política de Edad, Género y Diversidad (AGD), la Rendición de Cuentas (AAP), el enfoque de No Hacer Daño (Do No Harm) y los estándares de Prevención de la Explotación y el Abuso Sexual (PEAS).
- Participar en reuniones de seguimiento técnico, supervisión de casos y coordinación interinstitucional según los requerimientos operativos de la base.

**REQUISITOS, EXPERIENCIA Y COMPETENCIAS TÉCNICAS:**

**Educación:**

- Pregrado / Titulación universitaria en Ciencias Sociales, Salud o Humanidades (Psicología, Trabajo Social, Sociología, Orientación o áreas afines).

**Experiencia laboral:**

- Mínimo dos (2) años de experiencia práctica relevante en atención directa a personas sobrevivientes de VBG, gestión de casos de VBG o implementación de programas de protección de género/apoyo psicosocial.
- Experiencia demostrable en el trabajo con comunidades en situación de vulnerabilidad, población en movilidad/migración, comunidades rurales, indígenas o personas OSIEGD.
- Mínimo un (1) año de experiencia en contextos humanitarios o de cooperación internacional (deseable en el contexto venezolano).

**Conocimientos técnicos:**

- Dominio del modelo de Gestión de Casos de VBG y de las Directrices del IASC para la integración de intervenciones contra la Violencia Basada en Género en la Acción Humanitaria.
- Conocimiento del marco normativo nacional venezolano (Ley Orgánica sobre el Derecho de las
- Mujeres a una Vida Libre de Violencia, LOPNNA, entre otros) y de los servicios de atención institucionales y comunitarios.

jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. jobs.title: Oficial de Gestión de Casos - Caracas
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Gestión de Casos** altamente calificado con sede en **Caracas.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y tres oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del propósito / objetivo del cargo:**

Evaluar los casos remitidos por actores externos u otros sectores internos del DRC para la provisión de servicios de asistencia humanitaria complementaria de protección, EcRec y Ayuda Legal. Ser responsable por el desempeño eficaz y profesional de las actividades del proyecto. Con labores en oficina base Caracas con misiones frecuentes a Miranda y La Guaira.

- Bajo la supervisión del Líder de Equipo de Gestión de Casos de Protección, el/la Oficial de Gestión de Casos será responsable de recibir, evaluar, gestionar, acompañar y remitir casos con necesidades específicas de protección (salud, medicamentos de emergencia, apoyo psicosocial, transporte humanitario, alojamiento de emergencia, artículos en especie y ayuda legal).
- Remitirá de forma segura casos con criterios de VBG y PNNA a otros actores especializados y continuará la respuesta de ser necesario, con el resto de los miembros de los grupos familiares expuestos a otros riesgos de protección.
- Desarrollará y mantendrá buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas relevantes y otros actores humanitarios, para facilitar la implementación y coordinación adecuadas de las actividades de los proyectos de DRC-Caracas.
- Apoyar al Líder de Equipo de Gestión de Casos de Protección en garantizar la calidad de la planificación, implementación, seguimiento de las actividades de protección, dando cumplimento a los planes de acción construidos y priorizados en conjunto con las personas de interés.

**Responsabilidades:**

**Implementación del Proyecto de Protección.**

- Recibir remisiones externas e internas de casos de personas con necesidades específicas de protección, asignadas por la TL de manera equitativa a cada oficial y proceder con la evaluación de riesgo y gestión de casos una vez sean analizados los perfiles de protección según los criterios fijados por DRC.
- Coordinar con otras unidades del DRC, actores externos y organizaciones humanitarias para la respuesta integral de la gestión de los casos.
- Asegurar el consentimiento informado de las personas beneficiarias, y la asistencia humanitaria necesaria para abordar las necesidades de protección identificadas.
- Garantizar una escucha activa de las personas beneficiarias, con el objetivo de identificar el servicio de asistencia humanitaria más apropiado para abordar las necesidades de protección identificadas.
- Registrar los casos recibidos y aceptados en las carpetas correspondientes y bases de datos de la organización.
- Mantener actualizada constantemente la información contenida en las herramientas de gestión de casos.
- Manejar la información confidencial de manera correcta, gestionando los archivos físicos y digitales de protección de manera precisa, correcta y completa.
- Desarrollar planes de acción para abordar las necesidades específicas identificadas procediendo a entregar la asistencia humanitaria, incluidos los servicios médicos, agua, saneamiento e higiene, educación, alojamiento de emergencia, de transporte para reunificación familiar y entrega de artículos en especie.
- Asegurar la entrega de la asistencia humanitaria identificada manejando solicitudes de compras y, por ende, estableciendo articulación con el equipo de soporte quien será el encargado de articular con los proveedores de servicios.
- Asegurar la correcta legalización de los gastos efectuados para la provisión de servicios de asistencia humanitaria.
- Asegurar el seguimiento de los casos averiguando la satisfacción de los beneficiarios en la recepción de servicios.
- Asegurar el cierre de casos en un tiempo adecuado al marco de emergencia en el cual se implementa.
- Proporcionar información para informes semanales, mensuales, trimestrales y anuales según requerido por la persona Líder de Gestión de Casos de Protección o Gerente de Protección.
- Asegurar la más alta calidad de las intervenciones de gestión de casos y la coherencia entre todos los proyectos en curso y propuestos, de acuerdo con la estrategia general;
- Seguir los planes de trabajo y las directrices del proyecto manteniendo los principios de confidencialidad.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva del proyecto mientras sigue el plan de trabajo.
- Participar en la preparación de informes y presupuestos mensuales.
- Participar en la implementación de actividades generales de protección de acuerdo con los objetivos acordados.
- Monitorear y documentar continuamente las necesidades de las personas de interés en los formatos de seguimientos, además del desarrollo de planes de acción en un tiempo oportuno según sea el nivel de riesgo.
- Llevar a cabo tareas básicas dentro del área de protección, incluyendo recolección de datos, identificación de patrones y tendencias, como llegadas / salidas / nuevos flujos de personas de interés en el área, etc.
- Apoyar en otras actividades de programa y de los equipos multidisciplinarios del DRC base Caracas.

**Competencias esenciales:**

- Mínimo 2 años de experiencia relevante en protección humanitaria, de preferencia Gestión de Casos de Protección, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.

- Experiencia y habilidades demostradas en protección humanitaria y un enfoque diferencial en respuestas de protección.

jobs.title: Program Manager II
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** Program Manager II

**Reports to:** Head of Programming

**Department:** Programming

**Location:** Kampala

This position is open to **Ugandan nationals only**

**Deadline:** Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Candidates are encouraged to apply by November 6, 2026 no later than 11:59pm.

**Note:** CRS is recruiting in anticipation of an award – recruitment for all candidates is contingent upon successful award of the project.

**Job Summary:**

CRS is seeking to hire for an anticipated five-year health systems strengthening project in Uganda. The project aims to support the sustainability and resilience of faith-based health services through strengthened institutional capacity, improved community health financing mechanisms, enhanced governance, and locally led solutions that contribute to improved health outcomes. As **Program Manager II** of this project, you will lead, manage, and provide technical oversight for the development, implementation, and monitoring of project activities. You will ensure high-quality program delivery, effective coordination with faith-based and government stakeholders, strong partnership management, and compliance with donor and CRS requirements., advancing Catholic Relief Services’ (CRS) work in serving the poor and vulnerable. The Program Manager II will oversee project planning, budgeting, reporting, learning, and adaptive management while fostering locally led solutions that strengthen health systems, improve community health financing mechanisms, enhance governance, and contribute to sustainable health outcomes.

**Roles and Key Responsibilities:**

- Lead, manage and implement all activities throughout the project cycle, including start-up, implementation, monitoring, learning, and close-out, ensuring quality delivery in accordance with CRS program quality standards, donor requirements, and best practices. Ensure project staff and partners effectively utilize approved systems, tools, and processes. Work closely with partner leadership and technical teams to support partner-led implementation, jointly address challenges, and ensure effective coordination throughout project delivery.
- Foster and maintain collaborative relationships with faith-based health institutions, church structures, government entities, private sector actors, and other stakeholders to support project objectives and strengthen health system outcomes.
- Lead the development, implementation, and coordination of community health financing and other innovative approaches that promote sustainable access to quality health services and increased community ownership.
- Identify and cultivate strategic partnerships that contribute to project goals, strengthen local leadership, leverage resources, expertise, and opportunities for improved health outcomes. Support local partners to develop strategic relationships that enhance their influence, credibility, sustainability, and leadership within the health financing ecosystem.
- Serve as the primary point of contact with project stakeholders, ensuring effective communication, coordination, joint planning, and alignment of project activities. Facilitate transparent dialogue, collaborative problem-solving, and shared decision-making to foster trust, mutual accountability, and effective partnership performance.
- Support project design, business development, and proposal development efforts related to health systems strengthening, health programming, and institutional capacity strengthening.
- Strengthen and manage partnerships using CRS partnership principles, tools, and approaches, ensuring mutual accountability, collaboration, and long-term impact. Maintain regular engagement with partner leadership and staff, proactively address partnership challenges, facilitate joint planning and reflection processes, and support implementation of agreed Partnership Capacity Strengthening (PCS) priorities.
- Coordinate and monitor financial and material resources relevant to project needs, through planning and oversight to ensure efficient use of project resources.
- Supervise, coach, and mentor project staff, fostering professional growth, high performance, teamwork, and commitment to CRS values and program quality standards.
- Represent CRS in technical working groups, stakeholder forums, learning events, and coordination meetings at national and sub-national levels, promoting project visibility, collaboration, and influence
- Ensure timely preparation and submission of high-quality technical, financial, and donor reports, while documenting lessons learned, best practices, and project achievements.
- Ensure the integration of safeguarding, accountability, gender, localization, and locally led development approaches across all project activities and partnerships.

**Basic Qualifications**

- Bachelor’s degree in international development, Social Sciences, development studies and Health related management or relevant experience in related field.
- Minimum of 5 years' experience in relevant field-based project management experience required, with preferably at least 3 years’ working experience managing complex health, development, or health systems-strengthening programs in a leadership or management role.
- Experience in managing moderately complex projects

**Preferred Qualifications**

- Master’s degree in public health, Health Systems Management, Health Services Administration, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Business Administration, or related field.
- Experience in an international NGO an advantage
- Experience working in partnerships with local organizations and supporting partner-led implementation through technical accompaniment, capacity strengthening, coaching, and organizational development.

**Knowledge, Skills and Abilities**

- MEAL skills and experience required.
- Staff management experience and abilities that are conducive to a learning environment.
- Experience using MS Windows and MS Office packages (Excel, Word, PowerPoint), Web Conferencing Applications, information management systems.
- Good experience in project grants management, including project design, preferably for grants from multiple public donors, including USG, UN and other relevant donors
- Demonstrated ability to write high-quality technical proposals.
- Experience engaging with partner organizations
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with ability to make sound judgment and decisions and offer innovative solutions
- Strong relations management abilities. Ability to relate to people at all levels internally and externally. Strategic in how you approach each relationship.
- Good presentation and facilitation skills
- Proactive, resourceful, solutions-oriented and results-oriented
- Strong written and verbal communication skills with ability to write reports

**Required Languages** - Fluency in English is required

**Travel** - Must be willing and able to travel up to 40%.

**Supervisory Responsibilities -** Program Manager I – Community Based Health Insurance, Project Manager – MEAL.

**Key Working Relationships:**

Internal: CRS Country Representative, Head of Programs, Head of Operations, Uganda-based technical experts for MEAL, Gender, Youth and Social Inclusion (GYSI) and Partner Capacity Strengthening (PCS), Technical Health team, Regional and Headquarters technical staff.

External: Local partner staff, representatives from for-profit and other non-profit organizations and relevant national, district, sub-county, parish and other government stakeholders, community leaders.

*\*\*\*Our Catholic identity is at the heart of our mission and operations. Catholic Relief Services carries out the commitment of the Bishops of the United States to assist the poor and vulnerable overseas. We welcome as a part of our staff people of all faiths and secular traditions who share our values and our commitment to serving those in need. CRS’ processes and policies reflect our commitment to protecting children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.*

*Disclaimer: This job description is not an exhaustive list of the skill, effort, duties, and responsibilities associated with the position.*

**CRS' talent acquisition procedures reflect our commitment to protecting children and vulnerable adults from abuse and exploitation.**

**CRS is an Equal Opportunity Employer**

**Agency Competencies (for all CRS Staff):**

- **Personal Accountability** – Consistently takes responsibility for one’s own actions.
- **Acts with Integrity** - Consistently models values aligned with CRS Guiding Principles and mission. Is considered honest.
- **Builds and Maintains Trust** - Shows consistency between words and actions.
- **Collaborates with Others** – Works effectively in intercultural and diverse teams.
- **Open to Learn** – Seeks out experiences that may change perspective or provide an opportunity to learn new things.
- **Agency Leadership Competencies:**
- **Lead Change** – Continually looks for ways to improve the agency through a culture of agility, openness, and innovation.
- **Develops and Recognizes Others** – Builds the capacity of staff to reach their full potential and enhance team and agency performance.
- **Strategic Mindset** – Understands role in translating, communicating, and implementing agency strategy and team priorities.

jobs.title: PSS and Community Development Unit Manager
jobs.description:
**Job Title:** PSS and Community Development Unit Manager

**Location:** Erbil, Kurdistan Region of Iraq (KRI), with regular travel to other areas of KRI.

**Type of position:** Employment contract

**Length of Contract:** 12 Months

**Compensation and Benefits:** Competitive salary and benefits commensurate with skills and experience. Expatriate/National Compensation Package: includes local transportation allowances, Medical insurance and Life insurance

**About SEED**: SEED is a women-led, local NGO in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, dedicated to creating a thriving society by advancing social protection and human development. We support individuals, empower communities, and strengthen systems to drive lasting change and equal opportunity. With a focus on collaboration, we promote gender equality, protect children, combat human trafficking, and improve mental health and well-being. SEED’s holistic, locally-driven approach integrates transformational services, community development, training and education, and advocacy to create sustainable impact. SEED is committed to creating a just, equitable society where everyone's rights are protected, with healthy families and strong communities, and a future where everyone can thrive.

**Role of the PSS and Community Development Unit Manager:**

SEED is seeking a dynamic and experienced Psychosocial Support (PSS) and Community Development (CD) Manager to lead the PSS/CD Unit and guide on SEED’s strategic objective of engaging and empowering communities. The PSS/CD Manager will lead and plan for the implementation of community-based programming aimed at engaging and empowering communities towards the development of a strong, healthy, resilient, and cohesive society through community-based initiatives designed to foster social and emotional well-being, prevent violence and discrimination, and promote social and economic empowerment. The PSS/CD Manager will oversee and support the technical/thematic leads and implementation of PSS/CD programming across thematic pillars, various programs, and locations across Kurdistan. The Manager will lead a team to design, manage, adapt, and support implementation of programming that improves MH and psychosocial wellbeing, achieves gender equality and ends GBV, and protects children and empowers their development. The PSS/CD Unit Manager will work in close collaboration with the MEAL Unit to ensure communities are involved from the start until the end of each program and that feedback is collected and the learnings are at the foundation of any future programming and requests for funding. This position requires a leader with both a deep understanding of psychosocial support and the ability to design community-driven interventions that promote positive social behaviors. The role also includes managing PSS resources, managing staff and building their capacity, and planning and guiding the strategic direction and execution of SEED’s community programming. The ideal candidate will bring strong leadership, planning and management skills, along with technical expertise in PSS, community development, promoting equality and combating gender-based violence (GBV), protection, mental health (MH), social behavioral change, and social cohesion programs, and a passion for empowering communities through transformative, locally driven change. The PSS/CD Unit Manager will oversee the 3 Technical Thematic Leads and ensure activities are appropriately tailored to the needs of each community. This position is based in Erbil with frequent travel required to Sulaimani and surrounding areas.

**Specific Tasks:**

**Management, Leadership, and Technical Support (60%):**

- Lead and manage SEED’s PSS/CD Unit and its 3 Technical Thematic Leads, and provide strategic direction to SEED on its cross-cutting strategic objective to engage and empower communities.
- Develop technical strategies, guidelines, and standards for the unit and provide strategic direction and day-to-day management of SEED’s PSS and community development programming.
- Oversee development, adaptation and dissemination of technical resources, including group curricula, training manuals, facilitator guides, and standardized tools for PSS and community development interventions created by the Technical Thematic Leads.
- Support the Technical Thematic Leads with the design, adaptation and delivery of awareness-raising sessions, PSS group activities, and community development interventions.
- Collaborate with Program Managers and Coordinators to align community needs with interventions and ensure technical quality and consistency across projects.
- Ensure the formation of community led initiatives, social cohesion activities, and social behavioral change (SBC) programming.
- Ensure PSS teams have PSS outreach plans for all locations and provide inputs into new partnerships engagement.
- Identify, mitigate and manage risks related to program delivery, partnerships, safeguarding and community dynamics
- Develop policies related to PSS program implementation and community engagement and accountability.
- Ensure the development of partnerships to enhance SEED’s PSS portfolio.
- Ensure that all activities are implemented in accordance with donor requirements, organizational policies, and international standards and practices.
- Set project direction by prioritizing and organizing actions & resources to achieve objectives.
- Provide input into program development pertaining to SEED’s PSS/CD work.
- Support the recruitment, interviewing, and onboarding of Thematic Leads, PSS facilitators and coordinators working on various programs and across locations.

**Reporting, MEAL, and Communications (30%)**

- Work closely with the MEAL unit to ensure communities are actively engaged throughout the whole programming cycle.
- Support with the development and adaptation of MEAL tools that collect information from communities, stakeholders, and other relevant parties to ensure community based ownership.
- Monitor implementation quality and adapt programming based on learning and community feedback.
- Ensure quality assessments are taking place to understand community needs prior to starting programs / interventions, and use data to inform program adjustments and quality improvements.
- Contribute to the development of PSS tools to ensure that M&E systems provide adequate feedback.
- Measure impact of interventions through proper feedback mechanisms and data collection.
- Provide input on safe and ethical data collection and storage.
- Contribute to developing articles, flyers, briefs, and other communication materials as needed.
- Provide input into awareness raising campaigns and advocacy strategies on related topics / thematic areas.

**Coordination and Organizational Representation (10%)**

- Identify, build and manage collaborative partnerships with other partners, coordination bodies, local authorities and other stakeholders.
- Represent SEED in meetings with communities, stakeholders, NGOs, KRG, and with donors.
- Develop strategic partnerships and maintain effective working relationships with key stakeholders including donors, government actors, UN agencies, international and local NGOs.
- Work closely with program partners, consultants, contractors, and sub-grantees.
- Conduct external meetings, presentations, or trainings on PSS related topics as requested.

**Key values:**

- Serve as a positive role model and SEED ambassador at all times.
- Treat all people with respect regardless of age, gender, religion, nationality, sexual orientation, disability status, marital status and ethnicity.
- Working collaboratively with all colleagues, and maintaining a positive, cooperative attitude.

**Essential criteria:**

- Master’s degree in Psychology, Social Work, Gender Studies, International Development, Public Health or related field.
- Minimum of 5 years of experience in managing teams and building staff capacity through training, coaching, and supervision.
- Minimum of 7 years of relevant experience in PSS, community engagement, GBV prevention, social behavioral change, MH, and peacebuilding in humanitarian or development settings.
- Strong technical knowledge of gender equality, women and girls empowerment, GBV prevention, and social norm change with experience designing or leading awareness and social behavioral change initiatives.
- Strong knowledge of social change theories and approaches
- Experience in developing culturally sensitive messages and materials.
- Demonstrated leadership, strategic planning, and staff management skills.

jobs.description:

Created in 1979, Action contre la Faim is a non-governmental organization that fights against hunger. Its charter of humanitarian principals- independence, neutrality, non-discrimination, free and direct access to victims, professionalism, transparency - has been part of its identity for 45 years. Its mission is to save lives by eliminating hunger through the prevention, detection and treatment of under-nutrition, particularly during and after emergency situations linked to conflicts or natural disasters. jobs.title: Protection Cluster Co-Coordinator
jobs.description:
**Overall purpose of the role**

DRC co-leads the Sudan Protection Cluster in partnership with UNHCR, the Cluster Lead Agency, in line with Inter-Agency Standing Committee (IASC) and Global Protection Cluster (GPC) standards. The Co-Coordinator provides strategic and operational coordination to strengthen a principled, inclusive and evidence-based protection response across Sudan; elevate the voices of NGOs, particularly national and local actors; promote the centrality of protection across the humanitarian response; and translate protection risks, community priorities and response gaps into collective action, advocacy and resource prioritisation.

**Responsibilities**

Working jointly with the UNHCR Protection Cluster Coordinator and in consultation with cluster members, the Strategic Advisory Group (SAG), subnational structures and relevant Thematic group, the Co-Coordinator delivers the cluster’s agreed functions and workplan. The position complements UNHCR’s formal Cluster Lead Agency accountabilities while providing independent and meaningful NGO co-leadership.

***Protection Cluster Meetings, Information Exchange and Representation***

- Co-chair national Protection Cluster and SAG meetings with UNHCR; agree priorities, facilitate participation, document decisions and follow up on collective commitments.
- Connect national and subnational coordination structures through field missions, mentoring, timely information exchange and support to decentralised or area-based coordination arrangements.
- Promote complementarity with Child Protection, Gender-Based Violence and Mine Action Thematic groups and relevant housing, land and property (HLP) mechanisms, respecting their respective technical mandates.
- Represent agreed cluster positions in the Inter-Cluster Coordination Group (ICCG), relevant Humanitarian Country Team (HCT) engagements, donor dialogues, NGO fora and inter-agency initiatives.
- Maintain constructive coordination with OCHA, UN agencies, NGOs, community-based and women-led organisations, relevant authorities and other sectors, upholding neutrality and humanitarian principles.

***Strategic Planning and Reporting***

- Co-develop and regularly review the Sudan Protection Cluster strategy, workplan and contingency plans with UNHCR, the SAG, Thematic groups and partners, based on evolving conflict, displacement and access trends.
- Lead technical inputs to the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan (HNRP): protection needs, severity and people-in-need analysis, prioritisation, objectives, indicators, targets and financial requirements.
- Identify critical gaps, duplication and underserved locations through field evidence, service mapping, partner reporting and response-monitoring data; support coordinated corrective action.
- Support rapid-onset emergency coordination, field assessments, preparedness and integrated/mobile protection response approaches, with clear referral and operational linkages.
- Liaise with donors to mobilize resources for the joint protection response and update donors on protection cluster priorities and needs
- Contribute to the HCT centrality of protection agenda and to evidence-based inter-cluster priorities, advocacy, periodic situation reporting and response performance reviews.

***Capacity Building, Trainings and Promotion of Protection Mainstreaming***

- Provide technical guidance and capacity strengthening for partners and subnational coordinators on protection standards, risk analysis, safe referrals, protection monitoring and operational guidance/SOPs.
- Advance protection mainstreaming across sectors, including safe and equitable access, dignity, do no harm, GBV risk mitigation, child safeguarding, PSEA, accountability and age, gender and disability inclusion.
- Promote meaningful participation and leadership of national/local NGOs, women-led and community-based organisations; strengthen inclusive decision-making and locally led responses.
- Support harmonised technical guidance on cash for protection, coordinated mobile responses, safe referrals and other agreed protection interventions.

***Protection Tools and Protection Information Analysis***

- Coordinate harmonised protection monitoring, key informant interviews, field assessments and the Protection Analytical Framework; oversee analysis of protection risks, geographic severity, access constraints and emerging threats.
- Produce or coordinate Protection Analysis Updates, protection alerts, advocacy briefs, needs/gap analyses, and other timely, action-oriented information products for humanitarian decision-makers.
- Facilitate evidence-based collective protection advocacy on attacks against civilians, unsafe displacement and return, movement restrictions, violence, discrimination and denial of essential services.
- Work with information-management colleagues and Thematic groups to maintain reliable 5W/service-mapping, referral, response-monitoring and severity-analysis tools, with appropriate validation and disaggregation.
- Apply data responsibility, confidentiality, informed consent and survivor-centred standards; prevent unsafe collection or disclosure of sensitive individual protection data.
- Support the leading of Protection Information Management (PIM) systems to identify and address field-based protection concerns through state-level clusters and partner organisations

***Promote and Support Accountability to Affected Populations***

- Ensure affected people, including IDPs, returnees, host communities and persons at heightened risk, inform protection analysis, priorities, response design and feedback processes.
- Strengthen safe, confidential and accessible referral pathways and community feedback mechanisms, and encourage coordinated action on gaps and barriers to services.
- Promote adherence to humanitarian principles, international humanitarian and human rights law, safeguarding, PSEA and protection-sensitive approaches to movement, return and durable solutions.

***Qualifications, Experience and Technical Competencies***

- Postgraduate degree in international law, social sciences, humanitarian studies or a related field.
- At least three years of relevant humanitarian protection experience in complex emergencies; substantial inter-agency coordination experience, preferably in a Protection Cluster/Sector leadership role.
- Demonstrated expertise in protection risk analysis, monitoring, the humanitarian programme cycle, preparedness, coordination and collective advocacy.
- Strong understanding of IASC/GPC guidance, Thematic group mandates, protection principles, international humanitarian/human rights law and safe information management.
- Sound understanding of humanitarian coordination, funding, and leadership mechanisms, as well as experience in working with protection cluster coordination
- Proven ability to facilitate diverse partnerships, engage senior humanitarian leadership/donors, and draft concise, high-quality strategic and analytical products.
- Excellent understanding of protection issues in emergency and displacement situations, detailed knowledge of humanitarian principles, guidelines for humanitarian assistance, and relevant international legal frameworks
- Experience in Sudan or a comparable conflict-affected context, with field coordination, localisation and capacity strengthening, is strongly desirable.
- Excellent advocacy and representation skills including the ability to develop strong interpersonal relationships to facilitate communication within the cluster

**Languages:**

- Advanced Proficiency in written and spoken English.
- Fluency in Arabic is strongly desireable

**About you**

*In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:*

- *Striving for excellence:* You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.
- *Collaborating:* You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.
- *Taking the lead:* You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.
- *Communicating:* You listen and speak effectively and honestly.
- *Demonstrating integrity*: Upholding and promoting the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to DRC’s values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**Conditions**

*Contract:* One-year contract with possibility of extension, subject to funding and performance. Salary and conditions in accordance with the Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for International staff. This position is graded at Band NM.F

*Start Date:* December 2026

*Duty Station:* Khartoum, Sudan (with regular field travel)

Reports to: Country Director

jobs.title: Finance Partnerships Officer-Damascus
jobs.description:
**Background/Context:**

The IRC has operated in Syria since 2012, providing protection, health, economic recovery, and early childhood development programs in Idleb, Aleppo, Ar-Raqqa, Hassakeh, and Deir ez-Zor, with new programs expanding into Hama, rural Damascus, and Homs. With a team of over 750 members, the IRC has established trust and strong community relationships, ensuring access and effective service delivery. It plays a significant role in Syria’s NGO, donor, and coordination forums, holding key positions and adapting to the evolving context.

With the new realities under the new government, as of December 2024, the IRC has deployed a team to Damascus to set up operations and engage in coordination structures for newly accessible areas across Syria—including parts of NES, NWS, and other previously unreachable locations in South and Central Syria, adjusting operations to maximize coverage and efficiency.

**Job overview:**

The Partnerships Finance Officer is responsible for providing financial management to ensure that the country program has the appropriate financial structure and systems in place to support the partnerships' strategic ambitions. This position is responsible for ensuring effective partnership finance management, including timely advances/payments to partners to ensure program and service continuity in accordance with partnership agreements, and timely expense booking and reconciliations and timely action to resolve any challenges with financial management. The Partnership Finance Officer support partnership finance manager for the financial and compliance aspects of the Partnerships Department, including ensuring high-quality financial monitoring and support of the partners in the Syria country program. Under the support of the Finance Partnership Manager, the Partnerships Finance Officer will actively develop and roll out all initiatives related to capacity building of partners in collaboration with the partnership team and the finance staff. This position reports directly to the Finance Partnership Manager of the Syria country program.

**Responsibilities:**

**Partnerships Financial Management**

- Ensure effective partnership agreement finance management, including timely advances/payments to partners to ensure program and service continuity in accordance with partnership agreements as well PEER, and work closely with FM for timely action to resolve any challenges during work related implementation.
- Follow up with IRC HQ and partners to confirm transfer and receipt of payments, respectively. And update FM for any expected delays or challenges.
- Timely Initial verification of partner’s submitted financial reports and expense booking, making sure the reconciliation provided by partner is aligned with the ledger information. In case of any discrepancies, report immediately to FM, and do necessary communication and correction actively in close coordination with Partnership finance manager.
- In close coordination with FM, monthly review for the balance sheet accounts (partner advance, Partner Liability, Hawala), and control accounts as well expense accounts, ensuring the transaction currency and reporting currency are correctly presenting the partner’s accounting procedures.
- Implementing IRC partnership accounting procedures by applying the applicable SOP.
- Make sure accounting procedures are followed correctly and actively contribute on monthly closure in terms of partners’ accounting analysis and correction actives.
- Participate effectively in the month closure and Year end closure process.
- Give hands to the finance units at difficult times of pressure such as audit and month and year end closure.
- Being expert Integra user, making sure all partners accounting passed to the system with correct coding and currencies and sufficient supporting documents and correct posting profiles. Explore system troubleshooting, and be familiar with system errors, agilely fix the system errors and report to subject matter expert for those errors which need technical insight.
- Settle advance/ liability transactions on timely manner on system and making sure the ledger presents the partner’s financial position at any time.
- Close coordination with Partnership finance manager, Finance Coordinator-Accounting & Audit, in terms of timely partner’s accounting and reconciliation.
- Support FM in verification of partners’ financial reports and support documentation, ensuring that expenses are reasonable, allowable, and allocable to the approved budget and align with the donor’s regulations. Communicate findings to Partnership finance manager and ensure timely follow-up to provide solutions and document the findings. Reviews must be driven by contract guidance IRC policies and donor rules and regulations and based on partner risk and sampling or review of full documentation, as required.
- In close coordination with FM, ensure proactive communication with the partners about the submission of their financial reports according to the terms of their sub-awards. Ensure tracking of the partners' submission of financial reports, communicating delays to the Partnerships Coordinator, through Finance partnership manager.
- Ensuring that the sub-awardee financial reports are approved (signed) by the appropriate authority within IRC, preparing the Journal Voucher, fully coding and posting it to the system after final review from FM, under supervision of FM, respond to questions that arise from the Syria finance team and IRC HQ and audit regarding submitted financial reports.
- Do financial monitoring and spot check visits to sub-awardee offices are conducted according to IRC requirements and standards.
- Under direction of FM, ensure Partner monitoring visit plans are drafted and submitted ahead of visits to review and share monitoring visit reports in a timely manner to partners, the related Program team, and the Syria Partnerships Coordinator as well partnership finance manager after review from FM.
- Reconciling the partnerships' advances on a monthly basis or quarterly based on agreement reporting requirements. reports to partnership finance manager on all overdue, unliquidated advances, and updates daily bases dynamic and online tracking payment & expenses & partner updates sheets for sub-grants finances.
- Ensure that a sound, accurate, and organized archiving system is in place, both hard and soft (electronic) copies for all financial reports and their supporting documents and in line with IRC ERP system.
- Work with the partnership finance manager and Syria Partnerships Coordinator and the Finance team to collaborate on internal and external audits to ensure proper compliance with all regulations and to ensure that all sub-awardee files in hard and soft copy are always 100% audit ready, report samples through FM to partners and do follow up for complete submission, initial review for the provided documents from parter before sharing with FM for final review.
- Support Partnership finance manager that Partnership Capacity Analysis (PCA) is conducted for all new potential partners, as well as updating the PCAs for all existing partners, on an annual basis. Report partnership finance manager and the Partnerships Coordinator in Syria on the findings and provide recommendations for improvement.
- Participating to Partnership Project Opening, Review, and Closure Meetings, including review successes, challenges, and lessons learned with the partner, capturing effective financial practices for future partnerships.
- Provide Financial training and mentoring support to partners, in accordance with partner project support plans, with a focus on supporting the partner to strengthen the Finance systems and capacities that are responsive to the needs of the partner (rather than replicating IRC’s systems and policies).

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- At least a bachelor’s degree in accounting, finance, or any related field.
- Or at least institute degree and finance experience for at least 2 years’ experience in partnership financial work related.

**Work Experience:**

- Minimum 3 years of financial work experience.
- Good understanding of accounting processes and procedures.
- At least 1 years of experience in finance partnership sector in a non-profit setting.
- Experience in managing and handling partners’ projects funded by major institutional donors will be preferable.
- Knowledge of associated with funding from BHA or USAID, EU, UN, BMZ, GFFO, GAC, SIDA or FCDO rules and regulations will be a plus.
- Experience working with databases and/or other tracking software systems.
- Proven track record in developing the capacity of staff and pertners.
- Ability to work under work pressure and willingness\\ ability and flexible enough to work for extra hours when needed.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Computer literate and has strong competencies in MS Office package, especially Excel (e.g common formulas) and outlook
- Any ERP System experience is an advantage.
- Strong ability to work independently, organize work, meet deadlines, maintain composure, prioritize work under pressure, coordinate multiple tasks and maintain attention to details.
- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Credible written, presentation and verbal communication skills; ability to convey information effectively and solid experience providing training and staff development.
- Validated sense of professional discretion, integrity, and ability to handle complex situations diplomatically and to effective resolution.
- Excellent management and interpersonal skills and a solid ability to promote harmonious/cohesive teamwork, in a cross-cultural context.
- Validated ability to plan long-term, organize priorities and work under administrative and programmatic pressures with detail orientation and professional patience.
- Highly collaborative and resourceful; ability to establish positive working relationships with senior level management and all other partners to maximize cooperation and productivity.
- Curiosity, a desire to continually learn and develop is a must.
- Analytical ability in creating effective solutions to complex matters while adhering to labor laws and internal policies.

**Language/Travel:**

- Excellent written and oral communication in both English and Arabic are required; Kurdish is an advantage.
- Travel: 30% to field sites as well as attending regional and global workshops and meetings when required.

**Key Working Relationships:**

**Position Reports to:** Partnership finance manager.

**Position directly supervises**: N/A

**Key Internal Contacts:** Head of Teams (especially, Partnership Coordinator/Manager, Deputy Director - Programs, and the Deputy Director – Finance, Finance coordinator -accounting & audit), Budget Holders, and the Finance department team.

**Key External Contacts:** IRC partner organizations.

**Professional Standards:** IRC staff must adhere to the values and principles outlined in IRC Way – Global Standards for Professional Conduct. These are Integrity, Service, Accountability and Equality. In accordance with these values, IRC operates and carries out policies on Beneficiary Protection from Exploitation and Abuse, Child Safeguarding, Anti-Workplace Harassment, Respect at Work Fiscal Integrity, and Anti-Retaliation.

**Returning National Candidates:** We strongly encourage national or returning national candidates to apply for this position. If you are a citizen of the country where this position is based and are currently residing outside of your home country, you may be eligible for an attractive relocation package. Eligibility is determined based on IRC's operational needs and specific role requirements. IRC strives to attract, motivate, and retain qualified national staff in our programs.

**Accountability to Clients:** IRC staff must adhere to the commitment of contributing to the sustainability and development of its (CR) Client Responsiveness Mechanisms, preserving the culture of prioritizing the needs of our clients and affected communities by systematically listening to their perspectives and using their feedback to make programmatic decisions and give them greater influence over program design and delivery.

jobs.title: Senior Officer - Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (Climate, Natural Resources and Peace)
jobs.description:
This is an exciting opportunity to coordinate monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) activities across an impactful, international, multi-partner programme on water, peace and security. In addition, the successful candidate will also contribute to International Alert’s wider programming on climate and peace.

We are looking for an excellent candidate, with at least five years’ experience working in the development, peacebuilding, water or natural resource management sectors and substantive experience designing and delivering effective MEL. With a proven ability to collaborate, communicate and coordinate effectively with partners in different locations and from a range of sectors, you will support partners, including through training, to design and implement MEL data collection and analysis. In addition, the successful candidate will have the skills to help implement Alert’s projects on climate and peace, supporting evidence generation, policy influencing and advisory activities.

In return, you will have the opportunity to work for a dynamic, motivated and friendly team and the chance to contribute to the organisation’s mission, supporting people to build peace in countries affected by conflict.

**Job Purpose**

The Senior Officer - Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer (SOMEL) supports monitoring, evaluation and learning (MEL) processes across the organisation, helping to ensure that monitoring and evaluation is rigorous, high-quality and fit for purpose, and that learning is embedded in our approach to our work. Reporting to the Head of Peace Integration, the postholder will work with Alert’s network of MEL focal points in our country offices, building a common approach, sharing experiences and developing in-country capacity. They will develop and disseminate tools to enable us to plan for, measure and disseminate the impact of our peacebuilding work. The postholder will oversee annual reflection sessions across the organisation, ensuring we capture the outcomes of our work. The Senior Officer - Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning Officer will coordinate submissions of team annual reports and draft the organisation’s Annual Report.

**Duties & Responsibilities**

**Monitoring and Evaluation**

- Develop and disseminate common Alert M&E tools and resources, including drawing on global best practice to develop new resources when needed.
- Support country and global programmes to design programmes, develop realistic and useable theories of change and establish appropriate monitoring systems at both project and programme level.
- Convene the network of M&E leads across Alert’s programmes, to enable roll out of agreed organisational approaches to M&E, sharing of experiences, learning opportunities and peer support.
- Support capacity building of country programme Alert M&E staff by providing focussed trainings, inductions, and individual advice.
- Coordinate the annual reflection process with partners.

**Impact assessment**

- Oversee the annual reflection process across the organisation, ensuring teams have the necessary resources to undertake reflection sessions, collate and analyse the data.
- Strengthen our Outcome Harvesting (OH) practice, including encouraging facilitation of OH sessions by colleagues from other teams, and enabling partners involvement in OH reflection.
- Support the establishment of an organisational impact reflection and design reflection process
- Support country and global programmes in the design of programme evaluations.

**Learning**

- Establish processes and/or fora for Alert staff to regularly share, learn and challenge one another on peacebuilding practice and policy (in particular on Alert’s priority themes), drawing on internal and external knowledge and experience.
- Monitor developments in MEL practice and apply these to Alert’s approach, ensuring the continuing evolution and improvement of our MEL.

**Organisational contributions**

- Coordinate submissions of team annual reports and draft the organisation’s Annual Report.
- Contribute to internal communications and knowledge management and participate in organisation-wide events and discussions.
- Occasionally supervise volunteers and monitor the work of consultants as required.
- Undertake any other tasks commensurate with the role, as required by the - Head of Peace Integration

**Travel requirements**

Occasional travel to our countries of operation.

**Essential requirements**

- Knowledge of, and experience of applying to development or peacebuilding projects and programmes, monitoring and evaluation approaches and methodologies.
- Experience developing theories of change, indicators and logical frameworks for international development or peacebuilding projects and programmes.
- Understanding of peacebuilding and conflict transformation.
- Experience developing and implementing monitoring and evaluation systems for an organisation.
- Experience undertaking monitoring and evaluation in complex settings (such as fragile states)
- An understanding of current trends in M&E for international development, including using participatory M&E approaches that enable for staff, partners and participants to jointly reflect on the impact of their work.
- Experience working remotely with country teams, supporting and building capacity of others to undertake or plan monitoring and evaluation.
- Experience facilitating workshops, trainings and events, including remotely and with people with diverse first languages.
- Fluent written and spoken English; excellent analytic and report writing skills, including ability to simplify and explain technical issues.
- Excellent interpersonal skills and ability to engage with a wide spectrum of actors, including staff at all levels, partners, peers and donors.
- IT literate, including experience using Excel for budgeting, and using databases.
- Existing permanent right to work in the country in which you wish to be based, in which Alert has a registered office.

**Desirable Requirements**

- Fluent written and spoken French or Russian.
- Experience facilitating and coordinating Outcome Harvesting for a team or an organisation.
- Experience managing projects.
- Experience of cross-organisational coordination.

- The finance assistant should contact all suppliers and ask them to collect their dues on the determined distribution dates. Besides, for other types of payees such as IWS, beneficiaries .... etc. the finance assistant should ask all payments requestors to contact the payees and ask them to collect their dues on the determined distribution dates and follow up with requestors regarding any uncollected amounts to mitigate cash risk.
- Represent finance in the distribution sites if needed, sign & reconcile any related documents. Besides, verify the payees’ identities before disbursing as well as the letter of delegations from staff, suppliers or beneficiaries.
- Pay out all suppliers, incentive workers, vendors, advances, salary of staff when needed and deal with them in high performance of respect and integrity and in line with cash management SOP. Besides, before releasing the payments the finance assistant should make sure that all required approvals/ documents are available (make sure PO match invoice match payment in terms of amount and payee name), and he/she should take quick action and inform the head of finance department and line Supervisor in case of any findings.
- Ensure all documents are labeled as “PAID” once payment is cleared with vendors and in line with Cash management SOP.
- Conduct a cash count daily in a proper and secure way. Verify any discrepancies and report that immediately to the Finance & line managers if not resolved. Maintain cash tracking sheet on daily basis and keep the signed versions of cash count in the cash count file and keep scan copies on BOX, share the final cash count /bank statements after reconciliation with system with FM for action.
- Receive cash refunds from staff/contractors and charge them back to proper account codes, make sure that the receipt Voucher is signed by the staff and approved by the Sr. Finance Officer / Finance Officer.
- Support finance officer in providing any documents needed for audit purposes or any other reason. And help with the finance office admin work such as photocopying and scanning if any.
- Plan, organize and manage workload and be resilient in accepting new assignments and extra working hours during competing priorities.
- Contribute in the month & year end closing to ensure high quality of closing & meeting HQ deadlines. Besides, participate in coordination with the finance officer in the monthly review for the following balance sheet accounts: Cash in office, Petty cash, Advances, Accruals, Prepaid, Vendor payable, Miscellaneous Payables, Miscellaneous Receivable, Hawala/ Cash Transfer Agent/ bank statements.
- Support finance officer in preparing cash requested and fees allocation JVs resulted from: incentive workers payments, NES staff salary payments, drivers’ payments, and vendors payments.
- Attend distribution sites for staff salaries and vendors dues in program centers per need.
- Support finance officer in doing Pool cost allocation JVs Damasus office when needed.
- Support in Prepare cash projection on monthly basis, share with Finance Manager on time.
- Support in Conduct inventory check for warehouses and assets and property from time to time and per request from Supply Chain team.

**Job Requirements:**

**Education:**

- University or institution Degree in economics (accounting departments, business management or relevant financial studies), or any other college degree alongside one years` experience in accounting position preferably in an INGO.

**Work Experience:**

- Good understanding of accounting processes and procedures.
- Meeting targets and deadlines and being flexible and comfortable in multi-cultural workforce.
- Team player, cooperative and supportive to colleagues from same and different departments.
- Ability to work under pressure and load of work and willingness \\ ability to work for extra hours when and as needed.
- English is a plus.

**Demonstrated Skills and Competencies:**

- Computer literate and has strong competencies in MS Office package, especially Excel (e.g common formulas) and outlook
- Any ERP System experience is an advantage.
- Strong ability to work independently, organize work, meet deadlines, maintain composure, prioritize work under pressure, coordinate multiple tasks and maintain attention to details.
- A commitment to IRC’s mission, vision, values and IRC Way – Professional Code of Conduct.
- Credible written, presentation and verbal communication skills; ability to convey information effectively and solid experience providing training and staff development.
- Validated sense of professional discretion, integrity, and ability to handle complex situations diplomatically and to effective resolution.
- Excellent management and interpersonal skills and a solid ability to promote harmonious/cohesive teamwork, in a cross-cultural context.
- Validated ability to plan long-term, organize priorities and work under administrative and programmatic pressures with detail orientation and professional patience.
- Highly collaborative and resourceful; ability to establish positive working relationships with senior level management and all other partners to maximize cooperation and productivity.
- Curiosity, a desire to continually learn and develop is a must.
