jobs.title: Auxiliar Operativo de Proyecto en Manejo Efectivo de Áreas Naturales Protegidas - Xalapa
jobs.description:
Descripción del Proyecto:

El objetivo general del proyecto Sinergia+ es generar procesos de gestión que fortalezcan a la CONANP y que le permitan convertirse en una institución que planea con base en resultados, con finanzas fuertes y mecanismos de gobernanza y alianzas estratégicas eficaces, que contribuyan a incrementar la conectividad entre ecosistemas representativos para salvaguardar su biodiversidad y equilibrio ecológico.

El proyecto Sinergia+ tiene seis resultados estratégicos: 1) Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP; 2) Gobernanza y fortalecimiento de redes de colaboración; 3) Enfoque de género y fortalecimiento de la participación ciudadana; 4) Incremento de superficie de conservación con enfoque de conectividad ecológica; 5) Conservación y recuperación de especies en riesgo; 6) Proyectos Estratégicos.

En el marco del Proyecto Sinergia+, la persona a contratar contribuirá al fortalecimiento del Parque Nacional Cofre de Perote con la implementación, seguimiento de acciones y ejecución de acciones de manejo orientadas a la conservación de los ecosistemas y la biodiversidad del ANP, contribuyendo al cumplimiento de los objetivos establecidos en los Programas de Manejo, la normatividad ambiental aplicable y las estrategias institucionales de la CONANP.

Este puesto contribuye al logro de metas del Resultado 1 “Fortalecimiento institucional y gestión para la conservación efectiva en las ANP”.

Alcance del Trabajo:

Coadyuvar en la planeación, ejecución y seguimiento de las acciones de monitoreo de la biodiversidad implementadas por la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida, mediante la recopilación, sistematización y análisis de información de campo que contribuya a la evaluación del estado de conservación de los ecosistemas y sus especies.

Integrar, evaluar y dar seguimiento técnico a las acciones de restauración ambiental y a los proyectos estratégicos que se desarrollen en el Parque Nacional Cofre de Perote (PNCP), en apego a los programas de manejo y la normatividad ambiental aplicable; así como colaborar con la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida en la implementación, seguimiento y evaluación de las acciones y proyectos financiados mediante los programas de subsidio a cargo de la CONANP.

Colaborar con la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida en la planificación y desarrollo de actividades encaminadas a potenciar la gestión y metas del ANP mediante la formulación y seguimiento de los Programas Operativos Anuales (POA) dando el seguimiento técnico y generando los reportes de forma oportuna.

Apoyar a la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida en el seguimiento al cumplimiento de los acuerdos adoptados por el Consejo Asesor, así como promover su fortalecimiento como órgano de participación social, consulta y gobernanza para la gestión efectiva del Parque Nacional Cofre de Perote (PNCP).

Apoyar a la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida en la promoción, implementación y fortalecimiento de prácticas agroecológicas y Soluciones Basadas en la Naturaleza en las comunidades del Área Natural Protegida, favoreciendo la conservación y el manejo sustentable de los recursos naturales.

Coadyuvar con la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida en la planificación, implementación y fortalecimiento de las acciones de ordenamiento turístico, administración del cobro de derechos y vinculación con los prestadores de servicios turísticos, comunidades e instituciones relacionadas con el turismo de naturaleza, en apego al Programa de Manejo, la normatividad aplicable y los instrumentos de planeación del Área

Natural Protegida.

Apoyar a la Dirección del Área Natural Protegida el diseño e implementación de campañas de comunicación y/o iniciativas que promuevan la importancia de la conservación de la biodiversidad y recursos naturales del PNCP, Así como en la planeación y ejecución de reuniones de trabajo, coordinación y/o de planeación con los diversos actores de la sociedad civil, nacionales e internacionales y/o los tres órdenes de gobierno.

Acuerdo Institucional:

El o la persona contratada trabajará bajo la supervisión técnica de la Dirección del ANP Parque Nacional Cofre de Perote y la Dirección Regional Planicie Costera y Golfo de México, así como de la Coordinación General del Proyecto Sinergia+.

Competencias Esenciales:

Lograr Resultados: Nivel 1: Planifica y monitorea el trabajo propio, presta atención a los detalles, entrega trabajo de calidad en los límites establecidos.

Pensar Innovadotamente: Nivel 1: Tiene apertura a ideas creativas/riesgos conocidos, resuelve problemas de manera pragmática, realiza mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente: Nivel 1: Tiene mente abierta y curiosidad, comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad: Nivel 1: Se adapta al cambio, maneja la ambigüedad/incertidumbre demanera constructiva, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación: Nivel 1: Muestra determinación y compromiso, capaz de responder calmadamente ante la adversidad, confiado.

Participar y Asociarse: Nivel 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento hacia los demás, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión: Nivel 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, reconoce los sesgos inconscientes, confronta la discriminación.

Requisitos Acadpemicos Mínimos:

- Candidatos/as con Certificado de preparatoria/Bachillerato, es requisito.

- Estudios Universitarios concluidos en: Biología, Agronomía Forestal, Ecología, Ingeniería Ambiental o carrera afín, no es requisito, pero se dará debida consideración.

Años Mínimos de Experiencia Requerida:

- Para candidatos/as con Certificado de Preparatoria (Bachillerato), se requieren 4 años de experiencia en Programas y acciones de Conservación

- Para candidatos/as con Estudios Universitarios de primer nivel Licenciatura, se requiere 1 año de experiencia en los temas antes mencionados.

Habilidades Requeridas:

- Experiencia en: Elaboración de Informes técnicos.

- Experiencia en: Legislación ambiental.

jobs.title: Executive Coordinator
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Volunteers (UNV) programme is the United Nations system-wide service for volunteerism. Established by the General Assembly in 1970 and administered by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), UNV mobilizes qualified, motivated and diverse volunteers to support United Nations mandates in development, peace and security, human rights and humanitarian action, while promoting volunteerism as an important means of implementing the 2030 Agenda.

UNV works with organizations of the United Nations system, Member States, national and local institutions, civil society and communities. Its distinctive value lies in connecting the UN system with people and communities through volunteers, providing flexible talent and capacity solutions to UN entities while generating evidence, partnerships and policy support for volunteerism. The programme has evolved into a substantial global operation, with more than 17,000 UN Volunteers deployed in 172 countries in 2025, supported by close to 500 global personnel in UNV headquarters in Bonn, six regional offices and over sixty country presences and multi-country field units.

The current strategic context requires UNV to consolidate previous expansion and relevance as the system-wide service, while at the same time furthering its agility, efficiency, digital maturity, operational and financial resilience, and close alignment with the evolving needs of UN Country Teams and programme countries.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Executive Coordinator reports to UNDP Administrator and leads UNV within the policy, strategic and institutional framework established by the UN General Assembly, the UNDP/UNFPA/UNOPS Executive Board, UNDP Strategic Plan and the UNV Strategic Framework. The position combines the responsibilities of executive leader, strategic manager, and principal advocate of UNV.

The Executive Coordinator provides the overall vision, strategic direction and executive leadership required to fulfill UNV’s mandate and to translate the policy direction of the General Assembly and Executive Board into organizational priorities, strategies and partnerships. The incumbent leads the mobilization and stewardship of human, financial, institutional and partnership resources; represents UNV with Member States, UN entities and external stakeholders; and ensures that the programme operates with integrity, efficiency, transparency, accountability and strong results orientation.

The Executive Coordinator ensures that UNV remains responsive to Member States and UN partners while maintaining a strong focus on volunteer quality, inclusion, duty of care and the experience of volunteers throughout the service cycle.

The Executive Coordinator leads UNV in a way that continuously modernizes its service offer and promotes the strategic relevance of volunteerism in the UN system and beyond. He/she is accountable for positioning UNV as a trusted, effective and innovative system-wide service that enables the United Nations to draw on the skills, commitment and local knowledge of volunteers, while advancing recognition of volunteerism as a means of achieving peace and development.

In addition, the Executive Coordinator has delegated responsibility for coordinating daily management of common premises and common services for the organizations of the UN system at the UN Bonn campus, including related administrative, managerial and policy issues, as well as liaising with the Federal Government of Germany, the State Government of North Rhine-Westphalia and the City Municipality of Bonn on such matters.

1) Strategic leadership, planning and management

- Provide overall strategic leadership to UNV and translate General Assembly resolutions, Executive Board decisions, relevant UN system priorities and UNDP policies into organizational strategies, partnerships and practices.

- Lead the design and implementation of the UNV Strategic Frameworks, ensuring clear institutional priorities, implementation arrangements, measurable results, effective innovations and systematic monitoring of performance.

- Position UNV as an agile, fit-for-purpose and people-centered UN system-wide service, continuously adapting volunteer modalities, operating models and services to changing UN and country-level needs. Leads the institution in a way that continuously modernizes its service offer.

- Promote decentralization and appropriate delegation of authority so that UNV can respond effectively to country and regional requirements while maintaining corporate standards and accountability.

- Foster an organizational culture based on integrity, innovation, collaboration, inclusion, learning and service to UN partners and volunteers.

- Ensure that organizational structures, policies, business processes, digital capabilities and workforce arrangements remain aligned with strategic objectives.

- Inform and consult UNDP Administrator and senior UNDP leadership and ensure that UNV's governance and management arrangements remain consistent with its status as a UNDP-administered system-wide service.

2) External relations, representation and advocacy

- Serve as the principal spokesperson and representative of UNV with Member States, UN entities, civil society, academia, the private sector and other stakeholders. Contribute to intergovernmental dialogue on volunteerism, including follow-up to relevant General Assembly resolutions, Secretary-General reports, international observances and global policy processes. In doing so, demonstrates strong partnerships acumen and intuitional judgement.

- Advocate for volunteerism as a cross-cutting means of implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals and as a contributor to peace and security, human rights and humanitarian action.

- Sustain high-level partnerships for the integration of volunteerism into national plans and policies. Maintain strategic engagement with Resident Coordinators and UN Country Teams and promote the inclusion of volunteerism in Sustainable Development Cooperation Frameworks and country programming.

- Position UNV as a source of credible evidence, policy advice and innovation on volunteerism, including through research, data, knowledge products and global advocacy.

- Mobilize support for inclusive volunteerism, with particular attention to participation by women, young and older people, persons with disabilities, people from developing countries and other groups that may face barriers to participation.

- Strengthen UNV's public profile while ensuring communications are evidence-based, consistent with UN values and focused on the contribution of volunteers to tangible results. Represent UNV at high-level international forums and public events, communicating its mandate, results and strategic priorities with clarity and credibility.

3) Results and resources management

- Ensure that UNV delivers the results approved by its governing bodies and that organizational performance is systematically measured, analyzed, communicated and used for decision-making.

- Oversee the effective and transparent management of UNV's financial, human, digital and other resources, consistent with UNDP policies, UN rules and applicable accountability frameworks.

- Safeguard the financial sustainability of UNV, strengthen the resource base, diversifying strategic partnerships, and maintain appropriate balances between institutional resources and requirements.

- Provide strategic stewardship of the Special Voluntary Fund and other flexible resources, ensuring that they are deployed where they can respond to emergencies and/or generate catalytic and innovative high-value impact.

- Oversee enterprise-level risk management, internal controls, audit follow-up and evaluation, ensuring that risks are identified early and addressed decisively.

- Strengthen data-driven management, including the use of artificial intelligence, digital tools, analytics and evidence to improve organizational performance, decision-making, cost-effectiveness and efficiency gains.

- Report transparently on results, resources, risks and performance to the Executive Board, UNDP leadership, Member States and other relevant stakeholders.

4) People, innovation and organizational effectiveness

- Champion the principle that UNV's central asset is its people: UN Volunteers, staff and the communities and partners with whom they work. Translates general duty of care commitments onto practical arrangements and initiatives.

- Ensure that volunteerism is delivered through high-quality, safe, inclusive and meaningful assignments, with appropriate duty of care throughout the volunteer life cycle.

- Oversee continued modernization of volunteer management, including flexible, short-term, part-time, remote and other modalities responsive to the evolving needs of UN entities and programme countries.

- Ensure that innovation, digital transformation, automation and responsible use of data and emerging technologies improve service quality, accessibility, speed and efficiency.

- Encourage experimentation and learning while maintaining appropriate safeguards, ethical standards and accountability.

- Strengthen UNV's ability to identify emerging needs and rapidly adapt its operating model, particularly in fragile, conflict-affected, humanitarian and crisis contexts.

- Foster a culture of continuous improvement in which evidence from volunteers, host entities, programme countries, evaluations and operational experience informs policy and management decisions.

- Promote leadership development, collaboration across headquarters, regional and field structures, and a shared organizational identity centered on service, solidarity, professionalism and measurable impact.

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: The incumbent oversees the entire personnel of United Nations Volunteers.

Competencies

Core:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 4: Prioritize team workflow, mobilize resources, drive scalable results/strategic impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 4: Easily navigate complexity, encourage/enable radical innovation, has foresight

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 4: Create systems and processes that enable learning and development for all

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 4: Proactively initiate/lead organizational change, champion new systems/processes

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 4: Able to make difficult decisions in challenging situations, inspire confidence

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 4: Construct strategic multi-partner alliances in high-stakes situations, foster co-creation

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 4: Create ethical culture, identify/address barriers to inclusion

People Management:

UNDP People Management Competencies can be found in the dedicated site.

Cross Functional and Technical:

- Business Direction and Strategy - System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system. Business Acumen: Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks. Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization. Effective Decision Making: Ability to take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one's authority, area of expertise and resources.

- Business Management - Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritize and control the organizations programmes and projects, in line with its strategic objectives and capacity; ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives and the maintenance of business-as-usual, while optimizing return on investment. Communication: Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

- Partnership Management - Relationship Management: Ability to build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Finance - Development Finance Expertise: Ability to develop and work with innovative financing mechanisms and instruments, e.g. social/development impact bonds, guarantees, climate finance, etc.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in Social or Political Sciences, Economics, Public or Business Administration, Management or related field.

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in combination with two additional years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of a master's degree.

Experience:

- More than 15 years of relevant experience that combines policy, partnerships and programme leadership engagement, and strategic resource management is required.

- Progressively senior management experience with international organizations or Member States’ public service, with clear demonstration of high-level engagement in diplomacy, intergovernmental processes, and international political or development matters is required.

- Demonstrated ability to provide strategic leadership and position an organization effectively within a broader international context is required.

- Demonstrated experience in driving institutional modernization and change is required.

- Solid experience and proven track record in leading other managers and teams with integrity and duty of care is required.

- Demonstrated partnership acumen, ability to establish and maintain effective relationships with key partners, with strong communication and advocacy skills is required.

- Experience and demonstrated results in working on sustainable development issues at country level is a strong asset.

- Solid understanding of the UN system and intergovernmental processes is an asset.

- Knowledge of UN(DP) policies, rules and regulations is an asset.

- Experience of working on peace and security and humanitarian action is an asset.

- Experience in managing substantial regional or global operations is an asset.

- Experience in managing digital transformations is an asset.

- Experience of managing volunteer programmes or serving as a UN Volunteer is an asset.

Language:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Fluency in another official UN language is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Probation

For all new UNDP fixed term appointments (FTA), including for staff members being transferred or seconded to UNDP under the Inter-Organization Agreement concerning Transfer, Secondment or Loan of Staff, on an appointment of more than one year, continuation of the appointment beyond the initial 12 months is contingent upon the successful completion of a probationary period.

Right to select multiple candidates

We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.title: Compliance Specialist, Head of the Social and Environmental Compliance Unit (SECU) [Open to all applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Office of Audit and Investigations (OAI) reports to the Administrator and is responsible for internal audit and investigations services to UNDP and its affiliated entities. OAI has the sole responsibility for the conduct of all investigations within UNDP.

The Investigations Section of OAI is responsible for conducting UNDP’s independent investigative functions into fraud, corruption, sexual exploitation and abuse, and other wrongdoing.

Within the Investigation Section, OAI established the Social and Environmental Compliance Unit (SECU) in January 2015 as a separate mechanism to receive allegations of non-compliance with UNDP’s social and environmental commitments under the social and environmental standards (SES), and other relevant policies and procedures. The SES underpin UNDP’s commitment to mainstream social and environmental sustainability in its programmes and projects and are a corporate requirement across UNDP projects.

SECU operates a complaint mechanism for communities and public stakeholders and assesses such complaints against its eligibility criteria. Where the assessment determines that an investigation is warranted, SECU will investigate allegations of non-compliance with UNDP’s social and environmental policies and procedures. SECU’s assessment, investigation and reporting of alleged non-compliance is conducted in accordance with generally accepted international processes. Based on the evidence collected during the investigation, SECU will recommend action to address findings of non-compliance; and where relevant will make recommendations to improve UNDP systems in the future to reduce the risk of a recurrence of non-compliance.

Position Purpose

Under the supervision of the Deputy Director- Investigation, Head of Investigations and with the technical guidance of the Lead Compliance Officer (LCO), the primary roles of the Compliance Specialist, Head of SECU, are to

- Lead and manage the delivery of investigations into alleged non-compliance with applicable social and environmental standards and policies

- Lead and coordinate SECU’s advisory work

- Manage SECU’s proactive and self-initiated investigations

- Represent SECU as a member and leader to relevant professional networks within UNDP

- Lead SECU’s outreach strategy and activities

- Ensure that SECU conforms to and promotes internationally recognized best practices for independent accountability mechanisms

Within those roles, the Compliance Specialist, Head of SECU, will be OAI’s SECU Focal Point and will focus on the investigation of allegations of non-compliance with the SES.

The Compliance Specialist, Head of SECU, will supervise the work of all personnel at the P2 and P3 levels, and consultants on International Personnel Services Agreements (IPSAs) assigned to SECU and will complete their annual performance appraisals.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work when necessary, across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Key Duties and Responsibilities

1.) Leads and manages SECU and supervises the work of personnel assigned to SECU, as well as consultants.

- Plans the work of SECU personnel and distributes workload among SECU personnel appropriately.

- Provides senior expertise and advice to SECU personnel so that the work of SECU is performed in the most professional, efficient and timely manner.

- Appraises the work performance of SECU personnel.

- Coordinates the day-to-day work of SECU.

- Supports the intake of complaints and evaluates their eligibility.

- Manages compliance review teams.

- Recruits personnel for SECU as necessary.

2.) As Head of SECU, the Compliance Specialist oversees planning, evidence gathering, analysis and report-writing for investigations into social and environmental compliance.

- Provides oversight into the planning and strategic decision-making in compliance reviews to ensure that all appropriate lines of inquiry are identified, and resources are used effectively and efficiently to factually determine the issues relevant to a compliance review.

- Works closely with the LCO and case teams to ensure the quality of compliance reviews throughout the investigation lifecycle, identifying risks, methodological issues, evidentiary gaps, and resource requirements.

- Undertakes frequent, and at times extended missions to UNDP offices worldwide, including areas with hazardous working conditions.

- Manages SECU’s database and ensures that case files are up to date on cases under compliance review.

- Proposes action to close matters where appropriate.

- Works with SECU personnel to ensure that compliance reports are drafted to a high standard, providing an objective and factual summary of the investigation, with soundly based conclusions and recommendations supported by all evidence obtained in the course of the investigation.

- Leads SECU’s engagement with the Corporate Stakeholder Response Mechanism (CSRM), ensuring that grievances are channeled appropriately between SECU and CSRM and that there is effective coordination between SECU and CSRM throughout any jointly processed complaints.

3.) Provision of UNDP, UN, and external communication, representation and coordination.

- Liaises with the UNDP executive office to enhance case effectiveness, promote endorsement of recommendations, and monitor implementation of recommendations.

- Conducts in reach to UNDP business units to promote understanding and implementation of UNDP’s social and environmental commitments, and the role of SECU.

- Ensures appropriate lines of communication and knowledge sharing to promote lessons learned to UNDP regarding SECU’s case and advisory portfolio.

- Participates in OAI and stakeholder meetings, providing updates on SECU as requested.

- Prepares and disseminates outreach materials to inform stakeholders. Develops outreach strategies and implements plans for each key stakeholder group. Liaises with IAMs of other international organizations and with other offices as appropriate.

- Liaises with relevant internal and external stakeholder groups, including complainants, civil society organizations, international development organizations, independent accountability mechanisms, and other relevant offices in UNDP.

- Liaises with the compliance/investigation sections of other international organizations.

- Leads SECU’s work as Secretariat of the United Nations Accountability Mechanism Network (UNAMnet), a community of practice established by SECU which enables collaboration and resource sharing focused on issues related to social and environmental accountability in UN-supported activity.

- Represents SECU at the Independent Accountability Mechanism Network (IAMnet), a community of practice amongst accountability professionals across development and development finance institutions.

4.) Develops, maintains SECU Guidelines, Standard Operating Procedures, and Knowledge Management

- Jointly develops, maintains, and updates internal guidelines, methodologies, guidance notes, and standard operating procedures together with the LCO.

- Maintains awareness of developments in accountability mechanisms, social, environmental and human rights due diligence and related requirements, compliance review methodologies, reprisal risk management, and remedy practice.

- Jointly develops and periodically updates SECU's approach, methodology, and criteria for proactive and self-initiated investigations together with the LCO.

5.) Perform Other Tasks

- Contributes to the ongoing development of professional practices within SECU.

- participates in the implementation of his/her personal learning and training development plan.

- Performs other assignments or tasks as determined by the Deputy Director (Investigations).

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Supervisory/Managerial Responsibilities: This role requires the direct supervision of a number of expert compliance officers on IPSAs (3-8), 2 full-time staffers (P2 Compliance Analyst and P3 Compliance Specialist), interns, and other contractors/service providers.

Competencies Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

- Business Direction & Strategy — Effective Decision Making: Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one's authority, area of expertise and resources and take into consideration potential wider implications.

- Audit & Investigation - Investigation — Investigation management and investigative techniques: The ability to manage an investigation, choose avenues of inquiry and apply different techniques during an investigation, including investigative interviewing; seizure of documentary and electronic evidence; identification, collection, review and analysis of all types of evidence, including project, procurement and commercial business documentation and electronic communications; forensic analysis; verification site visits; open-source research

- Business Direction and Strategy — System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Business Management — Portfolio Management: Ability to select, prioritise and control the organization's programmes and projects in line with its strategic objectives and capacity Ability to balance the implementation of change initiatives with regular activities for optimal return on investment. Knowledge and understanding of key principles of project, programme, and portfolio management

Required Skills and Experience Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in International Development or related areas such as Globalization and Sustainable Development, Human Ecology or Law or Compliance/Investigations with a focus on the Environment, Human Rights or Cultural Anthropology is required. Or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 7 years (with master’s degree) or 9 years (with bachelor’s degree) of progressively responsible professional experience in International Development or Law or Compliance/Investigations with a focus on accountability or oversight in relation to social and/or environmental issues, including human rights, gender equality, biodiversity conservation, community health and safety, cultural heritage, displacement and resettlement, or indigenous peoples rights is required.

- Additional formal professional training in a range of compliance/investigation related areas is desired.

- Experience working with, or a detailed knowledge of, social and environmental accountability mechanisms is desired.

- Experience working with local communities and civil society organizations is desired.

- Experience in communications, outreach, and stakeholder engagement is desired.

- Working experience in the role of a leader or supervisor in managing varied caseloads of work relating to law or compliance or investigations is desired.

- Prior experience with UN/ UNDP will be an asset.

jobs.title: Engineering Analyst (Renewables), NPSA-9, DS- Kyiv or Lviv, National position
jobs.description:
Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) in Ukraine, through its Energy and Environment Portfolio, supports national and local authorities in restoring and transforming Ukraine’s energy infrastructure in line with the principles of sustainability, resilience, and transparency. Since the onset of the full-scale war, UNDP has prioritized assistance to ensure continuity of essential services and accelerate the green recovery of Ukraine’s public infrastructure.

Within this framework, UNDP is implementing the Technical Assistance to the Renewable Energy Solutions (RES) Programme, financed through the IKI Renewable Energy Investment Grant under the European Investment Bank (EIB) facility. The Action is delivered under the Direct Implementation Modality (DIM) and coordinated with the Ministry for Recovery, Infrastructure and Transport of Ukraine, the EIB, and GIZ.

The project aims to support the large-scale deployment of renewable energy technologies—including solar photovoltaic systems, biomass installations, and heat pumps—in public buildings such as schools, kindergartens, hospitals, and municipal facilities. This initiative is designed to reduce dependence on fossil fuels, enhance local energy resilience, and accelerate Ukraine’s alignment with EU Green Deal objectives.

The Action specifically contributes to:

- Strengthening local institutional capacity for project design, procurement, and implementation of renewable energy sub-projects;

- Ensuring technical quality, financial accountability, and environmental compliance during sub-project delivery;

- Supporting municipalities to obtain prosumer (active electricity consumer) status through the development of the net-billing mechanism;

- Enhancing transparency and governance through anticorruption and sanctions-screening systems;

- Promoting knowledge exchange, digital monitoring, and replication of successful models across Ukrainian communities.

UNDP’s Technical Assistance (TA) component serves as the enabling pillar of the RES Programme. It bridges investment, governance, and capacity development by providing:

1. Institutional support and capacity building for Final Beneficiaries (municipalities, utilities, and communal institutions);

2. Technical review of documentation provided for sub-project implementation and support for incorporating applicable environmental and social requirements into procurement and contract management;

3. Contract management for goods, works, and services financed under the EIB-BMWK framework;

4. Oversight, monitoring, and integrity assurance through red-flag tracking, sanctions screening, and compliance reviews;

5. Technical assistance for operationalizing the net-billing system and helping municipalities become self-sufficient clean-energy producers; and

6. Structured knowledge and digital platforms to enable real-time data tracking, reporting, and learning.

The project forms an integral part of UNDP’s Green Energy Recovery and Decarbonization Agenda and complements related EIB-financed frameworks.

Within this context, UNDP Ukraine is recruiting a highly qualified and experienced national professional for the position of Engineering Analyst (Renewables). The position will support the implementation of the RES Programme with a specific focus on the technical review of design documentation, support to procurement processes, and monitoring of the installation and commissioning of renewable energy and energy efficiency solutions in public facilities. The Engineering Analyst (Renewables) will help ensure the quality, safety, and compliance of implemented works, contributing to energy security, continuity of public services, and infrastructure resilience under wartime and post-war recovery conditions.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of Project Manager and in close collaboration with Project team,Engineering Analyst (Renewables) will perform the following:

1.Ensure technical review and engineering support for renewable energy and energy efficiency projects.

- Review and evaluate technical project documentation, baseline information, design calculations, drawings, Bills of Quantities (BoQs) and equipment specifications for solar PV, other renewable energy and energy efficiency projects under the RES Programme, assessing their completeness, consistency and suitability for implementation.

- Review project designs for compliance with national legislation, applicable regulations, technical standards and donor requirements, and recommend corrective actions to address identified discrepancies.

- Verify sub-project budgets, cost estimates and BoQs using specialised software, such as AVK, and applicable construction cost estimation methodologies.

- Support the preparation and review of technical and contract-related documentation, including scopes of work and technical specifications, ensuring that design requirements are accurately and consistently reflected in the relevant project documentation.

- Participate in technical evaluation panels, assess bidders’ qualifications and technical proposals, including the compliance of proposed equipment and materials and the completeness and consistency of BoQs, and provide recommendations in coordination with the procurement team.

- Prepare technical clarifications in response to bidders’ questions and support the resolution of technical issues related to project documentation, design solutions, equipment, materials and implementation requirements.

- Cooperate closely with GIZ and project stakeholders to identify appropriate technical solutions and provide technical advice during project planning, design review and implementation.

- Identify and assess technical requirements, constraints and implementation risks, and recommend appropriate mitigation measures.

- Review contractors’ proposed schedules for equipment supply, installation, testing and commissioning, and provide recommendations on their feasibility and alignment with project timelines.

- Support technical monitoring of contract implementation through site visits, review of progress reports and verification of equipment and works against contractual requirements, quality and safety standards, and agreed schedules.

- Review proposed changes to designs, equipment, materials or works, assess their implications for scope, cost and timelines, and provide technical recommendations for UNDP’s consideration and approval.

- Support the technical verification of completed works and supporting documentation for acceptance and payment, including records of testing and commissioning.

2.Support in contract management, construction supervision, and commissioning of the project sites.

- Monitor and supervise the implementation of construction and installation works carried out by contractors.\Manage technical aspects of contracts with construction companies and equipment suppliers.

- Ensure that installed equipment, materials, and works comply with approved project designs, technical specifications, contractual requirements, and quality standards.

- Coordinate and maintain effective communication with contractors, author and technical supervisions, final beneficiaries, and other relevant stakeholders.

- Conduct technical monitoring missions on sites and provide supervision throughout project implementation.

- Identify and address technical issues arising during construction and installation phases.

- Monitor compliance with UNDP and EIB social and environmental standards during the project implementation.

- Support testing, commissioning, and acceptance procedures for completed renewable energy installations.

- Verify completion of works and compliance prior to project handover.

3.Provision of operational support of the RES Project, monitoring, reporting, capacity building and facilitating knowledge sharing.

- Support final beneficiaries in obtaining prosumer status and completing related administrative and technical requirements where necessary.

- Monitor and evaluate the operational performance of installed renewable energy systems.

- Assess energy generation, energy savings, and greenhouse gas emissions reductions, including CO ₂ savings achieved through project interventions.

- Support the development and delivery of training activities for personnel of final beneficiaries to ensure proper operation and maintenance of installed systems.

- Collect, analyse, and document good practices, lessons learned, and project success stories.

- Contribute technical inputs to project monitoring, evaluation, and reporting requirements.

- Prepare and maintain technical records, performance data, and project documentation.

Support the dissemination of project results and knowledge-sharing activities.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Engineering Analyst will provide technical support for the implementation of the RES Programme, including the review of technical documentation, support to procurement, technical monitoring of contracts, and verification of completed works. The incumbent will work closely with the project team, procurement colleagues, contractors, final beneficiaries and other relevant stakeholders in accordance with the approved project document and UNDP rules and procedures

jobs.title: Asistente de Planificación Territorial - Geográfico - NPSA5
jobs.description:
1.Enfoque por niveles (Tiered Approach) para el reclutamiento

- En línea con el compromiso de salvaguardar la capacidad y apoyar al personal que ya forma parte de la Organización, la mayoría de las vacantes de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV se publican utilizando un proceso de postulación por niveles, mediante el cual: Nivel 0 (Tier 0): Personal internacional (IP) de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV con contratos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos serán abolidos o cuyos contratos serán terminados o no renovados durante 2026. Nivel 1 (Tier 1): Otros funcionarios de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV con contratos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA). Nivel 2 (Tier 2): Personal de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV con contratos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares, así como Voluntarios de la ONU en las categorías de Expertos y Especialistas. Nivel 3 (Tier 3) o sin nivel indicado: Todos los demás tipos de contrato de UNDP/UNCDF/UNV y de otras agencias, así como candidatos externos. Por favor, tome nota del(los) nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si corresponde, y asegúrese de cumplir con los criterios de elegibilidad para postular.

2. Oficina/Unidad/Descripción del Proyecto

Desde 2023, el Ministerio de Vivienda y Urbanismo (MINVU) y el Programa de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo (PNUD) mantienen un acuerdo de colaboración orientado a fortalecer la planificación urbana y territorial sostenible, promoviendo ciudades más integradas, resilientes y equitativas, en concordancia con los desafíos de desarrollo de la Región Metropolitana.

En este contexto, la Secretaría Regional Ministerial de Vivienda y Urbanismo de la Región Metropolitana requiere la contratación de un(a) Asistente de Planificación Territorial, con énfasis en aspectos geográficos, para apoyar los procesos de actualización, modificación y seguimiento del Plan Regulador Metropolitano de Santiago (PRMS), instrumento estratégico que orienta el desarrollo urbano y territorial de la Región Metropolitana.

La persona contratada participará en la elaboración de análisis y diagnósticos territoriales, formulación y evaluación de propuestas de planificación territorial, definición de criterios territoriales, actualización de la planimetría del PRMS y análisis de tendencias urbanas, aportando antecedentes técnicos para la gestión del crecimiento urbano, la protección ambiental, la identificación de riesgos y la localización de infraestructura y equipamientos. Asimismo, colaborará en procesos de Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica (EAE), coordinación interinstitucional y participación ciudadana asociados a modificaciones de instrumentos de planificación territorial.

Su trabajo contribuirá a fortalecer las capacidades técnicas de la SEREMI Metropolitana para la toma de decisiones y la actualización de instrumentos de planificación territorial, proporcionando antecedentes técnicos, cartográficos y normativos que favorezcan un desarrollo urbano sostenible, equilibrado y coherente con las políticas públicas regionales.

3. Alcance del trabajo

El objetivo principal del cargo es contribuir al desarrollo y coordinación y apoyar técnicamente el proceso de formulación, modificación, actualización, seguimiento e implementación del Plan Regulador Metropolitano de Santiago (PRMS), mediante la aplicación de criterios de planificación urbana y territorial, análisis espacial y herramientas de Sistemas de Información Geográfica (SIG), contribuyendo al desarrollo urbano sostenible y al ordenamiento territorial de la región.

Entre las funciones y resultados esperados se encuentran:

A. Planificación territorial y actualización del PRMS

- Participar en la elaboración, actualización y modificación de la planimetría del Plan Regulador Metropolitano de Santiago.

- Desarrollar análisis territoriales para la definición de áreas urbanas, rurales, de extensión urbana, protección ambiental, riesgo y planificación estratégica.

- Apoyar la definición de criterios territoriales para la toma de decisiones institucionales

B. Análisis espacial, diagnóstico y cartografía territorial

- Realizar diagnósticos territoriales, utilizando herramientas SIG y bases de datos espaciales

- Elaborar cartografía temática, normativa y de diagnóstico requerida en las distintas etapas de actualización de la planimetría del PRMS.

- Analizar tendencias de crecimiento urbano, expansión urbana, densificación, movilidad, equipamientos y usos de suelo.

C. Gestión de información geográfica y monitoreo territorial

- Construir, administrar y actualizar bases de datos geográficas para la gestión del PRMS como instrumento de planificación territorial.

- Desarrollar indicadores territoriales y sistemas de monitoreo para la gestión del PRMS.

- Apoyar la gestión y actualización de información territorial estratégica regional.

D. Evaluación, coordinación e integración de antecedentes y apoyo a la gestión del conocimiento

- Participar en procesos de Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica (EAE) del IPT.

- Revisar antecedentes territoriales provenientes de municipios, organismos públicos y consultorías externas.

- Participar en procesos de participación ciudadana y coordinación intersectorial vinculados a la actualización de la planimetría del PRMS.

- Capacitar y asesorar técnicamente a equipos internos según se requiera.

El/la titular podrá desempeñar otras funciones dentro de su perfil profesional que se consideren necesarias para el adecuado funcionamiento del proyecto, de las áreas relacionadas a éste y sus articulaciones.

4. Acuerdo Institucional

La persona contratada se desempeñará en forma presencial en dependencias de la SEREMI Metropolitana de Vivienda y Urbanismo, ubicada en Avda. Libertador Bernardo O`Higgins 874, Santiago, Región Metropolitana, además de asistencias en terreno. Se desempeñará bajo la supervisión directa de la jefatura del Departamento de Desarrollo Urbano e infraestructura de dicha SEREMI. Por parte del PNUD, administrativamente corresponderá al Coordinador/a del proyecto la respectiva supervisión. Se considera una jornada laboral completa, de lunes a viernes, en horario homologable al establecido para los demás profesionales de la SEREMI.

5. Competencias

Competencias Esenciales

Lograr Resultados - NIVEL 1: Planea y monitorea su trabajo, poniendo atención a los detalles, realiza un trabajo de calidad y a tiempo.

Pensar Innovadoramente - NIVEL 1: Abierto(a) a nuevas ideas, conoce los riesgos, resuelve los problemas en forma pragmática, hace mejoras.

Aprender Continuamente - NIVEL 1: Abierto(a) de mente y curioso(a), comparte conocimiento, aprende de los errores, pide retroalimentación.

Adaptarse con Agilidad - NIVEL 1: Se adapta a los cambios, maneja la incertidumbre/ambigüedad constructivamente, es flexible.

Actuar con Determinación NIVEL 1: Demuestra manejo y motivación, capaz de afrontar la adversidad calmadamente, seguro(a).

Participar y Asociarse - NIVEL 1: Demuestra compasión/entendimiento frente a otros, forma relaciones positivas.

Facilitar la Diversidad y la Inclusión - NIVEL 1: Aprecia/respeta las diferencias, es consciente de los prejuicios, confronta la discriminación.

Competencias Transversales y Técnicas

Gestión institucional - Comunicación

Comunicar de manera clara, concisa, sin ambigüedades, tanto de manera verbal como escrita; adaptar mensajes y elegir métodos de comunicación según audiencia. Habilidad de gestionar comunicaciones interna y externamente, a través de redes sociales, medios, y otros canales apropiados.

Gestión institucional - Gestión de proyectos

Capacidad para planificar, organizar, priorizar y controlar recursos, procedimientos y protocolos para alcanzar objetivos específicos

Gestión de asociaciones - Gestión de relaciones

Capacidad para relacionarse con un amplio abanico de asociados públicos y privados, así como para crear, mantener y reforzar las relaciones, la confianza y la comprensión mutua.

Entorno digital- Análisis geoespacial

Competencia en técnicas que estudian entidades a partir de sus propiedades topológicas, geométricas o geográficas.

Agenda 2030: Prosperidad - Crecimiento inclusivo

Desarrollo urbano y diseño inclusivo

Agenda 2030: Prosperidad - Crecimiento inclusivo

Infraestructuras y activos comunitarios urbanos

Agenda 2030: Planeta - Reducción del riesgo de desastres y recuperación

Resiliencia urbana.

6. Calificaciones mínimas de un NPSA

Educación académica mínima requerida

- Educación secundaria completa es requerida.

- Título profesional universitario (Grado de licenciado(a)) en áreas de la Geografía o equivalente, se dará debida consideración, pero no es un requisito.

Años mínimos de experiencia laboral relevante

- Mínimo de 5 años (con educación secundaria) o 2 años (con licenciatura) de experiencia relevante.

- Se entenderá por experiencia relevante al conjunto de experiencia laboral que incluya: Experiencia en formulación, evaluación o gestión de Instrumentos de Planificación Territorial y en estudios territoriales vinculados a Planes Reguladores Intercomunales, Metropolitanos o Comunales. Experiencia en instituciones públicas, municipalidades, gobiernos regionales o consultoras especializadas en planificación urbana y territorial. Experiencia en elaboración de cartografía temática y análisis geoespacial aplicado a la planificación urbana y en coordinación de estudios territoriales y gestión de información geográfica.

Habilidades competencias requeridas

- Experiencia en el manejo de herramientas de trabajo remoto y colaborativo, tales como Microsoft Teams, Zoom, Google Docs, Google Drive y nubes de almacenamiento.

- Experiencia en el manejo de herramientas tradicionales Microsoft Office: Word, Excel, Power Point.

- Experiencia en capacitaciones relacionadas con el ejercicio del cargo, tales como: Urbanismo, Planificación Urbana, Ordenamiento Territorial, Planificación Territorial, Desarrollo Urbano, Sistemas de Información Geográfica, Geomática, Gestión Territorial, Evaluación Ambiental Estratégica.

Habilidades y competencias deseables

- Contar con título profesional en el área mencionada (geografía o equivalente) .

- Contar con postítulo o postgrado en materias asociadas al cargo.

- Experiencia en el manejo avanzado de ArcGIS Pro, QGIS y Microsoft Office.

- Experiencia en el manejo intermedio de AutoCAD, PostgreSQL/PostGIS, GeoServer.

- Experiencia con la perspectiva de género en sus ámbitos de acción.

Idiomas requeridos (a nivel laboral)

Fluidez en el idioma español es requerida

Certificados profesionales

Se exigirá a los/as postulantes acreditar mediante certificados u otros documentos similares, su experiencia laboral y/o el manejo de las herramientas señaladas.

7. Viajes:

Eventualmente se prevén viajes oficiales para este puesto, dentro de Chile.

8. Los siguientes documentos deben requerirse a los aplicantes:

- CV personal y P11, indicando los puestos anteriores y sus funciones, la duración (mes-año), los requisitos, así como los detalles de contacto (correo y número de teléfono) del (la) candidato(a), y al menos tres referencias laborales de supervisores previos. Las referencias pueden incluir también a los colegas.

- Una carta de presentación (máximo una página) indicando por qué la persona se considera idónea para la posición.

- Los gerentes pueden requerir cualquier otro material relevante de su experiencia como reportes, presentaciones, publicaciones, campañas u otros materiales.

Consideraciones en su postulación:

- Complete el formulario en línea; es requerido.

- Adjunte también CV en formato libre, como complemento.

- Incluya una carta de presentación (máximo una página) indicando por qué se considera idónea(o) para la posición.

- Identifique al menos tres referencias laborales de supervisores(as) anteriores. Las referencias pueden incluir también a los colegas.

- Por tratarse de una posición nacional, las personas extranjeras deben contar con las condiciones habilitantes para trabajar en el país (residencia, permiso) al momento de postular.

Importante

Esta posición en categoría NPSA está sujeta a reclutamiento local.

Vacante Tier 3, es decir, abierto a postulaciones internas y externas.

Igualdad de oportunidades

Como empleador que promueve la igualdad de oportunidades, el PNUD valora la diversidad como una expresión de la multiplicidad de naciones y culturas en las que operamos y, en ese sentido, alentamos a personas calificadas de todos los orígenes a postular a puestos dentro de la organización. Nuestras decisiones de empleo se basan en el mérito y la idoneidad para el puesto, sin discriminación.

El PNUD también está comprometido con la creación de un entorno laboral inclusivo, en el que todo el personal esté empoderado para contribuir a nuestra misión, sea valorado, pueda desarrollarse y beneficiarse de oportunidades de carrera abiertas a todos.

Acoso sexual, explotación y abuso de autoridad

El PNUD no tolera el acoso, el acoso sexual, la explotación, la discriminación ni el abuso de autoridad. Por lo tanto, todos los candidatos seleccionados se someten a verificaciones pertinentes y se espera que cumplan con los estándares y principios correspondientes.

Derecho a seleccionar a múltiples candidatos

El PNUD se reserva el derecho de seleccionar a uno o más candidatos de este anuncio de vacante. Asimismo, podemos conservar las postulaciones y considerar a los candidatos que apliquen a este puesto para otras posiciones similares en el PNUD, al mismo nivel de grado y con requisitos de funciones, experiencia y formación similares.

Uso de IA por parte de los candidatos/as

Los postulantes están invitados a leer la respectiva guía: read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

jobs.title: Re-advertisement Project Coordinator GCF (N-PSA 10) (Open to Tier 1, 2 & 3 applicants)
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups, and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply. All applications will be treated with the strictest confidence.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous references and background checks.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. The UNDP Multi-Country Office (MCO) current support to the Government of Mauritius in the energy sector includes several on-going and pipeline projects, which are in line with the Nationally Determined Contribution under the Paris Agreement to reduce GHG emissions by 40% and increase the share of renewable energy to 60% in the national energy mix by 2030.

UNDP is the leading United Nations organization in fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations build integrated, lasting solutions for people and the planet. Learn more at undp.org or follow @UNDP.

The UNDP Mauritius Country Office (CO) consists of two distinct units including the Environment Unit and Socio-Economic Development Unit with a diverse portfolio worth USD 65 M including the Green Climate Fund (GCF), Global Environment Facility (GEF), Adaptation Fund (AF), European Union (EU), Japan Supplementary Budget (JSB), E-Health Portfolio and TRAC projects. The Environment Unit manages a portfolio covering various focal areas such as Climate Change Adaptation and Mitigation, Biodiversity, Sustainable Land Management, and Chemicals and Waste.

The unit will hire a project coordinator for the “Accelerating the Transformational Shift to a Low-Carbon Economy in the Republic of Mauritius” project which is implemented under National Implementation Modality (NIM).

The project is funded by GCF with implementation initiated in 2017. The objective is to overcome identified barriers to low carbon development and support the inclusive deployment of 25MW of PV system on the electrical grid. The implementing partner is the Ministry of Finance in collaboration with the Ministry of Energy and Public Utilities, the Central Electricity Board, the Outer Island Development Cooperation, and the Mauritius Renewable Energy Agency.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Project Coordinator (PC) will be locally recruited based on an open competitive process. His/ her responsibilities shall include:

- Overall management of the project, mobilization of all inputs, supervision of staff, consultants, and sub-contractors.

- Reporting to the Head of the Environment Unit and periodic reporting to the Project Steering Committee (PSC).

- Meeting government obligations under the project (NIM modality).

- Liaison with Government, UNDP, UN Agencies, NGOs, project partners, and donor agencies.

Summary of Key Functions

- Strategic project planning, coordination, and implementation,

- Management of the Project,

- Representation and Coordination,

- Management of communication flow,

- Partnership building and donor liaison.

Specific tasks and responsibilities:

- Ensures strategic project planning, coordination and implementation , focusing on achievement of the following results: Provides guidance and manages the overall implementation including planning, budgeting, implementation and monitoring, Ensures overall efficient coordination of programmes/projects including planning processes and timely delivery of results taking into consideration agreed-upon work plans with the UNDP country office and the participating ministries/organizations, Ensures identification and promotion of joint programming and planning opportunities Identifies and develops new programme and project opportunities, Supports capacity building of national counterparts, Oversees project implementation through close monitoring of results. Ensures effective application of RBM tools, management of scorecard targets and other benchmarks, Coordinates and follows through on decentralized local evaluations. Ensures full compliance with audit requirements and timely follow-up to audit recommendations. Promotes identification and synthesis of best practices and lessons learned for organizational sharing and learning.

- Responsible for effective project management focusing on achievement of the following results: Ensures smooth running of the project, builds an effective project team, promotes teamwork and an environment that is conducive to delivering results, Ensures full responsibility for the appropriate use and management of resources attributed to the project by tracking use of financial resources, ensuring the integrity of financial systems and consistent application of the Internal Control Framework and/or rules and regulations. Continually find ways to systematically identify and integrate efficiency gains and cost reductions in all operations. Approves contracts and ATLAS transactions under written delegated authority from the Resident Representative and/or Country Director. Has Atlas manager rights as delegated. Responsible for the management of the project staff, monitors their performance, completing performance assessments where necessary, Ensure timely and regular reporting, Build capacity of the project staff by identifying capacity needs and establishing training/learning programmes.

- Ensures effective management of the three components for proper implementation as per the funding proposal achieving the following: Contribute to preparation and revision of project work and financial plans, as required by UNDP, and support the operational and financial planning processes, Oversee and ensure timely submission of the Inception Report, Combined Project Implementation Review/Annual Project Report, Technical reports, quarterly financial reports, and other reports as may be required by UNDP, GCF and other oversight agencies, Contribute to the preparation and implementation of progress reports, and monitor all project activities, budgets and financial expenditures, Assist in the preparation of payments requests for operational expenses, salaries, insurances etc. as well as follow up on timely disbursements by UNDP CO, Maintain project correspondence and communication, Assist in logistical organization of meetings, training and workshops.

- Responsible for Representation and Coordination in the area focusing on achievement of the following results: Able to represent UNDP with UNCT and development partners if needed, Provides strong coordination support to national authorities and other organizations through the establishment of a wider consultation process, Ensures proper coordination and inputs to Interagency initiatives, Maintains collaboration and coordination with the other project managers to ensure programmatic integration and sharing of best practices.

- Promotes communication flow in the project focusing on achievement of the following results: Maximizes communication between the various portfolios and ensures that stakeholders (development partners, bilateral and multilateral donors, private sector, civil society, UN agencies and Government agencies) have one consistent UNDP counterpart, Ensures internal communication and coordination at project level and effective and proactive communication between relevant project units, Monitors the perception of the GCF project at the local level and suggest media activities that position the GCF project more strategically and effectively as a neutral broker for local development, Enhances local visibility for the project in development effectiveness, Ensures that local development results are effectively communicated in collaboration with Communication Office in the country office.

- Fosters partnership building and donor liaison focusing on achievement of the following results: Contributes to the development of the project Partnership and Resource Mobilization (PRM) strategy, including planning tools to implement the strategy, Identifies new partnerships and strengthens existing ones at the project level through innovative approaches to partnership development, Encourages ways of increasing project funding such as engaging in resource mobilization efforts in consultation with local counterparts and following up with donors on local opportunities.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Impact of Results

- The Project Coordinator is the UNDP senior representative in the project. The results of his/her work impact on the standing and reputation of UNDP in the country and with the Green Climate Fund. When requested by the Resident Representative or Country Director, the Project Coordinator represents UNDP in international and national forums, liaises with external clients and a broad range of constituencies and UNDP counterparts in the Government, local and international media, civil society as well as counterparts from other international organizations.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will work under the general supervision of the Head of the Environment Unit (who may delegate a direct supervisory role) in the UNDP MCO for Mauritius and Seychelles and will collaborate closely with the Project Director for National Implementation Modality (NIM) Projects.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

jobs.description:
Important: This post is opened in the context of the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) scheme sponsored by the Government of the Netherlands and is addressed exclusively to nationals from the Nedworc Foundation list of countries. Nationals of Jordan are not eligible to apply due to the restriction that nationals of the country where the position is located cannot be considered.
