For the minimum qualification requirements see the website of Nedworc Foundation:

Junior Professional Officer Programme - Nedworc Foundation

And the website of the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme:

https://www.undp.org/jposc

Background

UNRWA | United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees

The United Nations Relief and Works Agency for Palestine Refugees in the Near East (UNRWA) provides essential services and humanitarian assistance to Palestine refugees across Jordan, Lebanon, Syria, the Gaza Strip and the West Bank. Its services include education, health care, relief and social services, camp infrastructure rehabilitation, microfinance and emergency assistance.

The Department of Legal Affairs advises on and promotes the consistent interpretation and application of international law throughout the Agency. It develops strategies to promote and implement relevant areas of public international law, including international human rights law, international humanitarian law, refugee law and United Nations law. Particular emphasis is placed on the status and mandate of the Agency, the privileges and immunities of the Agency and its personnel, related responsibilities, and the observance of humanitarian principles.

The Department also provides legal advice and training on the interpretation and application of the Agency’s regulatory framework, including General Assembly resolutions, Staff and Financial Regulations and Rules, associated administrative issuances, and organizational directives. It advises Headquarters and Field departments on governance and management matters, particularly those involving administrative, contractual and procurement law. In addition, the Department provides technical expertise and advice on amendments to the Agency’s regulatory framework, including the drafting of regulations and rules, as well as the preparation and review of legal opinions on complex or sensitive financial matters, particularly those concerning the interpretation of the Agency’s Financial Regulations and Technical Instructions.

Furthermore, the Department reviews drafts of all types of Agency contractual instruments and arrangements, including complex contracts for the procurement of goods and services, memoranda of understanding with partners, and funding agreements. It also provides related training to strengthen the consistent interpretation, application and implementation of the Agency’s contractual and legal requirements.

Training component: Learning elements and expectations

Upon completion of the assignment the JPO will have/ will be able to:

- Legal research, analysis and application of international and general law.

- Legal drafting, advisory work and case management.

- Understanding of UNRWA’s mandate, operations and institutional framework.

- Interpersonal, communication and stakeholder coordination skills.

- Professional judgement, discretion, confidentiality and ethical conduct

The JPO training programme includes the following learning elements:

- Year 1 – Induction and practical learning: Structured induction, guided legal reading, mandatory UN training, daily on-the-job learning, progressive case management and potential Field Operations visits, followed by a review of learning needs and a development plan for Year 2.

- Year 2 – Advanced legal practice and collaboration: Increased responsibility for complex legal matters, including litigation, legal opinions, contracts and procurement, alongside participation in legal training and coordination across UNRWA and the wider UN system, strengthening legal expertise, professional judgement and stakeholder engagement.

- Year 3 – Consolidation and career development: Consolidation of legal expertise through progressively independent work, continued mentoring and feedback, and career development discussions to identify further learning needs and future opportunities within the UN system.

- Duty Travel and Training Allowance (DTTA) : An annual allowance of USD 4,000 supports relevant learning activities, duty travel and professional development related to the assignment.

Content and methodology of supervision:

- Director, Department of Legal Affairs. Purpose: direct supervision, guidance, advice, task assignment, performance monitoring and evaluation. Frequency: daily, through regular meetings, review of deliverables, and feedback on progress and quality of work.

- Heads of the General Law Unit and the International Law Unit. Purpose: substantive guidance, coordination and advice on assigned legal cases and activities across both Units. Frequency: as required, through regular interaction and review of ongoing work.

- Legal advisers and counterparts across the UN system: Purpose: professional exchange, coordination and exposure to legal practice across the UN system. Frequency: as required, through the legal advisers’ coordination mechanism.

- The Associate Legal Officer’s individual workplan will be based on the Department’s annual workplan and will define substantive activities and expected outputs. Progress will be monitored through regular discussions, review of assigned cases and deliverables, and ongoing feedback. The Associate Legal Officer will also participate in official meetings with the Director, as applicable and contribute to follow-up actions, ensuring practical exposure to the Agency’s legal mandate and the work of the Department.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Associate Legal Officer will report to the Director of Legal Affairs and work under their direct daily supervision, with full immersion in the Department’s daily work and activities. The role will have a cross-cutting focus, working closely with both the General Law Unit (covering international administrative law, commercial and institutional matters, and litigation), and the International Law Unit (covering privileges and immunities, protection, neutrality, international human rights mechanisms, and international humanitarian law). The JPO will handle a diverse portfolio of cases across both Units, participate in official meetings and related follow-up actions, gain a thorough understanding of the Agency’s legal mandate in a highly politicised context, and engage with legal advisers across the UN system.

Responsibilities (summary of duties/tasks):

1. Supports the Department’s Legal Advisory Work (30%)

• Participates in the daily work and activities of the General Law and International Law Units, gaining exposure to the full range of legal matters handled by the Department.

• Supports the Director of Legal Affairs in providing legal advice to UNRWA leadership and Directors of Divisions and Departments, including on sensitive and complex legal issues.

• Develops a comprehensive understanding of the Department’s legal functions, priorities and advisory responsibilities.

2. Manages an Assigned Portfolio of Legal Matters and Projects (30%)

• Handles an assigned portfolio of legal cases and issues across the General Law and International Law Units, under the direct supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

• Contributes to litigation and matters arising under the Agency’s internal justice system, the preparation and review of diplomatic correspondence, including notes verbal, and the provision of legal opinions on international law issues.

• Reviews commercial contracts and supports legal aspects of procurement and other operational activities.

• Undertakes designated legal projects to strengthen the Agency’s legal practices and frameworks, including the development of standard agreement templates for engagement with partners.

• Liaises with relevant Agency stakeholders, including Human Resources, Partnerships and the Executive Office, under the guidance and supervision of the Director of Legal Affairs.

3. Participates in Official Meetings and Follow-up Actions (25%)

• Participates in meetings led by the Director of Legal Affairs and other senior legal officers on substantive, operational and strategic legal matters.

• Contributes to meeting preparation and follow-up, including conducting legal research, drafting documentation and supporting the implementation of agreed actions.

• Develops an understanding of UNRWA’s management structures, decision-making processes and engagement with governments, beneficiaries, partners and other stakeholders.

5. Engages in Legal Coordination Across the United Nations System (15%)

• Participates, through the Director of Legal Affairs, in coordination and information-sharing with legal advisers and counterparts across the United Nations system.

• Gains exposure to the work of the United Nations Office of Legal Affairs and other UN legal offices, including inter-agency coordination mechanisms on legal matters.

• Develops an understanding of common legal issues, institutional practices and approaches to legal advice and coordination across the UN systems.

Competencies

Key competencies

- Excellent oral and written communication skills, including strong legal drafting and analytical skills.

- Ability to work effectively in an international and multicultural environment, maintaining confidentiality and discretion at all times.

- Legal Research and Analysis

- Negotiation and Problem-Solving

- Stakeholder Engagement

- Teamwork and Collaboration

- Planning and Organizing

- Analytical Skills

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Master degree or equivalent in law or a Bachelor’s degree in law plus a minimum of 2 years of paid and relevant working experience. Admission to practice at a national Bar.

- In exceptional cases candidates with a Bachelor’s degree plus a minimum of 4 years relevant working experience can be considered.

- Substantive parts of the candidates’ academic training (Bachelor and/or Master) must have taken place in a developing country that appears on the list of eligible countries. eligible-countries-DC-JPOs.pdf

Working experience:

- Minimum of 2 years relevant working experience after obtaining first university degree in the legal field, with an exposure to development and humanitarian activities of international organisations being an asset.

- Minimum of 4 years relevant working experience for candidates with a Bachelor’s degree.

- Specialisation in public international law and/or the law of international organisations is an asset.

- Experience in international administrative law and/or litigation is an asset.

- Work experience within the UN system should not exceed 1 year, including UNV, (paid) UN internship and UN consultancy.

- All paid work experience since obtaining Bachelor’s degree will/can be considered.

Languages:

- Fluency in English is required;

- Knowledge of Arabic or another UN official language is an asset.

Maximum age limit is 32 years as of 31 December of the year of application.

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The Energy and Environment Unit of UNDP Kazakhstan supports national efforts to advance a green, low-carbon and climate-resilient economy and achieve the Sustainable Development Goals. Its portfolio covers climate change mitigation and adaptation, renewable energy, energy efficiency and power system modernization, biodiversity conservation, sustainable agriculture and food systems, sustainable land and water management, waste management, disaster risk reduction and sustainable natural resource use.

Working with government institutions, the private sector, civil society, academia and international partners, the Unit provides policy advice, technical assistance and capacity development. It promotes green and sustainable finance, supports access to international environmental and climate funding, and helps develop investment opportunities and innovative financing instruments aligned with national development priorities. The Unit also strengthens institutional frameworks and supports the application of innovative and digital solutions, while integrating gender equality and inclusive development across its work.

Within this portfolio, the Government of Japan-funded project “The Project for Development of Sustainable Rare Metal and Rare Earth Minerals Value Chains through Environmental Measures” supports the sustainable development of Kazakhstan’s minerals sector. The project combines policy and analytical support, environmental monitoring and capacity development to promote environmentally responsible mineral value chains.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide Policy Advice

- Provide specialized knowledge and expertise in critical minerals, sustainable mineral value chains and natural resource governance within the context of the project;

- Analyze existing policies, frameworks and regulations governing the minerals sector at various levels to identify opportunities, gaps, and barriers for sustainable sector development;

- Assess the regulatory landscape to ensure alignment of mineral sector policies with national development priorities and relevant international environmental and sustainability standards;

- Support the development of policies, strategies and action plans for environmentally responsible mineral sector development, considering input from stakeholders and best practices;

- Establish mechanisms for monitoring and evaluating the effectiveness of relevant sectoral policies, providing recommendations for improvements;

- Analyze financial mechanisms and funding opportunities for sustainable mineral value chains and related environmental measures, identifying potential sources of support;

- Advocate for the integration of environmental sustainability, responsible resource management and value chain development into relevant sectoral policies, plans, and programs;

- Support the strengthening of institutional arrangements and procedures for sustainable mineral resource governance in Kazakhstan.

Collaborate with relevant government, industry representatives, research organizations and other stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of sustainable mineral sector policies and practices;

- Engage with policymakers, government officials, the private sector, NGOs, and community leaders to build consensus and support environmentally responsible mineral sector development;

- Coordinate between various stakeholders involved in mineral sector policy development and implementation to ensure coherence and efficiency;

- Translate complex technical and policy concepts into accessible language and communicate the importance of sustainable mineral value chains and environmental responsibility to different audiences;

- Design and conduct capacity-building activities related to critical minerals, sector governance and environmental sustainability, enabling stakeholders to understand and contribute to effective policy development and implementation;

- Prepare technical reports, policy briefs, and communication materials to communicate policy analysis, progress, and recommendations.

Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the project.

- Organize training, workshops, and capacity building activities in a consultative manner, involving technical experts and stakeholders that may include the government, private sector, NGOs, donors, and/or academia.

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

- Participate in and ensure sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice on project related issues. Support establishment of knowledge platforms for the project, facilitate innovative mechanisms for dissemination of knowledge from the project, and develop knowledge resources and products to share with project partners and to support UNDP’s engagement in this area.

- Promote advocacy on development trends and opportunities to collaborate in coordination with the project partners, stakeholders, and UNDP communications staff.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Analyst reports to the Project Manager. The job holder will ensure to provide quality advice to Project manager and comply with appropriate UNDP policies and procedures.

Competencies

Core competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Business Acumen Ability to understand and deal with a business situation in a manner that is likely to lead to a good outcome. Ability to make good judgments and quick decisions within such frameworks Knowledge and understanding of the operational frameworks in the organization.

- Negotiation and Influence Reach a common understanding/agreement, persuade others, resolve points of difference through a dialogue, negotiate mutually acceptable solutions and create ‘win-win’ situations.

Business Development

- Human-centered Design Ability to develop solutions to problems by involving the human perspective in all steps of the problem-solving process. Knowledge and understanding of human centered design principles and practices.

- Knowledge Generation Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- Collective Intelligence Design Ability to bring together diverse groups of people, data, information, ideas, and technology to solve problems and design solutions or services. Knowledge and understanding of Collective Intelligence Design principles, methodology and practices.

- Development Knowledge Facilitation Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

2030 Agenda: People

- Gender Gender Equality Seal for Development

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in Geology, Mining Engineering, Mineral Processing, Metallurgy, Environmental Sciences, Natural Resource Management, Environmental Policy, Natural Sciences, Economics, Public Policy, Law, or a related field, is required or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas mentioned above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience at the national or international level in the minerals sector, natural resource management, sectoral policy development, economic or environmental analysis, or related technical and project coordination roles.

Desired skills:

jobs.description:
Aproximaci6n por Niveles (Tiered Approach):

De acuerdo con el compromiso de salvaguardar capacidad y apoyar al personal actual de la Organizaciön, la mayoria de vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se han anunciado utilizando un proceso de aplicaciön por niveles (tiers) en donde:

• Nivel O: personal internacional del PNUD/UNCDFNNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA), cuyos puestos såran abolidos, o cuyos contratos serån rescindidos o no renovados durante el aio 2026.

• Nivel 1: otro personal del PNUD/UNCDFNNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA).

• Nivel 2: personal del PNUD/UNCDFNNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Eespecialistas de las Naciones Unidas Skip to main content.

• Nivel 3 0 sin nivel indicado: todos los dernés tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y dernås candidatos externos.

Descripción de la Oficina/Proyecto:

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

Por más de 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

 Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

 Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

 Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

Dentro del Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental, se brinda asistencia al Gobierno de Panamá en alineamiento con el Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible en Panamá 2026-2030 y el Plan Estratégico del PNUD 2026-2030, los cuales destacan la necesidad de fortalecer el capital humano, reducir las desigualdades y apoyar la innovación y el crecimiento sostenible.

El proyecto busca contribuir al desarrollo inclusivo y sostenible de Panamá al mejorar los niveles de cohesión social mediante la inclusión activa de niños, niñas y adolescentes en procesos colectivos de enseñanza musical. Su objetivo principal es cerrar brechas sociales y promover el sentido de pertenencia, confianza en las instituciones y participación ciudadana, especialmente en territorios marcados por la desigualdad y la exclusión.

Se basa en un modelo innovador de enseñanza colectiva de la música —a través de orquestas y coros infantiles y juveniles— que trasciende lo artístico y se convierte en una política pública transformadora que promueve ciudadanía, sentido de pertenencia, equidad de género y el respeto a la diversidad, al tiempo que ofrece nuevas oportunidades de vida para jóvenes en contextos de alta vulnerabilidad.

Alcance del trabajo:

Bajo la supervisión del Asociado/a de Proyecto, el/la Asociado/a de Coros realizará las actividades necesarias de apoyo a la coordinación académica y musical de la Red Nacional de Orquestas.

Las actividades específicas incluyen:

1. Apoyo a la Coordinación Académica y Musical:

• Apoyar en la implementación y actualización de los planes de estudio y formación coral establecidos por La RED.

• Colaborar en la organización y seguimiento de los repertorios secuenciales y repertorios compartidos de las agrupaciones corales.

• Brindar apoyo en el seguimiento de los procesos de formación de las agrupaciones y ensambles corales, de acuerdo con las directrices establecidas.

• Apoyar en la coordinación de metodologías de trabajo y actividades orientadas al fortalecimiento de los procesos musicales del programa coral.

2. Seguimiento y Monitoreo de Programas Corales:

• Dar seguimiento a los cronogramas de clases, ensayos, encuentros y demás actividades de las agrupaciones corales.

• Apoyar la ejecución de los procesos de monitoreo permanente de los programas corales a nivel nacional.

• Colaborar en la recopilación de información sobre el desarrollo de las actividades, avances, retos y resultados del programa.

• Contribuir a la documentación e identificación de lecciones aprendidas y buenas prácticas derivadas de la implementación de las actividades corales.

3. Apoyo Logístico y Operativo:

• Coordinar y dar seguimiento a los espacios, materiales y recursos requeridos para ensayos, encuentros, presentaciones y conciertos.

• Apoyar los procesos de identificación, inscripción y registro de participantes cuando sea requerido.

• Brindar apoyo logístico en la organización de actividades, eventos y presentaciones corales programadas por La RED.

4. Apoyo a Procesos de Evaluación y Selección:

• Participar en los procesos de audición, evaluación y promoción de integrantes de las agrupaciones corales cuando sea requerido.

• Colaborar en el seguimiento de los planes de formación, montaje de repertorios y desarrollo de actividades y etapas del programa coral.

5. Asistir en la Coordinación Institucional y Reportes, y apoyar la gestión de conocimiento:

• Elaborar y presentar informes periódicos sobre las actividades realizadas, avances, dificultades identificadas y recomendaciones de mejora.

• Participar en reuniones, capacitaciones, seminarios y actividades convocadas por La RED, MICULTURA, PNUD u otras instancias relacionadas con el programa.

• Mantener comunicación y coordinación permanente con el equipo técnico y administrativo para garantizar la adecuada ejecución de las actividades corales.

• Apoyar la generación y el intercambio de conocimientos, así como el desarrollo de capacidades, en relación con el proyecto.

El titular desempeña otras funciones dentro de su perfil funcional que se consideren necesarias para el funcionamiento eficiente de la Oficina y la Organización.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP: As the UN lead agency on international development, UN Development Programme (UNDP) works in 170 countries and territories, including those fragile and experiencing crisis, to eradicate poverty and reduce inequality. UNDP helps countries to develop policies, leadership skills, partnering abilities, institutional capabilities, and to build resilience to achieve the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP’s work is concentrated in three focus areas: (1) sustainable development, (2) democratic governance and peace building, and (3) climate and disaster resilience.

UNDP’s Rule of Law, Security, and Human Rights Team: The UNDP’s Rule of Law, Security, and Human Rights (RoLSHR) Team is responsible for policy and practice development in the areas of the rule of law, justice, security, human rights, including business and human rights (BHR), through the implementation of the UNDP Global Programme on Strengthening the Rule of Law and Human Rights for Sustaining Peace and Fostering Development for 2022-2025. The Global Programme is guided by and aligned with the UNDP Strategic Plan for 2022-2025 and provides tailored, context-specific technical, financial, and strategic support to contexts across the development spectrum.

UNDP’s B+HR Initiative: The RoLSHR’s programmatic work on BHR is provided through the global initiative on B+HR currently implemented in 53 countries (and growing) in Africa, the Arab States, Asia and the Pacific, Europe and Central Asia, Latin America, and the Caribbean, focusing on supporting:

- Governments (across sectors): in upholding their duty to protect human rights from businesses’ abuses, including by strengthening and enforcing robust regulatory frameworks on BHR;

- Businesses (across industries): in embedding their responsibility to respect human rights throughout their operational policies and practices, including to carry out human rights due diligence across supply chains, through the B+HR Academy , which trains approximately 1,300 businesses per year;

- Civil society and other relevant stakeholders: in monitoring businesses’ human rights performance, advocating for advancing corporate respect for human rights, and providing ‘ routes to remedy ’ to people adversely affected by businesses.

The UNDP’s global initiative on B+HR is coordinated from the Geneva Office (Switzerland) and led by the Global Policy Adviser on BHR, which supports and guides Regional B+HR Focal Points. Regional Focal Points are the entry point for requests of guidance coming from B+HR Focal Points at the Country Office level.

The UNDP’s global initiative on B+HR is supported by the Governments of Japan, Netherlands, Sweden, and the EU, and is part of the UNDP Global Programme on Strengthening the Rule of Law and Human Rights for Sustaining Peace and Fostering Development for 2022-2025.

The Business and Human Rights Specialist will work under direct supervision of the Global Policy Adviser on BHR, and in close coordination with the Senior BHR Specialist. They will also work directly with Regional Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Focal Points and/or B+HR Focal Points and provide technical and capacity-strengthening support to B+HR Focal Points at the Country Office level, as needed.

Scope of Work

1. Provide technical and programmatic advisory support in implementing the existing activities of the UNDP’s global initiative on B+HR, including by:

- Advising and supporting the implementation of the global, regional, and Country Office-level donor-funded projects with particular emphasis on the ‘Finance Against Slavery and Trafficking’ initiative.

- Supporting the preparation of global events and seminars held in Geneva;

- Coordinating logistical and substantive elements of UNDP’s participation in the UN Annual Forum on BHR.

- Developing concept notes and contributing to the drafting of project proposals for the purpose of resource mobilization.

2. Provide technical support in scaling up global initiative on B+HR, including by:

- Coordinating the implementation of the resource mobilization strategy (e.g., providing thematic and regional/country-specific research, liaising and partnering with other UN Agencies for joint resource mobilization initiatives and other UNDP Teams for portfolio programming, drafting project concept notes and documents, developing workplans and activity-based budgets);

- Promoting and supporting the positioning of UNDP as a ‘practice setter’ on BHR (e.g., ensuring its global visibility, contributing to the work of the Human Rights Council, UN Working Group on Business and Human Rights and other UN Special Procedures, participating in global and regional multi-stakeholder platforms);

- Developing new thematic offers and internal strategies for way forward of the existing thematic programming;

3. Contribute to the UNDP’s knowledge generation on BHR, including by:

- Contributing to the development of knowledge products on human rights due diligence, EU Corporate Sustainability Due Diligence Directive and other mandatory human rights due diligence legislation, modern slavery, Universal Periodic Review, etc.;

- Providing peer review of internal knowledge products and inputting into submissions for reports of the UN Working Group on Business and Human Rights and other UN Special Procedures, UN Agencies, UN Teams, multi-stakeholder platforms, etc.;

4. Support overall coordination of the work of the Global B+HR team, including by:

- Coordinating the implementation of the Team Work Plan and, in conjunction with the Project Associate, monitoring the team budget.

- Supporting Country Offices’ efforts in carrying out UNDP corporate private sector due diligence and supporting them in developing and implementing Development Service Agreements with business-partners at the country level.

- Consolidating contributions of the B+HR team to the Annual Report of the Global Program 5 (GP5) and on all submissions needed for GP5 Project Boards. Leading on ROAR reporting.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Business and Human Rights Specialist will work under direct supervision of the Global Policy Adviser on BHR, and in close coordination with other BHR Specialists in the team. They will also work directly with Regional Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights Focal Points and/or B+HR Focal Points and provide technical and capacity-strengthening support to B+HR Focal Points at the Country Office level, as needed.

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3 : Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies :

- Business Direction & Strategy — Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritised plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

- Business Direction & Strategy — System Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system

- Business Development — Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- Business Management — Partnership Management: Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies.

- Business Management — Results Based Management: Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

- 2030 Agenda: Peace — Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights: Joint programming for justice and security (GFP)

- 2030 Agenda: Peace — Rule of Law, Security and Human Rights: Safeguarding human rights and protecting vulnerable groups

Required Skills and Experience Education:

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- A minimum of 5 years (with a master’s degree) or 7 years (with a bachelor’s degree) of relevant professional experience on human rights and/or BHR is required.

Required skills and competencies:

- At least 5 years of relevant professional experience with intergovernmental organizations.

- Experience in human rights due diligence, particularly in the context of the triple planetary crisis.

- Previous experience in drafting project concept notes and documents and successful resource mobilization initiatives on human rights and/or BHR.

- Previous experience in global project management, including quality assurance, MNEL, partnerships, visibility, reporting, etc..

Desired additional skills and competencies:

- Experience using the application of the UNGPs to the financial sector.

- Experience with the UN Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights (UNGPs) .

- Previous experience working on human rights with UNDP and/or other UN Agencies.

- Previous experience in developing and implementing human rights-related services to the business sector.

- Expertise and previous experience in communications for development/human rights.

Languages:

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) Country Office in Tajikistan has been active since 1994 and is guided in its work by the Country Programme Document, which in turn builds upon the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP has made a significant contribution to developing the National Development Strategy, with an outline of policies and investments necessary to reach the SDGs by 2030. Together with the Government of Tajikistan, civil society and the people of Tajikistan, UNDP works towards identifying local solutions to global and national development challenges. Its main focus is reaching sustainable development by enhancing accountability of the current governance system, mitigating natural disaster threats, and contributing to environmental sustainability and biodiversity conservation.

The Climate Change, Energy and Environment (CCEE) Cluster of UNDP Tajikistan manages a diverse and growing portfolio of various projects currently under implementation across the country. The Cluster provides strategic, technical, and operational support to national counterparts in addressing Tajikistan’s key environmental, climate, and energy challenges, in line with national development priorities and international commitments. The Cluster’s programmatic focus spans several interrelated thematic areas, including climate change adaptation and mitigation, integrated water resources management, sustainable land management, urban resilience to disaster and climate risks, promotion of renewable and green energy solutions, and biodiversity conservation and ecosystem restoration.

In particular, with regard to biodiversity conservation and it’s biodiversity portfolio, UNDP's Country Office in Tajikistan is currently supporting the country’s National Biodiversity Strategy and Action Plan (NBSAP) update and implementation in alignment with the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework (KMGBF). As countries move from updating their NBSAPs towards implementation, targeted support is required to translate national biodiversity priorities into concrete actions and address critical implementation gaps.

In this context, the NBSAP Accelerator Action Account Multi-Partner Trust Fund (NBSAP AAA MPTF) provides targeted support to countries to accelerate implementation of their NBSAP priorities and translate national biodiversity commitments into concrete action. The Fund supports high-priority interventions that address critical policy, institutional, technical and financing gaps and that have not been sufficiently covered through other available resources. Its support is intended to strengthen national readiness for sustained biodiversity action, increase implementation ambition and create foundations for further investment in achievement of national biodiversity priorities and the KMGBF.

In Tajikistan, the project directly contributes to the objectives of the NBSAP AAA MPTF by providing targeted support for NBSAP implementation, with a particular focus on operationalizing KMGBF Target 6 on invasive alien species (IAS). The project will strengthen the scientific, technical and policy basis for the prevention, monitoring and management of IAS, including through establishment of a national IAS database and development of the country’s first State Programme and Action Plan on Invasive Alien Species. These interventions will help address critical data and policy gaps, strengthen national capacities for ongoing biological risk monitoring and management, and establish a more coherent framework for coordinated action on invasive alien species.

The project further contributes to strengthening the core functions of NBSAP implementation through institutional capacity development and strategic policy support, applying a “whole-of-government” and “whole-of-society” approach. It also contributes to KMGBF Target 23 on gender equality by integrating gender-responsive approaches and promoting the equitable participation of women and vulnerable groups within IAS knowledge, monitoring and policy systems. The initiative will additionally promote youth engagement and digital innovation in biodiversity information management, thereby supporting an inclusive, sustainable and potentially scalable approach to implementation of KMGBF priorities in Tajikistan.

Under the direct supervision of UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment, and overall guidance of the Deputy Resident Representative, the Project Coordinator will coordinate project interventions, liaise with national partners and support effective teamwork and strong partnerships. The Project Coordinator will provide technical and programmatic support to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality project results that strengthen national capacities, data systems and policy frameworks for the prevention and management of invasive alien species, in line with Tajikistan’s NBSAP and the KMGBF.

He/she will ensure implementation mechanisms and technical working groups are established and meet regularly, that all planned workshops, technical studies and other activities are organised in a timely manner, and that they meet expected quality standards. He/she will also specifically be responsible for outreach activities to relevant stakeholders, and the preparation of synthesis reports, policy briefs, press releases and briefing notes for Government, donor, UNDP, etc.

Duties and Responsibilities

1. Ensure effective technical support to the project focusing on achievement of the following results:

- General coordination and liaison of project activities with national counterparts, scientific institutions and relevant stakeholders.

- Coordinate the development and validation of the National IAS Catalogue and Database.

- Facilitate the development, testing and validation of standardized IAS risk assessment protocols.

- Coordinate the development of the multi-sectoral National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Ensure alignment of the project’s technical outputs with the NBSAP, the KMGBF, national biodiversity reporting processes and other relevant national policies and strategic frameworks.

- Facilitate technical assessments, field data collection, consultations and other analytical work required for the development of the National IAS Catalogue, risk assessment protocols, IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide substantive support to project stakeholders in reviewing and validating technical methodologies, assessments, databases, policy documents and other project outputs.

- Coordinate project activities among relevant stakeholders, including but not limited to the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Centre under the Committee for Environmental Protection, National Academy of Sciences of Tajikistan, Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry Agency, Customs Service, Food Security Committee, other relevant ministries and agencies, civil society organizations, academia and local communities, as specified in the Project Document.

- Facilitate the establishment and effective functioning of the Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group for technical coordination, policy dialogue and development and validation of project outputs.

- Ensure the elaboration of the Stakeholder Engagement and Gender Action Plan before the kickstart of project implementation, and further ensure their effective implementation and regular monitoring.

- Ensure that gender-responsive approaches and meaningful participation of women, youth and vulnerable groups are appropriately integrated into IAS assessments, data systems, consultations and policy development in line with the project’s Results Framework.

- Coordinate and follow up on implementation of relevant environmental and social safeguard measures.

- Review all technical reports as required. Fulfil substantive activities under the Project Work Plan which are not covered by consultants or other contracted experts.

- Support the timely technical review, validation, finalization and submission to relevant national authorities of key project outputs, including the National IAS Catalogue, standardized risk assessment protocols, national IAS Database and National IAS Programme and Action Plan.

- Provide necessary inputs to showcase project’s experience at national, regional and international forums/events as required.

- Upon request of the Programme Specialist, participate in and make presentations at conferences, working meetings, workshops, round-table discussions and other relevant events on the IAS project and its linkages with biodiversity conservation, NBSAP and KMGBF implementation.

2. Ensure effective operational and programmatic support for the project:

- Ensure operational and programmatic coordination of the project in accordance with the Project Document, approved work plans, Results Framework and applicable UNDP rules and procedures.

- Support the overall management and coordination of project implementation, ensuring timely and proper execution of activities by consultants, experts, contractors and project partners.

- Prepare Terms of Reference (ToR) for national and international consultants, experts, contractors and other service providers in line with the Project Document and relevant UNDP procedures; coordinate and guide their work and ensure compliance with agreed work plans and respective ToRs and the quality and timely delivery of outputs.

- Facilitate organization of the project Inception Workshop and support the establishment and functioning of the Project Steering Committee, Multi-Stakeholder Platform and Task Force Group/Thematic Working Group.

- Support communication and coordination with government institutions, scientific organizations, civil society organizations, local communities and other stakeholders involved in implementation of activities specified in the Project Work Plan.

- Prepare meeting agendas and background materials, take notes/minutes of project meetings and ensure timely follow-up on decisions and agreed actions.

- Support preparation and implementation of annual and detailed project work plans, including monitoring of implementation progress and follow-up on planned activities and deliverables.

- Monitor project progress against the Results Framework, including achievement of indicators and targets, and coordinate collection, verification and consolidation of supporting evidence.

- Collect and analyze project-related data and information from government counterparts, consultants, scientific institutions, implementing partners and other relevant sources for project monitoring and reporting purposes.

- Assume responsibility for the timely preparation of project progress reports and other required inputs in line with the reporting requirements of NBSAP AAA MPTF and corporate standards of UNDP.

- Support preparation of the project’s final report and project operational closure upon completion of project activities.

- Monitor project risks and issues in accordance with the Project Document and risk framework and ensure that emerging risks are promptly brought to the attention of the Programme Specialist and relevant project governance bodies.

- Support regular updating of project risk log and follow up on agreed risk mitigation measures.

- Monitor project expenditures, commitments and balances against approved project budget lines and work plans and bring potential deviations requiring management attention to the Programme Specialist.

- Coordinate project activities with other relevant biodiversity, climate and environmental initiatives and programmes in Tajikistan to ensure complementarity, avoid duplication and promote synergies, including with NBSAP update and national reporting.

- Provide assistance and substantive inputs to the Programme Specialist in preparation of project briefs, presentations, reports, talking points and other relevant materials.

- Ensure effective dissemination of and access to information on project activities and results, and support project outreach and communication activities in coordination with UNDP communications staff.

- Liaise with the NBSAP AAA MPTF focal point and relevant UNDP regional focal point(s) to ensure effective project implementation, seek and follow up on technical and operational guidance, address project-related issues and queries, and ensure alignment with applicable programme requirements and guidance.

- Support resource mobilization efforts by providing inputs to the new project ideas, concept notes, funding proposals, and other relevant resource mobilization materials.

3. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area.

- Organize trainings, technical workshops, consultations, awareness-raising events and capacity-building activities in a participatory manner, involving relevant government institutions, scientific / academic institutions, civil society organizations, local communities, women and youth groups, and other stakeholders.

- Support capacity building of decision-makers and relevant technical institutions on IAS identification, risk assessment, Geographic Information System (GIS)-based monitoring, data management, use of the national IAS Database to be established under the project, and relevant NBSAP and KMGBF frameworks.

- Support development and dissemination of technical guidance, IAS field guides, training materials, project briefs, factsheets, awareness materials and other knowledge products generated under the project.

- Identify, synthesize and document good practices, lessons learned and implementation experience generated by the project and its partners, including through maintenance of relevant project knowledge and lessons-learned records.

- Participate in and ensure substantive contributions to relevant knowledge networks, communities of practice and technical exchanges on IAS management, biodiversity conservation and implementation of the NBSAP and KMGBF.

- Promote awareness and advocacy on IAS-related biodiversity risks, prevention and management measures, and opportunities for collaboration in coordination with project partners, stakeholders and UNDP communications staff.

- Support engagement of women, youth and local communities in knowledge generation, awareness raising and dissemination of biodiversity information, in line with the project’s whole-of-government and whole-of-society approach.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office/Project and the Organization

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Coordinator will be based in Dushanbe, at the premises of either the National Biodiversity and Biosafety Center or the National Academy of Sciences, subject to management decision with frequent visits to the UNDP Country Office. Within his/her role, the incumbent will coordinate the achievement of the expected project results by providing strategic guidance to project staff and consultants and liaising among the targeted stakeholders to facilitate the implementation of relevant activities. The Project Coordinator will be accountable and report to the UNDP Programme Specialist on Climate Change, Energy and Environment.

Competencies

Core competencies:

Background

As all countries around the globe are seeking new ways to address complex and interconnected challenges such as shocks from crises, economic stagnation, inequality and poverty, providing access to clean and affordable energy, protect the environment, or mitigating and adapting to climate change, UNDP aims to develop integrated responses to these issues.

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In addition to multi-lateral and bi-lateral partnerships, UNDP provides countries with specialized integrated technical services for eligibility assessment, programme/project formulation and implementation, capacity development, policy advice, technical assistance, training and technology transfer, mobilization of co-financing, implementation oversight, results management and evaluation, performance-based payments and knowledge management services.

The UNDP Country Office (CO) in Brazil is a key development partner of the Brazilian government and supports national and sub-national public and private sector institutions and civil society to achieve a more sustainable and inclusive society by strengthening democratic institutions, improvement of governance effectiveness, reduction of poverty and inequalities and addressing climate change and biodiversity issues.

In the pursuit of aligning organizational resources with UNDP strategic objectives and serving as the overarching framework to propel the operational reform agenda and streamline the United Nations' (UN) operational presence in Brazil, the Country Office (CO) has structured its functional organization into three primary domains: the management support functions, the Programme team, and the Operations Team. The Operations Team is further comprised of units encompassing Finance, Human Resources (HR), Support to Projects, and the Common Back Office (CBO), which encompasses common services for the UN House, including Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Administration and Logistics, Procurement and Travel, and HR services tailored for UN entities and Protocol. All of these units bear the responsibility for ensuring the adherence to UN principles and UNDP policies and procedures in the realm of operational functions.

The Operations Team plays a pivotal role in enhancing the efficacy of UN operational services and UNDP Brazil. It does so by crafting a comprehensive service delivery platform aimed at providing operational solutions to all UN entities and UNDP programs and projects. Moreover, it coordinates operational services and explores their potential expansion to the UN Common Back Office.

Under the overall guidance of the UNDP Operations Manager in her role of the Common Back Office Manager and direct supervision of the ICT Analyst, the ICT Help Desk Support provides ICT and administrative support services to the CBO, provides daily technical support to users of information management tools and technology infrastructure. The ICT Help Desk Support promotes a client-oriented approach.

The ICT Help Desk Support works in close collaboration with the members of the CBO, Front Office, and relevant UN personnel in the CO and HQ to exchange information and ensure consistent service delivery.

The key results have an impact on the overall efficiency of the CBO including improved business results and client services. Forward-looking ICT management has an impact on the organization of office management, knowledge sharing, and information provision.

Duties and Responsibilities

Summary of key functions:

1. Provide support for the implementation of ICT management systems and strategies

• Assist with routine ICT activities, including basic testing of applications and digital tools, following established procedures and instructions.

• Maintain simple records of ICT activities and report technical issues to the responsible ICT personnel.

2. Provide support effective functioning of the CO (Country Office) hardware and software packages

• Support to respond to basic user requests related to computers, printers, mobile devices, standard applications, and other ICT equipment, providing initial assistance and referring unresolved issues to the ICT team.

• Support with the preparation of equipment for users, the installation of approved applications, and routine equipment and inventory checks, following established procedures.

3. Provide support to networks administration

• Assist users with basic connectivity issues involving Wi-Fi, internet access, VPN, and corporate networks, referring unresolved problems to the responsible ICT personnel.

• Assist with routine user access requests and report connectivity interruptions or suspected security issues in accordance with established procedures.

4. Provide administrative support

• Register and update ICT support requests in the designated system and maintain basic records of equipment, repairs, warranties, and related activities.

• Assist with the distribution, return, repair, replacement, and disposal of ICT equipment, as well as monitoring supplies and reporting replenishment needs.

5. Support knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO

• Provide basic guidance to users on commonly used ICT applications, tools, and services, including established cybersecurity practices.

• Assist with updating simple user instructions and documenting frequently reported issues and their solutions.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Project

The ICT Help Desk Support works in the local ICT team for CBO and reports directly to the ICT Manager.

Background

UNDP provides integrated programmatic, policy and financing solutions to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In this context, UNDP has created a Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. The Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) and the Crisis Bureau (CB) are the two anchor Bureau of the GPN.

In this context, the newly established Governance, Rule of Law, and Peacebuilding (GRP) Hub, a joint endeavor with the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS), provides leadership and advisory services to enhance UNDP’s impact on governance and peacebuilding, ensuring the integration of democratic governance and human rights into crisis response and recovery. The Hub aims to build an integrated portfolio collaboratively between the CB and BPPS and establish partnerships with various stakeholders including the UN System, IFIs, civil society, and the private sector.

Through Local Action, the GRP Hub seeks to contribute to peace and development, achieving a visible impact on communities and improving lives by delivering integrated solutions that harness global expertise and partnerships. The Local Action Unit works closely with local and regional governments as key development players, highlighting their role as public service implementers, as drivers of innovation and the closest institution to people.

Local and regional governments are already responsible of over 65% of the SDG targets, most of them linked to basic service provision from water, sanitation, mobility, climate action, health or education. Cities and territories are playing a big part on the implementation of SDGs, that are becoming a new tool for strategic planning and budgeting in the mid to long-term. Since 2015, local governments and their associations have been increasingly active in promoting the SDGs through advocacy, working with their local population and partners in transposing the spirit of Agenda 2030 in cities and territories. Local Governments have also started to use SDGs as a strategic framework to deliver better and more innovative public services linked to SDG targets and indicators.

Within this context, the SDG Local Action project is seeking to recruit a Communications and Research Analyst to contribute to the design of contents and communications tools to highlight the role of local and regional governments in implementing Agenda 2030.

The Communications and Research Analyst will also support participant local and regional governments exchange on SDG implementation, contributing to generate knowledge and replication of successful experiences to implement Agenda 2030 at local level. Finally, the Analyst will also support the communication and research needs of the Mayors Challenge project.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Communications and Research Analyst will report to the Learning and Knowledge Generation Analyst, who works home based (CET time zone).

SDGs are genuinely interlinked with service provision at local level. To be able to deliver on Agenda 2030, local and regional governments are innovating on the way they plan, design and implement public policy. The Analyst will support UNDP cities and their partners to generate knowledge through the exchange of experiences, organizing international events and elaborating policy briefs and other communication materials. The Communications and Research Analyst will also liaise with the different UNDP project personnel globally to collect information, monitor and lessons learnt issued from the Mayors Challenge project.

The Communications and Research Analyst will support participant local and regional governments to communicate their stories, analyzing project data and providing narratives for targeted public segments: including local population, central governments and the international community.

Summary of functions:

1. Elaborate communications products for local and regional governments on SDG implementation solutions

- Draft and design content for the project and UNDP social platforms and project newsletter;

- Elaborate “SDG stories” about how local governments are implementing Agenda 2030;

- Elaborate content for learning exercises targeting the participating local governments.

2. Conduct research on innovative delivery of public services by local and regional governments

- Elaborate knowledge products on how local governments are contributing to SDGs by innovating public service delivery;

- Elaborate policy briefs and easy communicable knowledge materials on the lessons learnt by participating local governments;

- Promote exchange of experiences amongst local governments on how their peers are implementing the SDGs at local level.

3. Contribute to the SDG Local Action advocacy strategy to showcase the key role of local and regional governments for Agenda 2030

- Develop advocacy, visibility and promotional material that are necessary for the project;

- Analyze project data and link with SDG targets and Agenda 2030 narrative;

- Maintain and regularly update the project repository/archive of all communications material including photos videos and audios;

- Assist the Research Analyst to design and implement baseline surveys, public perception surveys, impact assessments/ tracking surveys including the development of survey report templates, design and layout of reports and related tasks;

- Assist the Research Analyst in gathering information to prepare the project metrics reports;

- Support the project team, including the UNDP Country Office staff in addressing their communications needs in regards to SDG local action.

4. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area(s)

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Digital Awareness and Literacy: Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skilfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed.

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

- Media Relations: Ability to develop media relations across all aspects of media work including relationships with media and preparing media materials such as messages.
