jobs.title: Human Resources Assistant (1 vaga) (Home based) [Open to internal and external applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

In the context of the adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) by member States of the United Nations (UN), UNDP has supported Member States and other stakeholders in implementing commitments – which set concrete aspirations to end hunger and disease for all people in the world; fight inequality and discrimination; promoting sustainable production and consumption systems and combating climate change.

Supporting the implementation of the 2030 Agenda and the SDGs in Brazil is an essential part of UNDP’s mandate, and UNDP has been working, in partnership with the Brazilian government and other partners, on social mobilization and territorialization of the SDGs to reach areas and communities where progress has been slower and assure that “no one is left behind”. The focus is on strengthening institutional capacities and social participation mechanisms to ensure the design and implementation of inclusive public policies in a friendly and profitable business environment respecting and preserving the environment.

In aligning the organizational resources behind its strategy, the Brazil Country Office (CO) functional structure comprises three main areas, the management support functions, Programme team and Operations Team. The Operations Team is composed of Human Resources (HR), Finance, Support to Projects, and the Common Back Office (CBO), which encompasses common services for the UN House, including Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Administration and Logistics, Procurement and Travel, and HR services tailored for UN entities and Protocol. All of which are responsible for quality assurance for the implementation of UNDP policies and procedures in these operational functions.

The Operations Team plays a pivotal role in enhancing the efficacy of UN operational services and UNDP Brazil. It does so by crafting a comprehensive service delivery platform aimed at providing operational solutions to all UN entities and UNDP programs and projects. Moreover, it coordinates operational services and explores their potential expansion to the UN Common Back Office.

Under the overall guidance of the UNDP Operations Manager and UN Common Back Office Manager for Brazil and direct supervision of the Human Resources Associate and the overall supervision of the Human Resources Analyst, the Human Resources Assistant (HR) generalist provides support to the HR Unit with the contract administration of personnel hired under NPSA modality, including payroll management, strategic reports, recruitment and selection process, mainly for UNDP projects and UN Agencies, and ensuring high quality, accuracy and consistency of work.

The HR Assistant generalist will support our HR department in ensuring smooth and efficient business operations. This position will have both transational and strategic responsibilities, helping to plan and administer important functions, such as recruitment & selection and administration of contracts.

The HR Assistant generalist provides support to all employees and works in line with the HR Strategy, in close collaboration with the Operations, Programme and projects’ staff in the Country Office.

The incumbent will ensure consistent service delivery with full compliance with UN/UNDP rules related to HR processes, records, regulations, policies and strategies on the National Personnel Service Agreement modality.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provide support to the implementation of HR strategies related to project positions:

- Ensure full compliance of HR processes and records with UN/UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and strategies;

- Provide HR administrative support for the effective implementation of HR strategies and initiatives;

- Support in the elaboration of new SOPs and KPIs of HR Services;

- Suggests ideas for streamlining procedures to deliver optimal client service.

Provide support on Recruitment & Selection processes of project positions:

- Assist with the review of TORs and R&S documentation for completeness, consistency and compliance with applicable policies and procedures;

- Support the organization and follow-up of R&S processes, including recruitment timelines and process tracking;

- Support the publication and follow-up of vacancy announcements, ensuring accurate and timely dissemination through appropriate recruitment channels;

- Conduct initial screening of applicants against established minimum requirements and selection criteria;

- Assist with the preparation and administration of technical assessments and other recruitment tools, as applicable;

- Facilitate interview panels, including scheduling the preparation of documentation and interview materials, coordination with panel members, and preparation of minutes/reports;

- Facilitate information sharing and follow-up with Hiring Managers and relevant stakeholders throughout the R&S process;

- Maintain accurate and complete R&S records, ensuring proper filing and documentation of recruitment processes;

- Ensure accurate data management in official databases;

- Support the maintenance and update of recruitment metrics and tracking systems;

- Assist with the maintenance and management of CO rosters and talent pools, as applicable;

Implement HR services and act as Country Office (CO) Liaison with GSSC:

- Act as the primary focal point and liaison with the Global Shared Services Center (GSSC) for the end-to-end administration of project staff life-cycle transactions.

- Coordinate with GSSC to ensure timely processing of hires, contract extensions, lateral transfers, salary distribution setups, benefits, and separations.

- Track HR transactions related to positions, recruitment, benefits, earnings/deductions, retroactivity, recoveries, adjustments, and separations through ERP, in close coordination with GSSC as applicable.

- Monitor and support the collection of mandatory onboarding/offboarding documents from personnel, serving as the local administrative bridge to submit complete packages to GSSC.

- Maintain proper filing system for HR records and documents.

- Extract, input, copy and file data from various sources.

- Prepare routine correspondence, memoranda, and reports in accordance with CO needs and SOPs.

- Provide HR administrative support for the effective implementation of HR services to the UNDP project positions and partner agencies.

Supports effective communication and administration assistance for varied and inter-related services, including project operations support, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Maintenance of the filing system ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials. Use of automated filing system;

- Support the information flow in the office and dissemination of corporate and interoffice communication to personnel as required;

- Support the facilitation information sharing with Management Support and Programme and Operations Teams;

- Support the follow up of deadlines, established commitments, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to the HR Analyst;

- Draft routine correspondence, interoffice circulars, general briefing notes, documents, reports, minutes of meetings and translations when required;

- Support the administration of meetings, appointments and briefings within the HR Unit

- Assist and carry administrative tasks related to HR Unit.

Supports knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support the organization and delivery of training sessions for Operations and project staff on HR-related matters and other relevant topics;

- Contribute to knowledge sharing through HR-related guidance, knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Human Resources Associate, the Human Resources Assistant contributes to the HR Services, ensuring high quality of work, ensuring high quality on the delivery of the services needs.

Competencies

Core competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management | Communication: Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience

Abilit to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

Business Development | Integration within the UN: Ability to identity, and integrate capacity and assets of the UN system, and engage in joint work; knowledge of the UN System and ability to apply this knowledge to strategic and/or practical situations.

Business Development | Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Business Management | Customer Satisfaction/Client Management: Ability to respond timely and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs. Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy. Look for ways to add value beyond clients' immediate requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns

HR - Compensation/remuneration | Payroll management: Knowledge of and ability to apply mechanisms and tools to collect payroll data, process payroll, and manage payroll reports.

HR - People strategy and planning | People analytics: Ability to generate and align people data with business intelligence data to inform strategic decision-making; knowledge of databases, their architecture, integration and landscape; ability to create and use data models; knowledge of visualization techniques.

Gathering and using data and information to provide insights into people issues and guide decision-making.

HR - Recruitment | Assessment and selection: Knowledge and ability to apply various candidate

assessment and selection methodologies, tools and platforms; ability to effectively align them with specific recruitment needs

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA

Min. Education requirements

- Secondary education is required.

- A University degree (bachelor´s degree) in Business Administration, Psychology, Human Resources or related areas of humanities, Communications, Social Sciences or an equivalent field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Min. years of relevant work experience

- Minimum 4 years (with secondary education) or 1 year (with Bachelor´s degree) of relevant experience in Human Resources, preferably covering areas such as recruitment and selection, personnel administration, contract administration, payroll, benefits and entitlement management, among others.

Required skills

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, Power Point, etc.).

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Experience in Recruitment & Selection processes;

- Experience with personnel contract management and HR transactions;

- Experience in preparing reports, developing indicators, and monitoring administrative processes.

- Experience in maintaining and organizing personnel records and HR documentation.

- Experience in using Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) systems, particularly HR-related modules.

- Experience working with multiple stakeholders, including Hiring Managers, project teams, operations teams and/or shared service centres.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in Portuguese is required.

- Working knowledge in English is desirable.

Professional Certificates

- N/A

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

South Sudan gained its independence in 2011 following a long and protracted civil war. Since then, two significant conflicts broke out (December 2013 and July 2016) plunging the country into a deep economic, social, and political crisis which have undermined the development gains achieved since independence and exacerbated the continuing humanitarian crisis. The country is endowed with vast natural resources and economic potential that has not translated into improved standards of living for the citizens. It is extremely vulnerable to climate change impacts with rising temperatures and the increasing severity of drought and flood events having major negative impacts on lives and livelihoods. Such impacts compounded food insecurity, conflicts, and a macroeconomic crisis. Capacity-constrained institutions and fragile governance in the post-conflict context add to the challenges of climate change adaptation in South Sudan.

South Sudan is a low-income, oil-dependent economy, faces significant humanitarian, political, and climate-related challenges, categorized by limited infrastructure, high vulnerability to shocks, low domestic production, and a narrow export base dominated by oil. In 2026, the country's nominal GDP is estimated at approximately US$6.03 billion, with a GDP per capita of around US$345, substantially below the global average of US$10,589. Despite these constraints, South Sudan possesses considerable development potential, with approximately 70 per cent of its land being arable, although only about 4 per cent is currently cultivated. Economic growth continues to be hindered by prolonged crises, including economic decline, armed conflict, displacement, insecurity, climate shocks, and weak institutional capacity, all of which undermine domestic and cross-border trade as well as agricultural, livestock, and fisheries production. Nevertheless, the country offers significant opportunities for investment and economic transformation in sectors such as oil and gas, mining, agriculture, and infrastructure development, particularly in roads, telecommunications, and hydropower, which could drive economic diversification, job creation, and sustainable development if supported by greater stability, improved governance, and increased investment.

South Sudan is among the most climate-vulnerable countries in the world, facing recurrent floods, droughts, extreme weather events, and shifting rainfall patterns. These impacts exacerbate food insecurity, water scarcity, land degradation, and conflict over natural resources. With livelihoods heavily dependent on rain-fed agriculture and pastoralism, climate variability significantly undermines resilience and sustainable development. The environment and natural resources of South Sudan are the foundation for economic and social development to satisfy important economic, social, cultural, and political needs of its peoples. However, climate change coupled with human activities are posing a threat to the quality of environment, mostly resulting from unsustainable use of natural resources and pollution from agricultural development. Land degradation poses serious threats to food security, water availability, adaptation and mitigation to climate change and the livelihoods of the people of South Sudan.

Flooding has affected 1.35 million people across 39 counties in eight states, displacing nearly 375,600 people, many sheltering on higher ground with livestock. Sudan Conflict added to already worsen humanitarian situation. South Sudan received more than 1.35 million refugees and returnees, this situation requires a need for robust durable solution framework, strengthening the capacity of relevant institution such as Relief and rehabilitation and Ministry of Humanitarian Affairs and Disaster Management (MoHADM) to lead the preparedness response, recovery and reintegration efforts.

UNDP, in partnership with the Ministries of Environment and Forestry and Finance and Planning and other relevant stakeholders, will support the government to implement the NDC and NAP with a focus on: a) the government pledge to plant 100 million trees; b) promoting climate-smart and resilient agricultural technology and watershed development; c) providing thought leadership to various technical and strategic groups; and d) promoting the use of and increase access to clean energy through the generation and distribution of affordable, green energy solutions for public institutions and communities. In addition, the CO is also supporting Ministry of Environment and Forestry (MoEF) develop South Sudan's Carbon Market Readiness Framework under Article 6 of Paris Agreement, A new initiative on Biodiversity Finance (BIOFIN) is being rolled out which aims to develop national biodiversity finance plans (BFP).

Youth unemployment, estimated at 50%, is both a cause and a consequence of fragility. Therefore, addressing youth unemployment in South Sudan could drive its peace, stability and economic development. Thus, there is an urgent need for the creation of employment opportunities through strengthening the private sector, skills and entrepreneurship development, and promoting the provision of quality business development services, innovative financing and capital, facilitation of access to local and national markets, and strengthening the enabling environment for enterprise growth

The Stabilization Recovery and Resilience (StaRR) Unit adopted a portfolio approach in programming, establishing the complementarity and development of programmes and projects to enhance the achievement of relevant Country Programme Document (CPD) targets and focusing it on four major areas/portfolios, namely, Youth and Women Empowerment and Empowerment; Climate Change and Environment; Durable Solutions and Disaster Risk Management; and Trade. The programme portfiolio of the StaRR unit has been progressively expanding in terms of funding and engagement managing to significantly contribute towards the achievement of UNDP South Sudan’s CPD targets while expanding programmatic engagement and improving financial sustainability.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the direct supervision of the Deputy Resident Representative (Programme), the Programme Advisor Stabilization, Recovery and Resilience Unit will be responsible for providing technical advice for all aspects of UNDP South Sudan’s programme in the areas of youth and women empowerment, private sector development and trade, durable solution, disaster management and climate action, biodiversity, wildlife, providing strategic oversight to a portfolio of project initiatives, which are largely Directly Implemented (DIM) by UNDP, the main roles of the Programme Advisor are to provide strategic management of the Stabilization, Recovery and Resilience programme, including leading the programme strategic planning and identification of new programme areas, resources mobilization, reporting and communication and provide quality assurance more especially knowledge management.

Summary of key functions:

Lead effective programme management and strategic oversight for Stabilization Recovery and Resilience focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Provide intellectual and substantive programme leadership to enhance poverty reduction, inclusive growth, disaster risk management, durable solution and environment, private sector development, Youth and Women empowerment through policy development, programme design and implementation to support national priorities;

- Lead and guide programme and project formulation to support the development and implementation of effective pro-poor and inclusive and sustainable growth strategies and policies, including identification of strategic programme areas of cooperation;

- Provide top quality policy advice services to the Government and facilitate knowledge building and management particularly in the areas of poverty reduction and economic management issues;

- Analyses the socio-economic and political situation and trends in the area and identifies opportunities and entry points for UNDP;

- Ensures identification and promotion of joint programming and planning opportunities Identifies and develops new programme and project opportunities.

Provision of technical advisory leadership for programme implementation, including the development and oversight of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, and ensuring quality assurance across programme activities.

- Effective monitoring, measuring the impact of the UNDP Stabilization, Recovery and Resilience ( StaRR) programme and evaluation. Constant monitoring and analysis of the programme environment, timely readjustment of programme including follow-up on audit recommendations, and donor reporting;

- Provide technical leadership in the design and implementation of programme and project monitoring and evaluation (M&E) frameworks and plans, ensuring alignment of project results frameworks and M&E plans with the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and UNDP Country Programme results frameworks;

- Support the StaRR team and Country Office evaluations, manage engagement with the Evaluation Resource Centre (ERC), and follow up on the implementation of evaluation recommendations. Ensure UNDP’s active participation and representation in UNCT M&E working groups and related events and workshops;

- Ensure that UNDP quality assurance standards are consistently applied in project and programme progress reports, Annual Progress Reports (APRs), Results-Oriented Annual Reports (ROAR), Integrated Work Plan (IWP) updates, and other corporate accountability and performance reporting requirements.

Lead Strategic Partnership & Resource Mobilization and Facilitate Knowledge Management focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Ensure development and maintenance of relevant professional contacts and networks of cooperation and support resource mobilization in cooperation with the Programme Management Support Unit;

- Support the implementation of the UNDP South Sudan partnerships and resources mobilization strategy to achieve programme outcomes;

- Creation and coordination of partnerships with the UN Agencies, IFIs, government institutions, bi-lateral and multi-lateral donors, private sector, and civil society working on issues related to Human Development and Inclusive Growth;

- Determination of programmatic areas of cooperation, based on strategic goals of UNDP, country needs and donors’ priorities;

- Analysis and research of information on donors, preparation of substantive briefs on possible areas of cooperation, identification of opportunities for cost sharing;

- Ensure strong and strategic relationships with key government counterparts, and donors;

- Ensures strong coordination of the UNDP programme with other UN Agencies, the Resident Coordinator Office, relevant units of the UN Mission in South Sudan (UNMISS) and other entities, including South Sudan Government institutions and local and nongovernmental actors, members of the diplomatic community, and UN headquarters;

- Participates in relevant Government and UN interagency task forces, working groups, and/or theme groups for capacity development;

- Makes sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice;

- Determination of programmatic areas of cooperation, based on strategic goals of UNDP, country needs and donors’ priorities;

- Ensures proper coordination and inputs to interagency initiatives;

- Maintains collaboration and coordination with the other Agencies to ensure programmatic integration and sharing of best practices;

- Contributes to the development of the CO Partnership and Resource Mobilization (PRM) strategy, including planning tools to implement the strategy;

- Identifies new partnerships and strengthens existing ones at the SO level through innovative approaches to partnership development;

- Encourages ways of increasing Sub-Office funding base such as engaging in resource mobilization efforts in consultation with local counterparts and following up with donors on local opportunities;

- Makes sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

Institutional Arrangement

The Programme Advisor works in close collaboration with the other programme Units (Democratic Governance and Global Fund, Strategic Policy Analysis Unit SPACE, Programme Management Support Unit PMSU), and the Operations team in the UNDP South Sudan Office to ensure effective and efficient programme delivery within the overall strategy and approach of UNDP in South Sudan.

Competencies

Core competencies:

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

- System Thinking Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact other parts of the system

- Strategic Thinking Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Or a first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above in combination with an additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Minimum of 10 years (with master’s degree) or 12 years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience at the national or international level in programme management is required.

- Demonstrated experience in design, monitoring and evaluation of development programmes and projects;

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP is the United Nations’ lead agency on international development, working in 170 countries and territories to help people build better lives while protecting the planet. For 60 years, UNDP has supported countries to make progress on the issues that matter most, with human development at the core of its mandate. Our work is built on trust and long-term partnerships with governments, communities and organizations at every level.

UNDP Indonesia works with Indonesian partners to deliver an ambitious programme, fully aligned to the national priorities of Indonesia. The strategic priorities of UNDP Indonesia through its Country Programme 2026 -2030 are encapsulated under three outcome areas:

(1) Human Development

(2) Nature, Decarbonization and Resilience

(3) Economic and Digital Transformation

Operating in a Middle-Income Country brings its own set of complexities and opportunities. With 70% of the Indonesian economy directly or indirectly reliant on its natural resources, the link between nature, climate, jobs, and economic empowerment become critical. UNDP’s past experiences and support include innovative sustainable financing, digital health, energy transition and climate policies, improved service delivery that leaves no one behind. Enablers and multipliers such as digitalization and Artificial Intelligence are at the core of its efforts. Building on its vast and long experiences, and the knowledge of its entire team of professionals, UNDP Indonesia demonstrate its thought-leadership and translate knowledge into policy advice, investment opportunities and scalable solutions for Indonesia’s critical development priorities

The Food Systems, Land Use and Restoration (FOLUR) Indonesia Project is a Global Environment Facility (GEF)-funded initiative implemented by the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), in collaboration with the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO), under the leadership of the Coordinating Ministry for Food Affairs. The project promotes sustainable commodity production, responsible land use, landscape restoration and biodiversity conservation through an integrated landscape approach. Focusing on key commodities, including palm oil, cocoa, coffee and rice, the project aims to strengthen sustainable value chains, reduce deforestation, enhance multi-stakeholder collaboration and improve the livelihoods of smallholder farmers and local communities.

The Sustainable Landscape Programme Indonesia (SLPI) Phase II, supported by the Government of Switzerland through the Swiss State Secretariat for Economic Affairs (SECO), is implemented in partnership with the Government of Indonesia and relevant landscape partners, with UNDP providing programme-level coordination and technical support. The programme aims to advance sustainable landscape management, responsible commodity production, forest conservation and inclusive rural development by strengthening landscape governance, promoting sustainable land-use practices and fostering collaboration among government institutions, private sector actors and local communities.

Both FOLUR and SLPI share complementary objectives in promoting sustainable commodity systems, strengthening landscape governance, facilitating multi-stakeholder partnerships and advancing environmentally sustainable and inclusive development. To support effective implementation, results monitoring and evidence-based decision-making across both initiatives, UNDP seeks to recruit a Monitoring, Evaluation and Knowledge Management (MEKM) Analyst (NPSA-8). The Analyst will provide technical support to the development and implementation of project monitoring and evaluation frameworks, results-based reporting, data collection and analysis, knowledge management and learning activities. Working closely with the respective project teams and implementing partners, and relevant teams in the Country Office the Analyst will contribute to consistent monitoring of project performance, documentation and dissemination of results and lessons learned, and adaptive management, while ensuring alignment with each project's results framework, reporting requirements and applicable UNDP standards.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Knowledge Management (MEKM) Analyst will work under the overall day to day supervision of the Project Manager (matrix supervision), and report to the Programme Manager of the relevant NLCD cluster head. S/he will work in close coordination with project teams, implementing partners, government counterparts, and UNDP corporate functions.

The incumbent will serve as the portfolio focal point for monitoring, evaluation, reporting, knowledge management, and learning across the FOLUR and SLPI portfolios, ensuring the quality, consistency, and timely delivery of results-based management processes and products.

The Monitoring, Evaluation, and Knowledge Management Analyst (MEKM) will lead the strategic direction and implementation of the portfolio's M&E, reporting, and learning workflows, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

1. Provision of support to the implementation and refinement of the Knowledge Management (KM) & Learning Strategy, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Drive the ongoing implementation and adaptation of the project's KM and Learning Strategy to meet evolving project needs;

- Design and implement a systematic protocol for capturing, documenting, and archiving innovations, field experiences, and lessons learned continuously across the five target landscapes to prevent the loss of institutional knowledge;

- Act as the centralized focal point for all KM functions, establishing efficient data collection and knowledge-sharing workflows that relieve technical and management personnel from KM administrative burdens and allow them to focus on technical oversight;

- Establish, organize, and maintain digital knowledge repositories and databases to ensure all project-related information and knowledge products are systematically archived and readily accessible, in close collaboration with the UNDP Communications Unit, as well as the Management and Performance Oversight Unit;

- Facilitate adaptive management processes by ensuring that lessons learned and evidence from project activities are continuously captured and integrated into project planning and decision-making;

- Act as the coordinator for knowledge flows and information exchange between project partners, government stakeholders, and other relevant UNDP initiatives.

2. Coordinate on the development and dissemination of strategic knowledge products, focusing on the achievement of the following results. All of the expected results require close consultation and guidance from the UNDP Communications Unit:

- Support the development and dissemination of knowledge products, including policy briefs, case studies, lessons learned, best practice publications, articles, and knowledge notes;

- Compile, analyze, and synthesize project data, monitoring information, evaluation findings, and field evidence to identify key trends, lessons learned, and good practices;

- Translate project results, technical information, and field experiences into clear, evidence-based knowledge products and impact stories for internal and external audiences;

- Contribute to the preparation and quality assurance of reports, communication materials, donor updates, and knowledge products, ensuring consistency and accuracy of information;

- Support the development of multimedia and digital content that showcases project achievements, results, and lessons learned;

- Assist in documenting, packaging, and organizing methodologies, tools, manuals, and other knowledge assets to facilitate knowledge sharing, replication, and sustainability;

- Support knowledge-sharing events, learning exchanges, and dissemination activities involving project stakeholders, partners, and beneficiaries;

- Provide analytical and knowledge management inputs to project reporting, donor reporting, communications products, and learning activities.

3. Strengthen learning, capacity development, and knowledge exchange, focusing on the achievement of the following results:

- Design, organize, and facilitate a variety of learning events, including technical workshops, peer-to-peer exchanges, and webinars for project staff and stakeholders;

- Identify opportunities and coordinate knowledge-sharing initiatives to leverage expertise and lessons from other regions and projects;

- Foster and support communities of practice around key thematic areas of the project to encourage continuous learning and collaboration.

4. Avoid any kind of discriminatory behavior including gender discrimination and ensure that:

- Human rights and gender equality are prioritized as an ethical principle within all actions;

- Activities are designed and implemented in accordance with “Social and Environmental Standards of UNDP”;

- Any kind of diversity based on ethnicity, age, sexual orientation, disability, religion, class, gender are respected within all implementations including data production;

- Differentiated needs of women and men are considered;

- Inclusive approach is reflected within all actions and implementations, in that sense an enabling and accessible setup in various senses such as disability gender language barrier is created;

- Necessary arrangements to provide gender parity within all committees, meetings, trainings etc. introduced.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. 2030 Agenda : Peace

jobs.title: Intern - Effective Development Cooperation (Switzerland or Home-based) - 2 positions
jobs.description:
Background

Diversity, Equity and Inclusion are core principles at UNDP: we value diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate, we foster inclusion as a way of ensuring all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, and we ensure equity and fairness in all our actions. Taking a ‘leave no one behind’ approach to our diversity efforts means increasing representation of underserved populations. People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Working in about 170 countries and territories, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) supports governments in developing strong policies, institutions and partnerships to achieve the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and its 17 Sustainable Development Goals. It does so in part through its comprehensive knowledge network, which includes expert practitioners that provide focused advice and support in strategic policy areas.

Drawing on the comparative advantages of UNDP in strengthening country capacities to manage and coordinate development cooperation, the team is situated within the Bureau of External Relations and Advocacy (BERA) and supports the Global Partnership for Effective Development Co-operation, as part of the OECD-UNDP Joint Support Team.

UNDP’s work in this area is guided by principles of effective development cooperation and supports global policy dialogue and mutual learning on effective development cooperation, helping increase the availability of transparent data on development cooperation, while supporting countries in implementing and monitoring the effective development cooperation principles. In addition, cultivating networks of partners and development practitioners is another key element of UNDP’s support to the Global Partnership for Effective Development Co-operation (GPEDC).

The interns will work under the overall guidance of the GPEDC Senior Team, with one intern working under the direct supervision of the Policy Specialist and the other under the direct supervision of the Partnership and Advocacy Specialist. Both interns will ensure day-to-day reporting to relevant team members responsible for specific thematic areas.

Duties and Responsibilities

The interns will perform the following tasks:

Policy Analysis and Secretariat Support (40%):

- Provide support to activities of the 2027-2029 Work Programme as part of the OECD-UNDP Joint Support Team (JST), including research trends in development effectiveness /cooperation, and identify linkages/key areas of support for UNDP's work in advancing the global development effectiveness agenda for 100 countries.

- Contribute to the Global Partnership monitoring exercise and its 5th monitoring round, through policy research and the development of policy/practice products such as briefs, discussions papers, country stories, blog posts and practice notes.

- Support the roll out of the 5th GPEDC monitoring exercise, including drafting briefing and guidance materials, communicating with participating governments, and supporting related meetings with stakeholders.

- Provide administrative and analytical support to the JST’s follow-up with partner countries and other stakeholders, including support with data analysis, drafting analytical products and knowledge management practices.

Communications and Advocacy Support for Monitoring (40%):

- Support with the implementation of the 5th Monitoring Round launch plan, including drafting of newsletters, blogs, video interviews, stories of progress, key messages, talking points, social media content, updating the official Trello board .

- Support with the website updates, help maintain the data visualization platform and the monitoring of the Global Dashboard .

- Draft and publish on GPEDC’s official social media platforms (X and LinkedIn) in line with UNDP guidelines and update the GPEDC official Trello Board.

Events Liaison (20%)

- Provide logistical support to annual events, international workshops, side events, regional monitoring webinars and Steering Committee meetings, and other events led by the GPEDC team.

- Responsible for drafting emails, helping with event briefings and other events-related communications with multiple partners including OECD and GPEDC Steering Committee members, particularly the partner countries.

Competencies

- Excellent organizational, event planning, and time management skills.

- Keen attention to detail and commitment to accuracy.

- Ability to work independently, observe deadlines and achieve results.

- Good research and information gathering skills, with track record in producing development research and other materials.

- Team player; works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals.

- Excellent communication skills in English (written and oral).

- Demonstrates enthusiasm and commitment to learning.

- Demonstrates commitment to UNDP’s vision, mission, and values.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

To be eligible for the UNDP internship programme, applicants must meet one of the following criteria at the time of application:

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate degree programme (ie. Master’s programme or higher) in Development Studies, Economics, Public Administration, International Relations or related field;

- Be enrolled in the final academic year of a first university degree programme (ie. Bachelor’s degree or equivalent) in Development Studies, Economics, Public Administration, International Relations or related field;

- Have recently graduated with a university degree (as defined in (a) and (b) above) and, if selected, must start the internship within one year of graduation;

- Be enrolled in a postgraduate professional traineeship programme in Development Studies, Economics, Public Administration, International Relations or related field, and undertake the internship as part of this programme.

Experience:

- Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools.

- Strong online research skills.

- Familiarity with social media scheduling, monitoring, and analytics tools.

- Skills in graphic design and video production as well as advanced excel, database management skills and Power BI are an asset.

- Experience supporting communications campaigns, events, or digital outreach activities is an asset.

- Experience supporting social media content creation and management is an asset.

- Previous experience in research and policy development, communications, advocacy, or large-scale event planning is an asset.

- Knowledge of, or direct experience working with effective development co-operation issues is an asset.

- Experience working in developing countries is desirable.

Language skills:

- Fluency in spoken and written English is required.

- Knowledge of French or Spanish is an asset.

Conditions of Internship

General Conditions:

- In accordance with the UNDP Internship policy, UNDP interns are eligible to receive a monthly stipend, with a rate that varies depending on the duty location. The stipend will be paid monthly, and part-time internship arrangements are prorated accordingly.

- Where an intern is financially supported by an institution, government or third party, UNDP will pay the intern the difference, if any, between the external financial support provided and the applicable UNDP stipend.

- Except for the stipend, all other expenses connected with the internship will be borne by the intern, sponsoring government or institutions.

Application process:

Interested applicants must include the following documents when submitting their application:

- Updated CV as well as the contact details (email and telephone number).

- Motivation letter for the internship.

Please combine the above into one single PDF document as the system only allows uploading of a single document.

Selected candidates for the internship will be requested to submit electronic versions of the following documents:

- Letter from university confirming current enrolment and graduation date, and if a graduate, copy of certificate of graduation (internship must start within one year of graduation);

- Letter of endorsement/recommendation from a professor;

- Copy of recent school transcript;

- Copy of passport/national identification card;

- Recent Medical Certificate of Good Health from a recognized physician;

- Proof of medical insurance cover (medical/accident/repatriation) valid for the duration of the internship programme.

Please note that only applicants selected for an interview will be contacted.

Disclaimer

Applicant information about UNDP rosters

Note: UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Non-discrimination

UNDP has a zero-tolerance policy towards sexual exploitation and misconduct, sexual harassment, and abuse of authority. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks, and will be expected to adhere to these standards and principles.

UNDP is an equal opportunity and inclusive employer that does not discriminate based on race, sex, gender identity, religion, nationality, ethnic origin, sexual orientation, disability, pregnancy, age, language, social origin or other status.

Scam warning

The United Nations does not charge any application, processing, training, interviewing, testing or other fee in connection with the application or recruitment process. Should you receive a solicitation for the payment of a fee, please disregard it. Furthermore, please note that emblems, logos, names and addresses are easily copied and reproduced. Therefore, you are advised to apply particular care when submitting personal information on the web.

People who identify as belonging to marginalized or excluded populations are strongly encouraged to apply. Learn more about working at UNDP including our values and inspiring stories.

UNDP does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of harassment, including sexual harassment, and discrimination. All selected candidates will, therefore, undergo rigorous reference and background checks.

Objetivo do Cargo e Contexto Organizacional

O projeto "BRA/23/009 - Fortalecimento da inovação e efetividade na atuação da JFCE para uma Justiça Centrada nas Pessoas” tem como objetivo desenvolver subsídios (novas metodologias, ações piloto, estudos e ferramentas) para fortalecer ações de inovação e de melhoria da efetividade da atuação da Justiça Federal no Ceará, valorizando uma abordagem da Justiça Centrada nas Pessoas.

Para o alcance desses objetivos, o projeto prevê os seguintes eixos de atuação:

1. Plano de fortalecimento da experiência do usuário e melhoria dos serviços prestados pela JFCE, com foco no efetivo acesso à Justiça, desenvolvido e implantado;

2. Estratégia para fortalecimento da aplicação de mecanismos de inovação e de tecnologias disruptivas na JFCE concebida, implantada e avaliada;

3. Produção e gestão do conhecimento para fortalecimento do acesso à Justiça e da efetividade das soluções propostas pela JFCE;

4. Plano de fortalecimento da gestão de pessoas e valorização dos servidores da JFCE desenvolvido e implantado;

5. Plano de fortalecimento de capacidades institucionais de governança desenvolvido e implantado;

6. Gestão eficiente e gestão de conhecimento do projeto realizadas.

No âmbito da JFCE, as ações previstas nesse projeto estão em consonância com a missão da instituição, bem como com os principais desafios identificados para inovação e modernização da JFCE, conforme expresso no item anterior e segundo a definição expressa no art. 2º, inciso IV, da Lei nº 10.973/2004.

Sobre a adesão do projeto ao plano estratégico do PNUD, reconhece-se que o projeto contribuirá para o alcance dos Objetivos de Desenvolvimento Sustentável (Agenda 2030 da ONU), mais especificamente do “Objetivo 16 – Promover sociedades pacíficas e inclusivas para o desenvolvimento sustentável, proporcionar o acesso à justiça para todos e construir instituições eficazes, responsáveis e inclusivas em todos os níveis”.

O(a) Analista de Gestão de Projetos e Produtos de Inovação Tecnológica atuará de forma presencial em Fortaleza/CE, em articulação com equipes da JFCE e do PNUD, prestando assessoria técnica especializada ao Projeto BRA/23/009 em temas relacionados à arquitetura de microsserviços, integração entre sistemas e gestão de bancos de dados. Trata-se de uma posição sênior, voltada a profissionais com experiência em cooperação internacional e gestão de projetos de inovação, capazes de liderar equipes e contribuir para a continuidade das ações de gestão dos projetos, especialmente aqueles relacionados à tecnologia da informação.

Os resultados-chave esperados para este posto visam assegurar a qualidade, eficiência e efetividade das soluções de back-end implementadas, em alinhamento com as metas acordadas e com as prioridades da JFCE no âmbito do Eixo 2 do projeto: Estratégia para fortalecimento da aplicação de mecanismos de inovação e de tecnologias disruptivas na JFCE concebida, implantada e avaliada.

O projeto BRA/23/009 tem vigência prevista até 31 de dezembro de 2027, com possibilidade de prorrogação até 2028.

Deveres e responsabilidades

O(A) Analista de Gestão de Projetos e Produtos de Inovação Tecnológica trabalhará junto à coordenação do projeto na JFCE e da Unidade de Gestão de Projetos (UGP) no PNUD liderando iniciativas de transformação digital, de metodologias inovadoras e boas práticas na gestão de projetos relacionados à melhoria da efetividade da atuação da JFCE e do Tribunal Regional Federal da 5ª região.

A pessoa selecionada atuará sob a supervisão da Analista de Projetos – Coordenação Técnica e Inovação Institucional e da Especialista em Projetos de Justiça para o Desenvolvimento, no âmbito do PNUD, e do coordenador do Eixo 2 do Projeto, no âmbito da Justiça Federal do Ceará. Em conjunto, contribuirá para a supervisão do trabalho do time vinculado ao Eixo 2 do projeto e outros profissionais dedicados a temas de inovação e tecnologia da informação. Também será responsável por liderar a equipe na gestão de projetos e produtos com foco em inovação, tecnologia da informação e justiça, atuando de forma articulada com as áreas técnicas e operacionais do PNUD e da JFCE em demandas de natureza técnica e administrativa.

As atividades previstas para este posto incluem:

1. Monitoramento do Projeto

a. Em estreita articulação com a Analista de Projetos – Coordenação Técnica e Inovação Institucional e demais integrantes da equipe de coordenação, liderar iniciativas e projetos relacionados aos temas de tecnologia da informação, inovação e transformação digital, garantindo sua implementação eficaz, em conformidade com os objetivos estabelecidos e as regras de compliance do PNUD;

b. Apoiar o planejamento, acompanhamento e monitoramento do projeto, incluindo cronogramas, entregas, recursos, riscos, dependências e resultados esperados;

c. Gerenciar tarefas, prazos e fluxos de trabalho, identificando antecipadamente problemas, gargalos e riscos e propondo soluções para assegurar a continuidade e a qualidade das iniciativas;

d. Sistematizar e analisar dados e informações do projeto de forma crítica e articulada, produzindo subsídios para tomada de decisão baseada em evidências;

e. Acompanhar a execução do projeto e apoiar a coordenação na identificação de necessidades de ajustes de escopo, cronograma, recursos e prioridades;

f. Assegurar a adequada documentação e rastreabilidade das decisões, entregas e principais marcos do projeto.

2. Gestão e Desenvolvimento de Produtos Digitais

a. Atuar na gestão de produtos digitais desenvolvidos no âmbito do projeto, em articulação com as equipes técnicas, áreas de negócio, usuários e demais partes interessadas;

b. Apoiar a definição e atualização da visão, objetivos, estratégia de evolução e proposta de valor dos produtos, assegurando seu alinhamento aos objetivos institucionais do projeto;

c. Gerenciar e manter o backlog dos produtos, consolidando demandas, necessidades e oportunidades e conduzindo sua análise, organização e priorização de forma contínua;

d. Levantar, estruturar e apoiar a validação de requisitos funcionais e não funcionais, histórias de usuário, critérios de aceite e demais artefatos necessários ao desenvolvimento das soluções;

e. Elaborar, acompanhar e atualizar roadmaps e planos de evolução dos produtos, considerando prioridades estratégicas, necessidades dos usuários, capacidade técnica, recursos disponíveis, dependências e riscos;

f. Atuar como interlocutor(a) entre usuários, áreas de negócio, equipes de desenvolvimento, consultores, empresas contratadas e demais parceiros, promovendo alinhamento quanto às necessidades, prioridades e soluções a serem desenvolvidas;

g. Acompanhar os ciclos de desenvolvimento, testes, validação e implantação das soluções, apoiando a definição de prioridades e a verificação das entregas em relação aos requisitos e critérios de aceite estabelecidos;

h. Conduzir processos de descoberta e validação de soluções junto aos usuários e partes interessadas, utilizando metodologias ágeis e abordagens centradas no usuário;

i. Monitorar o desempenho e a evolução dos produtos, identificando oportunidades de melhoria e propondo ajustes de funcionalidades, processos e prioridades;

j. Apoiar a implementação e o aprimoramento de mecanismos de governança dos produtos, incluindo fluxos de decisão, gestão de demandas, priorização e acompanhamento das entregas.

3. Gestão Administrativa e Operacional

a. Acompanhar processos administrativos, como tramitação de documentos, aquisições, controle de agendas e cumprimento de prazos institucionais, assegurando que todas as etapas operacionais estejam dentro dos parâmetros estabelecidos;

b. Conduzir reuniões técnicas e operacionais, elaborando documentos sobre os temas tratados, além de acompanhar os encaminhamentos acordados, garantindo o alinhamento entre todos os envolvidos.

c. Apoiar processos de negociação, alinhamento e tomada de decisão relacionados ao escopo, prioridades, cronogramas e entregas do projeto e dos produtos;

d. Identificar e articular oportunidades de colaboração e integração entre diferentes iniciativas, equipes e parceiros, buscando potencializar os resultados do projeto;

e. Revisar produtos entregues por consultores, empresas contratadas e parceiros, verificando sua aderência aos requisitos, escopo, objetivos e padrões de qualidade estabelecidos.

4. Coordenação Técnica, Liderança e Gestão de Equipes

a. Supervisionar e coordenar tecnicamente as atividades de gestão de projetos e produtos de inovação tecnológica e equipes alocadas no eixo 2 do projeto;

b. Liderar a equipe técnica do eixo 2 do projeto, promovendo ambiente colaborativo, desenvolvimento de competências e alinhamento contínuo com os objetivos estratégicos;

c. Identificar e gerenciar riscos técnicos e operacionais, propondo soluções baseadas em evidências e reportando gargalos críticos à Coordenação-Técnica;

d. Orientar membros da equipe do projeto no desenvolvimento de competências técnicas;

e. Liderar os ciclos de avaliações da equipe sob sua supervisão, garantindo que as discussões de feedback ocorram nos prazos institucionais;

f. Construir as metas de trabalho individuais e coletivas, em consonância com documento de projeto e plano de trabalho;

g. Planejar e gerenciar escalas de ausências da equipe do projeto.

5. Inovação, Metodologias e Desenvolvimento de Capacidades

a. Identificar e integrar tecnologias emergentes que possam otimizar os processos, aplicando metodologias ágeis na gestão e implementação de projetos;

b. Participar ativamente de processos de recrutamento, lançamento de editais, integração de equipes, treinamentos e ações de desenvolvimento, em articulação com o PNUD e demais parceiros, visando melhorar a capacitação da equipe e a execução dos projetos;

c. Apoiar a criação de ambientes e processos que favoreçam a experimentação, aprendizagem contínua e melhoria das soluções desenvolvidas no âmbito dos projetos.

6. Gestão do Conhecimento e Produção Técnica

a. Elaborar e revisar relatórios técnicos, notas conceituais e pareceres estratégicos;

b. Sistematizar informações e dados relevantes do projeto, organizando-os de forma acessível para subsidiar a elaboração de publicações e produtos relacionados à temática de inovação, direitos humanos e justiça;

c. Apoiar a organização e estruturação de informações estratégicas do projeto.

O titular desempenha outras funções dentro do seu perfil funcional que considere necessárias ao bom funcionamento do Projeto.

Arranjo Institucional

O(A) Analista de Gestão de Projetos e Produtos de Inovação Tecnológica estará sob supervisão da Analista de Projetos – Coordenação Técnica e Inovação Institucional e da Especialista em Projetos de Justiça para o Desenvolvimento, no âmbito do PNUD, e do coordenador do Eixo 2 do Projeto, no âmbito da Justiça Federal do Ceará. O(A) profissional supervisionará a equipe técnica alocada no Eixo 2 do projeto e manterá interlocução regular com representantes da JFCE, do TRF5 e parceiros institucionais externos.

Competências

- Alcançar Resultados - NÍVEL 2: Amplia soluções e simplifica processos, equilibrando rapidez e precisão na execução do trabalho.

- Pensar de forma Inovadora - NÍVEL 2: Propõe novas ideias e está aberto a abordagens inovadoras, demonstrando pensamento sistêmico e integrado.

- Aprender Continuamente - NÍVEL 2: Sai da zona de conforto, aprende com os outros e apoia o aprendizado deles.

- Adaptar com Agilidade - NÍVEL 2: Adapta processos e abordagens para novas situações, envolvendo outros no processo de mudança.

- Agir com Determinação - NÍVEL 2: Persevera e lida com múltiplas fontes de pressão simultaneamente.

- Engajar e fazer Parcerias - NÍVEL 2: Atua como facilitador e integrador, reunindo pessoas e construindo ou mantendo coalizões e parcerias.

- Promover a Diversidade e Inclusão - NÍVEL 2: Facilita conversas para superar diferenças e leva isso em consideração na tomada de decisões.

Competências multifuncionais e técnicas

Direção e Estratégia de Negócios / Pensamento Estratégico

- Desenvolver estratégias eficazes e planos prioritários alinhados com a missão e os objetivos do PNUD, baseando-se em uma análise sistêmica de desafios, oportunidades e riscos potenciais; conectar a visão geral à realidade no campo para criar soluções tangíveis e direcionadas; aprender a partir de diversas fontes para antecipar e responder de forma eficaz às tendências atuais e futuras; demonstrar capacidade de previsão.

Desenvolvimento de negócios / Design centrado no humano

- Capacidade de desenvolver soluções para problemas envolvendo a perspectiva humana em todas as etapas do processo de resolução Conhecimento e compreensão dos princípios e práticas de design centrado no ser humano.

Gestão de negócios / Gestão de projetos

- Capacidade de planejar, organizar, priorizar e controlar recursos, procedimentos e protocolos para atingir objetivos específicos.

Gestão de negócios/ Trabalhar com Evidências e dados

- Capacidade de inspecionar, limpar, transformar e modelar dados com o objetivo de descobrir informações úteis, informando conclusões e apoiando a tomada de decisão.

Dados/ Análise de Dados

- Capacidade de extrair, analisar e visualizar dados para gerar insights significativos e apoiar a tomada de decisões empresariais eficazes.

Digital / Analise de Negócios Digitais

- Capacidade de apoiar processos de negócios digitais em uma variedade de projetos, programas e atividades digitais.

Agenda 2030: Paz / Estado de Direito, Segurança e Direitos Humanos

- Acesso à Justiça

Habilidades e experiência necessárias

Requisitos mínimos de educação:

- Diploma universitário avançado (Mestrado ou equivalente) nas áreas de Tecnologia da Informação, Ciências da Computação, Engenharia de Software ou áreas afins é necessário, ou

- Diploma de Ensino Superior (Bacharelado) nas áreas mencionadas acima, combinado com 2 (dois) anos adicionais de experiência qualificada, será devidamente considerado em substituição ao Diploma Universitário avançado.

Anos mínimos de experiência profissional relevante:

- Candidatos com Diploma Universitário avançado (Mestrado ou equivalente) em área relevante não precisam de experiência profissional. Candidatos com Diploma de Ensino Superior (Bacharelado) devem possuir, no mínimo, 2 (dois) anos de experiência profissional em gestão e/ou acompanhamento de projetos de desenvolvimento, implantação ou evolução de sistemas e soluções digitais, incluindo atividades de planejamento e monitoramento de entregas, gestão de demandas ou levantamento e acompanhamento de requisitos de sistemas.

Habilidades desejadas, além das competências abordadas na seção Competências:

- Experiência no desenvolvimento e implantação de soluções tecnológicas no setor público, organismos internacionais ou em organizações de impacto social;

- Experiência anterior no desenvolvimento de soluções tecnológicas para o Poder Judiciário será considerada um diferencial;

- Experiência em metodologias ágeis, em especial Scrum, e suas técnicas, artefatos, ferramentas e cerimônias (Kanban, Lean, user stories, brainstorming, Jira, entre outras);

- Experiência em liderança e supervisão de equipes, com ênfase em gestão de projetos, gestão por resultados e acompanhamento de entregas.

Idiomas exigidos:

- Fluência em português é requerido.

- Nível básico de inglês é desejável.

jobs.title: Security Operations Centre (SOC) Assistant
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) provides leadership, operational support and oversight for the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS). Its mission is to enable United Nations system operations through trusted security leadership and solutions, in pursuit of its vision of “Security for the UN, for a better world.”

The Security Operations Centre (SOC)* is a cost-shared resource that supports the safety and security of personnel, premises, assets and operations of the UNSMS organizations covered in its operational area. The SOC monitors, facilitates and coordinates data and voice communications, serving as a first point of contact for personnel in need of urgent assistance, and maintains the administrative data that underpins security communications, including contact data for UNSMS personnel, offices, vehicles and emergency services.

As UNDSS advances towards data-driven, analysis-led and digitally enabled security management, the SOC is a central node for situational awareness on security for the UN System in the country. It collects, verifies and consolidates information so that relevant stakeholders can take timely, well-informed decisions.

The SOC Assistant works in a fast-paced and at times unpredictable environment and must pass accurate information and instructions calmly and promptly to UNSMS personnel and partners. Under the overall supervision of the UN Security Adviser and UNDSS Representative, and the direct supervision of the Field Security Associate, the SOC Assistant supports the daily operation of the SOC. The role offers unique and valuable experience to work in a multicultural team that contributes directly to the work of the United Nations.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision described in Section 4, the SOC Assistant will deliver the following:

- Support security communications and situational awareness. Receive, verify, transmit and relay security and safety messages, alerts and instructions, as directed by the Security Adviser or designated security personnel, through all UN channels (radio, satellite, telephone, SMS, e-mail, web-based and mobile applications). Maintain continuous awareness of the operating environment and promptly flag significant or emerging developments to the supervisor.

- Incident notification and response support. On receipt of a security or safety incident report, log it and escalate it through the defined channels for follow-up and support. In line with local SOPs, alert response and support functions, maintain communication links with the personnel involved, give calm and clear guidance and feedback, and notify the security focal points of the affected UNSMS organizations or UN partners. Provide direct support to incident management when specifically directed by the Security Adviser or UNDSS security personnel and record all related information and communications accurately and in sequence.

- Movement monitoring and personnel accounting support Using UN communication platforms and other tools, monitor the movement of personnel and field missions as defined by the Security Risk Management (SRM) process and local SOPs. Conduct headcounts and accounting exercises in accordance with instructions from the Designated Official, the senior security professional or established SOPs, and report results promptly and accurately.

- SCS operation and readiness. Monitor the use of UN communication resources to ensure compliance with established SOPs and guide users on appropriate practices. Verify the operational status of the SOC (including radio checks and test calls) so that personnel can reliably access it, report anomalies to the appropriate authority for action, and support communications drills and exercises.

- Information management and record keeping support Maintain accurate and up-to-date contact details for UNSMS personnel, offices and vehicles, and for the emergency services and support structures of host-government authorities and contracted private security companies, and direct personnel to the nearest of these during incidents. Keep complete logs and records of actions and critical communications and handle all information with discretion and in line with United Nations information-security requirements.

6. Data analysis, reporting and visualization support

- Compile and analyze SOC data (such as incident logs, movement and communications trends) and prepare routine and ad hoc reports, dashboards and visual products that support SRM and UNDSS requirements.

- Use Office software tools and other approved analytical and visualization tools, including approved AI-enabled tools applied responsibly. Present findings clearly in briefings to security colleagues as directed by the UN Security Adviser.

7. Support with UNDSS functions and other duties.

- Facilitate requisite UNDSS functions, coordinate with UNSMS and partner focal points as required, and perform other duties as directed by the UN Security Adviser.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Institutional Arrangement

The SOC Assistant works under the overall supervision of the UN Security Adviser but operates under the oversight of the designated Field Security Associate on daily tasks. The SOC Assistant supports the UNSMS in the daily operation of the Security Operations Center and may be required to work shifts and in specific circumstances extended hours including weekends and public holidays, as operational needs require.

Competencies

Core

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans andmonitors own work,pays attention to details, delivers quality work by

deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open mindedand curious, sharesknowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respectdifferences, awareof unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Definition

unambiguous manner both through written and

verbal communication; to tailor messages and

choose communication methods depending on the

audience. Ability to manage communications

internally and externally, through media, social

media and other appropriate channels

guidance on security management, plan and coordinate security activities

management

measures, including ability to design and test safety and security plans. including ability to design and test safety and security plans

Knowledge of crisis management and response arrangements as well as the ability to prepare for,

respond to, support/manage security crisis events

Knowledge of air, roadand fire safetyprogrammes and systems, and ability to recognize risks and support mitigation measures.

Required Skills and Experience

Min. Education requirements

- Secondaryeducation is required. Or

- University degree (bachelor’s degree) in Political Science, Military Studies, Security Management, Management or a relevant field will be given due consideration, but it is not a requirement.

Min. years of relevant work experience

Minimum of 4 years(with Secondary Education) or 1 year(with bachelor’s degree) of relevant work experience in operational communications.

Required skills

- Computer skills and information management/processing experience; good command of computer-based toolssuch as the MS Office Suite and other web and smartphone applications

- Experience and ability to drive four-wheeled vehicles is a requirement.

- Valid driving license is required. (Copy of valid licenserequired to be submitted as part application)

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

- Professional experience in security, military, police, intelligence or national security work.

- Prior working experience within the UN system, an international NGO or another international organization

- Practical experience with visualization tools(such as PowerBI, Tableau, or Excel dashboards).

- Experience in operating telecommunication systems (HF/VHF radio networks, satellite phones, radio, satellite and web-based communication and specialized tracking platforms).

- Experience usingapproved digital tools,including mobile crisis management apps or basic productivity-boosting AI tools.

Required Language(s)

- Fluency in in Englishand Bahasa Indonesia is required.

Professional Certificates

- Applicablesecurity, police and/ormilitary training is desirable

- Advanced education or training in security management would be desirable

- Security/First Aid/CPR certification would be desirable

- Completion of UN security training such as Security Certification Programme/SCP, Security Analysis Process and Practice/SAPP andother similar coursesis an asset.
