jobs.title: Energy Specialist [Ouvert aux candidats Internes et Externes]
jobs.description:
Approche par niveaux

Conformément à l’engagement visant à préserver les capacités et à soutenir le personnel déjà en poste au sein de l’Organisation, la majorité des postes vacants du PNUD/FENU/VNU sont publiés selon un processus de candidature par niveaux, comme suit :

- Niveau 0 (Tier 0) : Personnel IP du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d’un engagement permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA), dont le poste sera supprimé ou dont le contrat prendra fin ou ne sera pas renouvelé au cours de l’année 2026.

- Niveau 1 (Tier 1) : Autres membres du personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaires d’un engagement permanent (PA) ou à durée déterminée (FTA).

- Niveau 2 (Tier 2) : Personnel du PNUD/FENU/VNU titulaire d’un engagement temporaire (TA), personnel sous contrat PSA régulier, ainsi que les Volontaires des Nations Unies de catégories Expert et Spécialiste.

- Niveau 3 (Tier 3) ou aucun niveau indiqué : Tous les autres types de contrats au sein du PNUD/FENU/VNU et des autres agences, ainsi que les autres candidats externes.

Veuillez prendre connaissance du ou des niveau(x) indiqué(s), le cas échéant, dans l’intitulé de l’avis de vacance et vous assurer que vous remplissez les critères d’éligibilité requis pour soumettre votre candidature.

Contexte du Poste

Le Gouvernement du Mali a fait de l'accès universel à une énergie moderne, abordable, fiable et durable un levier prioritaire de son développement économique, social et environnemental. Cette ambition est portée notamment par la Stratégie Nationale pour l’Emergence et du Développement Durable (SNEDD 2024-2033) et son Projet Structurant YEELEN KURA, la Contribution Déterminée au niveau National (CDN), ainsi que les engagements du pays en faveur de l'Agenda 2030 et de l'Accord de Paris sur les changements climatiques.

Malgré des progrès significatifs enregistrés ces dernières années, le secteur énergétique demeure confronté à d'importants défis structurels. Le taux d'accès à l'électricité reste particulièrement faible dans les zones rurales, où vivent la majorité des populations. Les systèmes énergétiques existants demeurent fortement dépendants des combustibles fossiles importés et de la biomasse traditionnelle, avec des conséquences importantes sur la sécurité énergétique, la compétitivité économique, la dégradation des ressources naturelles, les émissions de gaz à effet de serre ainsi que la santé des populations.

Cette situation affecte directement le développement des systèmes alimentaires, limite les opportunités économiques en milieu rural et réduit la résilience des communautés face aux effets du changement climatique. L'insuffisance des infrastructures énergétiques freine notamment le développement des usages productifs de l'énergie, notamment l'irrigation agricole, les chaînes de froid, la transformation agroalimentaire, les petites industries rurales ainsi que l'accès aux services sociaux de bases.

Parallèlement, le pays dispose d’opportunités importantes pour accélérer sa transition énergétique grâce au développement des énergies renouvelables décentralisées et à l’émergence de ressources énergétiques innovantes telles que l’hydrogène géologique, dont le potentiel identifié à Bourakébougou pourrait contribuer à diversifier durablement le mix énergétique national. Toutefois, l’exploitation de ces opportunités demeure limitée par l’insuffisance des investissements, le manque de projets techniquement et financièrement viables, la faible participation du secteur privé ainsi que des contraintes institutionnelles et de gouvernance qui freinent le développement du secteur.

Afin de répondre à ces défis, le Gouvernement du Mali, avec l’appui du PNUD, de l’UNCDF et de l’UNOPS, met en œuvre le Programme d’accélération de la transition énergétique et des systèmes alimentaires au Mali. Aligné sur les priorités nationales, notamment la SNEDD 2024-2033 et le Projet Structurant YEELEN KURA, ce programme vise à créer les conditions institutionnelles, techniques et financières nécessaires pour accélérer l’accès inclusif à l’énergie durable et soutenir la transformation des systèmes alimentaires.

Le programme prévoit notamment la réalisation d’évaluations énergétiques et d’études de faisabilité dans 100 localités rurales, l’identification d’un portefeuille de projets énergétiques bancables intégrant des usages productifs de l’énergie (irrigation, stockage frigorifique, transformation agroalimentaire), le développement d’une stratégie nationale d’investissement pour l’accès à l’énergie ainsi que la conception d’un mécanisme innovant de financement mixte destiné à mobiliser les ressources publiques, privées et celles de la diaspora malienne.

Le programme soutiendra également le développement des connaissances et des bases techniques nécessaires à l’intégration de l’hydrogène géologique dans la transition énergétique du pays à travers des études de cartographie, des analyses technico-économiques et la préparation d’un projet pilote de démonstration. Il contribuera en outre au renforcement des capacités des institutions nationales et locales, à la promotion d’une gouvernance inclusive sensible au genre et à la mobilisation des parties prenantes autour d’une vision commune du développement énergétique durable.

Dans ce contexte, le Bureau Pays du PNUD recrute un(e) Spécialiste Énergie chargé(e) d'assurer la coordination technique de l'ensemble des composantes du programme, d'appuyer le développement des investissements énergétiques, de superviser les études techniques, de renforcer les partenariats avec les institutions nationales et internationales et de contribuer à l'atteinte des résultats stratégiques du Programme conjoint.

Attributions et responsabilités

a. Assurer la coordination technique du Programme

Le/La Spécialiste Énergie assure la coordination de l'ensemble des activités liées au développement du Programme conjoint afin de garantir la qualité des interventions et l'atteinte des résultats attendus.

À ce titre, il/elle devra notamment :

- Élaborer, actualiser et suivre la planification annuelle des activités en cohérence avec le plan de travail global du Programme conjoint.

- Fournir des avis stratégiques au Bureau Pays du PNUD, aux partenaires nationaux et aux agences partenaires concernant les orientations techniques du programme.

- Coordonner la préparation des termes de référence des études techniques, des missions d'assistance technique et des prestations spécialisées relatives au secteur de l'énergie.

- Superviser les consultants nationaux et internationaux mobilisés dans le cadre des différentes études techniques.

- Assurer le contrôle qualité des rapports techniques, études de faisabilité, diagnostics énergétiques, analyses économiques, études d'investissement et autres livrables produits dans le cadre du programme.

- Garantir la conformité des études avec les normes internationales, les politiques nationales, les standards techniques du PNUD et les exigences des partenaires financiers.

- Veiller à la bonne articulation entre les différentes composantes du programme afin d'assurer une approche intégrée reliant énergie, systèmes alimentaires, développement économique local, adaptation au changement climatique et création d'emplois.

- Identifier les risques techniques susceptibles d'affecter la mise en œuvre du programme et proposer les mesures correctives appropriées.

- Assurer une veille permanente sur les innovations technologiques, les évolutions réglementaires et les meilleures pratiques internationales en matière d'accès à l'énergie, de mini-réseaux, d'usages productifs de l'énergie, d'hydrogène naturel et de financement de la transition énergétique.

b.Tâches et responsabilités techniques

Le/La Spécialiste Énergie est notamment chargé(e) de :

- Planifier, coordonner et assurer la mise en œuvre des activités du programme, conformément aux objectifs, au calendrier, au budget et aux procédures de gestion du Programme.

- Superviser la réalisation des études techniques, des analyses de faisabilité, des diagnostics énergétiques et des autres études spécialisées, en veillant au respect des normes internationales de qualité et à leur utilisation pour éclairer les décisions d'investissement.

- Coordonner le développement, l'évaluation et la structuration d'un portefeuille de projets énergétiques bancables, en assurant leur viabilité technique, économique, environnementale et financière afin de faciliter leur mobilisation auprès des investisseurs et partenaires financiers.

- Assurer le suivi technique des activités relatives à l'hydrogène géologique, notamment les études scientifiques, les analyses technico-économiques, les travaux préparatoires aux projets pilotes ainsi que les contributions au développement des cadres techniques, réglementaires et institutionnels de la filière.

- Fournir un appui technique au développement et à l'opérationnalisation du mécanisme de financement Mali Food Systems and Energy Transition Investment Facility (MFSET-IF), en contribuant à la structuration des mécanismes de financement innovants et à la mobilisation des investissements.

- Développer et entretenir des partenariats techniques et institutionnels avec les ministères, agences gouvernementales, agences des Nations Unies, partenaires techniques et financiers, institutions financières, secteur privé, centres de recherche et investisseurs afin de renforcer la coordination et la mobilisation des ressources.

- Préparer et produire, dans les délais requis, les rapports techniques, notes d'analyse, documents de capitalisation, produits de connaissance et autres contributions stratégiques nécessaires à la mise en œuvre, au suivi et à la visibilité du Programme.

- Veiller à l'intégration systématique des principes de développement durable, de résilience climatique, d'égalité de genre, d'inclusion sociale, de sauvegardes environnementales et sociales ainsi que de gestion axée sur les résultats dans la conception, la mise en œuvre, le suivi et l'évaluation de toutes les interventions du Programme.

c.Assurer le suivi-évaluation, la gestion des connaissances, le reporting et la capitalisation des acquis du Programme

Le/La Spécialiste Énergie veille à la production de connaissances, au suivi des résultats et à la diffusion des bonnes pratiques afin d'améliorer la performance du Programme conjoint et de renforcer les capacités nationales dans le domaine de la transition énergétique.

À ce titre, il/elle devra notamment :

- Collaborer étroitement avec l’ensemble des partenaires de mise en œuvre (le gouvernement, le Centre International d’Istanbul du PNUD pour le développement du Secteur Privé (ICPSD), et l’UNCDF afin d’assurer une mise en œuvre cohérente et intégrée des activités.

- Assurer le suivi de la mise en œuvre des activités du programme conformément au cadre de résultats, au plan de travail annuel et aux procédures de gestion axée sur les résultats du PNUD.

- Contribuer à l'élaboration et au suivi des indicateurs de performance relatifs aux investissements énergétiques, à l'accès à l'énergie, aux usages productifs, au développement institutionnel ainsi qu'aux innovations technologiques.

- Superviser la collecte, l'analyse et la validation des données techniques nécessaires au suivi des indicateurs du programme.

- Préparer les contributions techniques aux rapports trimestriels, semestriels et annuels du Programme, conformément aux exigences du PNUD et des partenaires financiers.

- Fournir les contributions nécessaires à la préparation des rapports destinés au Gouvernement, au Comité de Pilotage, aux partenaires techniques et financiers ainsi qu'aux organes de gouvernance du programme.

- Capitaliser les expériences, innovations, leçons apprises et bonnes pratiques issues de la mise en œuvre des différentes composantes du programme.

- Appuyer les activités de communication, de visibilité institutionnelle et de diffusion des résultats en collaboration avec les équipes de communication du PNUD et des agences partenaires.

- Veiller à ce que les connaissances produites soient mises à la disposition des institutions nationales afin de renforcer les politiques publiques, la planification énergétique et les futurs programmes d'investissement.

- Promouvoir l'intégration systématique des considérations relatives au genre, aux droits humains, à l'inclusion sociale, à la jeunesse, à la résilience climatique et aux sauvegardes environnementales dans les activités de suivi, d'évaluation et de capitalisation.

Dispositions institutionnelles

Sous la supervision générale du Chef de l'Unité Environnement et Changement Climatique du Bureau Pays du PNUD, le/la Spécialiste Énergie assure la coordination technique et opérationnelle du Programme Mali FS Energy Transition.

Il/elle est responsable de la planification technique, de la supervision des études énergétiques, du contrôle qualité des livrables, du développement du portefeuille de projets d'investissement, de la coordination des partenaires techniques, du suivi des activités relatives à l'hydrogène géologique ainsi que de l'appui au développement du mécanisme de financement mixte (MFSET-IF).

Il/elle assure un rôle de liaison entre les différentes parties prenantes (le Bureau Pays du PNUD, l’ICPSD, l’UNCDF et le MEE), afin de faciliter la coordination du projet, la circulation de l’information, d’appuyer l’alignement technique et opérationnel des activités, et de contribuer au renforcement de la collaboration institutionnelle dans le cadre du programme.

Le/La Spécialiste veille à ce que l'ensemble des interventions du programme soient mises en œuvre conformément aux standards techniques internationaux, aux politiques nationales, aux procédures du PNUD ainsi qu'aux principes de développement durable, de résilience climatique, d'égalité de genre, d'inclusion sociale, de sauvegardes environnementales et de gestion axée sur les résultats.

Il/elle contribue également au positionnement stratégique du PNUD comme partenaire de référence du Gouvernement du Mali dans le domaine de la transition énergétique durable, de l'accès universel à l'énergie et de la mobilisation des investissements verts.

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation

Le titulaire du poste accomplit d'autres tâches relevant de son profil fonctionnel, jugées nécessaires au bon fonctionnement du Bureau et de l'Organisation.

Compétences

Compétences fondamentales

Obtenir des résultats : NIVEAU 3 : Fixer et harmoniser des objectifs ambitieux mais réalisables pour plusieurs projets, et avoir un impact durable

Faire preuve d'innovation :NIVEAU 3 : Anticiper et atténuer les risques, développer de nouvelles idées pour résoudre des problèmes complexes

Apprendre en permanence : NIVEAU 3 : Créer et saisir des opportunités pour élargir ses horizons et diversifier ses expériences

S'adapter avec agilité : NIVEAU 3 : Initier et promouvoir le changement de manière proactive, gérer plusieurs demandes concurrentes

Agir avec détermination : NIVEAU 3 : Voir au-delà des tâches et des obstacles immédiats et prendre des mesures pour obtenir de meilleurs résultats

S'impliquer et établir des partenariats : NIVEAU 3 : Faire preuve de sens politique, évoluer dans un environnement complexe, promouvoir la collaboration interinstitutionnelle

Favoriser la diversité et l'inclusion : NIVEAU 3 : Reconnaître les avantages d’un personnel diversifié et promouvoir l’inclusion

Compétences transversales et techniques

-Programme 2030 : Partenariats / Carrefour de l'énergie durable: Énergies renouvelables Capacité à concevoir, promouvoir et superviser des initiatives liées au développement des énergies renouvelables dans le cadre de la transition énergétique.

-Programme 2030 : Partenariats / Carrefour de l'énergie durable: Financement de l'énergie Capacité à mobiliser et structurer les ressources financières et les mécanismes d'investissement destinés au développement durable du secteur énergétique.

-Gestion de l’organisation/Gestion de projet: Être en mesure de planifier, d’organiser, de hiérarchiser et de contrôler les ressources, les procédures et les protocoles afin d’atteindre des objectifs précis.

-Gestion des partenariats/Gestion des relations: Être en mesure de collaborer avec un large éventail de partenaires publics et privés, et de mettre en place, maintenir ou renforcer les relations de travail, la confiance et la compréhension mutuelle.

-Orientation et stratégie des affaires/Pensée systémique: Capacité à utiliser l'analyse objective des problèmes et le jugement pour comprendre comment des éléments interconnectés coexistent au sein d'un processus ou système global, et à considérer comment la modification d'un élément peut impacter d'autres parties du système

-Gestion de l’organisation/Suivi et évaluation: Être en mesure de contrôler systématiquement les résultats des stratégies, des programmes et des activités afin de s’assurer qu’ils sont mis en œuvre de manière efficace ; savoir fournir aux responsables et aux principales parties prenantes un retour et des rapports réguliers attestant de la cohérence ou des écarts entre les activités planifiées et la gestion et les résultats des programmes. Être en mesure de porter un jugement indépendant sur la gestion et les résultats des stratégies, des programmes et des activités sur la base des critères et des paramètres définis, en gardant à l’esprit les besoins et les préoccupations des clients, actuels et futurs. Connaître et comprendre les cadres, les concepts, les méthodologies, les systèmes, les processus et les outils de suivi et d’évaluation. Savoir porter un jugement indépendant sur la base des critères et des paramètres définis. Savoir anticiper les besoins et les préoccupations futurs des clients.

-Gender/Genre et énergie: Capacité à intégrer les considérations d'égalité des genres dans la conception, la mise en œuvre, le suivi et l'évaluation des politiques, programmes et investissements du secteur énergétique afin de garantir un accès équitable aux services énergétiques, aux opportunités économiques et aux bénéfices de la transition énergétique.

Qualifications minimales

Exigences minimales académiques

- Un diplôme universitaire supérieur (Master ou équivalent) en Génie Energétique, Génie Electrique, Ingénierie Electromécanique, Ingénierie en Energies Renouvelables, Politiques Energétiques, Economie de l'Energie, Ingénierie de l'Environnement et du Changement Climatique ou dans un domaine étroitement lié est requise, ou

- Un diplôme de fin de premier cycle (Licence) dans les domaines susmetionnes en combinaison avec deux (2) années supplémentaires d’expérience pertinente sera dûment pris en considération en lieu et place du diplôme universitaire avancé

Nombre d’années minimum d’expérience de travail pertinente

- Au minimum 5 ans (avec un master) ou 7 ans (avec une licence) d’expérience pertinente au niveau national ou international dans le domaine de la conception, la gestion ou la mise en œuvre de programmes ou projets dans le secteur de l'énergie, des infrastructures énergétiques, des énergies renouvelables ou du développement durable.

Expérience, connaissances et compétences

- Gestion de projets dans le secteur de l'énergie, des énergies renouvelables ou des infrastructures énergétiques ;

- Réalisation ou supervision d'études techniques, de faisabilité et d'analyses technico-économiques de projets énergétiques ;

- Bonne connaissance des politiques énergétiques, de l'électrification rurale, des mini-réseaux, des usages productifs de l'énergie et des enjeux de la transition énergétique ;

- Expérience de coordination avec les administrations publiques, les partenaires techniques et financiers, le secteur privé et les institutions financières ;

- Expérience démontrée dans l'intégration des considérations de genre et d'inclusion sociale dans les programmes, politiques ou projets de développement énergétique, rural, climatique ou de développement durable.

- Capacité prouvée à travailler sous pression et avec des équipes pluridisciplinaires

- Maîtrise des outils informatiques, notamment l’environnement Microsoft Office 365

Critères souhaitables

- Connaissance prouvée de l’environnement software des Nations Unies, notamment Quantum, UNALL, PIMS, serait un avantage.

- Expérience dans le développement ou l'exploitation de mini-réseaux, de solutions d'accès à l'énergie ou d'infrastructures énergétiques décentralisées est souhaitable

Langue(s) requise(s)

- La maitrise du français et de la langue nationale (bambara) est obligatoire

- La connaissance pratique de l’anglais est souhaitée.

Certificats professionnel

Non exigé

Égalité des chances

En tant qu’employeur garantissant l’égalité des chances, le PNUD valorise la diversité, qui reflète la multiplicité des nations et des cultures dans lesquelles il intervient. À ce titre, nous encourageons les candidats qualifiés, quels que soient leurs horizons, à postuler aux opportunités au sein de l’Organisation. jobs.title: Climate Policy Analyst [Open to Internal & External Applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, an organization advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. UNDP is on the ground in about 170 countries and territories, working with national counterparts on solutions to global and national development challenges.

In the programme countries, UNDP supports stabilization, state-building, governance and development priorities in partnership with the host governments, the United Nations system, the development partners and other partners to help the countries to achieve sustainable development by eradicating poverty in all its forms and dimensions, accelerating structural transformations for sustainable development and building resilience to crises and shock.

UNDP has been a trusted development partner of Thailand for more than 50 years, helping to reduce inequalities and exclusion in areas such governance, environment protection, climate change mitigation and adaptation. In each of its thematic areas of work, UNDP at the request of its national partners provides relevant policy advisory support, technical assistance, advocacy, and knowledge to help Thailand achieve its global commitment on Sustainable Development Goals (SDG).

UNDP is currently looking for a Climate Policy Analyst with a background in climate change policy, sustainable energy, climate adaptation and/or mitigation. The incumbent will provide research, policy analysis, project coordination, monitoring and implementation support for selected initiatives under the Climate Action Portfolio. The position requires strong analytical, communication, coordination and organizational skills, as well as the ability to work across interconnected climate and development issues.

In this context, under the direct supervision and strategic guidance of the Climate and Small Grants Programme Portfolio Manager, the Climate Policy Analyst will work cooperatively within an integrated programme comprising analysts and professionals from programme, operations, policy and project teams. The incumbent will provide technical and coordination support and collaborate with relevant project managers and team members in implementing, monitoring and reporting on assigned climate-related initiatives.

Background and scope of the climate action portfolio

Among several ongoing and pipeline climate-related activities, UNDP is working on topics related to: support to the implementation and reporting of climate policies (e.g. Nationally Determined Contribution, Long Term Low Emission Development Strategy, Biennial Transparency Report), climate finance, climate change adaptation and climate resilience for agriculture and water management, just energy transition/emission reduction, climate education, and others. The elements of human rights, gender, youth, minority groups, and most vulnerable communities are incorporated as core cross-cutting issues in all the initiatives.

In this context, UNDP in Thailand is looking for a Climate Policy Analyst who will perform under the direct supervision and strategic guidance of the Climate and Small Grants Programme Portfolio Manager. They would work cooperatively within an integrated programme, comprising analysts and professionals (operations, policy advisors, project and programme team).

Duties and Responsibilities

The Climate Policy Analyst will be based in Bangkok as part of the UNDP Thailand country office and will report to the Climate and Small Grants Programme Portfolio Manager. The Climate Policy Analyst will work in coordination with the other project managers in UNDP Thailand.

The Climate Policy Analyst will provide technical, analytical, coordination, monitoring and implementation support for assigned projects and initiatives under UNDP Thailand’s Climate Action Portfolio. The incumbent will undertake policy research and analysis, coordinate with implementing partners and stakeholders, monitor project progress and risks, contribute to reporting and knowledge products, and support the development of climate-related initiatives. The Climate Policy Analyst will perform these responsibilities in close collaboration with relevant programme, project and operations colleagues, in accordance with UNDP policies and procedures.

1. Support implementation and coordination of assigned climate-action projects

- Provide day-to-day coordination and implementation support for assigned activities under selected projects within the Climate Action Portfolio. The selection of the suite of projects will be guided by the Country Programme Document and existing pipeline of projects in a given year;

- Coordinate with implementing partners, responsible parties, consultants and relevant UNDP teams to support the timely delivery of agreed outputs;

- Support compliance with applicable UNDP and government procedures, including procurement, human resources, financial management and project implementation requirements, including in the UNDP’s internal EPR system (Quantum);

- Monitor the implementation of assigned activities against approved workplans, timelines and budgets, and bring potential delays or implementation issues to the attention of the supervisor;

- Prepare and follow up on requests for financial resources, including advances, direct payments, reimbursements and FACE forms, under the guidance of the supervisor and in coordination with the relevant operations team;

- Maintain project files, implementation records and supporting documentation in accordance with UNDP requirements;

- Support results-based implementation and coordination of project activities; and

2. Support project monitoring, reporting and risk tracking

- Monitor the implementation of assigned project activities and compile information on progress against agreed results, indicators, workplans and budgets;

- Support the review of programme results and the collection and verification of data and evidence used to demonstrate progress;

- Monitor project risks and issues, maintain the Project Risk Log and Issues Log, and bring emerging risks or proposed mitigation measures to the attention of the supervisor for review and possible escalation;

- Support the documentation and follow-up of project changes, issues and management decisions;

- Draft project progress reports covering implementation progress, results, risks, issues and expenditure for review and clearance by the supervisor;

- Support the timely preparation of quarterly financial and activity reports and follow up with relevant partners to obtain required information and supporting documentation;

- Contribute to the preparation of reports to donors, government counterparts and other stakeholders, ensuring the completeness and accuracy of assigned inputs; and

- Prepare briefing notes, presentations, talking points and background materials for meetings with government, development partners and other stakeholders.

3. Support stakeholder coordination and development of climate-related initiatives

- Support coordination with government agencies, development partners, civil society, the private sector, academia and local stakeholders for the implementation of assigned portfolio activities;

- Maintain regular working-level communication with partners and stakeholders and support the organization of consultations, technical meetings, workshops and other project activities;

- Contribute research, background analysis and technical inputs to concept notes, project proposals and resource-mobilization materials under the guidance of the Climate Action Portfolio Manager;

- Support the technical development of project proposals on just energy transition, climate mitigation, adaptation and related topics, including the proposed submission to the Mitigation Action Facility;

- Coordinate with other UNDP Thailand teams to identify operational and programmatic linkages and promote coherence across related projects and thematic areas;

- Support collaboration with other UN agencies on relevant joint activities, including initiatives addressing the needs of women, children, youth, persons with disabilities and other vulnerable groups; and

- Monitor and compile information on relevant policy developments, stakeholders and partnership opportunities and provide regular updates to the supervisor and project teams.

4. Support policy research, knowledge management and communication

- Conduct research and policy analysis on climate mitigation, adaptation, just energy transition, climate finance and other assigned topics;

- Prepare technical inputs, policy briefs, background notes, analytical papers and other knowledge products for review by the supervisor and contribute the CO’s overall pipeline development effort;

- Support the provision of technical inputs to UNDP Thailand, implementing partners and other stakeholders within the incumbent’s areas of expertise;

- Identify, document and synthesize good practices, lessons learned and evidence generated through project implementation;

- Contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice and support the dissemination of relevant knowledge products;

- Support the design and delivery of learning and capacity-development activities for government counterparts, implementing partners and other stakeholders; and

- Contribute to the implementation and periodic updating of the Climate Action Portfolio’s communication and knowledge-management activities.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Direction and Strategy

- Effective Decision Making: Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner inline with one's authority, area of expertise and resources and take into consideration potential wider implications.

Business Development

- Knowledge Facilitation: Ability to animate individuals and groups, internally and externally, and to design and facilitate activities, to share and exchange knowledge, information and ideas. Knowledge of tools and approaches to stimulate active participation, contribution, and exchange.

Business Management

- Project Management: Ability to plan, organize, prioritize and control resources, procedures and protocols to achieve specific goals.

- Monitoring & Evaluation: Ability to systematically monitor results of strategies, programmes, and activities with a view to make sure that they are being implemented effectively; Ability to provide managers and key stakeholders with regular feedback and reporting on the consistency or discrepancy between planned activities and programme management and results. Ability to make independent judgment of the management and results of strategies, programmes and activities based on set criteria and benchmark, keeping in mind the needs and concerns of client, current and upcoming. Knowledge and understanding of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, concepts, methodologies, systems, processes, and tools. Ability to make an independent judgement based on set criteria and benchmarks. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Partnership Management

- Strategic Engagement: Ability to capture and sustain attention, interest and agreement of high-level, influential policy and decision makers and secure their buy-in of high-level vision and objectives.

- Emerging Partnerships: Ability to engage with emerging partners, develop and manage a strategy and develop approaches to developing and managing these new strategic partnerships.

- Resource Mobilization: Ability to identify funding sources, match funding needs (programmes/projects/initiatives) with funding opportunities, and establish a plan to meet funding requirements.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Climate Change, Environmental Sciences/Engineering, Energy Engineering, Disaster Management, Environmental Economics/Management, International Relations, Political Science and/or relevant field is required, OR:

- A first level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with additional two years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of the advanced university degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.;

- Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in programme and project implementation, related to the area described above;

- Experience in project management including coordination, policy analysis and partnership management;

- Experience in working effectively with diverse groups of professionals towards common goals;

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and advance knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages.

Desired Additional Skills:

- Experience making new and useful ideas work, including the adaptation with complex concepts and challenges convention purposefully;

- Experience in policy analysis and development on just energy transition or climate resilience (or related fields);

- Research experience on just energy transition or climate resilience (or related fields);

- Experience and knowledge of the country’s institutional framework and policies of climate change;

- Experience with working with/in the UN Agencies is an asset

- Previous experience working with government, donors or the UN.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English and Thai is required.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

Background

UNDP Albania is realigning its structure to improve programmatic and operational efficiency, while retaining the required capacities for programme delivery and development, proper oversight, communications, and partnerships, as well as the needed operational capacity to deliver programmes at acceptable risk levels.

You are invited to join a team of dedicated development professionals whose primary role is to support Albania to achieve the 2030 Agenda. As part of the UNDP team, your focus will be to work with multiple stakeholders to find country-specific solutions that lead to the eradication of poverty and ensure no one is left behind—reaching those furthest behind first.

We place a premium on national ownership in the analysis, design, and implementation of solutions, as well as a partnership-based approach to leverage the range of skills and resources needed—both public and private. We work closely with all stakeholders in society to find innovative solutions to old development problems. We are looking for people who are enthusiastic, motivated, and committed to making a positive contribution to Development in Albania.

Duties and Responsibilities

Provision of Reliable and Secure Driving Services

- Drive office vehicles for the transport of the UNDP Resident Representative, other high-ranking officials, visitors, UNDP programme and operations staff, and facilitate VIP missions.

- Deliver and collect mail, documents, and other items to and from Government Offices, Embassies, Commercial Establishments, and UN Offices.

- Meet official personnel and visitors at the airport, assisting with visa and customs formalities and arrangements when required.

- Ensure that all immediate actions required by rules and regulations are taken in the event of an accident.

- Ensure that all assigned vehicles comply with the UN Security Standards.

Proper Vehicle Maintenance and Cost-Savings

- Ensure cost-saving through responsible driving and accurate maintenance planning.

- Maintain up-to-date and accurate daily vehicle logs, recording daily mileage, gas consumption, oil changes, servicing, greasing, and repairs.

- Assist in the registration and licensing of diplomatic and official vehicles as they come due.

- Conduct periodic check-ups of vehicles, emergency engine troubleshooting, and tune-ups.

- Keep all required documents and supplies inside the vehicle, including vehicle insurance, vehicle logs, office directory, map of the city/country, first-aid kit, and necessary spare parts.

- Ensure accurate and timely daily trip tickets are completed to support monthly billing/charges for driving services to various projects and units.

General Administrative and Logistical Support

jobs.title: Project Associate
jobs.description:
Background

The Philippines' recent transition to upper-middle-income status has increased the importance of aligning economic growth with sustainability, digital transformation, and human rights accountability. As sectors such as mining, renewable energy, agribusiness, tourism, infrastructure, and digital platforms expand, governance challenges related to community grievances, land and resource disputes, labor rights, environmental impacts, and stakeholder participation persist, often disproportionately affecting women and marginalized groups.

To address these challenges, the Philippines initiated work on a National Action Plan on Business and Human Rights (NAP-BHR), led by the Presidential Human Rights Committee Secretariat (PHRCS). While several ASEAN countries have already institutionalized their NAPs, the Philippines remains in the development stage. Recent efforts have accelerated under the 4th Philippine Human Rights Plan 2024-2028, including the establishment of a multi-agency technical working group to develop a NAP-BHR focused on responsible business conduct, Indigenous Peoples' rights, and ancestral domains.

The FAIR BHR Project seeks to strengthen Business and Human Rights (BHR) governance by promoting more integrated, participatory, and evidence-based approaches that connect sustainability, human rights, accountability, conflict sensitivity, and stakeholder engagement. The project will support the Philippine government in building evidence, raising awareness, strengthening coordination, and fostering inclusive dialogue to inform BHR reforms.

The initiative will also promote stronger collaboration among UN agencies, leveraging complementary expertise and positioning UNDP as a strategic convener. As an initial pilot, the project will generate evidence and lessons to inform longer-term programming and the development of a comprehensive Project Document supporting the institutionalization of BHR in the Philippines.

UNDP Philippines is seeking a Project Associate to support the Institutions and Partnerships (I&P) Programme Team. As part of the Project Management Unit (PMU), the incumbent will primarily support the implementation of the FAIR BHR Project and contribute to the effective coordination, implementation, and monitoring of the team's programme and project portfolio to ensure the timely delivery of activities and achievement of results.

Scope of work

Provides support to overall effective and efficient management and monitoring of project:

- Contribute to the development of project’s annual and quarterly work plans, procurement plan, human resources recruitment plan, travel plan and financial and physical progress reports;

- Keep track of the delivery of the project and contracted parties, and frequently report to the Project Coordinator on the delivery situation;

- Maintenance of the internal expenditures control system including budget checks and timely corrective actions on unposted vouchers, including the vouchers with budget check errors, match exceptions, unapproved vouchers;

- Work closely with the Programme Team, Results and Quality Team, Procurement Team and Finance Team to ensure efficient and transparent use of project resources in line with approved budgets and within UNDP rules and regulations;

- Support to the conduct of project reviews, audits, monitoring missions, evaluations;

- Support timely operational and financial closure of a project, determination of unutilized funds and processing operational/financial closure of projects;

- Support in drafting terms of reference and support the recruitment and management of national and international consultants, subject matter experts, consulting firms, and other such resources.

Ensures implementation of operational strategies, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Full compliance of operational activities with UNDP rules, regulations, policies, and strategies.

- Provision of inputs to the CO administrative business processes and implementation of the internal standard operating procedures (SOPs)

- Undertake administrative, finance and procurement procedures, such as travel processing, liquidations of cash advances, processing of payments to suppliers, canvassing/collection of price quotations and payment of utilities;

- Support to small-value procurement and coordinating with the suppliers for the delivery of goods;

- Raise requisitions as required and register as general user role in Quantum.

- Provision of inputs to the project team results-oriented workplan

Support to ensure the efficient administrative support, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support to the coordination of travel arrangements such as preparation of travel requests, coordination with travel unit for travel authorizations, booking and reservation of hotel rooms, ticket bookings, and visa.

- Support to the organization of workshops and meetings including transportation services, booking of conference room, compiling of documents, arranging of equipment, among other similar administrative activities.

- Support to maintain an accurate and reliable filing system;

Provides support to proper supply and assets management, focusing on achievement of the following result:

- Support to the coordination of assets management in the unit, timely preparation and submission of periodic inventory reports.

- Support to the coordination of the provision of reliable and quality office supplies.

Supports knowledge building and knowledge sharing in the CO, focusing on achievement of the following results:

- Support to organization of trainings and events

- Provision of inputs to lessons learnt and best practices in programme including meeting documentation, drafting of communication letters, and logging of minutes from project and partner meetings.

- Sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

- Support in preparation of Corporate Requirements including but not limited to annual work plan, quarterly report, and annual report.

- In collaboration with the I&P Team, support the implementation of the common activities of the programme team and the Country Office in general.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance of the Team Leader, Institutions and Partnerships (I&P) Programme Team, and the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator, with technical oversight from the I&P Programme Analyst for Governance and Rule of Law, the Project Associate will support the effective implementation and coordination of programme and project initiatives, primarily for the FAIR BHR Project.

CORE COMPETENCIES

Achieve Results

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, deliver quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

Adapt with Agility

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Act with Determination:

LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident

Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships

Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

CROSS-FUNCTIONAL & TECHNICAL COMPETENCIES

Business Management: Operations Management

Ability to effectively plan, organize and oversee the operation's business processes in order to convert its assets into the best results in the most efficient manner, Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms

Procurement: Procurement Management

The ability to acquire goods, services or works from an outside external source

Procurement: Contract Management

Knowledge of contract management concepts, principles and methods, and ability to apply this to strategic and/ or practical situations

Finance: Accounting (General)

Knowledge of accounting concepts, principles, frameworks, standards, regulations, policies and trends, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situations

Finance: Budget management

Ability to support budgetary aspects of work planning process, drawing and management of team budgets

Finance: Financial planning and budgeting

Ability to create and manage processes to achieve UNDP's long and short-term financial goals, including through planning, budgeting, forecasting, analysing and reporting.

Finance: Financial reporting and analysis

Understands changes in regulatory, legal and ethical frameworks and standards for financial reporting in the public sector. Ability to extract, evaluate financial data, derive relevant findings and present them in a meaningful and coherent manner to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring. Understands the benefits of integrated reporting, including non-financial resources such as human, social and intellectual capital, and environmental and governance performance

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum Academic Education

- Completion of secondary education is required.

- First level university degree (bachelor's degree) in Business Administration, Management, Entrepreneurship, Accounting, Economics, Finance or other related fields will be given due consideration but is not a requirement.

Minimum years of relevant Work experience

- Minimum of six (6) years (with secondary education) or three (3) years (with bachelor’s degree) of relevant experience in administrative, financial, procurement, and/or logistics support at the national or international level is required

Required skills and competencies

- Demonstrated proficiency in ICT applications and Microsoft Office Suite, particularly Excel, Word, and PowerPoint, for data management, reporting, and administrative support is required.

- At least three (3) years of progressively responsible experience in project and/or financial management is required, including planning and monitoring budgets, developing annual workplans, tracking project implementation, and preparing progress, performance, and financial reports.

Desired additional skills and competencies

- A minimum of three (3) years of experience providing administrative, financial, and/or procurement support to donor-funded, development, humanitarian, or government projects is desirable.

- A minimum of three (3) years of experience using enterprise resource planning (ERP), enterprise risk management (ERM), or other integrated corporate management systems is desirable.

- A minimum of three (3) years of experience working with United Nations agencies, international organizations, NGOs/INGOs, development partners, or government institutions is considered an asset.

Required Language(s) (at working level)

- Fluency in spoken and written English and Filipino is required

Professional Certificates

- Professional certification in procurement, finance, administration, or other relevant disciplines (e.g., CIPS, CPM, ACCA, CPA, or equivalent) is desirable

Travel:

Travels may be required for this position. The incumbent may be required to undertake travel within the Philippines to support project implementation, stakeholder consultations, coordination meetings, capacity-building activities, monitoring missions, and other project-related activities.

The following documents shall be required from the applicants:

- Personal CV or P11 , indicating all past positions held and their main underlying functions, their durations (month/year), the qualifications, as well as the contact details (email and telephone number) of the Candidate, and at least three (3) the most recent professional references of previous supervisors. References may also include peers.

- A cover letter (maximum length: 1 page) indicating why the candidate considers him-/herself to be suitable for the position.

- Transcript of Records and Diploma

- Copies of relevant training certificates (if applicable)

Background

The UNDP Global Centre for Technology, Innovation and Sustainable Development (GC-TISD) is part of UNDP’s Digital, AI and Innovation (DAI) Hub, which leverages digital, data, and systems innovation to help governments and partners address complex development challenges through more agile, adaptive, and inclusive approaches.

Based in Singapore, the Global Centre draws on the country’s strengths in technology, policy, and innovation, engaging a broad ecosystem of government agencies, private sector actors, academia, and thought leaders. Through this collaboration, the Centre connects policymakers, practitioners, and experts globally to exchange insights and co-create practical solutions that advance sustainable development.

UNDP is the development arm of the United Nations. Present in 170 countries with over 17,000 people, UNDP works on the world’s biggest challenges, from rising poverty and inequality to a rapidly changing climate, the emergence of crises and the continued degradation and destruction of our natural world. Our UNDP Digital Strategy 2022 – 2025 aims to support our partner countries to unlock the power of digital to tackle these pressing issues. The strategy lays out UNDP’s ambition to use a rights-based approach to digital technologies to improve our development results and help build inclusive digital ecosystems globally that leave no one behind. These aims are supported by the transformation of our internal, operational systems and building an agile, digitally capable workforce

Duties and Responsibilities

UNDP is looking for a Senior Programme Advisor to provide programme coordination, technical analysis, and stakeholder engagement support for the UNDP Global Centre for Technology, Innovation and Sustainable Development (the UNDP Global Centre). The Centre has a particular thematic focus on digital foundations and cyber resilience, trustworthy and inclusive AI, digital and systems thinking, and innovation for climate, sustainability and sustainable finance. The Senior Programme Advisor will report and provide direct support to the Chief Digital Officer and the Head of Global Partnerships and Engagement to scale impact and enable opportunities for collective action, especially through multi-disciplinary and multi-stakeholder coalitions across UNDP’s global network. This is a coordination and technical support role, with a unique opportunity to contribute to how UNDP leverages Singapore’s digital ecosystem to advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

Under the supervision of the Chief Digital Officer/Director of the DAI Hub, provide operational and analytical support for the annual workplan of the UNDP Global Centre, tracking implementation milestones and delivery of results. This includes:

Programme Planning and Implementation Support:

- Coordinating the design and implementation of the Centre’s programme activities in collaboration with the DAI Hub team and relevant partners;

- Supporting the Head of Global Partnerships on resource mobilization activities, including preparing concept notes and documentation to identify opportunities from development partners, private sector, and key stakeholders;

- Coordinating with the Head of Strategic Resourcing of the DAI Hub on budget tracking and financial management matters, ensuring alignment with UNDP policies, funding arrangements, and corporate requirements;

- Monitoring and providing regular progress updates on Centre activities, flagging implementation risks and proposing adjustments for the consideration of the Chief Digital Officer;

- Collaborating with DAI Hub colleagues to support the development of cohesive offers, proposals, programmes, and projects aligned to the Centre’s thematic focus areas;

- Supporting the Centre’s contribution to UNDP’s broader digital transformation agenda, ensuring the coherence of activities with the DAI Hub’s strategic objectives.

Technical Analysis and Knowledge Support:

- Continuously monitor emerging developments in digital policy, AI, innovation and technology with relevance to sustainable development, preparing research summaries and horizon-scanning briefs for the Chief Digital Officer and DAI Hub leadership;

- Prepare and contribute to knowledge products, policy briefs, reports and presentations that support the Centre’s role as a hub for digital and AI knowledge in development;

- Support the design and delivery of Centre activities, including events, workshops, and convenings, ensuring they are substantively grounded and relevant to policymakers, private sector, academia, and civil society stakeholders;

- Engage with relevant UNDP colleagues in regional bureaux and thematic teams to support alignment of the Centre’s programme with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, providing analytical inputs and briefings as requested.

Stakeholder Coordination and Engagement Support:

- Provide coordination, analytical, and operational support for partnership engagement activities with external and internal stakeholders, under the strategic direction of the Chief Digital Officer and the Head of Partnerships and Engagement of the DAI Hub;

- Under the guidance of the Head of Partnerships and Engagement, support the identification and analysis of partnership opportunities, particularly with private sector actors, digital and technology companies, and innovation institutions in Singapore and the Asia-Pacific region;

- Liaise and coordinate with UNDP regional and central bureaux, including the Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific, the Malaysia Country Office, and relevant Global Policy Network (GPN) teams, to ensure effective information-sharing and collaboration;

- Facilitate connections between external stakeholders and UNDP teams, supporting the brokering of knowledge exchanges, expert convenings, and collaborative initiatives under the direction of DAI Hub leadership.

Knowledge Management and UNDP Integration

- Support information flows within and between the UNDP Global Centre, the DAI Hub and its broader digital network, BPPS, and the wider UNDP Global Policy Network, continually identifying opportunities to contribute to UNDP’s impact;

- Keep abreast of major institutional initiatives and relevant events, identifying opportunities for DAI Hub and UNDP engagement, and preparing briefings and inputs as requested;

- Facilitate regular information-sharing and planning with different parts of the DAI Hub and UNDP, identifying opportunities, gaps, and areas for collaboration to ensure the value-added of the Centre’s activities;

- Coordinate the management of donor and partner reporting for the Centre, collecting key results, lessons, and ensuring sound reporting in collaboration with the DAI Hub Partnerships Team, Operations, and Finance;

- Contribute to institutional learning by documenting good practices, lessons learned, and Centre results in accessible knowledge products for the benefit of the DAI Hub and UNDP more broadly;

- Develop benchmarks and methods for monitoring the Centre’s programme performance and reporting against agreed results frameworks.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

- The position will report into Chief Digital Officer/Director of DAI hub.

Competencies

Core Competencies:

Achieve Results:LEVEL 3: Set and align challenging, achievable objectives for multiple projects, have lasting impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 3: Proactively mitigate potential risks, develop new ideas to solve complex problems

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 3: Create and act on opportunities to expand horizons, diversify experiences

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 3: Proactively initiate and champion change, manage multiple competing demands

Act with Determination: LEVEL 3: Think beyond immediate task/barriers and take action to achieve greater results

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 3: Political savvy, navigate complex landscape, champion inter-agency collaboration

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 3: Appreciate benefits of diverse workforce and champion inclusivity

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies:

Business Direction & Strategy: Strategic Thinking: Develop effective strategies and prioritized plans in line with UNDP’s mission and objectives, based on the systemic analysis of challenges, opportunities and potential risks; link the general vision to reality on the ground to create tangible targeted solutions; learn from a variety of sources to anticipate and effectively respond to both current and future trends; demonstrate foresight.

Digital: Digital Ecosystems: Knowledge of how they work, understanding of the opportunities and challenges for governments and Society.

Digital : Artificial intelligence thought leadership: Deep understanding of current and emerging trends in AI, along with their social, ethical, and economic implications, including data privacy and human rights.

Ability to engage with industry experts, government representatives, and academics to stay updated on latest trends and to form partnerships. Strong skills in conducting and interpreting research to support thought leadership initiatives, including white papers, policy briefs, or case studies. Understanding of global trends and cultural nuances, as they relate to the field of AI. Familiarity with international laws and standards regarding technology, particularly in a multi-stakeholder environment like the UN.

Data: Data Analysis: Ability to extract, analyse and visualize data to form meaningful insights and aid effective business decision making

Business Direction & Strategy: Systems Thinking: Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

Business Management: Results-based Management : Ability to manage the implementation of strategies, programmes, and projects with a focus at improved performance and demonstrable results. Knowledge and understanding of relevant theories, concepts, methodologies, instruments, and tools.

Business Management : Partnerships Management : Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (master’s or equivalent) in Public Policy, International Development, Digital Policy, Computer Science, or related discipline is required, or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above fields in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience will be given due consideration in lieu of a master’s degree.

Experience:

- Minimum 10 years of relevant work experience (with master’s degree) or 12 years of relevant work experience (with bachelor’s degree) in international development, digital policy, or technology for development (international organizations, government, private sector, or civil society.

Required Skills:

- Demonstrated experience in programme coordination and knowledge management within international or multilateral organizations;

- Proven track record of substantive experience in engagement with the Singaporean digital, AI and innovation ecosystem;

- Strong experience building partnerships and facilitating multi-stakeholder collaboration, particularly with private sector, government, and academia;

- Strong professional experience and understanding of the role of digital, technology, and innovation in sustainable development, including work on digital strategies or technology solutions;

- Proven experience developing impactful, outcomes-focused partnerships, particularly with the private sector and digital and AI innovation actors.

Desired Skills:

- Experience in resource mobilization support and donor/partner coordination for global or strategic programmes;

- Experience in working with the Singaporean ecosystem on areas of focus for the Centre;

- Experience working within UNDP or UN system.

Required Languages:

- Fluency in English is required.

- Knowledge of another official UN language (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian or Spanish) is an asset.

Equal opportunity

As an equal opportunity employer, UNDP values diversity as an expression of the multiplicity of nations and cultures where we operate and, as such, we encourage qualified applicants from all backgrounds to apply for roles in the organization. Our employment decisions are based on merit and suitability for the role, without discrimination.

UNDP is also committed to creating an inclusive workplace where all personnel are empowered to contribute to our mission, are valued, can thrive, and benefit from career opportunities that are open to all.

Sexual harassment, exploitation, and abuse of authority

UNDP does not tolerate harassment, sexual harassment, exploitation, discrimination and abuse of authority. All selected candidates, therefore, undergo relevant checks and are expected to adhere to the respective standards and principles.

Right to select multiple candidates

UNDP reserves the right to select one or more candidates from this vacancy announcement. We may also retain applications and consider candidates applying to this post for other similar positions with UNDP at the same grade level and with similar job description, experience and educational requirements.

Use of AI by candidates

Applicants are invited to read UNDP’s guidance for candidates on using AI responsibly in UNDP recruitment and selection

Scam alert

UNDP does not charge a fee at any stage of its recruitment process. For further information, please see www.undp.org/scam-alert.

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP is the leading United Nations organization fighting to end the injustice of poverty, inequality, and climate change. Working with our broad network of experts and partners in 170 countries, we help nations to build integrated, lasting solutions for people and planet. The Fiji multi-country office covers ten countries including Federated States of Micronesia, Fiji, Kiribati, Republic of the Marshall Islands, Republic of Naoero, Palau, Solomon Islands, Tonga, Tuvalu, and Vanuatu as well as provides support to regional initiatives.

UNDP in the Pacific has developed its Multi-Country Programme Document (MCPD, 2023-2027) to guide its interventions in the next five years in full alignment and directly to contribute to the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF, 2023–2027). The Office covers 10 countries in the Pacific with an extensive portfolio which has grown over time. The UNSDCF and UNDP MCPD are designed in full alignment with the 2030 agenda, Samoa Pathway, and 2050 Strategy for the Blue Pacific Continent, which is endorsed by the Pacific Island Countries (PICs) among others. The UNDP Pacific Office next five-year plan strategic priorities are encapsulated under three outcome areas: (i) Planet, (ii) Prosperity, and (iii) Peace. Following a strategic review process which was completed in June 2022, UNDP Pacific office structure is aligned to the emerging priorities of the office. In this regard, the programme portfolio will include mutually reinforcing work streams crafted around two clusters (i) Resilience and Climate Change; and (ii) Inclusive Growth and Effective Governance, supported by a policy and innovations team, operations team, management programme and oversight team, which provides strategic guidance on results management and compliance entrusted with the corporate alignment, programme finance management and quality assurance, and a strategic communications team, which provides knowledge management and communication support to all programme interventions.

Fiji is among the most disaster-prone countries in the Pacific and is exposed to tropical cyclones, floods, storm surges, landslides, droughts, earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic hazards, disease outbreaks and the increasing impacts of climate change. These hazards continue to affect lives, livelihoods, infrastructure, ecosystems and national development.

The National Disaster Management Act 2024 establishes the National Disaster Risk Management Office (NDRMO) as the lead agency responsible for coordinating disaster risk management, disaster risk reduction, disaster preparedness, response, and recovery and resilience-building across Fiji. The Act further provides for the establishment of Divisional Disaster Risk Management Offices to strengthen sub-national coordination and implementation of disaster risk management.

To support implementation of the National Disaster Management Act 2024, the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy 2018–2030, the National Disaster Risk Management Plan, the Early Warnings for All (EW4All) Initiative and the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) Roadmap, the Government of Fiji, through the UNDP Green Climate Fund Programme, will recruit an IT Assistant to manage and optimize its ICT infrastructure, enterprise platforms, and disaster information systems, while accelerating digital transformation initiatives across Fiji's emergency management system.

Working under the technical direction of the National Coordinator and the Project Manager - EW4All, the Project IT Assistant will ensure the continuous operation (24/7 operational readiness), security, interoperability, real-time disaster monitoring, multi-agency coordination, rapid public warning dissemination and enhancement of NDRMO's critical disaster information systems, including: the National Disaster Information System (NDRIS), the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy (NDRRP) Online M&E Tracker, the Asset Management Tracker, the National Emergency Operations Centre (NEOC) information and display systems, and the digital platforms driving the Multi-Hazard Early Warning System (MHEWS) and Common Alerting Protocol (CAP).

Duties and Responsibilities

The incumbent will serve as the primary focal point for:

- Enterprise ICT Infrastructure & System Administration.

- Multi-Hazard Early Warning & CAP Platform Integration.

- Disaster Information Systems & Analytics.

- 24/7 NEOC and Emergency Operations Support.

- Stakeholder Coordination, Policy & Innovation

1. Maintain enterprise ICT Infrastructure and system administration:

- Infrastructure Management: maintain, optimize, and secure NDRMO’s core servers, enterprise networks, databases, cloud platforms, and storage environments to guarantee high operational availability.

- Security & Continuity: implement robust cybersecurity protocols, role-based user access controls, automated data backup solutions, and disaster recovery plan (DRP) arrangements to ensure continuous service during crisis events.

- Asset Lifecycle & Standards: manage the ICT hardware asset register, software licensing, system upgrades, and hardware refresh planning in full compliance with Government and UNDP standards.

2.Support multi-hazard early warning & CAP platform integration:

- CAP Administration: administer the central National Common Alerting Protocol (CAP) platform, facilitating technical integrations with authorized warning authorities (e.g., FMS, MRD, MSAF, MoHMS).

- Interoperability & Connectivity: maintain digital gateways and API connections between NDRMO systems, the Ministry of Communications, telecommunications providers (mobile network operators), broadcasters, and digital channels for rapid warning fan-out.

- System Testing & Drills: conduct routine technical tests, simulation exercises, and operational readiness checks of all automated public warning dissemination systems.

3.Monitor disaster information systems & analytics:

- NDRIS Administration: maintain and scale the National Disaster Risk Information System (NDRIS) to secure data integrity across historical incident records, loss databases, and situational updates.

- NDRRP Online Tracker: oversee user administration, data quality control, and functional support for the National Disaster Risk Reduction Policy (NDRRP) M&E Tracker across participating Government bodies.

- GIS & Business Intelligence: develop dynamic operational dashboards, geospatial visualizations, and reporting tools to support real-time decision-making for leadership.

4. Ensure 24/7 NEOC and emergency operations support:

- NEOC Operational Readiness: maintain continuous availability of video conferencing, situational displays, incident logging systems, and communication tools within the National Emergency Operations Centre.

- High-Availability Emergency Support: provide 24/7 rostered on-call technical support during emergency activations to resolve critical ICT incidents rapidly.

5.Support stakeholder coordination, policy & innovation:

- Government ICT Alignment: work closely with the Ministry of Communications and national technology partners to align NDRMO systems with broader e-Government and national cybersecurity frameworks.

- Emerging Technologies: evaluate and advise leadership on integrating emerging technologies (e.g., geospatial analysis, automated alerts, AI analytics, mobile applications) into national disaster management.

- Capacity Building: develop technical documentation, standard operating procedures (SOPs), and user training programs for NDRMO personnel and inter-agency partners.

6.Support knowledge building and knowledge sharing relevant to the project:

- Participate in training on IT or related matters for the staff and provide support to the organization of training and other capacity building activities as needed.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Demonstrate focus on achieving quality results and impact

Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Look beyond conventional approaches and established methods

Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Actively pursue opportunities for learning and self-development professionally and personally

Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Be flexible in handling change, and adopt new ideas, approaches and ways of working

Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Pursue everything with motivation and drive

Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Act in a way that demonstrates empathy and emotional intelligence, showing consideration for the needs and feelings of others

Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Treat all individuals with respect, consider ethical implications and respond sensitively to all differences among people

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Direction & Strategy

- Systems Thinking : Ability to use objective problem analysis and judgement to understand how interrelated elements coexist within an overall process or system, and to consider how altering one element can impact on other parts of the system.

- Effective Decision Making: Take decisions in a timely and efficient manner in line with one's authority, area of expertise and resources and take into consideration potential wider implications.

Business Management

- Digital Awareness and Literacy: Ability to monitor new and emerging technologies, as well as understand their usage, potential, limitations, impact, and added value. Ability to rapidly and readily adopt and use new technologies in professional activities, and to empower others to use them as needed. Knowledge of the usage of digital technologies and emerging trends.

External Relations & Advocacy (Communications)

- Cybersecurity : Ability to analyze and advise on cybersecurity issues and policies for digital communications

Operations: IT -Information Management & Technology

- Network, Communication and Infrastructure Management: Ability to develop/integrate/operate/manage IT network, communications, Cloud or on-premise infrastructure, and new technologies like IoT. Cisco CCIE CCNP or similar is desirable

- IT Continuity and Disaster Recovery: Ability to advise on IT continuity and disaster recovery. Knowledge of ISO 22301 an asset.

- User Experience and business analyst: Capacity to translate efficiently users needs in IT requirements around human-centred design principles. Knowledge of Oracle Cloud, ServiceNow, SalesForce.com, and Microsoft product an asset.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
